## 39.3 Question 3 — AIMD. Does the ADR-012/014 judgement stand?

**Answer: yes, and κ does not touch it — because it was never mainly a cost decision.** But there
is exactly one purpose for which nothing else in our tool set will do, and I am naming it precisely
rather than saying "validation".

### (a) Why κ does not reopen this

ADR-014 Decision 4 is a **user instruction** (*"AIMD를 개발 과정에서 최대한 배제"*). ADR-025 then
scoped the exclusion to **(b) long, serial production AIMD** — leaving short, fully-parallel,
zero-chaining trajectories formally outside it (ADR-033 relies on exactly that reading). So the
door is ajar by prior decision, not by my argument. **But a cheaper κ is not a reason to walk
through a door the user narrowed.** ADR-050's lesson is that the lead reinterpreting a
user-declared requirement as a tradeoff is the failure, not the fix. ⟹ I put this to the user.

### (b) The specific purpose — and it is a transferability problem, not a validation nicety

Every S1 number we will ever compute is conditioned on **which cluster we compute it for**:
`Li⁺(EC)ₙ(EMC)ₘ`, n+m = 4-ish. The reduction barrier of EC is a strong function of the first
solvation shell composition and of whether the reduced species stays in the contact ion pair.
Where does that distribution currently come from? **Literature Li⁺ coordination statistics
(U-41), whose very existence is recorded as unverified.**

🔴 **That is a known-answer dependency of exactly the class ADR-014 outlawed.** For an unstudied
electrolyte there is no literature CN. ADR-051 ③ already rejected classical MD as a production
route for precisely this reason — per-composition force-field parameterisation is human labour that
does not transfer, and *"a literature CN is the same ADR-001 transferability violation"*.

So: **what element-agnostic instrument determines the Li⁺ shell distribution for a composition
nobody has studied?** Three candidates.

---

### Candidate 1: static cluster–continuum coordination equilibrium (no dynamics at all)
- **Physical assumption**: the shell distribution is the Boltzmann population over a set of
  `Li⁺(EC)ₙ(EMC)ₘ(PF6⁻)_k` cluster minima computed at our production level with SMD, with a
  standard-state/concentration correction for ligand exchange. **Breaks when** the second shell and
  the packing entropy of the bulk liquid contribute differentially across the competing
  stoichiometries — i.e. exactly the term the continuum smears out — and when the relevant
  ensemble is not a set of well-separated minima but a continuous manifold.
- **Expected accuracy**: shell *ranking* probably right; shell *populations* `[UNKNOWN]`. The
  standard-state correction for n ligands carries a `n·RT·ln(c°/c_solvent)` term that is
  ~0.05–0.1 eV per ligand and is a modelling choice, not a measurement.
- **Known silent-failure mode**: 🔴 it will always return a distribution. It cannot signal that the
  true liquid has no such well-defined shells. And §39.1(e) says these are precisely the clusters
  our optimiser fails on — a floppy manifold is the *physical* reason both for the optimiser failure
  and for the continuum approximation being weakest here. **The same physics breaks both.**
- **Verification**: against candidate 2 on the primary system; against Li⁺ solvation free energy
  and, if we can find it, EXAFS/NMR-derived CN for EC:EMC + LiPF6 (external, but only for the
  primary system — for an unstudied one, nothing).
- **Required input**: cluster geometries (already in the pool), ligand-exchange thermodynamic cycle.
- **Cost profile**: `N_stoichiometry × N_conformer × (opt+freq)`. Already largely inside the pool
  budget. ⚠ but see §39.1(e) — the per-species cost of this class is the open question.

### Candidate 2: short, unchained DFT MD, used **once**, to calibrate candidate 1
- **Physical assumption**: 5–10 ps of Born–Oppenheimer dynamics on a 40–60 atom periodic or
  cluster box samples the first-shell exchange statistics well enough to give the *populations*,
  even if it does not converge free energies. **Breaks when** first-shell residence times exceed
  the trajectory length — which is the real risk: Li⁺–carbonate exchange in carbonate electrolytes
  is on the order of hundreds of ps to ns, so 10 ps samples *fluctuations about* an initial shell,
  not the equilibrium *between* shells. 🔴 **I state this as the dominant weakness of this
  candidate, and it is the reason I am not asking for more AIMD than this.** Mitigation: run
  several independent trajectories with *different initial shell compositions* and compare
  stability/relaxation, i.e. use it as a consistency test on candidate 1's minima rather than as an
  ergodic sampler. That is a much weaker claim and it is the claim I am willing to defend.
- **Expected accuracy**: as an ergodic population estimate, poor. **As a falsifier of candidate 1's
  minima** ("does the cluster candidate 1 says is dominant survive 10 ps of dynamics in a
  condensed-phase box, or does a ligand leave in 2 ps?") — decisive, and that is the question I
  actually need answered.
- **Known silent-failure mode**: `T_eff` — ADR-051 ③ U-52 flags that G16 `ADMP`/`BOMD` with `NKE`
  initial excitation gives `T_eff ≈ T_init/2`, the same shape as ADR-047's DRC correction, factor
  unmeasured. **Used without correction, the sampling temperature is off by 2× and nothing crashes.**
- **Verification**: mutual with candidate 1; the observable is shell-composition survival, which is
  a discrete count, not an energy — so it is robust to the level of theory.
- **Required input**: an equilibrated liquid box. 🔴 We have no classical force field to
  pre-equilibrate with (LAMMPS is available but per ADR-051 ③ the parameterisation is the cost).
  **Packing a box from cluster geometries and annealing it inside the DFT MD is expensive and is a
  real, unbudgeted term.**
- **Cost profile**: `N_system × t_ps / dt × cost(SCF+gradient, 40–60 atoms)`, fully parallel across
  systems, zero chaining, each trajectory under the 48 h wall. Engineer5 asked.
- **Engines**: G16 `ADMP`/`BOMD` (permission cost 0, non-periodic GTO, no charged-periodic Poisson
  pitfall) or VASP (periodic, correct for a liquid, but a different level seam). **I lean VASP for
  a liquid box and G16 for cluster-in-continuum dynamics; that is a real choice and I do not have
  the data to make it.** `[UNRESOLVED — U-53]`

### Candidate 3: declare the shell distribution an explicit uncertainty axis and propagate it
- **Physical assumption**: none — we refuse to estimate the distribution and instead compute S1
  barriers for **every** plausible shell composition, then report the barrier as a *set* and let
  the microkinetics carry the spread as an ensemble (ADR-018's principle: the question is not
  "is it accurate" but "does the conclusion survive the error").
- **Expected accuracy**: exact in the sense that it makes no claim. **Its cost is interpretive**:
  if the barrier spread across shells is 0.3 eV, every downstream conclusion is reported as a
  50,000× rate band and the network cannot be ranked. **That is the failure mode, and it is loud
  rather than silent — which is its virtue.**
- **Known silent-failure mode**: essentially none. It fails visibly.
- **Verification**: the spread itself is the deliverable; the falsifier is whether ADR-018's
  robustness test (perturb, re-run, does the ranking flip) survives.
- **Required input**: n×m enumeration of shells — which multiplies S1 by the number of shells.
- **Cost profile**: `N_species × N_shell × N_conformer`, and 🔴 **it is the only one of the three
  that κ makes materially cheaper**, because it is pure enumeration with no human in the loop.

---

**🔴 My preference: Candidate 3 as the production route, Candidate 1 as its prior, and Candidate 2
once, on the primary system only, as the falsifier of Candidate 1.**

Reasoning, and it is a change of position from the "AIMD → 0" framing I helped build:
1. Candidate 3 is the only one that **transfers with no new input** to an unstudied electrolyte,
   which is the requirement. It converts an unknown parameter into a declared axis.
2. Candidate 3 alone is not enough, because a 0.3 eV band ranks nothing. Candidate 1 supplies the
   weights that collapse the band, and candidate 1 is nearly free (it is already in the pool).
3. **Candidate 1's weights are unfalsifiable without candidate 2.** A continuum calculation of a
   floppy coordination manifold will always return populations and cannot detect that it is wrong.
   §39.1(e) shows that this exact species class is already misbehaving numerically. One 4-trajectory
   experiment on the primary system converts "we assumed the shell weights" into "we measured
   whether the assumed weights survive dynamics", **once**, and the answer transfers as a
   *method-validity statement* even though the numbers do not.
4. What I am **not** proposing: AIMD to compute λ, to compute barriers, to discover reactions, or
   for any unstudied system. ADR-038/039's no-MD λ_out route survives the pilot (U-27 closed) and
   I am not reopening it.

🔴 **This is a USER decision.** It sits inside a line the user drew. It should go up with
engineer5's number attached and with the sentence: *"the alternative is that the Li⁺ shell
distribution — which every S1 barrier is conditioned on — is supplied by literature values that
do not exist for the systems this project is ultimately for."*

---

## 39.4 🔴 Question 4 — P1. The prescription.

### (a) The verdict "IRC ran to the same minimum in both directions" is an artifact. The IRC never left the saddle.

Four independent facts from `pilots[P1].detail`, all present in the returned report:

```
1. ENERGIES        TS (ts_qst2)      E = -350.011388718 Ha
                   IRC forward end   E = -350.011391520 Ha    ΔE = -2.8e-6 Ha = -0.00008 eV
                   IRC reverse end   E = -350.011389969 Ha    ΔE = -1.3e-6 Ha = -0.00003 eV
   🔴 Both "endpoints" are the transition state, to within 0.1 meV.
      A real IRC descends by 0.1–1 eV. This one descended by 80 µeV.

2. STEP COUNTS     irc_forward:  opt.cycles = 2,  converged = false
                   irc_reverse:  opt.cycles = 20, converged = false
                   n_frames_forward = 1, n_frames_reverse = 1

3. TERMINATION     irc_forward  normal_termination = true
                   irc_reverse  normal_termination = FALSE
                                "Error termination via Lnk1e in .../l123.exe"
                                l123 IS the IRC link. The reverse IRC crashed.

4. GRAPHS          endpoint_fragments both = "C3H4LiO3";  n_layer_c_bonds = 9 both sides;
                   layer_c_changes = [], layer_i_changes = [], bond_changes = []
                   — identical topology, identical hashes, both layers.
```
🔴 **CORRECTION, self-issued after §39.4(g) below.** In the first draft of this section I read fact 4
as *"a ring-opened product has one fewer bond, both endpoints have 9, therefore both are the closed
ring."* **That is wrong and I am leaving the error visible rather than editing it away.** The
ring-*closed* reactant has **10** covalent bonds and the ring-*opened* product has **9** (verified
in §39.4(g)). So 9 is the *opened* count, and both IRC endpoints — and therefore the TS itself —
already have the breaking C–O beyond the covalent cutoff.

🟢 **The conclusion of (a) is untouched**: facts 1, 2 and 3 each independently establish that the
IRC never left the saddle, and fact 1 (80 µeV of descent) is decisive on its own.
🔴 **But the correction produces a finding fact 4 did not have when I read it wrongly:**
> **For a late transition state, the covalent-bond graph cannot distinguish the TS from its forward
> product.** The TS already carries the product's bond count. ⟹ **a matching forward hash can never
> confirm that the forward IRC moved**, for any late TS, in any reaction. Only the *energy* can.
> 🔒 This is an independent argument for constraint **C-2**'s third clause
> (`|E_end − E_TS| > 0.05 eV`): the topological clauses cannot substitute for it, and a
> topology-only IRC gate is structurally blind to exactly this case.

⟹ **rule R3 was applied to two copies of the transition state.** The endpoint-comparison machinery
worked perfectly; it was fed the same geometry twice. It even ran its own threshold-sensitivity
check (±0.2 Å, 0 flips) and correctly reported robustness — of a comparison of a structure with
itself. 🔴 **The Li–X cutoff provenance flag (`[PLACEHOLDER-ESTIMATE]`) is irrelevant here; no
cutoff choice can separate a geometry from itself.**

🔒 **This is Rule 20 in its purest form yet, and it is the third instance this project has found:**
```
check that ran     : "the two IRC endpoint geometries are isomorphic"
property claimed   : "the two directions of the reaction path lead to the same minimum"
gap                : whether the IRC produced a path at all
```
The report **contains** the numbers that close the gap (`n_frames`, `normal_termination`,
`stage_rc.irc_reverse = 1`, the three energies). The verdict was rendered without consulting them.

🔒 **Coder constraint, blocking, and it belongs in the same family as ADR-048's asymmetric test:**
> **No chemical verdict may be issued for an IRC unless, for BOTH directions:
> (i) `normal_termination == true`, (ii) `n_points ≥ 5`, and
> (iii) `|E_endpoint − E_TS| > 0.05 eV`.**
> If any fails, the status is **`indeterminate`**, never `fail`. "The TS is wrong" and "the IRC did
> not run" must not share an exit code — they have opposite prescriptions and identical symptoms.

### (b) So: endpoint problem, IRC step-count problem, or wrong method? — In that order of certainty:

**1. It is *first* an IRC execution problem, and that is now established, not hypothesised.**
The mechanism is almost certainly this: G16's IRC (default algorithm HPC, default `StepSize = 10`
in units of 0.01 Bohr, default `MaxPoints = 10` — verified at `gaussian.com/irc/` this round)
terminates a direction when the gradient falls below its path-convergence threshold. **Along a
−105 cm⁻¹ mode the surface is nearly flat, so the very first step lands somewhere with a gradient
below threshold, and the IRC declares the path complete while still on the saddle.** Two forward
points and an 80 µeV descent is the signature of exactly that. The reverse direction did something
worse and crashed in l123 after 20 steps.

**2. It is *also* an endpoint problem — 🟢 and this has now been TESTED, at zero cost. See §39.4(g).
The answer is not the one I expected.**
QST2 interpolates between two supplied structures. If the two structures differ by a torsion or by
a Li⁺ hop between coordinating oxygens rather than by ring opening, QST2 will faithfully find a
**conformational** saddle — soft mode, ~100 cm⁻¹, IRC connecting two conformers that our graph
layer correctly calls the same species.
🔴 **The decisive check costs nothing: run the existing two-layer graph code (the same
`endpoint_comparison` machinery, `graph_layers.json`) on the two QST2 *input* geometries.**
```
hash_C(reactant_input) == hash_C(product_input)  ⟹ QST2 was asked for a TS between a
                                                   structure and a conformer of itself.
                                                   That alone explains everything observed.
hash_C differ by exactly the intended C–O bond   ⟹ endpoints were right, and the fault is
                                                   entirely in the IRC.
```
**This must be run before anything is resubmitted. 0 core-h.** It is the highest
information-per-cost item in this entire section.

**3. Is QST2 the wrong method? — Yes, as a *default*, though not necessarily as the cause here.**
QST2's weaknesses are exactly ours: it needs matched atom ordering, it is unreliable when reactant
and product differ by a large-amplitude rearrangement, and — critically — **it gives no diagnostic
when it converges to a saddle of the wrong coordinate.** It returns a converged stationary point
with one imaginary frequency, which is precisely what our acceptance gate asks for.

### (c) 🔴 The window is the wrong instrument, and −105 cm⁻¹ is not the reason

ADR-035 approved keeping `IMAG_WINDOW_CM1 = (−2000, −100)` while the lead recorded doubt (b):
*"the risk is not the width, it is the distance to the boundary; a shallow TS near −100 can leave
the window when the basis changes."* ADR-035's reopen-condition 2 is "if imaginary frequencies
cluster in −100…−250". We have n = 1 at −105. **That is not a cluster and I am not reopening
ADR-035 on the basis of one point.** I am reopening it on a different and stronger ground:

> 🔴 **The magnitude of the imaginary frequency is not evidence about whether a saddle is the
> transition state of the reaction we asked about. It is a property of the curvature; the question
> is about the *direction*.** A hindered methyl rotation at −40 cm⁻¹ and a ring-opening TS at
> −400 cm⁻¹ are both "exactly one imaginary mode". A magnitude window cannot distinguish them, and
> the P1 result is a demonstration: the frequency test **passed** (`freq.passed: true`) on a saddle
> that our own IRC could not connect to anything.

**Replace M2 with a mode-character test:**
```
M2′  Let b = the set of internal coordinates the NETWORK EDGE says should change
         (the break/form list; ADR-015's grammar guarantees |b| ≤ 4 and it is machine-readable).
     Let q = the mass-weighted imaginary-mode eigenvector.
     Require the normalised projection  Ω = |proj_b(q)| / |q|  ≥ Ω_min.
     Ω_min to be CALIBRATED, not asserted — from the human-reviewed S3 TS set (§39.7 candidate 3).
     🔴 Do not hard-code a threshold this round. That is how −100 got there.

M2″  Magnitude becomes a SOFT FLAG, not a gate:
       |ν_i| < 30 cm⁻¹   → reject (numerical noise / rotational artefact; a genuine floor)
       30–150 cm⁻¹        → flag, route to M2′ and to the connectivity test, DO NOT auto-reject
       150–2000 cm⁻¹      → normal
       > 2000 cm⁻¹        → flag (usually a bad Hessian or a broken geometry)
```
**Why this is strictly better for *this* project and not just in general:**
- 🔴 **It is element-agnostic and therefore transfers.** ADR-014's final requirement is an unstudied
  electrolyte. A cm⁻¹ window is implicitly calibrated on carbonate chemistry — the same reduced
  masses, the same bonds. A projection onto the edge's own bond-change list carries no chemistry.
- It is defined by the **edge**, which we already have; it needs no new input.
- It converts an unverifiable premise ("a 1,900 cm⁻¹ wide window covers basis-set drift of tens of
  cm⁻¹") into a measured quantity (the distribution of Ω over reviewed TSs).
- It removes ADR-035's whole open question, rather than answering it.
🔒 **The `IMAG_WINDOW_PROVENANCE` field ADR-035 created is the right pattern and must be kept and
extended to Ω** — that field, not the number, was ADR-035's actual product, and it remains so.

### (d) 🔴 What we change before retrying, in order. (Zero-cost items first — none of this is authorised yet.)

```
STEP 0  [0 core-h]  Run the existing 2-layer graph code on the two QST2 INPUT geometries.
                    Publish hash_C / hash_CI for both. This alone may end the investigation.
STEP 0b [0 core-h]  Publish the imaginary-mode eigenvector from the existing ts_qst2 log and
                    compute Ω against the intended C–O bond. We already have the Hessian.
                    🔴 If Ω is small, the saddle is a conformational one and no IRC setting
                       would ever have saved it.
STEP 0c [0 core-h]  Fix the solvent. P1's route is `scrf=(smd,solvent=acetonitrile)`.
                    Our production spec (§26.5) is `solvent=generic` with the seven SMD
                    descriptors volume-weighted for EC:EMC 3:7. Acetonitrile has ε = 35.7 against
                    EC:EMC's ≈ 18–20 — roughly a factor of two on the reaction field. For a
                    charge-localising ring-opening of an ion pair this is not cosmetic. It was
                    presumably a pilot placeholder; it must not survive into S3.
```
Then, **and only if STEP 0 shows the endpoints were genuinely distinct**:
```
STEP 1  Replace the TS-location method. Candidates in §39.4(e).
STEP 2  Replace the connectivity test. Primary = displaced-mode optimisation, not IRC:
          from the converged TS, displace ±0.15–0.3 Å along the imaginary mode and run a
          PLAIN geometry optimisation in each direction.
          · robust where IRC is fragile — it is an ordinary optimisation, no path integrator
          · costs ~2 opts instead of ~80 core-h of IRC (P1: irc_fwd 25.4 + irc_rev 56.2)
          · 🔴 HONEST WEAKNESS: it can skip over a shallow intermediate that a true IRC would
            resolve, so it answers "which minima does this saddle connect" and NOT "what is the
            path". For a reaction NETWORK we need the former; for a mechanism claim we need the
            latter.
          ⟹ RATIO, not replacement: displaced-opt on all, full IRC on the subset that is quoted,
            anchors the surrogate, or shows any ambiguity. The IRC/displaced-opt AGREEMENT RATE
            on that subset is a reportable number and is the falsifier for the substitution.
STEP 3  If IRC is run, change its settings for soft modes:
          larger StepSize (default 10 = 0.10 Bohr → 20–30), MaxPoints well above the default 10,
          `Recalc` rather than `CalcFC`-once, and consider tighter SCF (the flat-surface case is
          where SCF noise becomes comparable to the true gradient).
          ⚠ exact keyword syntax to be verified by coder against the G16 manual, not from me.
```

### (g) 🔴🔴 STEP 0 EXECUTED — the QST2 endpoints are in the repository, and the root cause is now established

The two QST2 endpoint geometries are **not on the cluster** — they are in the delivered package, at
`src/pilot_package/inputs/li_ec_radical_{reactant,product}.xyz`. So the zero-cost diagnostic I
prescribed in §39.4(d) STEP 0 could be run immediately, and I ran it. **No compute was used; this is
arithmetic on two 11-line text files.**

#### Result 1 — my leading hypothesis is REFUTED. The endpoints are topologically correct.

```
reactant  10 covalent bonds  C1-O2 C1-O5 C1-O6 O2-C3 C3-C4 C3-H7 C3-H8 C4-O5 C4-H9 C4-H10
                             ring closed: C1-O2-C3-C4-O5-C1        d(O2-C3) = 1.400 Å
product    9 covalent bonds  C1-O2 C1-O5 C1-O6       C3-C4 C3-H7 C3-H8 C4-O5 C4-H9 C4-H10
                             ring OPEN                              d(O2-C3) = 3.088 Å
difference = exactly one bond, O2-C3 — the alkyl (ethereal) C-O, which is the intended coordinate
```
🟢 **QST2 was not asked for a saddle between a structure and a conformer of itself.** The endpoints
differ by precisely the bond the reaction is supposed to break, and by nothing else. **Hypothesis
refuted, at zero cost, before anything was resubmitted. That is what the test was for.**

#### Result 2 — 🔴 the actual root cause, and it is worse, because it is a protocol defect

**Both files declare in their own header line that they are not optimised.**
```
reactant header: "... ring-closed. charge 0, mult 2. GUESS GEOMETRY (idealized, not optimized)."
product  header: "... ring-OPENED radical (alkyl C-O bond broken). ... GUESS GEOMETRY."
```
And the coordinates confirm it beyond the header:

| evidence | what it shows |
|---|---|
| every C–H is **1.062 Å**, all four identical (product: 1.062/1.064) | a drawing value, not an optimised one |
| the whole ring sits at one bond length: C1–O2 = C1–O5 = 1.399, O2–C3 = C4–O5 = 1.400, C3–C4 = 1.398 | 🔴 a real carbonate has C(sp²)–O ≈ 1.33–1.36 Å and O–CH₂ ≈ 1.44–1.46 Å, and C–C ≈ 1.52 Å. **These five bonds are drawn equal. No such molecule exists.** |
| the product is the reactant with **atom 3 translated and nothing else relaxed** — C3–C4 goes 1.398 → 1.500, every other coordinate is byte-identical | the carbonate fragment does not relax on ring opening, when in reality it becomes carboxylate-like and its C–O lengths change substantially |
| 🔴 **Li sits 1.85 Å from the carbonyl O in BOTH structures**, in a linear C=O···Li arrangement | in the real ring-opened radical Li⁺ migrates toward the newly formed alkoxide oxygen. **Li was not permitted to move along the reaction at all** — and Li⁺ migration is very likely *part of* the true reaction coordinate |
| 🔴 **every heavy atom has z = 0 in both structures**, and the H's sit at mirror-symmetric ±0.880 / ±0.850 | **both endpoints are planar by construction (Cs).** The reduced EC ring puckers and the ring-opened radical is not planar. |

#### Result 3 — this explains every observation, including the −105 cm⁻¹ and the dead IRC

```
QST2's premise      : its two endpoints are OPTIMISED MINIMA on the PES.
what it was handed  : two idealised, planar, non-stationary structures differing by a RIGID
                      TRANSLATION of one CH2 group.
what it therefore   : the saddle of the artificial path between two points that are not on the
optimised toward      surface's minima at all.
```
1. 🔴 **The soft mode is explained.** A saddle for a rigid-fragment displacement between two
   non-stationary points has small curvature. −105 cm⁻¹ is what that looks like. **No IRC setting
   and no window threshold would have rescued it.**
2. 🔴 **The planarity is a second, independent defect.** Both endpoints are Cs-symmetric, so the
   QST2 path preserves the mirror plane, and the optimiser can converge to a stationary point
   *within the symmetric subspace*. Such a point is routinely a saddle with respect to the
   **symmetry-breaking out-of-plane mode** rather than with respect to the reaction coordinate —
   which is a textbook way to obtain exactly one small imaginary frequency that means nothing about
   the reaction. **Our acceptance gate asks for "exactly one imaginary mode" and this produces one.**
3. 🔴 **The dead IRC is explained.** If the imaginary mode is a low-curvature out-of-plane or
   rigid-translation mode, the first IRC step lands where the gradient is already below the path
   threshold, the direction terminates after 2 points, and the reverse direction — trying to
   integrate a path on a nearly flat surface — crashes in l123. **Everything observed follows from
   Result 2. There is one cause, not three.**

#### Result 4 — 🔒 and it is the same failure shape as the rest of this project

```
information present  : the file's own header says "GUESS GEOMETRY (idealized, not optimized)"
what consumed it     : nothing. QST2 was run on it directly.
cost                 : 302 core-h, one wrong saddle, one dead IRC, and a "chemical failure" verdict
                       on a workflow whose input was never a minimum
```
🔒 **Fifth instance of the same pattern in this project**, after `cores_observed`, the module-name
`rstrip()`, the availability-from-a-name-in-a-list inference, and `converged` in §39.1: **the
disqualifying fact was written down, in the artefact itself, and no step read it.** Here it was
written in English, in the second line of the file, by whoever built the input.

⚠ **I want to be careful about blame, because it is not a coder error.** The pilot's purpose was to
measure *cost*, and for measuring the core-h of a QST2 stage an idealised guess is a perfectly
reasonable input — the arithmetic in ADR-064 (302 core-h, `longest_stage` 3.45 h ≪ 40 h tripwire) is
sound and survives. **What went wrong is that a cost pilot was also read as a chemistry result**,
because its acceptance criteria were chemical (`imag_freq_count`, `irc_endpoints_distinct`). 🔴 **A
cost probe should not carry a chemical pass/fail. It cannot earn one, and when it renders one the
whole team spends a round on it.**

#### 🔴 Revised prescription — what changes before a retry

```
P-1  🔴 OPTIMISE BOTH ENDPOINTS FIRST, and verify each has ZERO imaginary frequencies.
        This is QST2's stated precondition and it was not met. 2 cheap opt+freq runs.
        🔒 CODER CONSTRAINT (C-8): a TS search must refuse to start unless both endpoint
           structures are converged minima with n_imag == 0 at the same level. Not a warning.
P-2  🔴 BREAK THE SYMMETRY. Optimise the endpoints in C1 with no symmetry constraint, and
        perturb the planar guess out of plane before starting. A planar guess on a species that
        is not planar will optimise to a planar saddle and report one imaginary mode.
        🔒 CODER CONSTRAINT (C-9): never submit a TS search from a guess in which all heavy
           atoms are coplanar unless the species is genuinely planar. Detect and perturb.
P-3  🔴 LET Li MOVE. The product guess holds Li⁺ on the carbonyl oxygen. If Li⁺ migration is part
        of the coordinate, an endpoint that forbids it defines the wrong reaction.
        ⟹ the ring-opened endpoint must be optimised freely, and if Li relocates, THAT is the
           product — which is itself a result worth recording.
P-4  Fix the solvent (STEP 0c): `solvent=generic` with EC:EMC descriptors, not acetonitrile.
P-5  Only then: run §39.5's B1-F bake-off. QST2 from PROPERLY OPTIMISED endpoints is now a fair
     comparison against the relaxed-scan route, which it was not before.
     🔴 P1 does NOT constitute evidence against QST2. It was never given QST2's preconditions.
        My §39.4(e) preference for candidate B stands on its own arguments — scalability, no
        endpoint pairing, driven by the edge, transfers — and NOT on P1's failure.
        Correcting this is the difference between a bake-off and a formality.
```

#### 🟢 What this buys, stated plainly

```
before  : "P1 failed chemically. 302 core-h. Is the reaction wrong, the method wrong, or the gate
           wrong? Retry cost unknown, and the retry might fail the same way."
after   : one cause, identified from two text files at zero compute; a retry whose preconditions
           are now met; two new coder constraints that generalise beyond P1; and a correction to
           my own leading hypothesis before anything was resubmitted.
```
🔒 **The zero-cost diagnostic returned more than the 302 core-h run did.** I am recording that not
as a boast but as a scheduling principle: **§39.5's B1-F must be preceded by P-1…P-4, and no S3
production may start before a TS search has succeeded once under conditions we control.**
🔴 **U-56 stands and is now sharper: our TS success rate is not "0 of 1". It is UNMEASURED, because
the one attempt was run outside the method's stated preconditions and cannot be counted either way.**

### (e) TS location — the actual method choice

---

### Candidate A: keep QST2, fix the endpoints
- **Physical assumption**: a linear-synchronous/quadratic-synchronous interpolation between the two
  minima passes near the saddle. **Breaks when** the rearrangement is large-amplitude, when the
  atom ordering is not matched, or — our case — when a floppy coordination manifold offers many
  low saddles between the endpoints and the interpolation finds the nearest one.
- **Expected accuracy**: not an accuracy question; a *success-rate* question. `[UNKNOWN]` for our
  chemistry. **Our only datum is 1 attempt, 1 wrong saddle.**
- **Known silent-failure mode**: 🔴 **precisely the P1 failure** — it returns a converged saddle
  with one imaginary mode and no signal of which coordinate it belongs to.
- **Verification**: connectivity test (STEP 2) + Ω (M2′).
- **Cost**: measured, 220.8 core-h for the QST2 stage on an 11-atom system at the composite
  geometry level. ⚠ that is the cost of a *wrong* answer.

### Candidate B: relaxed surface scan along the designated breaking coordinate → TS optimisation
- **Physical assumption**: the edge names the bond(s) that break, so a constrained relaxed scan of
  that coordinate crosses the barrier; the scan maximum is a good TS guess. **Breaks when** the true
  saddle requires simultaneous motion in a second coordinate (concerted ET/ring-opening is exactly
  such a case — and it is the physics of our S1) so a 1-D scan gives a guess displaced from the
  saddle; the subsequent `opt=ts` must fix it. Breaks badly if the scan is discontinuous
  (electronic state change along the scan — real risk for radical anions).
- **Expected accuracy**: for the *barrier*, whatever the level gives; the scan only supplies the
  guess. **The important number is the TS-convergence success rate**, which for scan-seeded searches
  is generally much higher than for QST2 on floppy systems. `[UNVERIFIED — I am asserting a
  qualitative expectation, not a measured rate. It should be measured on the S3 pilot batch.]`
- **Known silent-failure mode**: a scan that quietly changes electronic state mid-way and produces a
  cusp read as a barrier. **Detectable**: monitor ⟨S²⟩ and the SCF solution along the scan; ADR-029's
  `stable=opt` recommendation applies here more than anywhere.
- **Verification**: Ω against the scanned coordinate (near 1 by construction if it worked — which
  makes Ω a *weak* test for this method and means STEP 2 connectivity carries the load).
- **Required input**: the edge's break/form list. **We already have it — it is what the grammar
  emits.** No conformer matching, no atom-order matching between two structures.
- **Cost profile**: `N_scan_points × (constrained opt at cheap level)` + one `opt=ts`. Scan points
  can be run at the cheap level or even xTB. 🔴 **Cheaper than QST2 and the guess is better**, but
  it is `N_scan` serial-ish steps, so wall-clock per TS may be worse than QST2's — an
  engineer question.

### Candidate C: double-ended path method (GSM / NEB-style), driven by our own edge definition
- **Physical assumption**: an elastic band / growing string between the two endpoints converges to
  the minimum-energy path, and the highest image seeds `opt=ts`. **Breaks when** endpoints are
  mis-specified (same as QST2) but it is far more tolerant of large-amplitude motion, and the band
  gives you the *path*, so a wrong-coordinate saddle is visible before you optimise it.
- **Expected accuracy**: best of the three for finding the *right* saddle. Same barrier accuracy
  once at `opt=ts`.
- **Known silent-failure mode**: band collapse into a local channel; sensitivity to the initial
  interpolation for floppy coordination (our problem again).
- **Verification**: the band's energy profile is itself the diagnostic — you can see whether the
  maximum sits on the intended coordinate before spending an `opt=ts`.
- **🔴 Tooling constraint**: pyGSM and standard NEB drivers are **not in the allowed engine set**
  ({G16, VASP, LAMMPS, xTB, +CP2K conditionally}). VASP has NEB but it is a plane-wave periodic
  code and using it for a solvated molecular TS would create a level seam of exactly the kind
  ADR-026/§26.4 spent two rounds eliminating. **Implementing a string method as our own driver over
  G16 gradients is possible and is a coder cost, not a core-h cost.** `[UNRESOLVED — U-54: is an
  in-house double-ended driver over G16 gradients within scope, or does it violate the spirit of the
  engine restriction?]` **This one needs the lead, possibly the user.**
- **Cost profile**: `N_images × N_band_iterations × gradient` — the most expensive of the three per
  attempt, the highest success rate per attempt. Whether that trade is good depends on the QST2
  failure rate, **which we do not know from n = 1**.

---

**🔴 My preference: Candidate B as the S3 default, Candidate A retained only where the two endpoints
are unambiguously distinct heavy-atom topologies, Candidate C escalated by hand.**

Reasoning: (i) B is driven by the **edge**, which is the object our whole architecture produces, so
it needs no endpoint pairing and no atom-order matching — the two things that make A brittle at
scale and that no human will be available to fix 500 times; (ii) B's guess quality is checkable
before the expensive step; (iii) B transfers to an unstudied electrolyte with no new input, and A's
endpoint construction does not obviously do so.
🔴 **But I want to be explicit that I am preferring B on an argument, not on data.** The honest
statement is: **we have one TS attempt and it failed, so our TS success rate is unmeasured, and
every S3 cost and schedule number in `03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md` rests on an assumed 40 % failure rate that
has now been sampled once, unsuccessfully.** ⟹ **§39.5 puts a 6-attempt method bake-off (A vs B on
3 reactions each) into the launch, and I would rather delay S3 than scale a method we have never
seen succeed.**

### (f) One more thing the P1 record says, that nobody asked about
`degraded: true`, `crest_skipped: true` — the 302 core-h **excludes conformer sampling entirely**
(the report's own estimate: −5 to −15 %), and `hessian_recomputed_per_irc` inflates it by
+10 to +25 %. Net `[−5 %, +20 %]`. **But the far larger correction is the one nobody labelled: 302
core-h bought a wrong saddle and a dead IRC. The unit cost of a TS is not 302 core-h; it is
302 core-h divided by an unmeasured success rate.** With the plan's assumed 40 % failure rate that
is ~500 core-h; with our observed rate it is undefined. 🔴 **This number must not enter a schedule
until §39.5's bake-off measures the denominator.**

 B1-F     6 runs  🔴 TS METHOD BAKE-OFF (from §39.4): 3 reactions × {QST2, relaxed-scan → opt=ts},
                     each followed by displaced-mode optimisation for connectivity, and full IRC
                     on whichever succeed. Deliverables: success rate per method, Ω distribution,
                     IRC-vs-displaced-opt agreement, and the TRUE per-success TS cost.
                     🔴 Without this, every S3 number in 03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md has an unmeasured
                     denominator (§39.4(f)).
                     ⚠ MUST be preceded by §39.4(d) STEP 0/0b/0c at zero cost.
```
```
TOTAL B1 ≈ 630 runs + 6 TS attempts.
COST PROFILE (no absolute number until B1-D exists, and that is the point):
   Σ_species [ u_cheap(species) ] × r_composite(1.14–1.30)  +  6 × (TS attempt)
   u_cheap is 3–5 core-h for small species and UNBOUNDED for the class B1-D probes.
   🔴 I refuse to publish a total that averages over a distribution whose tail is the thing we are
   measuring. Ceiling requested from engineer5; B1 will be recut to fit it.
   Priority under a cut:  B1-D > B1-A > B1-F > B1-E > B1-C > B1-B.
   (B1-D first because it is the only one whose result can invalidate the others' cost model.
    B1-B last because LIBE calibration is useful but it is the only item with a substitute:
    experimental ΔG_f° anchors, §26.4.)
```

### (c) X1 / X2 overlap — the explicit statement the question asked for

```
X1 (level / benchmark calibration)      → B1-B (subject sample) + B1-C (its null control L_A′)
X2 (xTB↔DFT topology mismatch)          → B1-A supplies the DFT REFERENCE half.
                                          The xTB half is separately near-free and runs on the
                                          FULL pool, not just the sample.
🔴 X2's standing rule (§21.4-B1) applies from day one: every species discovered OUTSIDE the pool by
   S2-B/S2-C is added to the X2 comparison set. Otherwise X2 measures agreement only where the
   grammar already looked, which is where the two engines are least likely to disagree.
🔴 X2 is a species-level diagnostic with ZERO reactions in it. That is deliberate (§21.5) and it is
   what makes it an unbiased anchor. Do not let it acquire reactions to "make it more useful".
```
**⟹ B1 is 630 runs delivering: pool thermochemistry (its nominal purpose), X1, X2's DFT half,
σ_protocol, ADR-032(c)+(d), the coordination-cost probe, and the TS method success rate.** Nothing
in it is a study run for its own sake; the diagnostics are carried by species we need anyway.

### (d) Generation depth and the discovery ledger — the two constraints that must be in place *before* B1

🔒 **ADR-051's ledger constraints are pre-conditions, not follow-ups**, and ADR-051 flags that the
ledger does not yet exist, so whoever creates it is the person who can lose this irrecoverably:
`seed_id` and `generation_depth` as **two separate columns**, `seed_id` sharing its definition with
`sei_pilot/seeding.py::provenance`. Without them D1 (seed-split capture–recapture) is impossible
after the fact, and D1 is what replaced axis 3.

**Generation depth for the first pass**: I do **not** set a depth number. ADR-015 §1 is explicit
that an extensional boundary ("N generations") is answer-dependent and therefore does not transfer;
the boundary is the *discovery-rate* convergence (per-stratum `Ĉ_M ≥ 0.95`, Chao1 increment < 5 %).
**B1 does not need a depth at all** — it is thermochemistry on an already-enumerated pool. Depth
becomes live at the first reaction-generation round, and it should be set by the rarefaction curve
B1's ledger starts, not by me now. 🔒 **This is ADR-025's "stop refining before measurement"
principle and I am obeying it deliberately.**

## 39.6 🔴 Question 6 — U-15. The principle for the principal set of an unstudied electrolyte.

### (a) The reason U-15 has stayed open is that it is two questions wearing one name

§16.2(b) already found the distinction and did not generalise it: *"pool membership ≠ initial
condition."* HF was in the pool without H2O, and was still unreachable in practice, because a node
with no flux into it is not a species — it is a drawing.

```
G — the GENERATOR set.      Determines what the grammar can REACH. A reachability boundary.
I — the INITIAL-CONDITION set. Determines what carries concentration at t = 0. A flux boundary.
```
**These have different failure modes and different correct principles, and every prior discussion
of U-15 — including ADR-016's — has treated them as one list.** That conflation is why it looks
unresolvable: the answer for I is easy and the answer for G is the hard one.

### (b) I — the easy half, stated for completeness
```
· every formulation component gets its formulation concentration. Requires no chemistry knowledge:
  it is what the person specifying the electrolyte already wrote down.
· contaminants get a DECLARED TRACE with a MANDATORY SCAN, never a point value (§39.5(a)).
  🔴 Rule: any species whose stoichiometric coefficient cancels over a closed cycle (i.e. any
  catalyst) MUST be scanned, because its concentration sets a rate and not a yield, and a rate
  parameter presented as a fixed input is an undeclared assumption.
· the electrode is a boundary condition (e⁻ flux at a potential), not a species with a
  concentration (ADR-002 keeps the surface implicit).
· everything else starts at zero.
```

### (c) 🔴 G — the hard half. Proposed principle: **the generator set is not chosen, it is grown to a measurable fixed point.**

The trap in "how do we pick the principal list for a system nobody has studied" is that every
answer of the form *"include the species you expect to matter"* is a known-answer dependency and
therefore forbidden by ADR-014. The escape is to make the list an **output of a terminating
procedure** rather than an input.

```
G₀  = formulation as declared  ∪  {H2O}  ∪  {e⁻ / Li⁺ reservoir}
      — zero chemical judgement; anyone specifying an electrolyte supplies exactly this.

F(G) = the FRAGMENT set generated by the grammar from G
      (bond cuts ≤2 and their connected components; §10.1)

ITERATE:  run one generation of the grammar from G_k.
          Promote a discovered species s into G_{k+1} iff s is a genuine minimum AND
          F(G_k ∪ {s}) ⊋ F(G_k)  — i.e. s contributes a BONDING MOTIF not derivable from G_k.
STOP when  F(G_{n+1}) = F(G_n).
```
🔴 **Why this terminates, which is the part that makes it a principle and not a wish:** the fixed
point is taken over **fragments**, not species. Species proliferate without bound under
recombination; fragments do not — they are bounded by the element set and by the cut depth (≤2
bonds). So `F` is a finite lattice and the iteration is monotone increasing in a finite set. **It
must terminate, and the number of iterations is itself a reportable statistic** — it says how many
layers of chemistry deep the formulation's own fragments failed to reach.

**Why this is the right *kind* of answer for this project:**
- it is composition-agnostic — it names no element and no functional group, so it transfers, which
  is the requirement the grammar was already designed to meet (ADR-015 §1);
- it makes the principal set **auditable**: for an unstudied electrolyte we can report *"G grew from
  6 to 9 entries in 2 iterations, and here are the three promoted motifs"*, which is a
  method-relative completeness statement of exactly the form ADR-050 asked for;
- it is nearly free — it is enumeration, plus a stability check per promoted candidate.

### (d) 🔴 The falsifier — and it is available now, at essentially zero cost

> **Retro-test on our own system.** Start from `G₀ = {EC, EMC, Li⁺, PF6⁻, H2O, e⁻}` — deliberately
> *excluding* `LiPOF4`, which a human put in the list after reading Spotte-Smith et al.,
> *ACS Energy Lett.* **8**, 347 (2023) (§25.5) — and run the fixed-point iteration.
>
> **Does the procedure promote `LiPOF4` (or the POF-motif that generates it) on its own?**
>
> · **Yes** ⟹ the principle recovers, without literature, an entry we could only get from
>   literature. U-15 closes with evidence.
> · **No** ⟹ the principle is insufficient, **and we know it before we ship it**, and we know
>   exactly which motif class it is blind to.

This is E1 (blind rediscovery, §14.5) applied to the *principal list itself* rather than to the
products — the same instrument, one level up. 🔒 **And per ADR-015's independence rule, the target
list for this test must be built by critic, not by me: if the method designer writes the answer key,
the key contains only what the method can find.**

### (e) What the principle does NOT solve — stated so it is not quietly assumed away

1. 🔴 **The element set is still declared.** If an unstudied electrolyte contains an element whose
   chemistry we have no parameters or no validated functional behaviour for, the grammar will
   happily enumerate it and every barrier will be wrong. **The fixed point measures closure, not
   correctness.**
2. 🔴 **The fixed point is over the grammar's fragments, so a motif the grammar cannot cut to is
   invisible to the test as well as to the search.** This is ADR-015 §2's honest limitation
   (`Ĉ` measures the sampler's own distribution) reappearing at the level of the generator set,
   and it cannot be removed from inside. It is the same structural zero.
3. **Solids.** Phase-tagged solids (ADR-027 D-2) enter G by a different route — they are *products*
   that must be fed back as *reactants*. The fixed-point iteration handles this naturally if
   precipitation is written as the reversible pair ADR-021 specifies, but only if the ledger's
   generation loop is allowed to see condensed-phase nodes. **Coder constraint: the promotion step
   must not filter on phase.**
4. **A leave-one-principal-out sensitivity is still required and is cheap**: drop each entry of the
   final G in turn, regenerate, and measure the fraction of working-network flux that disappears.
   That does not tell us what we *missed* — nothing can — but it measures **what one missing
   principal costs**, converting an unbounded unknown into a bounded risk. 🔴 For the primary
   system, `H2O` should top that ranking; if it does not, the catalytic cycle of §16.2(c) is not
   being represented and something upstream is broken.

**⟹ Proposed disposition: U-15 moves from `[UNRESOLVED]` to `[RESOLVED IN PRINCIPLE, PENDING THE
§39.6(d) RETRO-TEST]`.** I am not claiming it closed. I am claiming it now has a procedure with a
termination proof and a falsifier that costs nothing, and that is the first time it has had either.

---

## 39.7 What to do with eased compute — the three candidates, since this is the real question behind Q1

---

### Candidate 1: more demo systems (1 → 2, possibly 3)
- **Physical assumption**: transferability is demonstrated by demonstration, not by statistics
  (ADR-017's own argument). **Breaks when** two systems are too similar to constitute a
  leave-one-chemistry-out — which is why the *choice* of system is the whole content (§29.4).
- **Expected accuracy**: not an accuracy item. It is the only item that produces evidence for
  ADR-014's final requirement rather than better numbers for a requirement we already meet.
- **Known silent-failure mode**: 🔴 **looking at demo 2 during development destroys E3 and leaves
  no trace.** The freeze date must be an ADR, not an intention.
- **Verification**: E3 against Bernhard–Metzger–Gasteiger (2015) gas quantification, pre-registered.
- **Cost**: one incremental pipeline pass. Consumes ADR-017's schedule buffer (§39.2(b) R-1).

### Candidate 2: more of the same system — bigger pool, deeper generation, more X2 sample
- **Physical assumption**: `Ĉ_M` is below target because sampling is incomplete. **Breaks when** the
  shortfall is structural rather than statistical — in which case more sampling raises `Ĉ_M`
  without finding anything, which is ADR-015 §2's warning exactly.
- **Expected accuracy**: improves the completeness *estimate's* precision; improves coverage only
  within the reach of `M`.
- **Known silent-failure mode**: 🔴 `Ĉ_M` rises and the missing chemistry stays missing, and the
  number looks like progress. **D2 (§ADR-051 ⑤) is the only detector and it must be printed in the
  same paragraph as `Ĉ_M`.**
- **Verification**: E1 rediscovery rate reported alongside, never separately.
- **Cost**: linear in pool size; **this is what ADR-051 ⑦ says is the *correct* response to a low
  `Ĉ_M`, so it is the default use of eased κ and needs no special justification.**

### Candidate 3: 🔴 an unreviewed cheap-TS tier whose only consumer is the barrier surrogate
- **Physical assumption**: a TS located at the cheap level, screened *automatically* by the repaired
  instrument (Ω from M2′ + displaced-mode connectivity), yields a barrier good enough to serve as a
  **training anchor** for the ADR-018 hierarchical model, even though it is not good enough to
  report. Formally: it is a low-fidelity level in the multi-fidelity Δ-learning ADR-018 §4 already
  adopted. **Breaks when** the cheap-level error is not a smooth function of family — i.e. when
  Δ-learning's core assumption fails — and when the automatic screen's false-positive rate is high
  enough that the training set contains saddles of the wrong coordinate.
- **Expected accuracy**: individually poor, `[UNKNOWN]` until measured; **collectively, the relevant
  metric is not per-TS error but ADR-018's `precision@k` after training.** This is the ADR-018
  judgement principle applied to its own training data.
- **Known silent-failure mode**: 🔴 **P1's exact failure, industrialised.** If the automatic screen
  is the ADR-035 magnitude window, we would generate thousands of conformational saddles labelled as
  reaction barriers, and the surrogate would learn them. **This candidate is only admissible on top
  of §39.4(c)'s M2′ and §39.4(a)'s IRC precondition. Without those it is actively dangerous and I
  would oppose it.**
- **Verification — and this is the part that makes it defensible**: the ~300–500 human-reviewed S3
  TS become the **calibration set**. The automatic screen's false-positive and false-negative rates
  are measured against them; the cheap-vs-composite barrier residual is measured on the overlap;
  and the falsifier is ADR-018's `precision@k` computed with and without the cheap tier. **If adding
  10× more cheap anchors does not improve precision@k, the tier is worthless and we stop — that
  test costs one retraining.**
- **Required input**: the repaired S3 instrument; the edge break/form lists (already produced);
  no human time.
- **Cost profile**: `N_TS × (cheap opt=ts + Hessian + 2 displaced opts)`. 🔴 **zero human hours** —
  which is the entire point, because human hours are the binding constraint and core-h are not.

---

**🔴 My preference: 1 > 3 > 2.**
Candidate 1 because it produces evidence for the project's *stated final requirement* and nothing
else in the list does. Candidate 3 second because it is the only proposal that converts the currency
κ actually released (machine time) into progress on the bottleneck ADR-015 §5 identified (the
surrogate), without touching the currency we do not have (human review) — but **strictly gated on
the §39.4 repairs, and I want that gating in the ADR, not in a paragraph.** Candidate 2 last, not
because it is wrong — ADR-051 ⑦ makes it the default and it needs no defence — but because it is
the one that will happen anyway and does not need a decision.

## 39.8 🔴 The error budget — where the largest error actually is

I am required to name the dominant error source, and after this round I can, with a caveat.

```
FUNCTIONAL              ~0.10 eV   ⟵ 🔴 DOMINANT
BASIS (composite vs full-high)  0.008 eV measured (n = 1, hco3), 0.03–0.08 eV expected for
                                   association/dissociation  [predicted, §29.1; UNMEASURED]
PROTOCOL (σ_protocol)   UNMEASURED — P5 empty. This is the floor and we do not know it.
SOLVATION (SMD, mixed solvent by volume-weighted descriptors)  UNMEASURED, plausibly ≳0.1 eV
                                   for charged species, and P1 ran in acetonitrile by mistake
SOLVATION SHELL choice  UNMEASURED, plausibly the largest of all for S1 (§39.3)
```
Basis for the functional number: benchmark studies of range-separated hybrids on reaction energies
and barrier heights place ωB97X-V at MAD ≈ 2.2 kcal mol⁻¹ on MOR41, with double hybrids around
1.85 kcal mol⁻¹ *(Santra/Goerigk-type benchmark literature; **read at abstract/summary level via
search this round, full text not consulted — `[ABSTRACT-LEVEL]`**)*. 2.2 kcal mol⁻¹ = **0.096 eV**.

🔴 **Read that against our own stated sensitivity: 0.1 eV at 298 K is a factor of ~50 in rate.**

```
⟹ Our chosen functional's benchmark error is, to within rounding, EXACTLY our sensitivity unit.
⟹ Every barrier we produce is a rate uncertain by ~50× before any other error is added.
⟹ Therefore: refining the BASIS below that (composite vs full-high, def2-TZVPD vs def2-TZVPPD)
   is chasing a term an order of magnitude smaller than the dominant one.
   🟢 This CONFIRMS the composite decision from a direction ADR-032/034 never used.
⟹ And it means NO ABSOLUTE BARRIER we produce should be quoted as predictive on its own.
   What survives is RELATIVE ordering within a family (where the functional error is largely
   systematic and cancels) — which is precisely what ADR-018's surrogate and P-1…P-5 selection
   consume. 🔒 The architecture is already built for this. What is missing is that we have never
   said it out loud in a place a reader of the final report will see.
```
⚠ **Caveat I am obliged to state**: MOR41 is metal–organic reactions, not Li⁺-carbonate radical
anions in a low-ε solvent. **The transfer of that MAD to our chemistry is an assumption, not a
measurement.** The only way to replace it with a measurement is an external anchor that is not
another hybrid functional — hence B1-E and the double-hybrid tier I asked engineer5 to price
(item #3), with experimental ΔG_f° anchors (§26.4) as the fallback if double hybrids are out of
scale in G16 without RI.

🔴 **And the honest bottom line on "does this flip our conclusions":** for *ranking within a
family*, no. For *absolute rates in S4*, yes — a 0.1 eV systematic on a rate-determining step moves
the SEI growth time scale by ~50×. **⟹ S4 must be run as an ensemble over the barrier uncertainty
from the start, not as a point calculation with error bars added afterwards.** That is ADR-018's
principle applied to S4, and I do not believe it is yet written into S4's design.

## 39.9 What I changed my mind about

1. 🔴 **AIMD.** I helped write "development AIMD = 0" and I argued in §11/§30 that λ decomposition
   makes it unnecessary. **I still believe that about λ.** What I did not see then is that the
   *solvation-shell distribution* — an input to everything in S1 — was being supplied by literature
   coordination numbers, which is exactly the known-answer dependency ADR-014 outlawed, and which
   *by construction* does not exist for the unstudied systems the project is for. I was consistent
   about λ and inconsistent about the ensemble λ is evaluated over. **§39.3, and it goes to the user.**
2. 🔴 **The imaginary-frequency window.** In §27.4 I wrote the coder constraint that M2's *magnitude*
   threshold must be recalibrated for the cheap basis. ADR-035 then spent a round on whether the
   number was right. **The number was never the instrument.** Magnitude is a proxy for curvature;
   the question is direction. I asked for a recalibration when I should have asked for a different
   measurement. §39.4(c).
3. 🟡 **I over-trusted a summary of a measurement.** I was given `r_composite ≈ 1.04–1.14` and my
   first instinct was to reason from it. The correction in §39.1 exists only because I opened the
   raw JSON. 🔒 This is ADR-034 §6's rule (*"`[MEASURED]` means 'it was measured', not 'we know what
   was measured'"*) and it now has a fifth instance — this time caught before it was built on,
   which is the first time.
4. 🟢 **I now think κ's real purchase is machine-only work, not more of anything human-touched.**
   The lead's framing (κ buys compute, not transition states) is right and I had not drawn its
   corollary: the surrogate is the one large consumer with no human in the loop. §39.7 candidate 3.
5. 🔴 **Three times in one round, within hours of writing them.** (i) I read the IRC endpoint bond
   count backwards (§39.4(a) correction). (ii) I named "QST2 was asked for a TS between a structure
   and its own conformer" as the likely cause; the zero-cost test refuted it (§39.4(g)). (iii) I
   called the Li⁺ floppy-manifold reading *"the most consequential thing in the pilot"* and sent it
   to engineer5 as grounds to revise their S2 line; the same check withdrew it (§39.1(e-bis)).
   🔒 **All three are the same error on my part: I reasoned about the chemistry before checking the
   input.** And in all three cases the disqualifying fact was written in the artefact — a header
   line, a `converged` field, a bond count — and unread.
   > 🔴 **Rule I would like promoted to an ADR: before attributing a computational failure to the
   > chemistry, check the input. The chemistry hypothesis is the expensive one, and it was the
   > second thing to check every time.**
6. 🟢 **And the round has ONE defect, not three.** P1's "chemical failure", `r_composite ≈ 1.04`,
   and the floppy-manifold reading all trace to idealised, unoptimised, over-symmetric input
   geometries. **That is a much better outcome than three problems: it is one fix.**

## 39.14 🔴 MLIP for the Li⁺ solvation shell — judgement on the user's fine-tuned model

> **New fact (user, via lead)**: *"I have a fine-tuned MLIP that can run MD for the Li⁺ solvation
> shell. The solvation shell can be extracted from it."*
> This section answers the lead's five questions (a)–(e), plus the priority question.
> 🔒 **Judgement only. Nothing here authorises a run.**
> ⚠ Per user instruction, technical terms stay in English: `solvation shell`, `coordination number`,
> `MLIP`, `RDF`, `CIP`/`SSIP`.

### (a) 🔴 The instrument does not merely substitute — it changes class

My §39.3 candidate 2 was **deliberately a weak falsifier**, and I said so at the time:
> *"first-shell residence times exceed the trajectory length — Li⁺–carbonate exchange is on the
> order of hundreds of ps to ns, so 10 ps samples fluctuations ABOUT an initial shell, not the
> equilibrium BETWEEN shells. I state this as the dominant weakness of this candidate. Mitigation:
> use it as a consistency test on candidate 1's minima rather than as an ergodic sampler. That is a
> much weaker claim and it is the claim I am willing to defend."*

```
DFT MD    high per-frame accuracy, CATASTROPHICALLY UNDERSAMPLED (10 ps ≪ ns exchange time)
          ⟹ can only test "does the dominant cluster survive 10 ps" — a weak claim
MLIP MD   lower per-frame accuracy, PROPERLY SAMPLED (10³–10⁶× cheaper ⟹ ns–µs reachable)
          ⟹ can test the actual equilibrium DISTRIBUTION — a strong claim
```
🔴 **For a distribution question, sampling dominates.** A converged distribution from a slightly
wrong PES beats an unconverged distribution from an exact one — **provided you can bound how wrong
the PES is**, which is exactly what §39.14(e) is for.

⟹ **This is not a cheaper way to do what I asked for. It is a better instrument for the question,
and it removes the weakness I had already flagged as dominant.** I would take it over the DFT MD on
scientific grounds even if the DFT MD were free.

### (b) Question (a) — falsifier or only population-generator? **Falsifier, and here is the reason.**

The requirement on a falsifier is not accuracy. It is that **its failure mode be structurally
independent of the failure mode it is testing** — the same principle as ADR-015/ADR-020's
capture–recapture, applied to a different problem.

**Enumerate the continuum's failure modes precisely, then check each:**

| # | how the static cluster–continuum route fails | does an explicit-solvent MLIP MD share it? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | second and outer shells replaced by a structureless dielectric ⟹ **differential packing entropy across competing stoichiometries is smeared out** | 🟢 **No.** Explicit atoms, explicit outer shells, real packing. |
| 2 | enumerates **discrete minima**; if the liquid is a continuous manifold, the discretisation *is* the error | 🟢 **No.** Samples a continuous trajectory; never enumerates minima. |
| 3 | the standard-state / concentration correction `n·RT·ln(c°/c_solvent)` is a **modelling choice** worth ~0.05–0.1 eV per ligand | 🟢 **No.** Populations come from **counting configurations**, not from a thermodynamic cycle. There is no such term. |
| 4 | no dynamics ⟹ no residence times, no exchange | 🟢 **No.** That is what it does. |

⟹ **On all four, the MLIP is structurally independent.** And the reason is not incidental:

> 🔒 **The continuum's error is a MODEL-FORM error — the physics is deliberately replaced.
> The MLIP's error is an INTERPOLATION error — the physics is fitted.**
> These are different *kinds* of error, and they can only become correlated by one route:
> **if the MLIP was fitted to data generated under the continuum's own approximations.**

⟹ **That single sentence is why (b) provenance is decisive, and the lead is right to make it the
gate.** Everything in this section is conditional on it.

### (c) Question (b) — 🔴 exactly what to ask the user. Eight items; **#1, #2 and #8 are the decisive ones.**

```
🔴 1. WHAT WERE THE REFERENCE LABELS COMPUTED ON?
      (i)  periodic condensed-phase configurations (bulk liquid box)          ⟹ INDEPENDENT 🟢
      (ii) isolated clusters in implicit solvent                              ⟹ INHERITS failure
                                                                                 modes 1 and 2.
                                                                                 Independence is
                                                                                 ILLUSORY. 🔴
      (iii) isolated clusters in vacuum                                       ⟹ partially inherits
      **This one question decides whether the whole proposal stands.**

🔴 2. HOW WERE THE TRAINING CONFIGURATIONS GENERATED?
      (i) classical MD snapshots / (ii) AIMD / (iii) active learning with uncertainty sampling
          ⟹ independent 🟢
      (iv) normal-mode or random displacement AROUND CLUSTER MINIMA
          ⟹ 🔴 the sampling is CENTRED ON THE SAME MINIMA the continuum enumerates.
             Correlated blindness. This is the subtle failure and it will not be visible in
             any RMSE the model reports.

   3. Reference level of theory — functional, basis / plane-wave cutoff, dispersion treatment.
      And: was Li⁺ present in the training data AT REALISTIC CONCENTRATION? A model fine-tuned
      mostly on neat solvent with occasional Li⁺ has thin statistics exactly where we need them.

   4. Base model + what was fine-tuned (e.g. MACE-MP-0 → fine-tuned).
      🔴 ADR-051 recorded that MACE-MP-0-class foundation models have NO CHARGE CHANNEL and
         cannot distinguish EC from EC⁻. See §39.14(d) — this is fine for the pre-reduction
         electrolyte and fatal for the reduced species. The boundary must be drawn explicitly.

   5. Composition coverage — which solvents, which salt anion, what concentration range?
      Bears directly on (e) transferability and on whether PF6⁻ is described at all.

   6. Reported validation — force/energy RMSE, and MUCH more importantly any STRUCTURAL
      validation (RDF, coordination number) against a reference. RMSE on a held-out set drawn
      from the same distribution is not evidence about structure.

   7. Does it carry an uncertainty estimate (ensemble / committee)? If yes we can FLAG
      out-of-distribution frames instead of assuming there are none.

🔴 8. ELECTROSTATICS: short-range only (local cutoff, typically 5–6 Å), or explicit long-range
      Coulomb / charge equilibration?
      **Why this is decisive and not a detail:** Li⁺ solvation is dominated by long-range
      electrostatics, and the CIP ⇌ SSIP equilibrium involves Li⁺···PF6⁻ separations of ~2–7 Å,
      which STRADDLES a typical MLIP cutoff. A purely short-range model can reproduce first-shell
      Li–O structure and still get the contact-ion-pair fraction wrong.
      🔴 And the CIP fraction is not a side quantity for us — it determines whether Li⁺ remains
         attached to the reduced species, which is the S1 question itself.
```

### (d) Question (c) — which MLIP blind spots actually bite? **The lead is right on two of three, and wrong on the one that matters.**

| blind spot | bites equilibrium solvation structure? |
|---|---|
| out-of-distribution near transition states | 🟢 **No.** We cross no barriers. Lead's reading correct. |
| high-T bias distorting branching | 🟢 **No, at 298–330 K.** ⚠ **But there is a trap**: ligand exchange is slow (hundreds of ps–ns), so there is a standing temptation to run hot to accelerate it — **which reintroduces the bias precisely to fix the problem the MLIP was supposed to solve.** ⟹ **run at the physical temperature and pay in trajectory length. If a hot arm is run, it is a separate, separately-reported arm — never merged.** |
| 🔴 **no charge-transfer physics / no charge channel** | 🔴 **The lead's reading is right for half the question and wrong for the other half.** For the **pre-reduction** electrolyte every species has a fixed, well-defined charge (Li⁺, PF6⁻, neutral EC/EMC) ⟹ **does not bite.** But my §39.3 purpose statement includes *"and whether the reduced species stays in the contact ion pair"* — and a model with no charge channel **cannot distinguish EC from EC⁻**. ⟹ **the MLIP can supply the shell distribution of the electrolyte BEFORE reduction; it cannot supply the shell of the reduced species unless it was explicitly trained with reduced/charged species.** |

🔴 **⟹ The scope must be cut accordingly, and this is a real reduction in what the MLIP buys:**
```
✅ IN SCOPE   the Li⁺(EC)ₙ(EMC)ₘ(PF6⁻)_k distribution of the UNREDUCED electrolyte
              — which is what conditions the S1 initial state, and is the larger half
🔴 OUT OF SCOPE  the shell of EC⁻ / the post-reduction CIP question
              — unless provenance item #4 says reduced species were in training
              ⟹ this half stays with the static route, or stays UNKNOWN and declared
```
🟢 **One blind spot the MLIP REMOVES, and it is the one I named as dominant**: non-ergodicity of
shell exchange. See §39.14(a).

### (e) Question (d) — 🔴 the validation ladder. *"We have an MLIP"* is not evidence, and the lead is right to say so.

**V-1 — external structural anchors. 🔴 And the literature is messier than I expected; see §39.14(g).**
```
✅ USE (well determined):  Li–O first-peak distance   ·  ∠Li···O–C angle  ·  Li–P/Li–F CN (CIP fraction)
🔴 DO NOT "VALIDATE" AGAINST:  the EC coordination number.
   The experimental literature does NOT AGREE on it (§39.14(g)). Validating against a contested
   quantity is not validation; it is choosing which paper to agree with.
   ⟹ report our value ALONGSIDE the experimental spread, do not tune to any point in it.
```

**V-2 — DFT single points on MLIP-sampled configurations. 🔴 Two separable questions; do not merge them.**
```
V-2a  IS THE MLIP FAITHFUL TO ITS OWN REFERENCE LEVEL?
      N frames from the trajectory, STRATIFIED (modal shell + rare shells + high-uncertainty
      frames), recomputed AT THE MLIP'S REFERENCE LEVEL.
      🔴 The read-out is NOT force RMSE. It is the RELATIVE energy of competing shell
         stoichiometries — because populations depend on relative free energies, not on absolute
         accuracy. Threshold: relative energies tracking to ~0.05 eV across shell types.
      ⚠ periodic frames ⟹ VASP, not G16. That is fine (allowed engine, already in use) and it
        introduces no seam, because we are testing the MLIP against ITS OWN reference.

V-2b  IS THAT REFERENCE LEVEL ADEQUATE FOR Li⁺ COORDINATION ENERGETICS?
      Compare the MLIP's reference functional against OUR production level on a handful of
      Li⁺(L)ₙ clusters.
      🟢 NEARLY FREE — B0-D already computes exactly those clusters at our production level
        (§39.13(b)). One extra column, not one extra experiment.
```

**V-3 — 🔴 the actual falsification test, and it must be PRE-REGISTERED, because disagreement is the informative outcome and will otherwise be rationalised.**
```
Compare the MLIP-derived shell population distribution against candidate 1's continuum-derived one.
🔒 AGREEMENT IS NOT THE GOAL. If they agree we gain confidence; if they DISAGREE we have learned
   the continuum is wrong, which was the entire purpose. Write the rule down first:

  |Δ population| over the dominant shell stoichiometries
    < 10 percentage points  ⟹ continuum weights ADOPTED; MLIP corroborates
    10 – 30 pp              ⟹ adopt MLIP weights for system 1 AND carry the spread as an
                               uncertainty axis into §39.3 candidate 3's ensemble
    > 30 pp                 ⟹ 🔴 the continuum route is REJECTED as a source of shell weights.
                               For unstudied systems the shell is then reported as an uncertainty
                               axis WITH NO WEIGHTS (candidate 3, unweighted).
🔒 That last branch is the one that costs us something, which is exactly why it is written now.
```

**V-4 — MLIP committee/ensemble uncertainty on the sampled frames.** Report the fraction of frames
flagged out-of-distribution. Not a validation on its own; it is the only cheap detector of
extrapolation, and it is what selects V-2a's "high-uncertainty" stratum.

### (f) Question (e) — transferability. 🔴 **Admissible, in exactly the scope I already specified — and it needs a hard quarantine constraint.**

The danger the lead names is real and is the same failure as literature CN, by a different
mechanism: **if the MLIP becomes the production source of shell weights, the pipeline acquires a
dependency it cannot carry to an unstudied electrolyte**, violating ADR-014 exactly as literature CN
did. And we cannot promise to produce a fine-tuned MLIP for an arbitrary new system — engineer's
earlier analysis (per-chemistry active learning ≈ 6 weeks) is what removed MLIP from the production
path in the first place. **A model the user happens to have is a gift, not a capability.**

🟢 **But that is not what I proposed, and the architecture already handles it:**
```
production route  candidate 3 — enumerate shells as a DECLARED UNCERTAINTY AXIS.
                  Transfers with no new input. Unchanged.
weights           candidate 1 — static cluster–continuum. Nearly free, already in the pool.
falsifier         ONE-TIME, PRIMARY-SYSTEM-ONLY test of whether candidate 1 can be trusted.
🔒 WHAT TRANSFERS IS THE METHOD-VALIDITY STATEMENT, NOT THE INSTRUMENT.
   "the cluster–continuum coordination equilibrium does / does not reproduce condensed-phase
    populations" is a conclusion about a METHOD, and it is portable even though the MLIP is not.
```

🔴 **CONSTRAINT — the MLIP is quarantined from the production path. This must be in an ADR, not
only here:**
```
The MLIP output MAY:   (i) validate or reject candidate 1
                       (ii) set the UNCERTAINTY BAND on shell weights
The MLIP output MAY NOT: supply the weights used in production FOR ANY SYSTEM, INCLUDING SYSTEM 1.
```
**Why "including system 1", which looks over-strict:** if system 1 uses MLIP weights and system 2
(LiTFSI, no MLIP) uses continuum weights, then **any difference in E3 performance is confounded
between the chemistry and the method.** E3 is the strongest deliverable this project can produce
(§39.13(c)) and it is a single shot. **Do not spend it on a comparison with a method change baked
into it.** ⟹ same method on both systems, in both branches of V-3: if V-3 passes we use continuum
weights on both; if V-3 fails at >30 pp we use unweighted candidate 3 on both. **The architecture
holds either way, which is how I know the constraint is not arbitrary.**

### (g) 🔴 External evidence I found this round — and it cuts harder than I expected, in our favour

⚠ **Provenance labelling, strictly**: item 1 was verified at the **arXiv abstract**; items 2–4 come
from **search-result summaries whose full texts I did not consult**. Labelled accordingly and **not
to be quoted as measured until the papers are read.**

**1. `[ABSTRACT-LEVEL — arXiv abstract read directly]` Skarmoutsos, Ponnuchamy, Vetere & Mossa,
"Li⁺ solvation in pure, binary and ternary mixtures of organic carbonate electrolytes",
arXiv:1411.7171 (2014, rev. 2015). Classical MD + DFT — COMPUTATIONAL, NOT EXPERIMENTAL.**
Preferred coordination = **4 solvent molecules**. And the finding that matters:
> 🔴 **Li⁺ preferentially coordinates the LESS polar carbonate (DMC) over the more polar ones in
> binary and ternary mixtures, attributed to tetrahedral packing effects causing dipole
> cancellation.**

🔴🔴 **This is a published, independent instance of precisely the failure mode I named for
candidate 1** — *"differential packing entropy across competing stoichiometries, i.e. exactly the
term the continuum smears out"*. A static cluster–continuum calculation sees electrostatics plus a
dielectric, and on that basis would rank the **more polar** solvent first. The condensed-phase
result is the **opposite**, and the stated cause is a many-body packing effect a continuum cannot
represent.
> ⟹ **The risk is not that the continuum gets the populations slightly wrong. It is that it gets
> the shell composition RANKING BACKWARDS.** That is a far sharper statement than the one I made in
> §39.3, and it substantially raises the value of any explicit-solvent instrument.
⚠ **Honest caveat**: that paper's own result is classical-force-field-dependent. But **the
mechanism** — packing / dipole cancellation — is a real condensed-phase effect that no continuum
model can represent regardless of whose force field found it.

**2. `[SEARCH-SUMMARY-LEVEL]` PC neutron diffraction (time-of-flight):**
`Li⁺···O(PC) = 2.04(1) Å · CN = 4.5(1) · ∠Li⁺···O–C = 138(2)°`
🔴 **Compare `li_ec2_cation.xyz` (§39.1(e-bis)): Li–O = 2.100 Å and ∠Li–O=C = 90.3°.**
The distance is close; **the angle is off by ~48° against a well-determined structural parameter.**
⟹ **my §39.1(e-bis) correction now has an external anchor rather than only my chemical judgement.**
The idealised input is not merely "unoptimised" — it is **wrong against measurement**, in the one
coordinate that defines how Li⁺ meets a carbonyl.

**3. `[SEARCH-SUMMARY-LEVEL]` LiPF6/DMC first shell = 2.8 DMC + 1.1 PF6⁻ ⟹ contact ion pairs form.**
⟹ **CIP is real and measurable in this chemistry.** V-1 must therefore include a **Li–P or Li–F
coordination number**, not only Li–O — and this is the observable most at risk from provenance
item #8 (short-range cutoff).

**4. 🔴 `[SEARCH-SUMMARY-LEVEL]` The experimental literature does NOT converge on the EC
coordination number.** NMR has been read as up to **6**; Raman points much **lower**; at least one
report gives **2** above 0.5 M.
> 🔴 **This is stronger than the argument I made in §39.3.** I argued *"literature CN does not exist
> for an unstudied electrolyte"*. The true and stronger statement is:
> **literature CN does not converge even for the studied one.**
> ⟹ the case for *computing* the shell distribution rather than looking it up **does not depend on
> the transferability requirement at all.** It holds for system 1, today.
> ⟹ and it caps what V-1 can do: **CN cannot be a validation target.** Distance, angle and CIP
> fraction can.
