## 39.15 🔴 MLIP provenance ruling — SevenNet-0 / PBE. The level seam, and what the answer does *not* answer

> **Provenance received (user, via lead)**: base `SevenNet-0`, fine-tuned · training level `PBE` ·
> `BJ-D3` supported and switchable at MD time · user states it is *"verified to a trustworthy level"*.
> 🔒 **Judgement only. Nothing here authorises a run.** Terminology in English per user instruction.

### (a) 🔴 FIRST — what this provenance establishes, and what it leaves exactly where it was

`[SEARCH-LEVEL, verified this round]` **SevenNet-0** is a NequIP-architecture equivariant
message-passing GNN (MDIL-SNU), pretrained on **MPtrj — the Materials Project relaxation-trajectory
dataset, ~1.5 M structures / 146 k compounds, computed with VASP at PBE.**
🟢 **And it parallelises through LAMMPS** — which ADR-050 explicitly permits. **No new package, no
exception needed.** That is a genuine and unanticipated convenience.

🔴 **But now read what MPtrj is.** It is **inorganic crystalline solids and their relaxation
trajectories.** It contains essentially **no molecular liquids, no organic carbonates, no explicit
solvent, and no liquid-phase configurational sampling at all.**

```
⟹ The base model's provenance is maximally DISTANT from our problem.
⟹ Therefore essentially EVERYTHING that makes this model applicable to Li⁺ in a carbonate liquid
   came from the FINE-TUNING set.
⟹ And the fine-tuning set is exactly what we have not been told.
```

🔒 **My §39.14(c) items #1 and #2 are unanswered.** This is not a complaint about the user — the
question asked and the question answered are different, and it is my job to notice that rather than
let "SevenNet-0, PBE" be filed as though provenance were discharged.
```
ANSWERED    the BASE model's identity, architecture and pretraining level
UNANSWERED  🔴 #1  what the FINE-TUNING reference labels were computed on
                   — periodic condensed-phase boxes, or isolated clusters in implicit solvent?
            🔴 #2  how the FINE-TUNING configurations were generated
                   — MD / AIMD / active learning, or displacement around cluster minima?
            🔴 #8  now partially answered by architecture, and NOT in our favour ↓
```

**#8 is answered by the architecture, and the answer is the limiting one.** NequIP-class models are
**local message-passing with a finite cutoff**; the receptive field is (cutoff × n_layers), typically
~10–15 Å in total, with **no explicit long-range Coulomb and no charge channel.**
```
🟢 first-shell Li–O structure        well inside the receptive field  ⟹ expect it to be fine
🔴 CIP ⇌ SSIP balance                Li⁺···PF6⁻ separations ~2–7 Å, and the free-energy difference
                                     is set by screened long-range electrostatics
                                     ⟹ THE OBSERVABLE MOST AT RISK, and it is the one that decides
                                       whether Li⁺ stays on the reduced species
🔴 no charge channel                 confirms U-64: EC vs EC⁻ cannot be distinguished.
                                     The post-reduction shell is OUT OF SCOPE. Not negotiable.
```

### (b) 🔴🔴 THE LEVEL SEAM RULING — the lead's distinction is right in kind, and incomplete in a way that decides the whole question

The lead's reading: ADR-026's LIBE seam was fatal because we would mix **energies** from two levels
into one thermochemical network; here the MLIP supplies a **structural ensemble** and we compute
every energy ourselves; *"a seam in geometry is not the same object as a seam in thermochemistry."*

**I agree with the conclusion and I want to state the reason more precisely, because the precise
reason draws a line the loose reason does not:**

> 🔴 **ADR-026's seam was fatal because two levels appeared on OPPOSITE SIDES OF A SUBTRACTION.**
> A reaction ΔG is a *difference* of species free energies; if two species come from two levels, the
> difference inherits an uncontrolled offset that never cancels. **That is the whole of ADR-026.**
> **Here, nothing is subtracted.** No MLIP number is an addend in any energy expression.

**But the MLIP does not actually output "geometry". It outputs a POPULATION. And a population is a
free-energy difference wearing a disguise:**
```
P(shell A) / P(shell B) = exp( −ΔG_AB / kT )
⟹ taking the MLIP's WEIGHTS means importing ΔG_AB computed at PBE-D3.
⟹ that IS a thermochemical import, whatever we call it.
⟹ and at 298 K, telling a 10 pp population apart from a 50 pp one requires ΔG_AB to ~0.04 eV.
   PBE for Li⁺–carbonate ligand-exchange energetics is not obviously that good.
```

🔴 **⟹ The seam is structural or thermochemical depending on WHICH PART of the distribution we take.
That is the line, and it is the answer to the lead's question:**

```
USE 1 — THE SUPPORT.  "Which Li⁺(EC)ₘ(EMC)ₙ(PF6⁻)ₖ compositions OCCUR in the condensed phase,
                       and which never do."
   ⟹ a STRUCTURAL question. A composition either appears in the trajectory or it does not.
     Set by sterics, ionic radius and packing — NOT by exchange admixture. PBE will not invent
     or forbid a coordination number that a hybrid would forbid or invent.
   🟢 ADMISSIBLE FOR PRODUCTION. No thermochemical seam. Report with a threshold
     (e.g. population > 1 %) AND the raw counts, so the threshold is visible.
   ⚠ robust GIVEN ADEQUATE SAMPLING — a real but rare composition can be missed. That is a
     sampling question, and sampling is precisely this instrument's advantage.

USE 2 — THE WEIGHTS.  "...and with what probability."
   ⟹ exp(−ΔG/kT) at PBE-D3. A THERMOCHEMICAL IMPORT.
   🟡 ADMISSIBLE ONLY AS (i) a falsifier of candidate 1 and (ii) an uncertainty band.
     NEVER as the production weight — the §39.14(f) quarantine, which now has a SECOND and
     INDEPENDENT reason: not just the E3 confound, but the seam itself.

USE 3 — ENERGIES, BARRIERS, ANYTHING ENTERING THE NETWORK.
   🔴 FORBIDDEN. This is ADR-026's case exactly and it is not reopened.
```

🟢 **And the good news is that USE 1 — the seam-free one — is the higher-value use anyway.**
> §24.1, my own argument, and ADR-032 was adopted on it: **a hole is worse than noise.** A missing
> species removes every reaction through it and is a **structural zero that capture–recapture
> cannot detect.** The support tells us *which clusters to enumerate at our own level*. It converts
> a guess about the shell into an observation, and thereby converts potential holes into computed
> species. **The support is worth more than the weights, and it is the part with no seam.**

⚠ **Honest note against my own framing**: the motivating result I cited in §39.14(g)-1 — Li⁺
preferring the *less* polar carbonate through packing/dipole cancellation — is a **ranking** claim
and therefore lives in USE 2, not USE 1. So the headline example sits in the category I am
restricting. **That is consistent, not contradictory**: USE 2 *is* admissible as a falsifier, which
is precisely the role, and the restriction is only on production weights.

### (c) PBE specifically — I am **less** worried than the lead about one thing and **more** about another

The lead: *"PBE tends to over-delocalise and can misdescribe charge transfer, and Li⁺–carbonate
coordination is exactly where that would show."*

🟡 **I think this is over-stated for the neutral shell.** Li⁺–carbonate is a **hard closed-shell
cation binding an ion–dipole/polarisation contact**; charge transfer into Li 2s is small. GGA
self-interaction error does its real damage in **radicals, mixed-valence systems, charge-transfer
complexes and transition states** — a Li⁺···O=C dative contact is none of those. **For the
pre-reduction shell I expect PBE-D3 to be adequate for structure and marginal for relative
energetics**, which is exactly the USE 1 / USE 2 split above, arrived at independently.

🔴 **Where I am MORE worried than the lead, and it is the same place twice:**
```
The excess-electron / reduced species. GGA over-delocalises an excess electron across several
solvent molecules instead of localising it on one — a known, severe GGA failure for excess
electrons in molecular liquids, and EC⁻ is exactly that object.
🟢 CONVENIENTLY, this coincides with the architectural limit: SevenNet-0 has NO CHARGE CHANNEL,
   so it cannot represent EC⁻ anyway.
⟹ TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS for the same scope boundary (U-64). The exclusion is doubly safe,
   and I would hold it even if a charge channel appeared.
```
🔴 **The other PBE risk that IS live for us**: plain PBE badly underbinds molecular liquids —
densities off by order 10 %. **Packing is the mechanism the arXiv:1411.7171 result attributes the
shell composition to.** ⟹ dispersion is not optional here, which is (d).

### (d) 🔴 BJ-D3 — this is not a preference, and being *asked* as a preference is itself the finding

The lead asked whether I want D3 on. **The correct answer is not a preference: it is determined by
what the fine-tuning labels were.**
```
labels were PBE, NO D3       ⟹ the network learned to reproduce UNDISPERSED PBE. Switching D3 on
                               at MD time ADDS A TERM THE NETWORK WAS NEVER TRAINED AGAINST, on
                               top of a fit that may already have absorbed dispersion-like
                               behaviour from the data. 🔴 RISK OF DOUBLE-COUNTING.
labels were PBE-D3(BJ)       ⟹ D3 MUST be on at MD time; turning it off is the error.
```
🔴 **⟹ "SevenNet supports BJ-D3 and it can be switched on during MD" is a flag, not a
reassurance** — it says the setting is a runtime choice, when it is actually fixed by the labels.
**And that it can be asked as a preference tells us the labels have not been specified.**

⟹ **New provenance question, and it is short: were the fine-tuning reference labels PBE, or
PBE-D3(BJ)?** *(Ancillary, my inference to verify: MPtrj's standard Materials Project workflow is
plain PBE / PBE+U with no dispersion — so if the fine-tuning used D3 there is a pretrain/fine-tune
target mismatch, which fine-tuning should largely wash out but which is worth knowing.)*

🔒 **My position once the labels are known**: dispersion must be present in **exactly one place,
consistently** — and it must be present, because second-shell structure and intra-shell
ligand–ligand repulsion are dispersion-dominated and a dispersion-free PBE ensemble would be a
different answer to the question we are asking.

for **coordination-number populations**, which is a different observable and the one we consume.
**Three checks, in the order I want them. All three are standard MD analysis and take minutes if the
trajectory exists.**

**V-1′ — Li–O and Li–P/Li–F radial distribution functions with running coordination number.**
Report: first-peak position, **first-minimum position**, and `n(r)` integrated to the first minimum.

                  ∠Li···O–C distribution peaking near ~138°  [same source]
                  Li–P / Li–F coordination ⟹ THE CIP FRACTION, which is the observable most at
                  risk from the finite receptive field (§39.15(a))
🔴 DO NOT validate against the EC coordination number — U-65, the experimental literature does not

🟢🟢 **AND V-1′ PAYS FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY, INDEPENDENT OF EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS SECTION.**

> **`🔴 [PLACEHOLDER-ESTIMATE: 실측 필요]`** and an explicit instruction that it *"must be replaced

**V-1″ — density.** If any NPT run exists: does it reproduce the experimental density of
EC:EMC 3:7 + 1 M LiPF6 (≈1.2 g cm⁻³)?
🔴 **This is the cheapest global test of whether the packing is right — and packing is the mechanism
arXiv:1411.7171 attributes the shell composition to.** An MPtrj-pretrained model applied to a
molecular liquid is exactly the case where this can go wrong. If density is off by >5 %, the packing
is wrong and USE 2 is dead on arrival, while USE 1 may still survive.
*(`[SEARCH-LEVEL]` there is an active benchmark literature on precisely this — evaluating universal
MLFFs against experimental measurements, e.g. arXiv:2508.05762 "UniFFBench". Cited as evidence that
this is the recognised check for this model class, not as a result.)*

**V-2a / V-2b — unchanged from §39.14(e), with one sharpening now that the level is known.**
V-2a's reference level is **VASP PBE(-D3)** — available and measured (6.4.3). And 🔴 **V-2b becomes
the test that decides USE 1 vs USE 1+2**:

compare PBE-D3 against our production level on Li⁺(L)ₙ LIGAND-EXCHANGE ΔG   (rides on B0-D, ~free)
   agree to ≲0.05 eV  ⟹ USE 2 admissible as a falsifier with quantitative weight
   disagree > 0.05 eV ⟹ the WEIGHTS cannot rank shells at the precision we need.
                        🟢 THE SUPPORT IS STILL FINE. Use 1 only.
```
🔒 **That is a clean, pre-registered, nearly-free decision rule for the exact question the lead

🔴 Q3  Were the fine-tuning labels PBE, or PBE-D3(BJ)?                       [decides the D3 setting]
🟢 Q4  (bonus, likely already in hand) Do the Li–O and Li–P/Li–F RDFs and an NPT density exist
       from runs already performed?                                          [V-1′ and V-1″ for free]
```
🔒 **Q1 and Q2 are the same two questions I asked before, unchanged.** The provenance we received
answered the base model, and **the base model is the part that is least relevant** — MPtrj is
inorganic crystals. **Everything load-bearing is in the fine-tuning, and that is still dark.**

## 39.16 V-2a sizing — the box, the frame count, and the VASP settings. Answering engineer5's collapsing question.

> engineer5 priced V-2a at **4,000–60,000 ref-core-h** from a real anchor (§R16.8: periodic static
> SCF, 100–250 atoms, 30–250 core-h/point) and correctly identified that **box atom count** is the
> lever that collapses most of the range. That is a method question, so it is mine. Here it is,
> derived rather than guessed. 🔒 Judgement only.

### (a) 🔴 First — what V-2a compares, because it determines the box and rules out the cheap option

V-2a asks **"is the MLIP faithful to its own reference level?"** — i.e. does `E_MLIP` track `E_DFT`
across configurations. That is a comparison of **two potentials evaluated on identical atomic
configurations**, so the box is not a modelling choice about chemistry; **it is whatever box the
configurations live in.**

🔴 **This rules out the obvious cheap option, and the reason matters.**
> One could extract Li⁺ plus its first and second shells (~60–120 atoms) and compute that as a
> cluster in vacuum or implicit solvent. **That would be self-defeating**: it re-introduces exactly
> the cluster-in-continuum approximation the MLIP is being brought in to test. **We would be
> validating the explicit-solvent instrument inside the implicit-solvent assumption.**
⟹ **V-2a must be fully periodic condensed phase. There is no cheap cluster shortcut.**

🟢 **But the box size is still a free design parameter, because we do not have to sample from the
production trajectory.** The MLIP is cheap; a *dedicated, smaller* validation box is legitimate and
is the right instrument.
```
production MLIP MD  large box, many Li⁺, long trajectory    → supplies SUPPORT and WEIGHTS
V-2a validation box small box, ONE Li⁺, same density        → supplies FRAMES for VASP
```

### (b) The box — **~150–250 atoms, L ≈ 12–14 Å.** Derived from the density.

At the physical composition (EC:EMC 3:7 v/v, 1 M LiPF6, ρ ≈ 1.2 g cm⁻³), a cell containing
**exactly one Li⁺** is fixed by the concentration:
```
1 M  ⟹  one Li⁺ per  1/(6.022e23 × 1000 mol m⁻³)  ≈ 1660 Å³  ⟹  L ≈ 11.8 Å
mass in (12 Å)³ at 1.2 g cm⁻³  =  1728 Å³ × 1.2  ≈ 1250 amu
composition check: 1 LiPF6 (152) + 6 EC (88) + 6 EMC (104)  =  152 + 528 + 624  ≈ 1304 amu ✅
atom count:        LiPF6 8  +  6×EC 60  +  6×EMC 90         =  158 atoms
```
🟢 **⟹ ~158 atoms at L ≈ 12 Å.** That sits **inside** engineer5's R16.8 anchor range (100–250
atoms), so it is an interpolation on their cost curve rather than an extrapolation.

🔴 **CORRECTION to my own first draft, which said "~250 atoms at L ≈ 14 Å for margin". Withdrawn.**
**The box is NOT a free margin parameter — it is tied to the concentration:**
```
L = 12.0 Å, 1 Li⁺  ⟹  1.0 M   ✅  158 atoms — the physically determined choice
L = 14.0 Å, 1 Li⁺  ⟹  0.6 M   ❌  that is a different electrolyte, not "margin"
L = 15.1 Å, 2 Li⁺  ⟹  1.0 M   ✅  ~316 atoms — correct, but 120 frames of it ≈ 51,000 core-h
```
**⟹ one choice, not a range. You cannot buy margin by enlarging the cell without changing the
chemistry.**

🔴 **And a drafting error of mine that propagated, recorded because the mechanism is instructive.**
§39.16(a) names the rejected cluster option **with a number attached ("~60–120 atoms")**.
engineer5's re-price came back pinned at *"40–100 atoms"* — i.e. **the number attached to the option
I explicitly rejected travelled, while the rejection did not.** That mis-pin was ~15× low in cost.
🔒 **Same shape as everything else this round: the disqualifying fact was present in the artefact
and was not the part consumed. My error in drafting, not theirs in reading — I will stop attaching
figures to options I am ruling out.**
⚠ Secondary tell that should have caught it from either side: **40 atoms is *below* engineer5's own
anchor range, so the mis-pin forced an extrapolation where the correct value is an interpolation.**

⚠ **The honest caveat, and its control.** A NequIP-class receptive field is ~10–15 Å
(cutoff × layers), so in a 12 Å cell **the MLIP sees its own periodic images.** DFT in a small cell
has its own finite-size error too.
```
🟢 Why it is still valid: we compare ENERGY DIFFERENCES BETWEEN FRAMES IN A FIXED BOX, and both
   potentials see the identical atoms, so systematic finite-size error largely cancels.
🔴 But "largely" is an assumption, so it gets a control rather than a promise.
```
🔴 **REVISED CONTROL — my first version (10 DFT frames at 400–500 atoms) was over-specified and
would have roughly DOUBLED the item** (~950 core-h/frame on engineer5's N^2.31 ⟹ ~9,500 core-h).
```
(i) 🟢 THE ARTEFACT IS AN MLIP ARTEFACT, SO TEST IT ON THE MLIP SIDE — FOR FREE.
    The concern is a ~10–15 Å receptive field wrapping in a 12 Å cell. Run the MLIP ALONE in a
    12 Å and a 24 Å box and check whether its own energy differences between equivalent local
    configurations shift. Zero DFT, zero cluster core-h.
    🔴 Note this cannot be avoided by enlarging the DFT box: escaping the wrap needs L > 20–30 Å,
       which is unaffordable at any frame count. ⟹ the cancellation argument is LOAD-BEARING,
       and after this control it is the ONLY remaining assumption.
(ii) 3 DFT FRAMES at the 2-Li⁺ / 15.1 Å / 316-atom box  ≈ 3 × 429 = ~1,300 core-h.
    🟢 Better than what I first asked for: it controls box size AND Li⁺–Li⁺ image interaction
      simultaneously, AT THE SAME CONCENTRATION.
```
🔒 Same discipline as B0-D's arm 2: do not assume the artefact is absent, measure it cheaply —
**but measure it with the cheap instrument where the artefact actually lives.**

### (c) The frame count — **120 + 10, not 200.** My 200 was pulled from nothing; this one is derived.

The read-out is the **mean MLIP−DFT residual PER SHELL STOICHIOMETRY CLASS** (that is what decides
whether the weights can rank shells).
```
per-frame residual scatter   ~0.1 eV        [ESTIMATE — this is the number I am least sure of]
target precision on a class mean  0.02 eV
⟹ n per class ≈ (0.1/0.02)² ≈ 25
⟹ 5–6 relevant stoichiometry classes × 25  =  125–150 frames
```
⟹ **120 stratified frames** (by stoichiometry class, plus a high-uncertainty stratum from V-4 if the
model carries a committee) **+ 10 finite-size control frames = 130.**
⚠ If the per-frame scatter comes back much larger than 0.1 eV, `n` grows as its square — **so the
first 20 frames should be run and the scatter measured before the remaining 110 are committed.**
That is a gate inside a gate, and it costs nothing to impose.

### (d) 🔴 The VASP settings — and this is the second big lever, which nobody has pulled

engineer5's anchor used **ENCUT 600 eV and k-spacing ≤ 0.03 Å⁻¹**. Those are §26.4's *lattice-energy
and phonon* settings, where high absolute precision is required. **V-2a is a different job.**
```
🔴 k-points:  Γ-POINT ONLY.
   A 12–14 Å box of a wide-gap molecular liquid has negligible band dispersion. k-spacing 0.03 Å⁻¹
   in a 12 Å cell demands ~18 k-points per direction — MASSIVELY over-converged for this purpose
   and the single largest avoidable cost in the estimate.
🔴 ENCUT:  ~500–520 eV, not 600.
   O and F PAWs are hard so 400 would be uncomfortable, but 520 is the standard Materials Project
   setting and is more than adequate for RELATIVE energies at FIXED geometry.
   ⟹ and 520 is very likely the right number for an independent reason ↓
```

🔴 **Constraint that overrides my preferences: the settings must MATCH the settings that produced the
fine-tuning labels.** V-2a asks whether the MLIP is faithful *to its own reference*; if we compute
the reference with different ENCUT or different PAWs, a disagreement is our disagreement, not the
model's.
```
⟹ NEW PROVENANCE QUESTION (Q5): what VASP settings produced the FINE-TUNING labels —
   ENCUT, PAW dataset version, and whether MP-standard conventions were followed?
🟢 MPtrj / Materials Project standard is ENCUT 520 eV, so if the fine-tuning inherited MP settings
   the answer is probably 520 — which is BOTH the physically adequate choice AND cheaper than 600.
🔒 It rides on the provenance request already outstanding (U-62/U-66). No extra round trip.
```

### (e) 🟡 On κ for VASP — I think engineer5's flag points the wrong way here, and this is the one place I expect GOOD news

engineer5 correctly notes that plane-wave VASP is a **third workload class**, distinct from the
SCF-gradient probe κ was measured on, and applies my own `[UNQUANTIFIED]` caveat. Agreed on the
caveat. **But I think the sign is different from the other two cases, and the reason is physical:**
```
KNL's weakness    scalar, memory-latency-bound, poorly-vectorised code
                  ⟹ why I flagged Hessian-heavy work and out-of-core MP2 as "possibly worse"
KNL's strength    wide-vector FFT and dense BLAS — which is what AVX-512 was built for
plane-wave DFT    is FFT + dense linear algebra dominated
⟹ VASP is historically one of the BETTER cases on KNL, not one of the worse ones.
```
🟡 **So my expectation is κ_VASP ≲ κ_G16, i.e. V-2a may be relatively cheaper on this machine than a
naive κ = 2.4 suggests.** 🔴 **Still `[UNQUANTIFIED]` and I am not proposing a factor** — but the
*direction* is opposite to the two flags I raised last round, and an engineer sizing a reservation
should know that the three workload classes do not all move the same way.

### (f) Summary for the re-price

```
box            ~158 atoms at L ≈ 12 Å  (derived from 1 M + ρ 1.2 g cm⁻³ + one Li⁺)
               up to ~250 atoms at L ≈ 14 Å for margin
               + 10 control frames at ~400–500 atoms
frames         120 stratified + 10 control = 130     (not 200)
               🔴 with a sub-gate: run the first 20, measure the residual scatter, then commit
k-points       Γ ONLY  (not k-spacing 0.03 — the single largest avoidable cost)
ENCUT          ~520 eV (not 600), and it MUST match the fine-tuning labels — provenance Q5
functional     PBE(±D3(BJ)) — matching the labels, per U-66
κ              [UNQUANTIFIED], but expected FAVOURABLE for plane-wave work on KNL, unlike the
               Hessian and MP2 cases
```

> 🔴 **This subsection was originally headed "Final number". It was not final — (j) raised the
> reserve to 17,000 on exponent sensitivity two rounds later.** The label is left visible with the

120 frames × 86 core-h   (158 atoms, L = 12 Å, 1 Li⁺, 1 M)      ≈ 10,400
  3 control × 429        (316 atoms, L = 15.1 Å, 2 Li⁺, 1 M)     ≈  1,300
  MLIP-side finite-size check                                    =      0
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V-2a point estimate at exponent 2.31                             ≈ 11,700 ref-core-h

🟢 **Both dominant levers are now pinned (box by the concentration, k-points by physics), so this is

🔴 **And Γ-only is NOT waiting on the user.** It is my method call, made in (d) on physical grounds.
engineer5 recorded it as a pending user question and was reserving against it; it is closed.

### (h) 🔒 CONSOLIDATED V-2a SPEC — supersedes every V-2a number earlier in this section

**Why this block exists**: two consecutive exchange rounds lost a revision — the box pin picked up
the figure attached to an option I had *rejected* (§39.16(b)), and the next round's control line kept
a version I had *withdrawn*. **Both corrections were in the message; the superseded value is what got
recorded.** The cause is not competence on either side: I had been sending **deltas embedded in
argument**, and a delta embedded in argument is exactly what gets skimmed past.
🔒 **Rule adopted: numeric specifications go in a single consolidated block. If a later prose number
of mine conflicts with the block, THE BLOCK WINS until a replacement block is issued.**

```
V-2a — CONSOLIDATED SPEC
  primary frames    120
  primary box       158 atoms · L = 12.0 Å · 1 Li⁺ · 1 M · (1 LiPF6 + 6 EC + 6 EMC)
  control frames    3
  control box       316 atoms · L = 15.1 Å · 2 Li⁺ · 1 M
                    (controls box size AND Li⁺–Li⁺ image interaction, at fixed concentration)
  MLIP-side check   12 Å vs 24 Å box, MLIP ONLY                    → 0 cluster core-h
  k-points          Γ ONLY — proposer method call, NOT pending anyone
  ENCUT             ~520 eV, MUST match the fine-tuning labels      → user Q5, pending
  functional        PBE ± D3(BJ), matching the labels               → U-66, pending

```

### (i) 🔴 Open question back to engineer5 — is the periodic-VASP anchor `[MEASURED]` or `[ESTIMATE]`?

engineer5 priced V-2a from §R16.8 (30–250 core-h/point, 100–250 atoms), described as *"a real
anchor, not a guess"* — but then reported **not knowing its k-point scheme**, which is unusual for a
measurement. The §26.4 spec I wrote for that work says **k-spacing ≤ 0.03 Å⁻¹**, and in VASP's
convention `N_k = ceil(|b|/KSPACING)`, `|b| = 2π/a`:
```
a = 12 Å   (our liquid box)        → 18 k-points per direction
a = 20–25 Å (a phonon supercell)   →  9–11 per direction
```
🔴 **Nobody runs a 250-atom molecular crystal on an 11×11×11 mesh.** So either that anchor did not
follow the §26.4 spec, or **it was never a run.**
```
[MEASURED] ⟹ the k-mesh is known and the Γ-only ratio follows directly (≈ 1/N_k)
[ESTIMATE] ⟹ 🔴 V-2a's price is a bracket on an estimate on an estimate, and the
              "×0.05–×0.30 Γ-only discount" is COMPOUNDING rather than bounding
```
🔒 **ADR-034 §6 pointed the other way for once** — *"`[MEASURED]` means it was measured, not that we
know what was measured."* Asked, not asserted; the label is doing work in a number we are reserving
against.

🟢 **But the bracket does not need to collapse before the run.** The phasing gate already adopted —
first 20 frames, then commit — **measures the actual core-h/frame at the same time as it measures
the residual scatter.** ⟹ the k-point uncertainty resolves itself on 20 frames, at ~1/6 of the item,
with no user round trip and no anchor archaeology. It becomes worth resolving in advance **only** if
the answer is `[ESTIMATE]`, because then the top of the bracket is itself unanchored and the
reservation could be the wrong order of magnitude in either direction.


### (j) 🔴 Two caveats on the converged ≈12,000 — recorded so the precision is not read as accuracy

engineer5 independently re-derived ≈11,650 and it matched my ≈11,700 to rounding. **That checks the
arithmetic and is not evidence about the cost.**
```
🔒 We both applied ENGINEER5'S N^2.314 law to ENGINEER5'S 30 core-h @ 100 atoms base.
   Two people applying the same power law to the same base always agree.
   It tests nothing about whether the base is right.
⟹ INTERNAL CONSISTENCY IS NOT VERIFICATION — my own standing rule, turned on this exchange.
⟹ and §39.16(i)'s question (is R16.8 [MEASURED] or [ESTIMATE]?) is still unanswered, now with a
   doubly persuasive number sitting on top of it.
🟢 Mitigation is already in place and needs no action: the 20-frame phasing gate measures the real
   core-h/frame. The agreement must simply not be recorded as if it were the measurement.
```

**Second caveat — the exponent is a two-point fit across two different systems.**
The endpoints are phonon supercells of molecular crystals at 100 and 250 atoms, plausibly at
different k-meshes and densities. **That is a line through two points that differ in more than N.**
And physically, plane-wave DFT is not one power law but `a·N²(FFT) + b·N³(subspace diagonalisation)`,
whose terms are comparable at 100–320 atoms for a molecular liquid — **a two-point fit cannot
distinguish 2.31 from a 2/3 mixture.**
```
exponent 2.0   ≈  9,700 ref-core-h
exponent 2.31  ≈ 11,650      ← adopted
exponent 3.0   ≈ 17,000      ⟹ the adopted value would be ~40 % low
```
🟢 **Recommendation: reserve 17,000, not 12,000.** The extra 5,000 is **0.3 % of the 1.79 M
headroom** — trivial insurance against being *under*-reserved, which is the worse planning failure.
The frame-20 gate then replaces the estimate with a measurement.
🟢 Fortunate rather than clever: **the exponent uncertainty barely touches the control line, because
it had already been cut to 3 frames.** The 316-atom extrapolation is simultaneously the least
reliable point in the set and the smallest.

🔒 **And the durable fix for the two lost revisions is neither party's discipline rule.** My
"don't attach figures to rejected options" and engineer5's "check the source, not the cited range"
both depend on someone remembering to apply them under time pressure. **The consolidated spec block
(h) does not.** Same principle this project keeps arriving at: **a structure outside the loop beats
care inside it.**


## 39.17 🔴🔴 engineer5's answer is bigger than V-2a — **we have no measured VASP basis, and no evidence VASP runs at all**

> engineer5 checked and answered: **R16.8 has never been measured.** `plan.json` shows RT-1's task
> list is **G16-only, zero VASP entries.** They relabelled V-2a `[ESTIMATE derived from an ESTIMATE]`
> and attached the label to the number. 🟢 That is the right handling and the answer cost them
> something to give.
> **But the consequence is larger than the item that surfaced it.**

### (a) 🔴 What else rests on that unmeasured anchor

```
V-2a  MLIP validation single points                             17,000   [ESTIMATE²]
🔴 §26.4 LATTICE ENERGIES — LEDC and LiPO2F2 (class B solids)               [ESTIMATE²]
   ⟹ feeds ΔG_precip  ⟹  feeds the LiF : Li2CO3 ratio  ⟹  ADR-003 AXIS (b), A REPORTED OBSERVABLE
   and it includes FINITE-DISPLACEMENT PHONONS, which are the expensive part (§26.4 flagged
   LEDC phonons as "the bulk of the pessimistic estimate")
any future periodic work                                                    [ESTIMATE²]
```
🔴 **A reported observable is sitting on a cost basis with no measurement anywhere in its lineage.**
V-2a is the small item; the lattice-energy line is the one on the critical path.

### (b) 🔴🔴 And the deeper problem is not cost — **it is that "the binary exists" has never been tested against "VASP runs our systems"**

RT-1 measured `vasp_std = "vasp.6.4.3 19Mar24 (build Jun 24 2026 10:34:25) complex"`.
🟢 Version resolved: **6.4.3 ≥ 6.3 ⟹ r2SCAN-D4 is available**, which closes half of U-24.
🔴 **But a VASP binary without a POTCAR library computes nothing.** POTCAR pseudopotential files are
licensed separately from the source and are **not produced by building the code.**

```
grep -rn "POTCAR|potpaw|pseudopotential|PAW dataset"  over docs/ and src/
  → ZERO hits for VASP, anywhere: not in the pilot, not in the probe, not in the compute plan
```

🔒 **And the team already identified this exact failure mode — for a different code.**
`03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md:5986` records, for CP2K:
> *"basis set · pseudopotential data bundled (`$CP2K_DATA_DIR`) | `[NOT MEASURED]` — **실무상 가장
> 자주 깨진다**"* (*in practice this is what breaks most often*)

and `src/experiments/p7_cp2k/P7.sh:45` warns that CP2K **does not die** when it cannot find those
files — it **silently falls back to defaults.**

🔴 **The lesson was learned, written down, and never transferred to the analogous code.**
This is the same shape as RT-1's two lost round trips, where availability was inferred from a name
in a module list. 🔒 **Rule 20 applies to any inference from a proxy — including a proxy that
worked for one code.**

### (c) 🔴 The VASP-specific silent failure is NOT the missing file — it is the wrong variant

```
POTCAR ABSENT        → VASP stops. Loud. Survivable.
🔴 POTCAR WRONG VARIANT → VASP runs perfectly and returns different energies.
   Li vs Li_sv (semicore 1s in valence), O vs O_h, F vs F_h, P vs P_h — all valid, all different.
```
🔴 **And for V-2a this is not a quality question, it is a validity question.** V-2a asks whether the
MLIP is faithful **to its own reference**. MPtrj/Materials Project uses a *defined* POTCAR set
(`Li_sv` among them). **Compute the reference with a different variant and any disagreement is ours,
not the model's — and the item measures our own inconsistency at full cost.**
⟹ **POTCAR variant joins Q5.** It is the same argument I already made for ENCUT, now with a concrete
mechanism attached.

### (d) 🟢 The fix is two items, and the first one costs zero core-hours

```
VASP PRECONDITION BLOCK  (consolidated spec — supersedes any prose version of this)

 V-P1  POTCAR INVENTORY.  0 core-h — it is a directory listing.
       Record, in the next probe reply:
         · does a POTCAR library exist and is it readable by us?
         · which VARIANT directory exists for each of  C · H · O · Li · P · F
           (report the exact names, e.g. "Li_sv", "O", "F", "P", not a boolean)
         · the library's own version/date stamp if present
       🔴 Report NAMES, not a boolean. A boolean cannot answer the variant question and we
          would need a second round trip to ask it.

 V-P2  VASP LAUNCH SMOKE.  minutes, one tiny cell (e.g. rocksalt LiF, 8 atoms, Γ-only, low ENCUT).
       Proves: the binary launches under MPI on a COMPUTE node · POTCARs are actually consumed ·
       a CONTCAR/OSZICAR is produced · and it returns the project's FIRST VASP core-h datum.
       🔒 STATE records that P6 — the item that produced κ — was the ONE item with no cheap smoke
          gate in front of it, and that this was named as a defect at shutdown.
          🔴 DO NOT REPEAT IT FOR VASP. V-P2 is that gate.
```

### (e) 🟢 And the 20-frame phasing gate is now more valuable than when I proposed it

It was a cost gate for V-2a. With (a) established, **it is the project's first VASP cost measurement
of any kind.** ⟹ instrument it accordingly: record core-h/frame, peak memory, wall, k-point count,
ENCUT, POTCAR variants and atom count, so that **one gate anchors two consumers.**
⚠ **Honest limit**: a liquid-box datum does not size a crystal phonon supercell — different system,
different cell, different settings, and phonons are finite-displacement *sets* of runs rather than
single points. **It establishes the machine's VASP throughput class, not the lattice-energy line.**
That line still needs its own measurement, and it should be added to whatever probe carries V-P2.

### (f) Does this change my recommendation? **No — it changes its character.**
`Reserve 17,000` stood on exponent uncertainty. It now stands on *"no measurement anywhere in the
lineage"*, which is a weaker basis for any number, including mine.
🔒 **I am not raising the reservation further, because a larger number derived from the same
nothing is not more conservative — it is more confident.** V-P1 and V-P2 are what replace the
guess, and they cost approximately nothing.


## 39.18 🔴 SELF-CORRECTION on §39.17(a) — I attributed the wrong observable. The right one is worse.

> Sent to engineer5 and the lead immediately, because engineer5 was escalating my framing to the
> lead as I wrote this. 🔒 Judgement only.

### (a) What I got wrong

§39.17(a) said the unmeasured VASP basis feeds *"ΔG_precip ⟹ the LiF : Li2CO3 ratio ⟹ ADR-003 axis
(b)"*. **The middle link is false, and §26.4 — which I wrote — says so:**
```
CLASS A  LiF · Li2CO3 · Li2O · LiOH   🔴 "VASP를 쓰지 않는다" — EXPERIMENTAL ΔG_f°(s) anchors
CLASS B  LEDC · LiPO2F2               VASP, with a δ correction anchored on class A
```
⟹ **LiF and Li2CO3 do not depend on VASP for their thermodynamics.** VASP carries **LEDC and
LiPO2F2**, plus class-A calculations used *only* to derive the systematic correction δ.
🔒 Same error I have been catching in others all round: **a chain quoted without the middle link
being checked.** Corrected in both directions before it propagated further.

### (b) 🔴 But the correct consequence is worse than the one I stated, and it is structural

**§26.4's class-A route is an experimental anchor — which is a known-answer dependency, exactly the
class ADR-014 outlawed.**
```
For an UNSTUDIED electrolyte, there is no experimental ΔG_f°(s) for its novel solids.
⟹ EVERY solid is class B.
⟹ THE EXPERIMENTAL ROUTE DOES NOT TRANSFER. THE VASP ROUTE DOES.
```
🔴 **This inverts §26.4's own framing.** I chose experiment there because it converted a DFT↔DFT
seam into a DFT↔experiment seam, and wrote that this is *"strictly better"*. **It is strictly better
for accuracy on system 1 and strictly worse for transferability, and I did not notice at the time.**
It degrades gracefully — most Li-ion electrolytes still make LiF and Li2CO3, so δ can usually still
be anchored — but the *production* path for novel solids is VASP and only VASP.

> ⟹ **V-P1 and V-P2 do not gate a budget line. They gate whether the pipeline can meet its
> top-level requirement (ADR-014) for any electrolyte at all.**
> **If VASP does not run on this cluster, the pipeline cannot handle a novel solid in ANY system,
> studied or not.** That is a larger claim than the one I made in §39.17 and it is the correct one.

### (c) The fallback ladder, so the finding does not arrive without a plan

If V-P1/V-P2 come back negative, or the lattice-energy line proves unaffordable:

**F-1 — precipitation of class-B solids becomes a declared uncertainty axis. 🟢 PREFERRED.**
ADR-021 already represents precipitation as a reversible pair governed by a computed `K_sp`. If
`K_sp` is unavailable, **scan it over a physically bounded range and report the sensitivity of the
predicted composition** rather than reporting a number. 🟢 Element-agnostic, so it **transfers** —
and for an unstudied electrolyte it is the *only* honest treatment anyway, since novel solids have
neither experiment nor (in this branch) a periodic code. 🔒 Consistent with ADR-018's principle and
with §39.3 candidate 3: convert an unknown into a declared axis rather than a fabricated value.
**Cost: zero. Loss: the organic precipitation channel is reported as a band, not a value.**

**F-2 — cluster-extrapolated lattice energy in G16.** Monomer → dimer → tetramer → extrapolate.
🔴 **Poor for this case and I would not lead with it**: LEDC is an *ionic, layered* crystal
(Li⁺ + dicarbonate²⁻), and the Madelung sum converges conditionally, so cluster extrapolation is
slowly and unreliably convergent exactly where we need it. **Available, bounded, and low-accuracy —
worth having as a sanity bracket on F-1's scan range, not as a value.**

**F-3 — literature thermodynamics for LEDC.** `[UNVERIFIED — needs a literature check I have not
done]`. LEDC has been synthesised and characterised, but whether *thermodynamic* data exist is
unknown to me. **Cheap to check and it should be checked before F-1 is adopted**, because if the
data exist, class B shrinks to LiPO2F2 alone and the whole issue becomes minor for system 1.
⚠ **It still does not transfer** — that is F-1's point.

### (d) What does not change
The finding itself (U-69/U-70), V-P1, V-P2, the 17,000 reserve, and the POTCAR-variant addition to
Q5 are all unaffected. **Only the downstream attribution changed — and it moved from "a reported
observable" to "the pipeline's top-level requirement".**

An RDF is a **one-dimensional, species-averaged projection**. Our estimand is a *multi-dimensional
composition*: `Li⁺(EC)ₘ(EMC)ₙ(PF6⁻)ₖ`.
```
A total Li–O CN of 4.0 is equally consistent with  m=4,n=0 · m=2,n=2 · m=1,n=3 · any mixture.
A TOTAL Li–O RDF cannot separate EC oxygen from EMC oxygen.
And the composition split is exactly the quantity §39.14(g)-1 is about — WHICH solvent Li⁺ prefers,
not how many neighbours it has.
```

the **CIP fraction**, the observable §39.15(a) flagged as most sensitive to a finite receptive field.

### 39.21.3 🔴 (c) The EC⁻ boundary — the training set is the wrong place to look. The architecture is.

**ADR-051's limitation is architectural, not a data gap, and more data does not fix it:**
```
NequIP/SevenNet input = atomic positions + species.  Output = one energy.
⟹ There is no total-charge input. For IDENTICAL nuclear positions the model returns ONE energy.
⟹ It cannot return different energies for EC and EC⁻ at the same geometry.
🔴 AND ADDING REDUCED SPECIES TO TRAINING MAKES IT WORSE, NOT BETTER: the network would see two
   different labels for near-identical inputs and learn an average.
```
So *"spanning candidate chemistry"* at >200 k structures does **not** by itself move the boundary.

🟢 **But there are two cases, and only one of them is blocked — this is where the boundary can move:**
```
CASE 1  THE ELECTRON-TRANSFER EVENT ITSELF (EC → EC⁻ at fixed geometry)
        🔴 IMPOSSIBLE FOR THIS ARCHITECTURE, PERMANENTLY. Not a data question.
        🟢 We do not need it — S1 barriers are computed at our own level, not by the MLIP.

CASE 2  THE EQUILIBRIUM SOLVATION SHELL OF AN ALREADY-FORMED REDUCED SPECIES
        🟡 POSSIBLE, because EC⁻ is geometrically distinct (pyramidalised / ring-opened), so the
          model can learn "this geometry ⟹ this energy" implicitly, WITHOUT a charge channel.
        🔴 AND THE PERIODIC-CELL ARGUMENT MAKES THIS SHARPER: a bare EC⁻ in a periodic cell needs a
          compensating background and carries a known artefact. But **Li⁺EC⁻ as a NEUTRAL CONTACT
          PAIR needs none** — and that is precisely the species our chemistry produces
          (P1's system is exactly `LiEC•`, charge 0, mult 2).
        ⟹ IF neutral Li⁺EC⁻-type configurations were in the training set, CASE 2 IS IN SCOPE.
```
🔴 **The single question that settles it** (the lead asked for one):
> **"Did the training set include reduced / radical species — specifically neutral Li⁺·EC⁻-type
> contact pairs — and were those PBE labels spin-polarised?"**

**Both halves are needed and the second is the tell**: an open-shell radical labelled with a
non-spin-polarised calculation is mislabelled regardless of what was in the set. If the answer is
yes+yes, **U-64's boundary moves and the post-reduction shell comes into scope.** If no, the
boundary holds and that half stays with the static route — **which is where §39.3 already put it, so
nothing downstream breaks either way.**

### 39.21.7 🔴 HANDOVER SPEC — what must come off the GPU machine with the ensemble

The user has the configuration-sampling code and it runs off-cluster. Our cluster work consumes an
ensemble produced elsewhere. **The following is what must arrive WITH it. Per §39.16(h)'s rule, this
is a consolidated block and it wins over prose elsewhere.**

```
ENSEMBLE HANDOVER — CONSOLIDATED SPEC

FORMAT
  extended XYZ (extxyz), one file per trajectory, or an ASE-readable trajectory.
  Rationale: lossless, human-inspectable, and carries per-frame key-value metadata natively,
  so the metadata below cannot become separated from the frames it describes.
  🔴 Do NOT hand over frames and metadata as two files. That is the failure this project has
     hit six times — a fact in one place and the thing that qualifies it in another.

PER-FRAME (in the extxyz comment line)
  seed_id            🔴 ADR-051 CONSTRAINT. Must share its DEFINITION with
                        sei_pilot/seeding.py::provenance. UNRECOVERABLE AFTER THE FACT.
  trajectory_id      🔴 separate column from seed_id — do NOT merge them (ADR-051)
  frame_index, time_ps   🔴 required to compute autocorrelation. See SAMPLING below.
  cell               full 3×3 matrix, not a single length (the cell may not be cubic)
  temperature, density
  composition        species counts
  d3_setting         🔴 the VALIDATED setting (39.21.2), recorded PER FRAME so it cannot drift
  model_id + hash    which MLIP produced this frame
  uncertainty        per-frame model uncertainty if the model provides one (drives V-4 and the
                     stratification in V-2a′)

GLOBAL (one manifest per handover)
  model identity and hash · sampling protocol · thermostat/barostat and parameters
  equilibration length DISCARDED (and it must be discarded, and stated)
  ensemble type: NPT or NVT, and if NVT the density used
  🟢 VALIDATION MANIFEST: the RDF and NPT density results already obtained, WITH the settings
     they were computed under — because 39.21.2 makes production settings inherit from them.

🔴 SAMPLING — THE ONE METHODOLOGICAL REQUIREMENT, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT THE MODEL
  N_frames IS NOT THE SAMPLE SIZE.
  Consecutive MD frames are correlated; Li⁺ first-shell residence times are hundreds of ps to ns.
  Draw 120 frames from one trajectory at a 1 ps stride and you have far fewer than 120 independent
  shell compositions — and every population uncertainty computed from them is too small by the
  autocorrelation factor.
  ⟹ REQUIRED: report the autocorrelation of the SHELL COMPOSITION (not of the energy) and the
     resulting EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE.
  ⟹ PREFERRED: multiple INDEPENDENT SEEDS rather than one long trajectory.
     🟢 This is free here — the MLIP is cheap — and it simultaneously satisfies ADR-051's D1
        (seed-split capture–recapture), which needs independent seeds by DESIGN rather than by
        assumption. One choice, two requirements.
```

### (c) 🔴 F-1 is not a fallback. It is the DEFAULT for novel solids — and this is the durable half of §39.18.

The lead is right that F-1 survives the cancellation, and the reason is stronger than "keep it in
case". **§26.4's VASP route is not self-sufficient — it depends on an experimental anchor:**
```
ΔG_lattice(class B) = VASP(class B) + δ,      δ = VASP(class A) − EXPERIMENT(class A)
⟹ δ requires class-A species WITH EXPERIMENTAL DATA to anchor it.
🔴 For an UNSTUDIED electrolyte, a novel solid may have NO experimental analogue AT ALL —
   in which case δ CANNOT BE ANCHORED, and the VASP number carries an UNCORRECTED SYSTEMATIC ERROR
   OF UNKNOWN SIZE. This is true EVEN THOUGH VASP RUNS PERFECTLY.
```
> 🔴 **⟹ F-1 inverts status. It is not the fallback for "VASP unavailable" — it is the PRODUCTION
> TREATMENT for solids without experimental anchors, and the VASP+δ route is the SPECIAL CASE that
> works only where anchors happen to exist.**

```
RULE (transferable, element-agnostic, resolves U-72):

                                                                                    Li2CO3, Li2O, LiOH
                                                                                    anchor LEDC/LiPO2F2)
  NO experimental anchor for the class               ⟹  F-1: K_sp as a DECLARED
                                                          UNCERTAINTY AXIS, scanned over a
                                                          physically bounded range, with the
                                                          composition's SENSITIVITY reported
                                                          instead of a value
```

candidate 3 and ADR-018's principle for the third time: **convert an unknown into a declared axis
rather than a fabricated value.** F-2 (cluster extrapolation) stays a bracket, never a value.

change the rule above, because the rule exists precisely for the case where no literature exists.**

## 39.23 🔴 "Multiple independent seeds" needs one condition and one free diagnostic, or it measures the wrong thing

> The lead is adopting **multiple independent seeds instead of one long trajectory** as a
> *requirement*, and is right that `N_frames is not the sample size` is the item most likely to be
> skipped *"because it costs nothing to ignore and produces confident-looking error bars."*
> 🔴 **But "multiple seeds" alone does not deliver what it is being adopted for, and the gap is
> already written down in this project as ADR-051 U-51.**
> ⚠ V-P2's cancellation is already handled in §39.22 — the messages crossed; nothing to redo there.

### (a) 🔴 The gap — more seeds does not fix a biased initial condition, it measures the bias precisely

```
IF each trajectory is shorter than the Li⁺ shell-exchange time (hundreds of ps – ns)
AND the initial configurations are sliced from one parent trajectory
⟹ every "independent" seed inherits the parent's shell composition
⟹ THE ENSEMBLE REPORTS THE STARTING DISTRIBUTION, NOT THE EQUILIBRIUM ONE
⟹ and it does so with SMALL, CONFIDENT ERROR BARS, because the seeds agree with each other —
   they agree because they are the same configuration.
```
🔒 **This is ADR-051's U-51 verbatim, in a new context:** *"replica 초기조건이 같은 스냅샷 풀의
상관 구간에서 나오면 D1 전체가 무너진다"* — if replica initial conditions come from a correlated
stretch of one snapshot pool, **D1 collapses entirely.** It was written for the xTB reactive-MD
replicas. **It applies here identically, and D1 is the device that replaced axis 3.**

🔴 **⟹ The requirement is not "multiple seeds". It is "multiple seeds whose INITIAL CONFIGURATIONS
ARE INDEPENDENTLY EQUILIBRATED."** Those are different specifications and only the second one works.

### (b) 🟢 And there is a standard, free diagnostic that tests it rather than assuming it

**Gelman–Rubin `R̂`, computed on the shell composition as the scalar** (e.g. `n_EC` in the first
shell), across seeds:
```
R̂  compares BETWEEN-seed variance with WITHIN-seed variance
   R̂ → 1     seeds have mixed ⟹ trajectories long enough AND seeds genuinely independent
   R̂ ≫ 1     🔴 chains have not mixed — trajectories too short, or starts too similar
             ⟹ EXACTLY the failure in (a), detected rather than assumed
ESS  the companion statistic — the EFFECTIVE sample size, which is the number §39.21.7 asked for
```
🟢 **This replaces both of my earlier requests with one standard pair.** §39.21.7 asked for
*"report the autocorrelation of the shell composition"* and *"report the effective sample size"* as
two separate items. **`R̂` + `ESS` over seeds is the standard, well-defined form of both**, is a few
lines of analysis, and the user's existing analysis tooling may already produce it.
🔴 **And it does something neither of my original requests did: `R̂` detects the (a) failure — the
one that produces confident-looking error bars — because that failure shows up as
between-seed variance being too SMALL, which an autocorrelation time computed within a single
trajectory cannot see.**

### (c) Revised handover requirement — supersedes §39.21.7's SAMPLING clause

```
SAMPLING — CONSOLIDATED (supersedes the SAMPLING clause of §39.21.7)

  seeds        ≥ 8–10 independent trajectories
               rationale: enough that the D1 A/B split can be RESAMPLED (jackknife over seeds)
               rather than being a single arbitrary partition. With 2 seeds there is one split
               and no way to estimate variance between splits.

  🔴 starts    INITIAL CONFIGURATIONS INDEPENDENTLY EQUILIBRATED.
               NOT frames sliced from one parent trajectory.  ← the whole point of (a)
               If they must come from a parent run, the slices must be separated by more than the
               shell-exchange time, and that separation must be STATED.

  length       each trajectory ≥ the shell-exchange time where achievable.
               🟢 affordable here — this is the MLIP's advantage over the DFT MD it replaced.

  🔴 report    R̂ and ESS on the SHELL COMPOSITION (not on the energy — energy mixes far faster
               than composition and would read as converged while composition has not moved).
               Report per composition variable (n_EC, n_EMC, n_PF6), not pooled.

  equilibration  discarded length reported, per seed.
```
🔒 **Why `R̂` on composition and not on energy, stated separately because it is the kind of thing
that gets substituted**: the potential energy of a liquid decorrelates in picoseconds; the identity
of Li⁺'s first-shell ligands does not. **An `R̂` computed on energy would read ≈1 while the quantity
we actually consume has not mixed at all** — which is the same class of substitution as
`cores_observed`, `converged`, and every other item in this round's list.

### (d) 🟢 One choice, three requirements — unchanged and now stronger
```
independently-equilibrated multi-seed sampling satisfies simultaneously:
  · the effective-sample-size problem (§39.21.7)
  · ADR-051's D1 seed-split capture–recapture, BY DESIGN rather than by assumption
  · ADR-051's U-51, which is the condition D1 needs and which nothing else in the plan supplies
🔒 and R̂ turns "we assumed the seeds are independent" into "we measured whether they are", at
   approximately zero cost. That is the shape this project keeps converging on.
```

## 39.24 🔴 V-2a′ finite-size control — DECIDED: none needed, and the reason is recorded so it is not re-added as an oversight

> engineer5 flagged rather than decided: *"constructing specific rare compositions is a different
> design than statistically sampling a distribution, so R35.8's control logic doesn't obviously
> transfer."* 🟢 **Correct to flag it. Decided below, not split.**

### (a) 🟢 DECISION: no separate finite-size control frames. The cancellation is STRONGER here than in V-2a, not weaker.

The lead's suspected asymmetry is real and **cuts further than the lead suggested.** The reason is
that V-2a′'s read-out is a **double difference**:
```
Δ_MLIP  = E_MLIP(constructed) − E_MLIP(reference frame)
Δ_DFT   = E_DFT (constructed) − E_DFT (reference frame)
READ-OUT = Δ_MLIP − Δ_DFT       "does the MLIP over-penalise this composition?"
```
```
V-2a  compared MLIP vs DFT across DIFFERENT SAMPLED FRAMES, which can differ in their whole global
      arrangement ⟹ cancellation was partial and deserved a control.
V-2a′ compares two configurations IN THE SAME CELL that differ ONLY BY A LOCAL SWAP near Li⁺.
      ⟹ protected TWICE: once by MLIP-vs-DFT on identical atoms, and again by the two
        configurations being related by a local rearrangement in an otherwise identical box.
      🔴 The periodic image sits ~12 Å away; the DIFFERENCE between the two configurations is
        localised within ~5 Å of the cell centre. The image contribution largely cancels in the
        difference, and what remains is second-order.
```
🔒 **Recorded so it is not re-added later as an oversight (the lead's explicit request): the control
was dropped BY ARGUMENT, on the double-difference structure — not by forgetting, and not to save
money.** Anyone re-adding it should first show that the double difference does not cancel.

### (b) 🔴 But the control is replaced by three construction constraints, and two of them are free diagnostics

**C-1 — the construction must be a SWAP, not a substitution.**
```
🔴 EC = 10 atoms, EMC = 15, PF6⁻ = 7. A first-shell SUBSTITUTION is NOT atom-conserving and
   changes the density — which would inject a finite-size artefact rather than test for one.
🟢 CORRECT CONSTRUCTION — a ligand EXCHANGE within a fixed, neutral cell:
     Li⁺(EC)ₘ(EMC)ₙ + EMC(bulk)  →  Li⁺(EC)ₘ₋₁(EMC)ₙ₊₁ + EC(bulk)
   move molecule A out of the first shell to a bulk position, and molecule B from bulk into it.
   ⟹ atom count, cell, density and TOTAL CHARGE all conserved.
   ⟹ and it is EXACTLY the physical process whose free energy sets the composition, so the
     quantity computed is the one we actually want.
⚠ EC↔PF6⁻ and EMC↔PF6⁻ exchanges are the CIP⇌SSIP construction. The cell stays neutral
  (the anion remains in the box, only its position changes), so the missing charge channel is
  not engaged. 🟢 This is how the CIP question gets probed without needing a charged cell.
```

**C-2 — the bulk swap partner must be chosen away from the cell boundary, and the choice AVERAGED.**
🔴 The one contribution that does *not* obviously cancel is the **bulk** partner: if it happens to
sit near the cell edge it is close to an image.
```
🟢 FREE FIX AND FREE DIAGNOSTIC: repeat the exchange with ≥3 DIFFERENT bulk partners and report the
   SPREAD. The spread over bulk-partner choice IS the finite-size diagnostic —
     small spread ⟹ the wrap does not matter for this read-out (the (a) argument confirmed)
     large spread ⟹ it does, and we have measured it rather than promised it
   🔒 This is the original control's PURPOSE, achieved inside the experiment instead of beside it.
COST: the spread is a property of the CELL AND METHOD, not of each composition.
      ⟹ estimate it ONCE on 2–3 compositions × 3 partners (≈6 extra frames) and apply the
        resulting variance as an uncertainty to all the others.
      ⟹ ~30 → ~36 frames. **≈ +20 % on the item, not ×3.** engineer5 to re-price.
```

**C-3 — relax with the MLIP, evaluate BOTH at that geometry, and report the DFT FORCES.**
```
A naive swap creates bad contacts, so a local relaxation is required. Relax with the MLIP, then
single-point BOTH MLIP and DFT at that same geometry.
🟢 Conservative in the right direction: the MLIP-relaxed geometry is the one MOST FAVOURABLE to the
   MLIP, so it MINIMISES the apparent penalty. If a penalty still appears, it is real.
🔴 AND THE FREE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SEPARATES TWO FAILURE MODES: report the DFT FORCES at that geometry
   (they come with the VASP single point at no extra cost).
     small forces + large Δ ⟹ the MLIP over-penalises the COMPOSITION   ← the structural-zero risk
     large forces           ⟹ the MLIP has the wrong GEOMETRY for this composition
   Without the forces these two are indistinguishable and would both be read as the first.
```

### (c) Revised V-2a′ spec — CONSOLIDATED, supersedes §39.21.4
```
V-2a′ — STRUCTURAL-ZERO PROBE
  purpose      is any plausible shell composition being ARTIFICIALLY EXCLUDED from the ensemble?
  construction LIGAND EXCHANGE (swap, not substitution) within a fixed neutral cell — C-1
               includes EC↔EMC, EC↔PF6⁻, EMC↔PF6⁻ (the last two are the CIP⇌SSIP probe)
  relaxation   MLIP-relaxed; both potentials single-pointed at that geometry — C-3
  frames       ~30 compositions + ~6 for the bulk-partner spread  ≈ 36
  box          158 atoms · L = 12.0 Å · 1 Li⁺ · 1 M   (unchanged)
  settings     ENCUT 520 · Li_sv · Γ-only · PBE ± the VALIDATED D3   (unchanged, now fully pinned)
  read-out     (Δ_MLIP − Δ_DFT) per composition · the bulk-partner spread · DFT FORCES
  finite-size  🔴 NO separate control frames — see (a). The bulk-partner spread carries it.
  gate         run the first 5, measure the residual scatter AND the cost, then commit
               🔴 and if those 5 fail, READ PLUMBING BEFORE PHYSICS (§39.22(b), U-74)
```

🔒 **Net for engineer5: ~30 → ~36 frames (+≈20 %), no separate larger-cell control, and one extra
output field (forces) that costs nothing.** Everything else in the 3,600 reserve stands.

## 39.25 🟢 A and B answered — CONSOLIDATED MLIP WORKFLOW, and what the static route now owes

> ```
> A  D3 was ON in the validated runs   ⟹ production inherits D3 ON, unchanged
> B  reduced species were NOT in the training set  ⟹ the EC⁻ boundary holds
> ```
> 🔒 Reliability is closed by the user and is not reopened anywhere below.

### (a) 🔴 ONE CORRECTION to how the boundary should be recorded — the lead's version is too strong in one half and too weak in the other

The lead asks that it be recorded so *"a future reader does not conclude the boundary is liftable by
retraining"*, on the grounds that the architecture rather than the data is the operative constraint.
**That is right for one of my two cases and wrong for the other, and the distinction is the whole
value of the record.**

```
CASE 1 — THE ELECTRON-TRANSFER EVENT ITSELF (EC → EC⁻ at fixed nuclear geometry)
  🔴 NOT LIFTABLE BY RETRAINING. EVER. Architectural: positions+species in, ONE energy out, so
     identical geometries cannot yield different energies. Adding reduced species makes it WORSE —
     the network sees two labels for near-identical inputs and learns an average.
  🟢 And we do not need it: S1 barriers are computed at our own level, never by the MLIP.

CASE 2 — THE EQUILIBRIUM SHELL OF AN ALREADY-FORMED REDUCED SPECIES
  🟡 IS, IN PRINCIPLE, LIFTABLE BY RETRAINING — with neutral Li⁺·EC⁻ pairs and SPIN-POLARISED
     labels — because EC⁻ is GEOMETRICALLY distinct (pyramidalised / ring-opened), so the model
     can learn "this geometry ⟹ this energy" implicitly without a charge channel.
  🔴 BUT WITH A SPECIFIC HAZARD, and this is the part worth recording:
     the model would learn a SINGLE-VALUED function of geometry through a region where the true
     surface is DOUBLE-VALUED (two electronic states). It would SMOOTH THE AVOIDED CROSSING.
     ⟹ tolerable FAR from the electron-transfer seam — which is where an equilibrium shell sits.
     ⟹ NOT tolerable near it — which is Case 1 again, arriving by a different route.
```
🔒 **So the honest record is neither "liftable" nor "permanent" but: Case 1 is permanent; Case 2 is
liftable far from the seam and not near it.** ⚠ And one guard in the other direction: *"architectural"*
is a statement about **this architecture**, not about MLIPs as a class — charge-conditioned and
charge-equilibration architectures exist. **A future reader should not conclude that no MLIP could
ever do this; only that this one cannot, and that more data for this one is the wrong lever.**

🟢 **Nothing downstream moves either way**, because §39.3 put the reduced half with the static route
before B was asked. **That is why a "no" closes cleanly instead of forcing a redesign** — and it is
the argument for choosing architectures before answers, not after.

### (a) 🔴 Q1 RULING — arm 1 uses `xtb --metadyn`. ETKDG+MMFF is withdrawn.

**The contradiction is real and it is mine.** §37.2.3 rules ETKDG *undefined* for Li⁺(EC)₃₋₅ — it is
a **non-covalent complex, not one covalent molecular graph** — and MMFF has **no Li parameters**.
§39.13(b) then specified exactly that method for exactly that class.
🔴 **And `02_METHOD_SPEC:4554` claimed "ASE, RDKit already vendored", which is FALSE against the
tree.** Corrected in place this round. **That false line is what made arm 1 look runnable**, and it
is the same failure as every other one this round: a claim in the document, unchecked against the
artefact.

🟢 **RULING: adopt §37.2.3 option (ii) — `xtb --metadyn` (MTD → opt → RMSD dedupe → Boltzmann).**
Its pre-registered activation condition was *"only if the CREST binary does not run on KNL"*; the
condition is now satisfied **in the stronger form — CREST does not exist to be run.** 🔒 This is a
pre-registered fallback firing, not a new choice made under pressure.

🟢 **And it is an upgrade, not a concession — say so in the write-up:**
> ETKDG+MMFF is a **covalent-organic-chemistry** toolchain with element-coverage limits; for an
> unstudied electrolyte carrying novel elements it may have **no parameters at all**. GFN2-xTB
> covers H–Rn. ⟹ **the substitution improves ADR-014 transferability**, independently of
> availability. The forced move is the better move.

**Protocol (coder6 may implement exactly this; do not vary it):**
```
1  MTD at GFN2-xTB with RMSD bias, per species, from the idealised structure
   🔴 A NON-COVALENT COMPLEX CAN DISSOCIATE UNDER MTD. Ligands can simply leave.
   ⟹ detect dissociated structures (any Li–ligand contact beyond the Layer-I cutoff) and
     🟢 COUNT THEM, DO NOT SILENTLY DISCARD. The dissociation rate is a DIRECT MEASUREMENT of
       how floppy the cluster is — which is B0-D's actual question. Report it as an output.
2  GFN2-xTB optimise every surviving snapshot
3  RMSD dedupe
4  keep all within ~0.3 eV at xTB (a WIDER window than DFT's, because xTB energies are worse),
   then cap at 10 per species by xTB energy
   🔴 REPORT how many were inside the window, so a truncation is visible rather than silent
5  DFT-optimise the survivors; THEN apply ADR-032(e)'s ±0.1 eV SVPD window + TZVPPD re-rank
```
🔴 **And one comparison rule, because arm 1 (an ensemble) and arm 2 (one structure) are not
like-for-like:**
```
arm1-BEST vs arm2       → "was the idealised guess bad?"   ← the §39.1(e-bis) question
arm1-ENSEMBLE vs arm1-BEST → "what does conformer search buy?"  ← R-4's question
🟢 Both fall out of the same runs at no extra cost. Report both; do not collapse them.
```

route work"*, not *"does ETKDG work"*.** 🟢 `arm1 ⊖ arm2` is unaffected.

     reactant  one-electron-reduced Li⁺(EC)₂
     product   ring-opened, second EC intact and still coordinated
     BREAK     O(ethereal) – C(ethereal) IN ONE OF THE TWO EC LIGANDS
     FORM      none
     🟢 Same chemistry as R-A at production size ⟹ gives U-56 a denominator AT REALISTIC SIZE,
       and simultaneously measures whether the SHELL CHANGES THE BARRIER (§39.25's
       shell-conditioning question) at zero extra cost.
```
🟢 **Why these three and not three unrelated reactions:** R-A vs R-B tests **selectivity** (P1's exact
failure mode); R-A vs R-C tests **size scaling**; and all three are the *same chemical family*, so a
failure is attributable to **the method** rather than to unfamiliar chemistry. **A bake-off across
three different chemistries could not distinguish those.**

🟢 **§39.13(a)#4 satisfied exactly**: R-C run under both methods = **2 of 6 attempts production-sized.**

🔴 **Coder constraint on the break/form list — the reason it is required:**
```
Ω is DEFINED as the projection of the imaginary mode onto the break/form list (§39.4(c)),
and the same list IS the relaxed-scan coordinate for the scan-based method.
⟹ WITHOUT IT, B0-F CAN MEASURE COST BUT CANNOT ANSWER "WHICH METHOD WORKS",
  and C-10 forbids a cost probe from rendering a chemical verdict.
🔴 The lists above are given by CHEMICAL ROLE, not atom index. The builder MUST emit the
   role→index mapping alongside each deck, and that mapping is what Ω is computed against.
```

## 39.27 🔴 R-C's reactant, the bound check, and the ε scan's scope — three rulings

### (a) 🔴 RULING (1) — option (a), but REFRAMED: B0-D has a stratification hole that exists independently of R-C

The lead is right that R-C's reactant (`Li⁺(EC)₂•⁻`, charge 0, **multiplicity 2**) is in neither
batch. **But the interesting part is why, and it is not about R-C.**

```
B0-D's 19 species are ALL CLOSED-SHELL SINGLETS.
🔴 AND HALF OF THE PRODUCTION POOL IS OPEN-SHELL — every reduced species in S1/S2 is a radical.
⟹ B0-D was specified to answer "how expensive and how convergent is this species class?"
   and it samples ONLY THE CLOSED-SHELL HALF OF IT.
```
🔴 **Open-shell SCF convergence is a distinct and well-known failure mode** — spin contamination,
symmetry-broken solutions, multiple SCF minima. ADR-029 recommends `stable=opt` for radical anions
**precisely because of it.** ⟹ **B0-D as written cannot see the failure mode most likely to bite
production**, and that is true whether or not R-C exists.

🟢 **⟹ The fix is not "bolt a species on for B0-F". It is "close the hole, which also supplies
B0-F."**

```
RULING — add an OPEN-SHELL STRATUM to B0-D: the one-electron-reduced counterparts of 4 members
  Li(EC)•          11 atoms   ← ALSO R-A's AND R-B's reactant
  Li(EC)₂•         21 atoms   ← ALSO R-C's reactant
  Li(EC)(EMC)•     26 atoms   ← mixed-ligand open shell
  Li(EC)(PF6)•     18 atoms   ← open shell WITH the anion present
  all charge 0, multiplicity 2.  B0-D: 19 → 23 species.
```
🟢 **This supplies the endpoints for ALL THREE B0-F reactions, not just R-C** — R-A and R-B's
reactant is `Li(EC)•`, whose only existing geometry is the idealised `li_ec_radical.xyz`, i.e.
**exactly the kind of guess that produced P1.** So all three needed conformer-searched open-shell
reactants regardless; R-C merely made it visible.

🟢 **And it dissolves the lead's option-(b) objection**: *"C-8 then applies to a geometry no arm
validated."* With the open-shell stratum, **arm 1 validates it** — MTD → opt → DFT opt+freq,
`n_imag = 0` — which is precisely what C-8 demands. Nothing special-cased.

🔴 **The contamination the lead warned about is real and is handled by REPORTING, not by exclusion:**
```
u_cheap MUST BE REPORTED SEPARATELY FOR THE CLOSED-SHELL AND OPEN-SHELL STRATA. Never pooled.
⟹ pooling would let the open-shell members distort a distribution they are not drawn from
  (the C-10 shape the lead correctly named)
🟢 AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE STRATA IS ITSELF A MEASUREMENT WE NEED:
  "does open-shell cost more, and does it converge worse?" — directly relevant to production,
  where half the pool is open-shell and NOTHING in the plan currently measures it.
```
**Arm 1 extends naturally** (`xtb --uhf 1` for the doublets). **Cost: +4 of 23 species, and
open-shell UKS runs ~2× closed-shell RKS ⟹ roughly +25–40 % on B0-D.** engineer5 to price; still
small in absolute terms and it buys a failure mode we could not otherwise see.

🔒 **Option (c) is refused for the reason the lead gave: dropping R-C costs the size-scaling axis,
which was one of the three stated reasons for the R-A/R-B/R-C family.**

### (b) 🟢 RULING (2) — CONFIRM coder6's extension, and BROADEN it. Do not narrow it.

coder6 derived `bound_check_required` from `charge < 0`, catching three species rather than my one
named. 🟢 **Confirmed — the lead's reasoning is right: applying a general rule generally is not an
extension.**

🔴 **But I am broadening it, because `charge < 0` is a PROXY and the PROPERTY is free to read.**
```
check that coder6 wrote     charge < 0
property actually wanted    "is the highest occupied orbital BOUND?"
🔴 A formal charge is not the criterion. The classic unbound case in OUR chemistry is a
   RADICAL ANION — and gas-phase EC has a negative adiabatic electron affinity, which is exactly
   why ADR-029 insists on diffuse functions and why gas-phase EA has no predictive power here.
   ⟹ once §39.27(a)'s open-shell stratum lands, we will have NEUTRAL species whose SOMO
     boundness is the live question, and `charge < 0` would skip every one of them.
```
🔒 **RULING: read and report the HOMO/SOMO energy for EVERY species, not only for `charge < 0`.**
It costs nothing — the orbital energies are already in every log — and it is the physical criterion
rather than a correlate of it.
🟢 **This is Rule 20 applied to a check I myself asked for**: coder6 substituted a proxy for a
property, the property is free, and I only noticed because the open-shell stratum made the proxy's
blind spot concrete. 🔒 **Keep coder6's `CODER EXTENSION, FLAGGED FOR CONFIRMATION` labelling
mechanism — it is what made this cheap to adjudicate, and the broadening is one config line.**

### (c) 🟢 RULING (3) — the ε scan rides on B0-F, and it is designed so that not knowing ε does not matter

**Scope: reactions, not species.** ε sensitivity is a property of a *reaction* — what matters is
whether `ΔG‡` and `ΔG` move with ε, and the sensitive cases are those that change charge separation
or localisation. A species-level scan would not answer the question.

```
RIDES ON B0-F. No separate tranche, no new cost line.
  set        R-A · R-B · R-C  (the three B0-F reactions)
  points     reactant · TS · product     — geometries ALREADY COMPUTED by B0-F
  ε values   3, 20, 90        (three single points each)
  total      3 reactions × 3 stationary points × 3 ε = 27 SINGLE POINTS at SP level
  🟢 essentially free — SPs are cheap and no new geometry is generated
```

🔴 **The design point that makes this worth doing FIRST — the bracket removes the dependence on the
unknown:**
```
ε ≈ 3    ≈ pure EMC        the low end
ε ≈ 20   ≈ the nominal mixture
ε ≈ 90   ≈ pure EC (at 40 °C)  the high end
🔴 THE TRUE MIXTURE VALUE MUST LIE BETWEEN THE TWO PURE COMPONENTS.
⟹ WE DO NOT NEED TO KNOW THE CORRECT MIXED ε IN ORDER TO BOUND THE ERROR OF NOT KNOWING IT.
⟹ IF ΔG‡ MOVES BY < 0.05 eV BETWEEN ε = 3 AND ε = 90, THEN NO DESCRIPTOR PRECISION MATTERS
  AT ALL AND §39.26(b) COLLAPSES ENTIRELY.
```
🔒 That is why this is ordered before sourcing descriptors, and it is ADR-018's principle used as an
**ordering** rule rather than an interpretive one.

**Two honest limits, stated so they are not discovered later:**
```
1  SP-only measures the ELECTROSTATIC response at FIXED GEOMETRY. Geometry relaxation in the
   reaction field is second-order, so a SMALL SP-level spread bounds the full response.
   🔴 A LARGE SP-level spread does NOT bound it — it only proves sensitivity.
   ⟹ TIERED: if the SP spread exceeds 0.05 eV, escalate to RE-OPTIMISATION on one reaction.
2  ε bounds the DOMINANT (electrostatic) term. It does NOT bound the CDS term, which is driven by
   the surface-tension descriptor. ⚠ Recorded as a residual, not opened as a new item: if the ε
   scan says the electrostatics are insensitive, the CDS term is the remaining question and is
   cheaply bracketed by two built-in solvents spanning the expected γ.
```
