## 39.38 🔴 THE USER'S TWO-STAGE PROTOCOL — ruling on rough→tight (proposer6, 2026-08-19)

> ADR-099 released B0 with: *"단분자 계산이 아니니까 rough한 계산으로 먼저 돌리고, 이 계산이 끝난 이후
> tight한 조건에서 opt+freq 계산을 하는게 좋겠어."* Answering the lead's three questions and nothing
> else. 🔒 **I did not re-cut the method to fit the staging** — the ruling below happens to be
> compatible, and where it is not I say so in (d).

### (a) VERDICT ON THE LEAD'S THREE POINTS — all three CONFIRMED, one mechanism corrected

```
1  nosymm + the C-9 perturbation belong to the ROUGH stage, perturbation BEFORE stage 1   ✅ CONFIRM
2  a new `endpoint_opt_rough` job_type, BOTH stages in _nosymm_required_job_types          ✅ CONFIRM
3  the F1 emit-list must ALSO fire at stage-1 exit                                          ✅ CONFIRM
                                                                                    — and it is FREE, see (c)
```
**🔴 But the stated mechanism needs one correction, because it matters for how hard to push.** The
lead wrote that a symmetric stage 1 makes stage 2 *"certify the wrong structure with every log
saying converged."* **That is true only if `nosymm` is missing from BOTH stages.** If stage 2 carries
`nosymm` + `CalcFC` + an honest `freq`, a structure sitting on the element yields `n_imag ≥ 1`, the
mode-following restart fires, and C-8.3 blocks certification. ⟹ **the freq gate still holds; what a
symmetric stage 1 costs is RESTARTS AT TIGHT PRICE, not correctness.**

🔒 **Which is an argument FOR the lead's ruling, not against it, and I want the real reason on
record rather than the alarming one:**
```
· the failure is fully silent ONLY if nosymm is forgotten TWICE — and stage 1 is far the easier
  one to forget, because "it's only a rough opt" is exactly the sentence that omits it.
· doing the perturbation late throws away stage 1's work: you displace a converged geometry and
  re-do stage 1 inside stage 2 at TIGHT thresholds. The perturbation is cheapest to relax when it
  is applied before the cheap stage.
· 🔴 G16 re-imposes the point group within its own tolerance (B-2). Without `nosymm` on stage 1,
  the perturbation is UNDONE AT STEP 1 and stage 2 inherits the pristine symmetric structure — so
  the perturbation must be applied before stage 1 AND protected there, or it may as well not exist.
```
🟢 **A loose stage 1 does NOT pull the perturbation back out.** If the symmetric point is a saddle,
forces point away from it; if forces fall below the loose threshold the optimiser simply stops and
**the displacement remains in the geometry.** (If it *is* a minimum along that mode, returning is
the correct answer.) ⟹ my §39.32(e) arithmetic is unaffected by staging: the kick does its work at
**stage 2**, where `Opt=Tight` makes 0.25 Å amply sufficient (ν ≳ 30 cm⁻¹, ≳ 70 with the
delocalisation factor). **Stage 1 only has to not destroy it.**

🔴 **One addition of my own: the perturbation is applied ONCE, before stage 1, and is NOT re-applied
between the stages.** Re-kicking a converged geometry displaces it off a real minimum and buys
nothing. If stage-1 exit is still on the element, the correct response is stage 2's CalcFC imaginary
eigenvector — **a measured direction, strictly better than a random kick** (§39.32's restart rule).

### (b) 🔴 WHAT "ROUGH" IS — same functional, same basis, same solvent, SAME GRID. Only the thresholds move.

**The lead asked whether my Q1 argument binds here. It does not, and the distinction is exact:**
```
STAGE 1 PRODUCES A STARTING GEOMETRY.   A guess carries NO claim. A better guess is cheaper; a
                                        worse one is dearer. There is nothing to be valid ABOUT.
STAGE 2 PRODUCES A CERTIFICATE.         `n_imag == 0` is a property OF A SURFACE — so the
                                        certification must be on the TS-search surface. (Q1)
⟹ the "certified on the wrong surface" error is the error of TRANSFERRING A CLAIM across surfaces.
  Stage 1 transfers no claim, so a cheaper rough level does NOT commit that error.
```
**🔴 BUT A CHEAPER ROUGH LEVEL COMMITS A DIFFERENT ONE, AND IT IS SILENT — and it happens to be
worst for exactly the species B0 is made of.** A cheaper surface can have a different basin
ordering. Stage 1 then *selects* a basin that the tight surface would not have chosen, stage 2
optimises honestly inside it, and `n_imag == 0` is **true**. ⟹ **the certificate is honest and the
minimum is the wrong one.** Not a certification error — a **sampling** error, and no internal check
can see it, because nothing is inconsistent.

```
🔴 THE CLASS THIS BREAKS IS OURS. Li+-coordinated complexes have near-degenerate coordination
   isomers and conformers separated by less than the error of any cheap surface. That is the
   whole content of U-55, and it is why the user's own reason for staging ("이건 단분자 계산이
   아니니까") identifies precisely the species for which a CHEAP rough stage is least safe.
```

**⟹ RULING:**
```
ROUGH = SAME functional · SAME basis · SAME solvent (SMD generic EC:EMC) · SAME integration grid
        Only the CONVERGENCE THRESHOLDS differ.
🔴 THE GRID IS PART OF THE LEVEL. A coarser grid is a DIFFERENT SURFACE and reintroduces the basin
   error through a door nobody watches. `Int(Grid=UltraFine)` in BOTH stages, stated explicitly.

STAGE 1   #p nosymm {func}/{basis} {solv} opt=(loose,maxcycles=100) Int(Grid=UltraFine)
          🔴 NO CalcFC (empirical Hessian is right here) · NO freq
STAGE 2   #p nosymm {func}/{basis} {solv} opt=(tight,calcfc,maxcycles=200) freq Int(Grid=UltraFine)
          starts from stage 1's converged geometry; `opt … freq` in ONE route so the Hessian is
          taken at the geometry the opt converged to, with no drift and no level mismatch
⚠ Gaussian's numeric `Opt=Loose` thresholds are [UNVERIFIED] by me. They do not affect this ruling.
  🔒 Do NOT copy them from documentation — G16 PRINTS the active criteria in the log; record them
  from the log into the route provenance. (Same discipline as §0-e: go to the artefact.)
```
🟢 **AND THE PROTOCOL IS BETTER THAN WHAT I ORIGINALLY SPECIFIED, for a physical reason, not a cost
one.** I pre-registered against myself (§39.34(e)) that **`CalcFC` on a hand-drawn guess yields an
initial Hessian with tiny or negative eigenvalues and erratic first steps.** Two-stage removes that
exact defect: the one analytic Hessian is now taken at a **loose-converged** geometry instead of at
`GUESS GEOMETRY (idealized, not optimized)`. 🔒 **The user's instinct corrects a weakness I had
flagged in my own recommendation and could not remove without this staging.** That is the ruling's
main scientific justification; the cost saving is a second, independent benefit.

**Second independent benefit — it interacts with the ratified budget rule (§39.34).** Stage 1's
converged geometry is a **checkpoint**: if stage 2 is killed by the cumulative budget, work restarts
from stage 1 rather than from the guess. Under a cumulative budget that is the difference between a
partial result and none.

### (c) 🟢 THE FREQ BELONGS ONLY AT STAGE 2 — and the stage-1 Hessian you were worried about is already paid

Confirmed: no `freq` at stage 1. An analytic Hessian is the expensive item and stage 1's geometry is
not final. **But nothing is lost, because of an identity worth stating plainly:**

```
🔒 STAGE 2's `CalcFC` IS A HESSIAN AT STAGE 1's EXIT GEOMETRY. It is computed at step 1 of stage 2,
   before anything moves. ⟹ WE ALREADY HAVE n_imag AT STAGE-1 EXIT, FOR FREE, IN EVERY RUN.
   The question "should we freq at stage 1" is therefore moot — we do, and the only thing that was
   missing is that nobody EMITS it.
```
⟹ F1's `n_imag_at_guess` is re-scoped to **`n_imag` at the geometry ENTERING stage 2** (= stage-1
exit), which is the more informative quantity and costs nothing. The `config/f1_required_observables.json`
entry is updated accordingly. **This is the cheapest possible detector of the lead's failure mode:**
if stage 1 stayed on the element, stage 2's CalcFC says so at step 1, before a single tight cycle is
spent. Together with the point group and ∠Li–O=C at stage-1 exit (free, geometric), the lead's
point 3 is fully discharged **at zero compute**.

### (d) 🔴 WHERE TWO-STAGE WOULD BE SCIENTIFICALLY WRONG — asked for, and the honest answer is narrow

```
SAME-LEVEL rough (ruled above)   ⟹ 🟢 NOT wrong for ANY species class. It is one optimisation with
   an intermediate stop on ONE surface. Worst case it is cost-neutral (a few extra cycles); it
   cannot select a wrong basin, because there is only one basin structure in play.
CHEAPER-LEVEL rough              ⟹ 🔴 WRONG FOR EXACTLY B0's CLASS — Li+-coordinated multi-molecular
   complexes with near-degenerate coordination isomers. It silently selects the isomer, and the
   resulting certificate is honest about the wrong minimum. If it is ever adopted for cost reasons
   it must carry (i) F1's EXTERNAL structural checks (∠Li–O=C toward ≈138°, ring bonds separating)
   and (ii) a stage-1→stage-2 IDENTITY check (heavy-atom RMSD + connectivity), and even then it is
   a managed risk, not a free saving.
SEMI-EMPIRICAL rough (GFN2)      ⟹ 🔴 NOT for endpoints. §0-g measured that a GFN2 `--opt tight`
   moves every distance and does not break the degeneracy, and GFN2's basin ordering for Li+
   complexes is the specific thing U-55 says we do not trust. GFN2/CREST keeps its existing job —
   CONFORMER GENERATION, applied symmetrically to both endpoints (§39.32(c)) — and its output is
   still never an endpoint.
```

### (e) What this does not change, and the falsifier

Unchanged: C-8.1–8.3 (certification at the TS-search level, analytic freq, every negative counted);
the seven U-56 conditions (§39.32(g)); the cumulative-budget and wall-clock rulings (§39.34), which
now span **both** stages — budget is cumulative per endpoint across stage 1 + stage 2 + all restarts;
F1's binding emit-list.

## 39.39 🔴 U-56 REDEFINED — a RATE was the wrong instrument for a GATE (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use in this section**: `U-56` = the open unknown *"transition state (TS)
> search success rate is unmeasured"*. `B0` = the gate batch; `B0-D` = its solvation-cost arm;
> `B0-F` = its TS-method bake-off arm. `B1` = the first production batch. `S3` = the pipeline stage
> that computes pathway + barrier per reaction. `C-2/C-5/C-8/C-10/C-11` = coder constraints
> (glossary §4). `IRC` = intrinsic reaction coordinate. `PCM` = polarisable continuum model.
> `ADR-NNN` = architecture decision record in `01_DECISION_LOG.md`.
> **Binding facts I did not choose and did not re-open**: 🔒 P1 (the plan item) is permanently out
> by user ruling (`05_STATE.md` §0-p, `plan.py` C-8-2 cancellation record). Nothing below revives it,
> depends on it, or reads on it.

### (a) The answer in six lines

```
DEFECT      U-56 fuses a GATE question with a SIZING question into one scalar. The gate needs an
            EXISTENCE PROOF (n = 1); the sizing needs a RATE (n >> 1). One symbol, two estimands —
            structurally the same fusion C-10.1 fixed for cost probes (§39.33(c)).
SPLIT       U-56a  binary FEASIBILITY: has ONE TS search met every condition, end to end?
            U-56b  the per-attempt SUCCESS FRACTION and COST DISTRIBUTION. A planning input.
GATE        The S3 production block hangs on U-56a ONLY. U-56b is measured DURING S3 wave 1.
            🔴 As currently worded the gate is UNACHIEVABLE — see (c)-2. Nobody decided that;
            it is what the words say once you do the binomial arithmetic.
MINIMUM     one certified reactant endpoint (ALREADY IN FLIGHT) + ONE single-ended TS attempt on
            R-A. No product endpoint. No QST2. No P1. Details in (e).
CONDITIONS  §39.32(g)'s seven become EIGHT, and condition 3 is SUPERSEDED BY ADR-108 — as written,
            a compliant B0-F run FAILS ITS OWN CONDITION by construction. See (b).
```

### (b) 🔴 BEFORE ANY OPTION — §39.32(g) condition 3 is stale, and it would have voided the attempt silently

`§39.32(g)-3` reads *"solvent = generic/EC:EMC (C-5)"*, i.e. SMD with EC:EMC descriptors. **ADR-108 ①
moved B0 to PCM with numeric ε = 18.5**, because SMD-generic was unexecutable at all (seven Abraham /
surface-tension descriptors nobody has, §39.26(b)). ⟹ **every run that obeys ADR-108 violates
§39.32(g)-3, and a run that violates a U-56 condition counts in NEITHER direction.** That is P1's
failure repeated one level up — in the rule instead of in the run — and it would have been discovered
after the compute was spent.

```
CONDITION 3, AMENDED (this is a re-statement of its REASON, not a weakening):
  the continuum must carry ε ≈ 18.5, i.e. B1's measured EC:EMC value (ADR-104), by ANY
  implementation ADR-108 sanctions. It must NOT be acetonitrile (ε 35.7).
  🔒 The original reason — "35.7 vs ~18-20 is a factor of two on the reaction field for a
  charge-localising ion-pair reaction" — is UNCHANGED and is what condition 3 was always about.
  The SMD-vs-PCM identity was incidental to it and is now decided elsewhere (ADR-108).

CONDITION 8, NEW — the deck must be verified as APPLIED, not merely accepted:
  `deck_verification.json` must show G16's OWN SCRF block reporting ε, not an echo of our input.
  🔴 ADR-108's reading rule was written for COST, where a silently-ignored deck yields a
  low-biased number. FOR CHEMISTRY THE SAME EVENT IS WORSE AND OF A DIFFERENT KIND: an ignored
  `scrf=(pcm,read)` means the job ran effectively GAS-PHASE, and a gas-phase barrier for a
  charge-localising ion pair is not a barrier with an error bar — it is a different quantity.
  ⚠ `criteria/g16.py::parse_scrf_dielectric` matches `eps=` ANYWHERE in the text, so the parser
  cannot make this distinction; a human reads the raw-context field. That is why this is a
  CONDITION and not a test.
🔒 ADR-108 opened the deck gate DELIBERATELY for a cost round. A chemistry round does not inherit
  that permission. Opening a gate and verifying a thing are different acts (ADR-108's own words).
```

### (c) Why the gate cannot be a rate — two independent arguments

**1. A rate has no reference population here, BY DESIGN.** §39.26(d) chose R-A/R-B/R-C to be *one
chemical family* precisely so that a failure is attributable to the method rather than to unfamiliar
chemistry. 🔒 That design is correct for a bake-off **and it is exactly what makes the resulting
fraction non-transferable to S3's target set** — a purposive sample cannot estimate a population
rate. This is the same argument §39.5(b) uses to protect B1-A as the unbiasedness anchor, applied
to ourselves.

**2. The arithmetic — 6 attempts cannot deliver a usable rate even if all 6 succeed.**
```
6 successes of 6   exact one-sided 95 % lower bound on p = 0.05^(1/6) = 0.607   [ESTIMATE, standard
4 successes of 6   exact 95 % interval on p ≈ [0.22, 0.96]                       Clopper-Pearson]
S3 sizing consumes 1/p  ⟹  the cost multiplier is uncertain by 1.6x at BEST and ~4.4x at 4/6.
```
⟹ **B0-F was never able to close U-56-as-a-rate.** Gating S3 on a quantity B0 cannot produce is a
permanent block by arithmetic. 🔴 **And note the direction of the error I am correcting: I am making
the gate EASIER TO SATISFY, which is the direction this project has been wrong in before (§0-h).
So the burden is on me, and (b)'s two conditions are the price — the gate gets strictly stricter
per attempt while requiring fewer attempts.** Nothing currently forbidden becomes permitted except
the specific act of starting S3 wave 1 on n = 1, which (d)-U56-3 then bounds.

**What B0-F CAN deliver, and it is what S3 actually consumes**: existence (U-56a), a *cost*
distribution per attempt (which drives S3's budget far more than p does — engineer's R-04 spread is
8×), and a method ranking if the difference is large.

## 39.40 🔴 METADYNAMICS (MTD) FOR S2 REACTION DISCOVERY — VERDICT: ADOPT, as an `engine-E3b` UPGRADE, with one free pre-check that can kill it (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use in this section**: `MTD` = metadynamics. `S2` = the pipeline stage that
> discovers products / builds the reaction network. `GFN2-xTB` = Grimme's semiempirical tight-binding
> method (the `xtb` binary, vendored, version 6.7.1 verified by execution). `MD` = molecular
> dynamics. `NVT` = constant particle-number / volume / temperature ensemble. `RMSD` = root-mean-
> square deviation. `CV` = collective variable. `capture–recapture` = the multi-source completeness
> estimator of ADR-015/019.
> 🔴 **NOTATION COLLISION (glossary §0)**: `E1/E2/E3` means TWO different things in this project.
> Everything below uses **`engine-E1/E2/E3a/E3b`** (ADR-019's discovery engines). The blind
> rediscovery test is **`test-E1`** (ADR-015's transferability tests) and is a different object.

### (a) The verdict in six lines

```
SCIENCE       SOUND, as a DISCOVERY engine. This is the published use of the tool, not a
              repurposing — Grimme, JCTC 2019, 15, 2847-2862 (doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00143) applies
              RMSD-biased GFN2 MTD to conformer search, NANOREACTOR reaction-space exploration, and
              reaction-path guessing IN ONE PAPER. [LITERATURE — title/venue/DOI verified 2026-08-20;
              I have NOT read the primary text, only the abstract and the CREST documentation.]
POSITION      `engine-E3b` upgrade. NOT a replacement for `engine-E2`. (b)
LEAD'S CALL   correct on every point I could check, with TWO refinements — the capture–recapture
              damage is smaller than stated, and the hyperparameter gap is larger. (b), (c)
BLOCKER       🔴 conformer-scale bias hyperparameters CANNOT find reactions. The published
              nanoreactor setting is ~19x our kpush and adds a confining wall we do not have. (c)
PRE-CHECK     one FREE GFN2 scan decides whether the arm can work at all, before any pilot. (d)
RATE BAN      unchanged and now enforceable in code: MTD supplies DISCOVERY EVENTS ONLY. (f)
```

### (b) Position in the engine table — confirming the lead, with two refinements

ADR-019's independence table is exactly as the lead quoted: `engine-E2` = GFN2 energy + **graph-edit,
deterministic** search; `engine-E3b` = GFN2 energy + **stochastic MD** search. An RMSD-biased MD is a
stochastic MD. ⟹ **MTD sits in `engine-E3b`'s seat, and replacing `engine-E2` with it would delete
the project's only deterministic enumerator** — the engine whose *support* is statable, which is what
§18.2 rests layer-I unbiasedness on. **Confirmed, and for a stronger reason than independence: a
stochastic engine has no support statement at all.**

**🟢 REFINEMENT 1 — the capture–recapture damage is SMALLER than the lead's message implies, and the
reason is already in this document.** §18.5 already merges `S₂ = engine-E2 ∪ engine-E3b` into ONE
capture source precisely because they share the GFN2 Hamiltonian. ⟹ upgrading `engine-E3b` does not
touch the three-source estimator's structure at all; it **raises S₂'s recall**, which is a gain, not a
risk. Nothing about ADR-019's independence needs re-deciding.

**🟡 REFINEMENT 2 — what it DOES disturb is §18.5's free odds-ratio diagnostic, and the fix is a
field, not an arm.** `OR(engine-E3b)` vs `OR(engine-E3a)` measures the shared-Hamiltonian correlation
*of the engine actually in use*. Change the search operator and the quantity is still well defined —
it is simply about the new engine. ⟹ **no plain-MD baseline arm is needed.** What IS needed is
`engine_variant` on every ledger row (`e3b_plain` / `e3b_mtd`), so the odds ratio is computed per
variant and a mixed pool is never averaged into one number. 🔒 Zero compute; a column.

### (c) 🔴 THE ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE THIS FAIL SILENTLY — conformer-scale bias cannot open a ring

```
OURS (B0-D arm 1, config/b0_conformers.json)   kpush 0.05 · alp 0.8 · 400 K · no wall · 5-20 ps
                                               🔒 labelled CODER-CHOSEN AND UNTUNED, and it is a
                                               CONFORMER setting — that is its job.
PUBLISHED NANOREACTOR (CREST docs, rcontrol)   kpush 0.96 Eh · alp 1.0 bohr^-2 · logfermi wall,
                                               spherical cavity from a target density, wall
                                               temperature 6000 K
                                               [LITERATURE — read from crest-lab.github.io
                                               crest-docs utils_6, 2026-08-20]
GAP                                            ~19x in kpush, PLUS a confinement term we have
                                               nothing equivalent to.
```
**Why the wall is not optional, stated as physics rather than as a recipe.** The bias rewards
*distance from previously visited structures in Cartesian RMSD after optimal alignment*. For a
multi-fragment assembly, **the cheapest way to increase that distance is to translate a fragment
away** — it costs one bond-dissociation energy and then buys unlimited RMSD for free, whereas a ring
opening costs a barrier and buys a bounded RMSD. ⟹ **without confinement, an RMSD-biased MD on
Li⁺(EC)ₙ is a ligand-stripping machine.** 🟢 This is not a prediction: §39.26(a) warned it, and the
project has already MEASURED the phenomenon at conformer-scale bias (`dissociation` classes in
`b0_conformers.json`, with `ligand_dissociated` and `ligand_fragmented` deliberately kept in separate
buckets).

**⟹ SPEC CONSEQUENCE (three items, and the third is the one that gets skipped):**
```
1  reaction-scale (kpush, alp) — start from the published nanoreactor pair, run >= 2 pairs
   (§39.28(b) CHANGE 1 applies unchanged: one pair explores ONE characteristic length scale).
2  a `$wall` logfermi confinement, radius set from a TARGET DENSITY, reported per run.
   🟢 **VERIFIED BY EXECUTION 2026-08-20 (lead, ADR-109)**: vendored xtb 6.7.1, `$wall` logfermi
   alone rc=0 and prints `spherical wallpotential with radius 4.36 Å`; `$metadyn` + `$wall`
   together rc=0, kpush echoed, normal termination. [MEASURED, dev box] ⚠ **dev box, not the
   cluster** — the cluster re-check rides on the next submission's smoke. My original demand
   (verify by execution, never from memory — RT-1, and b0_conformers.json's `_version_note`
   discipline) is DISCHARGED for the binary and OPEN for the machine.
3  🔴 classification on QUENCHED structures ONLY. A molecular-graph comparison on RAW MD FRAMES is
   wrong and the project has the counter-example in hand: a real trajectory frame reaches
   Li-O = 2.688 A, past the 2.4 A contact cutoff, in an OTHERWISE INTACT complex
   [MEASURED, b0_conformers.json::optimisation]. ⟹ MTD frame → GFN2 opt → graph → compare.
```
**🟢 On PLUMED — I disagree with adding it, and the disagreement is cheap to act on.** A true
bond-distance CV would be scientifically nicer, but xtb 6.7.1 carries native `$metadyn` + `$wall`,
both already inside the air gap, and RMSD-bias-plus-wall is the *published* configuration for exactly
this task. Adding PLUMED buys a better CV and pays with a new-tool availability risk on a machine
where **CREST turned out not to exist at all** (§39.26(a)). 🔒 **Skip PLUMED. Revisit only if (e)'s
pilot fails for a reason attributable to the CV, which is a diagnosable outcome, not a guess.**

**Before asking a GFN2 MTD to *discover* EC⁻ ring opening, measure whether GFN2 has a ring-opening
path at accessible cost at all.** If GFN2's barrier for R-A's coordinate is far outside the window a
bias can reach in the run length we can afford, **no hyperparameter choice will ever find it, and the
pilot's failure would be misread as "MTD does not work for us."**

COST       minutes on one core. The 5 ps MTD on 11 atoms took 74 s wall on 12 threads = 0.25 core-h

                                                property of GFN2, which is a transferability fact

🔒 SAME SHAPE AS ADR-067 for the fifth time: check the input — here, the ENGINE's own surface —

   sections and it gates the more expensive one.
⚠ GFN2's open-shell treatment is not a UKS calculation (b0_conformers.json::_gfn2_open_shell_caveat)

              T3  C2H4 elimination from a ring-opened intermediate

              [LITERATURE, SEARCH-LEVEL — both channels are reported for reduced EC; the project's

GRADING       RECALL over the sealed target list. 🟢 False positives are NOT penalised — §14.3

              positive costs one cheap classification.

              ADR-024 temperature ladder), NOT against unbiased MD at 400 K. Unbiased MD at 400 K
              will find nothing in 20 ps for a ~0.5 eV barrier, and beating it proves nothing.
              A comparison rigged in the new method's favour is worse than no comparison.
SEEDS         >= 3 independent seeds per configuration. ADR-051's D1 (seed-split capture-recapture)
              needs independent seeds BY DESIGN, and §39.23's condition applies here too.
🔴 STAGE 0    **ADDED 2026-08-20, §39.42(d), AND IT RUNS FIRST**: the COMPARATOR ALONE (unbiased
              NVT at the ladder's TOP rung, >= 3 seeds, ~10 core-h). A 1-seed 5 ps run at 1500 K
              opened the ring in UNDER 1 ps for ~2 core-h [MEASURED]. If stage 0 recovers T1-T4,
              **the pilot is not funded on this system** and any MTD case must be re-registered
              for a different reaction class. F13 is LIVE.
ADOPT IF      T1 recovered in >= 2 of 3 seeds AND total recall >= T1+T2 at matched compute.
REJECT IF     T1 not recovered in >= 2 of 3 seeds. 🔴 Pre-registered as a REJECTION, not as a
              prompt to retune — the retune-until-it-works loop is how a discovery engine's recall
              becomes unmeasurable.

              **INDETERMINATE, never REJECT** — a compute-capped run that never had a chance is a

              his §R39.13; see §39.44(b)), **and the run LENGTH is whatever C buys.** Length is a

### (f) Ledger, discipline, and the rule that stops an MTD number becoming a rate

```
LEDGER (ADR-027's append-only discovery ledger; fields already are: species|reaction, engine,
        round, discovery temperature, time, initial-condition hash)
  ADD  engine_variant           `e3b_mtd` vs `e3b_plain`   (§(b) refinement 2)
  ADD  bias_active              boolean
  FOLD INTO initial_condition_hash:  kpush, alp, wall type + radius, MD length, dump interval,
        thermostat, seed, and the hash of the PRE-OPTIMISED start structure.
        🔒 A bias hyperparameter is part of the initial condition. If it is not in the hash, two
        runs that explored different chemistry look identical in the ledger and capture-recapture
        counts them as one source.
  KEEP two temperature fields   temperature_requested_k / temperature_measured_k. Never one.
        [MEASURED: 564 K vs a 400 K setpoint under bias, from the SAME optimised geometry that
        holds 395 K unbiased.]

🔴 THE RATE BAN, made enforceable rather than remembered:
  any consumer that computes a rate, a branching ratio, a Boltzmann weight or a mean lifetime
  MUST REFUSE a record with `bias_active == true`. Same shape as the `deck_verified` gate in
  ADR-108's addendum — a rule with no mechanism becomes a rule with an exception.
  🔒 Reason, unchanged from §39.29: an MTD trajectory has no defined temperature, the excess is
  intrinsic to the bias, and it CANNOT be removed by fixing the thermostat or the input.

🔴 AND THE ENDPOINT RULE, which is where the money actually is:
  an MTD discovery yields a pair of GFN2 minima. §39.38(d) already rules that GFN2 minima are
  NOT endpoints — they enter the DFT two-stage certification like any other guess.
  ⟹ EVERY promoted discovery costs 2 endpoint certifications + 1 TS attempt downstream.
  🟢 The discovery is cheap and the CONSEQUENCE of a discovery is not. That, not the MTD cost,
  is what the pruning rule has to control, and it is why the ledger/work-network split (ADR-027)
  is what makes this affordable: discover without limit, PROMOTE under a budget.
```

named the wrong item, which is the failure mode this project keeps recording: a correct intuition
attached to the nearest available token.** §39.39(g) is corrected in place.

### (c) Correction 2 accepted — quench trigger APPROVED, with a sharpening that removes its measured failure mode

engineer7 is right on both the number and the principle. **His distinction is valid and I want it on
record in my own words, because it is the kind of distinction that gets collapsed later:**
§39.40(c)-3 forbids **classifying** on raw frames. Using a raw-frame graph change as a **trigger for
whether to spend a quench** is a different act: its only failure mode is a **false negative** (a real
event missed), and the 5 ps backstop bounds the loss. Every classification still happens on a
quenched structure. **Approved.**

**🔴 The sharpening, and it comes from a measurement this project already owns.** §39.40(c)-3's
warning was derived from a *coordination* observation: a real frame reached Li–O = 2.688 Å past the
2.4 Å contact cutoff **in an otherwise intact complex** [MEASURED, b0_conformers.json]. That is the
floppiest coordinate in the system and it is exactly what a naive graph trigger would fire on.
```
⟹ THE TRIGGER USES COVALENT BONDS ONLY. No Li-coordination edges, no contact cutoffs.
   The measured false-positive channel is then excluded BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by tuning,
   and a C-O bond change is far less prone to transient excursions than a Li-O contact.
⟹ REQUIRED READ-OUT (free): report quenches by ORIGIN — trigger-fired vs backstop-fired — and how
   many NEW graphs each origin found. 🔴 If backstop-fired quenches keep finding new graphs, the
   trigger is too coarse and the false-negative rate is not bounded by argument any more. That is
   a MEASUREMENT of the trigger, not a hope about it.
⟹ the trigger threshold and the backstop interval JOIN the initial-condition hash (§39.40(f)).
   They change what is discovered, so they are part of the initial condition.
```

**Decision: drop T21-se from U56-2 this round. Keep E21. U56-2 becomes R-A × {double-ended,
single-ended} + R-B × single-ended = 3 attempts, all 11-atom, plus 2 endpoint certifications at
11 atoms and 1 at 21 atoms.** Exactly the pre-registered cut shape (§39.39(d)): a cut, not a re-plan.

**Why the obvious justification is NOT good enough, and I am refusing it**: one could argue that
E21 measures the per-sub-job unit at 21 atoms and a TS attempt is a known number of sub-jobs, so
T21-se's cost is recoverable by arithmetic. 🔒 **That argument is mine from §39.33(b) and it fails
here for the reason I gave there**: `cost = N_cycles × cost_per_cycle`, and E21 transfers only
`cost_per_cycle`. **`N_cycles` for a TS search is set by the chemistry and does not transfer.**
⟹ dropping T21-se leaves the production-size cycle count UNMEASURED, and I will not pretend
otherwise.

**The reason I take the cut anyway** is that the measurement is not lost, it is **relocated to where
it is already paid for and has a decision attached**:

  therefore contains production-sized attempts BY CONSTRUCTION, budgeted, with a stopping rule

· in B0-F the same attempt buys one number and no decision. In wave 1 it buys the same number AND
  feeds the futility rule.
· U-56a — the gate — hangs on R-A at 11 atoms and is untouched. F10's branch is untouched.
· E21 survives on FOUR independent justifications, none of which is T21-se: the §39.40(e) MTD
  pilot's start structure, B0-D's open-shell stratum, the 21-atom cost-per-cycle unit, and U-55's
  production-size convergence test.
```
**What is lost, stated so the lead and the user can judge it rather than me**: §39.13(a)#4's
production-sized attempt count goes 1 → 0 *in B0*, and U-56b gets no 21-atom point *in B0*. Both
return in wave 1. 🔴 **If wave 1 is deferred or cut, this cut becomes a real deletion and must be
re-argued, not inherited.**

*"the scan coordinate is not the reaction coordinate — then the scan returns a saddle whose IRC does
not connect the intended pair"* as the breaking condition, and P-3's *"we do not know whether ring
opening is concerted with Li⁺ migration"* as the open question. **It is no longer open at GFN2, and
the answer is the unfavourable one.**

   distinction -- and the DFT freq + IRC are what certify). R-C's is a guess taken AT A

   OPPOSITE ways: the single-ended scan needs a SECOND coordinate; the double-ended synchronous
   interpolation degrades exactly when the endpoints differ by a bond change PLUS a cation

   §39.0 as "low urgency". THAT LABEL IS NOW WRONG. A string method lets both coordinates move and
   is the standard remedy for exactly this. I am not adopting it -- I am RE-CLASSIFYING it from
   "nice to have" to "the production-size case currently has no demonstrated method", which is a
   different sentence and belongs in front of the user.
3  🟢 CHEAP MITIGATION IF SINGLE-ENDED IS KEPT AT PRODUCTION SIZE: a 2-D relaxed scan over
   (d(O2-C3), d(Li-O2)). It is N_scan^2, so it is only affordable at GFN2 -- which is exactly
   where it should be run, because it is a GUESS GENERATOR. [ESTIMATE: minutes.]
4  ⚠ WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that the DFT surface is concerted the same way. GFN2 is a
   semiempirical method with a non-UKS open-shell treatment, and the two abrupt steps may partly

## 39.42 🔴 THREE ANSWERS AND ONE MEASUREMENT THAT INVERTS THE MTD PILOT (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers `coder10`'s two chemistry questions (relayed by the lead) and `engineer7`'s §R39.13.
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `MTD` = metadynamics; `NVT` = constant particle-number /
> volume / temperature ensemble; `T1…T4` = §39.40(e)'s sealed rediscovery targets;
> `E21` = the 21-atom endpoint certification for R-C's reactant; `⟨S²⟩` = the spin-squared
> expectation value. New artefacts: `data/gfn2_pes_precheck_20260820/{10_seed_basins,11_md1500}/`.
> All measurements below: **GFN2-xTB, vendored 6.7.1, dev box, 0 cluster core-h.**

### (a) coder10 Q1 — the R-C reactant seed: **APPROVED, with one change and two required emissions**

**The question is sharper than "is this structure good enough", and the sharp version has a
measured answer.** §39.38(d) says a GFN2 structure is *never an endpoint*. It is not being used as
one: it is the **starting geometry** for the DFT two-stage certification, and a starting geometry
carries no claim (§39.38(b)). 🔴 **But §39.38(d)'s real objection survives that distinction** — a
cheap surface *selects a basin*, stage 2 then certifies honestly inside it, and the certificate is
true about the wrong minimum. **So the question is: how basin-hostage is this particular start?**

**I measured it instead of arguing it.** Six kick seeds (±0.25 Å in z, GFN2 `--opt tight`, 21 atoms,
reduced Li⁺(EC)₂, charge 0 / uhf 1), `10_seed_basins/`:
```
5 of 6 seeds  ->  E = -41.683700 +- 0.000002 Eh   THE SAME BASIN. The 20260820 draw is NOT lucky.
1 of 6 (s2)   ->  +0.686 eV, Li-O(EC#2 ethereal) 1.693 vs 1.753   a DIFFERENT, HIGHER structure
⟹ a SINGLE-SEED protocol fails roughly 1 time in 6 at this size [MEASURED, n=6 -- the rate is
  poorly determined, the EXISTENCE of the failure is not].
```
```
🟢 RULING: use the kicked GFN2 structure as the DFT start — APPROVED. It is reproducible, it is a
   GFN2 minimum (n_imag = 0), and the alternative (the idealised guess) is MEASURED to be worse:
   §39.40(d)-RESULT found the un-kicked optimisation of that same file sitting 0.835 eV high with
   FIVE imaginary modes. 🔒 There is no basin-free option here; a human's drawing selects a basin
   too, and worse-motivated than GFN2's.
🔴 CHANGE: NOT ONE SEED. Generate >= 3 (cheap: GFN2 minutes), apply §39.32(e)-2's floor test
   (redraw if the achieved out-of-plane deviation < 0.5 x kick), keep the LOWEST, and REPORT the
   spread and how many distinct basins appeared. A basin choice made by an unrecorded seed is a
   silent input to every number downstream.
```
**🔴 AND THE FINDING I DID NOT EXPECT, which is the load-bearing part of this answer.** Two of the
five degenerate seeds differ in `d(Li–O2)` by **0.9 Å** (2.72 vs 3.61 Å) at **the same energy to
within 1 µEh** — Li sits over one EC's ethereal oxygen or the other's. By symmetry these are the
same structure relabelled; **but `O2` is the atom whose bond R-C breaks, and §39.41(e) measured that
Li MIGRATES ONTO THAT OXYGEN during the reaction.**
```
⟹ ENDPOINT DEGENERACY DOES NOT IMPLY BARRIER DEGENERACY. Two reactants identical in energy differ
  by 0.9 A in a coordinate the reaction is measured to use. Choosing between them by an unrecorded
  seed silently chooses a barrier.
⟹ REQUIRED, and both are free:
   1  emit `d(Li–O_break)` on the certified endpoint as a COVARIATE (data, no verdict — C-3 style).
   2  if two isoenergetic basins differ in it, run the GFN2 scan from BOTH (free) and escalate to
      DFT only if the barriers differ. Do not resolve it at DFT price.
⟹ AND FOR coder10's DEDUPE: `b0_conformers.json::dedupe` states it does no permutation search and
  does not identify mirror images. These two structures are exactly that case ⟹ the ensemble will
  DOUBLE-COUNT them. Not a bug to fix today; a count to distrust until it is.
```
**On the lead's two specific worries:**
```
spin contamination  🟢 NOT a GFN2 issue — GFN2's open-shell treatment is not a UKS calculation, so
   there is no <S^2> to contaminate. 🔴 IT IS A DFT ISSUE AND IT IS CURRENTLY UNEMITTED. A reduced
   EC radical is exactly the class where a UKS reference contaminates. ⟹ REQUIRED EMISSION at both
   endpoint stages: <S^2> before AND after annihilation. For a doublet the clean value is 0.75;
   report the number, render no verdict (C-3). 🔒 An "endpoint" with a badly contaminated
   reference is not the species we think we certified, and nothing else in the chain would notice.
kick biases the reaction coordinate?  🟢 NO, and it is checkable rather than arguable: the kick is
   out-of-plane (z) while the reaction coordinate is in-plane (d(O2-C3) stretch) plus the in-plane
   Li approach. Measured: d(O2-C3) is 1.406 un-kicked vs 1.413 kicked — 0.007 A. The kick does not
   move the breaking bond.
```

### (b) 🔴 AND THE PROBE FOUND SOMETHING NEITHER OF US ASKED FOR — the 1-D scan OVERESTIMATED the barrier by 0.10 eV, and the mechanism generalises

```
1-D relaxed scan, 0.01 A grid (09_scan_rc_fine)   max +0.955 eV
2-D grid MEP            (12_scan2d)               max +0.855 eV   <- 0.10 eV LOWER
```
**Li was FREE in the 1-D scan.** A relaxed scan lets every unconstrained coordinate relax, so the
1-D maximum should already have been the 2-D maximum. It was not — and the reason is a property of
how relaxed scans are run, not of this molecule:
```
🔒 A SEQUENTIAL RELAXED SCAN CARRIES THE PREVIOUS POINT'S BASIN FORWARD. Each step starts from the
   last converged structure, so a coordinate that must undergo a LARGE, DISCRETE change (here: Li+
   translocating 0.9 A onto the leaving oxygen) changes LATE and ABRUPTLY, when the driving force
   finally overcomes the local basin. That is HYSTERESIS, and its signature is exactly what we
   saw: a jump in the profile and a maximum that is TOO HIGH.
⟹ RULE FOR S3, and it is not about R-C: ANY single-coordinate relaxed scan on a system where a
  CATION MUST TRANSLOCATE will overestimate the barrier by hysteresis. 🔴 The measured size here
  is 0.10 eV = ~50x in rate at 298 K, i.e. EXACTLY the sensitivity this project is built around.
⟹ DETECTOR (free, and it is the same trigger §39.42(b) already installs): a discontinuity in a
  relaxed-scan profile is not noise and must never be smoothed or re-gridded away. IT IS THE
  SIGNATURE OF A MISSING COORDINATE. Refine first; if the jump survives refinement, add the
  coordinate — do not proceed with the 1-D guess.
⚠ NOT CLAIMED: that 0.855 eV is the saddle. The 2-D grid is coarse (0.09-0.13 A x 0.15 A) and its
  maximum is still an UPPER BOUND. It is a guess generator; the DFT freq and IRC certify.
```

### (e) 🔴 item 4's real consequence — the production class fills a whole round, so STOP BUYING PRODUCTION-SIZE BARRIERS ONE AT A TIME

engineer7 found that a production-class TS attempt is `≤ 3` or `≤ 2` per round and **fills the round
on its own**. His conclusion — that this strengthens rather than weakens my cut — is right. **But the
consequence is larger than the cut, and it is a methodology question, so it is mine:**

```
IF a production-size barrier costs a round, THEN S3 CANNOT BUY PRODUCTION-SIZE BARRIERS PER
REACTION. The network has hundreds of reactions and we can afford 2-3 attempts per round.
⟹ THE ONLY AFFORDABLE DESIGN IS TO BUY THE **SHELL-CONDITIONING CORRECTION** ONCE:
   barrier(production species) = barrier(small-cluster analogue) + Δ_shell ± σ_shell
   where Δ_shell is measured on a MATCHED PAIR — the same chemistry at both coordination numbers.
🟢 THAT PAIR ALREADY EXISTS AND IT IS WHY B0-F WAS BUILT THIS WAY: §39.26(d) states R-A vs R-C
   "tests size scaling" and §39.25 asks the shell-conditioning question directly. The design
   anticipated this; what is new is that it is now the ONLY affordable route, not a bonus.
🔴 AND THE CORRECTION IS NOT SMALL — I have a measurement:
   GFN2 relaxed-scan maxima:  R-A (11 atoms, 1 EC) +0.486 eV   vs   R-C (21 atoms, 2 EC) +0.855 eV
   ⟹ Δ_shell ~ 0.37 eV at GFN2 = ~6 Boltzmann decades at 298 K.  [MEASURED, GFN2, upper bounds
   on both sides, so the DIFFERENCE is less well determined than either term — see the caveat.]
   ⟹ A pipeline that computed every barrier on the small cluster and ignored Δ_shell would be
   wrong by far more than the 0.1 eV threshold. This is not an optional refinement.
```
```
WHAT THIS BUYS: the production-size budget stops being "how many production barriers can we
  afford" (answer: ~0) and becomes "how many matched PAIRS can we afford" (answer: 1 per round,
  and one pair may serve a whole reaction class). 🔒 That is the difference between a plan and no plan.
WHAT IT ASSUMES, and it must be tested, not asserted:
  🔴 that Δ_shell TRANSFERS across reactions within a class. UNTESTED. One pair measures it; a
  SECOND pair (a different reaction at both sizes) is what tests transferability, and until that
  exists Δ_shell carries an uncertainty that is ITSELF unmeasured. I will not pretend otherwise.
  ⚠ both GFN2 numbers are relaxed-scan maxima, and R-C's is now known to be hysteresis-inflated
  (b). Using the 2-D value, Δ_shell ~ 0.37 eV; using the 1-D value it would have read 0.47 eV.
  🔒 THE CORRECTION'S OWN ERROR IS OF THE SAME ORDER AS THE THING IT CORRECTS unless both sides
  are measured the same way. That is a protocol requirement, not a caveat: MATCHED METHOD ON BOTH
  MEMBERS OF THE PAIR, or the difference is not a difference.
⟹ FOR THE LEAD/USER: this reframes what S3's production budget is FOR. It is a decision about the
  observable (ADR-003), not a scheduling detail, and it should be taken deliberately.
```

## 39.44 🔴 STAGE 0 FIXED AT 50 ps — and four timing measurements that say the shipped xtb cost anchor is 33× too high (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers engineer7 §R39.18. Artefacts: `data/gfn2_pes_precheck_20260820/{13_scaling,14_threads}/`.

> core-h needs `κ_xtb`, which is still UNMEASURED (bracket 2.4–12). Do not mix the two.

### (a) 5 ps → 50 ps ACCEPTED, and the symmetric clause is written

engineer7's catch is exact and it is my own INDETERMINATE clause run backwards. **Stage 0's decision
is asymmetric**: "comparator recovers the targets" retires the pilot cheaply, but **"targets unfound"
FUNDS C** — so a too-short comparator commits the pilot's whole budget on an absence that has nothing
to do with either engine. **A too-short biased run risks a false REJECT of MTD; a too-short unbiased
run risks a false FUND of it.** Same defect, opposite sign, and he priced the fix at 6 % of what it
gates.

```
🔒 STAGE 0, PRE-REGISTERED: 3 seeds × 50 ps, unbiased NVT at the ladder's top rung.
🔴 AND THE READ-OUT IS A PER-TARGET FIRST-PASSAGE TIME, NEVER A BOOLEAN.
   The finding is "T2 unfound in 3 × 50 ps", NEVER "T2 absent". An unfound target reports its
   CENSORING TIME, exactly as a survival analysis does — and censoring is what a boolean throws away.
🟢 WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN A LONGER RUN: a first-passage time gives the pilot a MEASURED baseline
   to be scored against, which is what §39.42's restructure asked for and a boolean cannot supply.
🟢 AND IT MAKES A NULL INFORMATIVE: T1 first-passage is <1 ps [MEASURED]. If T3/T4 are still
   unfound at 50 ps — 50× longer — that is not a null, it is a MEASUREMENT that the secondary steps
   are rate-limited relative to ring opening, which is chemistry ADR-003 axis (a) wants anyway.
```
🔴 **One caveat that gets worse with length, and it is mine to raise because it is chemistry.** The
comparator runs at 1500 K. **The longer it runs, the more it decomposes into things that are on
nobody's target list**, and a T3/T4 hit at 40 ps at 1500 K may be a thermal artefact rather than
chemistry accessible at 330 K. ⟹ the first-passage instrument does double duty and must record
**what else appeared, and when, before each target** — ADR-024's discovery-temperature covariate
applied along the time axis instead of across the ladder. Free; it is the same event log.

   scaling, and nothing licenses reusing 1.218/2.4. Stage 0 measures it as a by-product (b).
ENGINEER7's (pricing)
 · every xtb figure anchored on 0.247 core-h reprices. I am not doing that arithmetic.
 · the MTD/plain overhead is ~1× per step, so a per-ps model calibrated on the MTD anchor
   over-estimates PLAIN MD by whatever the anchor's inflation is.
CAVEATS I ATTACH TO MY OWN NUMBERS, because they are single runs
 · n = 1 per point, no repeats, no error bars. The exponent 2.01 rests on two timings.
 · dev box, not KNL. KNL's memory bandwidth and core speed differ and the THREAD SCALING in
   particular may not transfer — a KNL core is weaker, which can make 4+ threads pay better there.
   🔴 ⟹ the <= 4 core rule is a DEV-BOX MEASUREMENT and must be re-checked by stage 0 on the
   cluster before it becomes a scheduling constraint. I am stating it as a hypothesis with a
   number attached, not as a rule.
 · `/usr/bin/time` user-time is USELESS for this code: it read ~3.8 × wall at 4 threads for every
   run, i.e. OpenMP BUSY-WAITS. 🔒 Anyone measuring xtb parallel efficiency from CPU time will
   conclude perfect scaling. Wall clock at fixed thread count is the only honest instrument here,
   and that is why (c) is a 1-thread measurement.
```

## 39.45 🔴 THE DISCONTINUITY GATE (spec for coder10) AND THE Δ_shell SHAPE PROBE — first results, and they do not say what I expected (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers the lead's two instructions and engineer7 §R39.19. Artefacts:
> `data/gfn2_pes_precheck_20260820/{15_ra_2d,16_ec3,17_reverse}/`.
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `Δ_shell` = the shift in activation barrier caused by adding a
> co-ligand to Li⁺'s first solvation shell; `MEP` = minimum-energy path; `CN` = coordination number;
> `T21-se` = the 21-atom single-ended TS attempt on R-C. All energies: **GFN2-xTB, dev box, 0
> cluster core-h.** 🔴 GFN2 numbers. They size things and rank things. They are not barriers.

### (a) 🔴 THE GATE — and the instrument is NOT the refine trigger. It is a bidirectional scan.

The lead asked whether the funding gate can reuse §39.42(b)'s refine trigger. **It cannot, and the
reason is that the two actions have opposite error costs:**
```
REFINE TRIGGER   action = spend ~8 more GFN2 points.  A false positive costs ~nothing.
                 ⟹ make it SENSITIVE. §39.42(b)'s |dE| > 0.05 eV / max-at-range-end stands.
FUNDING GATE     action = WITHHOLD ~660 core-h (11 atoms) / ~6,400 (21 atoms).  A false positive
                 blocks a legitimate attempt and looks like a pipeline failure.
                 ⟹ make it SPECIFIC. A different instrument, on a refined profile.
```
🔒 **And a jump on a coarse grid is EXPECTED — it is just a steep barrier sampled coarsely.** Firing
the gate on that would block every steep reaction we have. So the gate must distinguish *steep* from
*discontinuous*, which a single |ΔE| threshold cannot do at any value.

**🟢 THE INSTRUMENT, and I tested it before specifying it: RUN THE RELAXED SCAN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.**
Hysteresis *is* path dependence, so measure path dependence directly instead of proxying it with a
jump size. Cost: one extra GFN2 scan — negligible, and the plan of record already scans on GFN2.

**Validation on R-C** (`17_reverse/`, forward = the existing 33-point scan, reverse = product →
reactant on the same grid):
```
FORWARD max  +0.856 eV        REVERSE max  +0.320 eV (from its OWN endpoint)
🔴 AND THE TWO SCANS DO NOT EVEN END AT THE SAME STRUCTURE. At the identical constrained value
   d(O2-C3) = 1.40 A the forward scan has d(Li-O2) = 2.73 A and the reverse scan has 2.13 A, and
   the reverse endpoint sits 0.482 eV ABOVE the certified reactant: the reverse scan never puts Li
   back. Absolute saddle heights differ by 0.054 eV; APPARENT BARRIERS differ by 0.536 eV.
⟹ path dependence is not subtle here. It is the largest number on the page.
```
**⟹ GATE SPECIFICATION — hand this to coder10 as written:**
```
G-SCAN-1  every relaxed scan used to generate a TS guess is run in BOTH directions on the SAME grid.
G-SCAN-2  🔴🔴 **SUPERSEDED BY §39.48(b) — THIS VERSION IS FALSIFIED.** The n = 1 (R-A) path
          fails it with ΔE = 0.000 eV and Δbarrier = 0.013 eV, because d(Li–O_break) is a SOFT
          coordinate there. A structural test cannot separate a soft-mode displacement from a
          reaction-relevant one, which is the gate's whole content. **The corrected test is
          ENERGETIC and self-referential: fire unless the reverse endpoint's ENERGY matches the
          certified reactant AND the two directions' BARRIERS agree, both within the scan's own
          resolution.** Structural identity is demoted to a reported covariate. Original text kept:
          🔴 THE PRIMARY TEST IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ENERGETIC, AND IT HAS NO THRESHOLD:
          THE REVERSE SCAN MUST TERMINATE AT THE CERTIFIED REACTANT.
          Compare the reverse scan's final structure to the C-8-certified reactant endpoint by
          heavy-atom RMSD after alignment AND by every distance in the break/form role list
          (§39.26(d)) PLUS d(Li-O_break). Mismatch ⟹ the scan is path-dependent.
          🔒 No arbitrary constant. It checks identity against a structure we already certify,
          which is why it transfers to reactions nobody has looked at.
G-SCAN-3  SECONDARY, energetic: the two profiles' ABSOLUTE energies must agree at every grid point
          within the grid's own resolution (estimate that from the refine pass, do not assert it).
G-SCAN-4  EITHER FIRES ⟹ DO NOT FUND `ts_opt+freq` OR THE IRC ON THAT GUESS. Two permitted
          responses, both cheap: (i) re-scan in 2-D with the suspected second coordinate — cost is
          GFN2, ~21-35 core-h; (ii) record `indeterminate, missing coordinate`, which §39.39(f)
          already accepts as an outcome with a KNOWN CAUSE and which therefore enters U-56b's
          denominator without contaminating U-56a.
G-SCAN-5  the gate's own firings are COUNTED and REPORTED. 🔴 If it never fires, it is unreached
          (§0-o.4's rule 2); if it always fires, the scan design is wrong, not the chemistry.
⚠ WHAT THE GATE IS NOT: it does not certify that a passing guess is good. It removes one KNOWN
  failure mode. The freq and the IRC remain the certification.
```

### (b) 🔴 Δ_shell — I checked my own matched-method requirement against my own number, and then measured n = 3

**First, the self-check.** §39.43(e) quoted Δ_shell ≈ 0.37 eV from R-A's **1-D** value (0.486) and
R-C's **2-D** value (0.855) — 🔴 **a mismatched pair, by the very rule I had just written two
paragraphs earlier.** So I ran R-A in 2-D (`15_ra_2d/`):
```
R-A 2-D forward barrier = 0.489 eV      vs 1-D 0.486 eV   ⟹ agreement to 0.003 eV.
🟢 NO HYSTERESIS AT 11 ATOMS — which is the prediction §39.43(b) makes, since there is only one
   ligand and Li has nowhere else to go. The mechanism and the measurement agree.
⟹ MATCHED-METHOD Δ_shell(1→2) = 0.855 - 0.489 = 0.366 eV. My 0.37 SURVIVES.
🔒 It survived by luck, not by method. I am recording that the check was necessary and that I had
   published the number before running it.
```

**Then the scope question the lead approved — and the first pair of it is already run.** I built
Li(EC)₃ (31 atoms, reduced radical), applied my own multi-seed rule from §39.42(a) (3 kick seeds,
keep the lowest — and they spread by 0.017 eV, so the rule earned nothing here and cost a minute),
and ran the same 2-D scan on the same coordinates (`16_ec3/`):
```
                     2-D forward barrier      reaction energy       Δ_shell vs previous n
Li(EC)•        n=1        0.489 eV                -0.317 eV                 —
Li(EC)2•       n=2        0.855 eV                +0.090 eV              +0.366
Li(EC)3•       n=3        1.045 eV                +0.202 eV              +0.190
                                                       [MEASURED, GFN2, 2-D MEP, dev box, n=1 each]
```
```
🔴 Δ_shell DOES NOT SATURATE AT n = 2 — but it DECELERATES, roughly halving (0.366 -> 0.190).
   [EXTRAPOLATION, explicitly labelled: if the halving continues, n=3->4 ~ 0.10 and the total
   1 -> 4 shell effect is ~0.65 eV ~ 11 Boltzmann decades at 298 K. I am not measuring n=4 today
   and this line is an extrapolation from two differences.]
🔴 AND THE REACTION TURNS FROM EXOTHERMIC TO ENDOTHERMIC between n=1 and n=2. The single-ligand
   cluster is not a small version of the real system; it is a different thermodynamic sign.
```

### (c) 🔴🔴 THE CONSEQUENCE IS BIGGER THAN THE CORRECTION — the barrier depends on a number we have already established does not converge

```
Δ_shell(n) is ~0.19-0.37 eV PER LIGAND at GFN2 — 3 to 6 Boltzmann decades each.
U-65 (§39.0, open): THE EXPERIMENTAL Li+(EC) COORDINATION NUMBER DOES NOT CONVERGE, which is why
  §39.0 already rules that CN cannot be used as a validation target.
⟹ THE BARRIER IS STRONGLY SENSITIVE TO AN INPUT WE HAVE ALREADY DECIDED WE CANNOT PIN DOWN.
```
🔒 **This is not a new problem; it is an existing one whose size was unknown until now.** §39.25 asked
the shell-conditioning question and §39.26(d) built R-A vs R-C to answer it. What is new is the
magnitude, and the magnitude changes what the deliverable should be:

```
🔴 DO NOT PICK n. Reporting a barrier "for Li+(EC)2" silently reports an answer for one point of a
   distribution whose spread is 3-6 decades per unit.
🟢 PROPOSAL, and it reuses a pattern this project has already ratified: TREAT THE SHELL
   DISTRIBUTION AS A DECLARED UNCERTAINTY AXIS, exactly as §39.0's U-72 ruling makes K_sp one
   (F-1: "a declared uncertainty axis - preferred, cost 0, transfers").
   ⟹ compute barrier(n) for the n we can afford, take P(n) from the solvation-shell statistics the
     MLIP/MD work already produces, and report the SHELL-AVERAGED rate with the spread attached.
   ⟹ this converts an unconvergeable input from a hidden assumption into a reported axis, and it
     costs nothing we were not already going to compute.
   ⚠ It ASSUMES the shell interconverts slowly relative to the reaction, so that a static average
     over n is meaningful. That assumption is testable and UNTESTED, and it is the one to attack.
🟢 AND IT MAKES THE DECELERATION DECISION-RELEVANT: if Δ_shell converges by n=4-5, the average is
   over a short, tractable list. THAT is why the remaining pairs are worth running.
```

**Remaining scope (lead-approved, next chemistry-probe slot, all dev box, ~0 cluster core-h):**
```
P-A  Li(EC)4•             does Δ_shell converge?  🔴 HIGHEST VALUE — it decides whether (c)'s
                          shell average is over a short list or an open one.
P-B  Li(EC)(EMC)•         co-ligand IDENTITY at fixed n=2. Is Δ_shell a family constant or
                          ligand-specific? engineer7's "constant offset vs +-0.2 eV swing".
P-C  Li(EC)(PF6)•-        a CHARGED co-ligand — the largest expected perturbation, and the
                          contact-ion-pair limit that ADR-003 axis (b) cares about.
P-D  R-B channel at n=1 and n=2   REACTION dependence. 🔴 This is the actual transferability
                          question: Δ_shell is only usable as a correction if it transfers ACROSS
                          REACTIONS, and P-A/P-B/P-C all vary the shell instead.
ORDER  P-D first if only one can be run. A correction that does not transfer across reactions is
       not a correction, and no amount of shell variation would reveal that.
🔴 STATED BLIND SPOT, engineer7's and mine: this buys the SHAPE of the spread, never its DFT
   MAGNITUDE. GFN2's own Δ_shell error is unmeasured, and nothing here substitutes for the one
   DFT pair. It is a proxy with a named limitation, offered as such.
```

### (b) 🔴 BUT THE TWO ANCHORS ARE WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and that is the durable finding

```
b0_conformers.json's 0.247 core-h   wall x 12 THREADS on a job that uses ~2.
                                    ⟹ counts a charge NOBODY MAKES (it is a dev box).
                                    ⟹ TOO HIGH by 33x.  [§39.44]

🔒 **Same conflation, opposite signs: WORK COST vs CHARGED COST.** One anchor charged threads it never
used; the other counted work the allocation does not bill by. **Neither is a wrong calculation — both
are correct calculations of the wrong quantity**, which is §39.33(b)'s sentence for the third time in
this project.

```
🟢 RULE — cheap, and it makes packing efficiency a MEASUREMENT instead of an assumption:
   every xtb cost datum carries BOTH
     work_core_h     = threads_actually_used x wall
     charged_core_h  = allocated_cores x wall
   and every downstream number states WHICH ONE it used.
   packing_efficiency = work / charged  is then observed per job, not assumed.
🔴 A single `core_hours` field cannot express this, and its inability to is EXACTLY the 33x error
   and exactly the P3 ambiguity. This is engineer7's "threads and wall recorded separately",
   sharpened by what the P3 read showed: recording the inputs is not enough if the two DERIVED
   quantities are then collapsed into one name.

## 39.47 🔴 THREE FINAL NUMBERS — the scan budget (coder11 is blocked on this), stage 0's length, and the Δ_shell ladder (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `G-SCAN-1…5` = the discontinuity-gate rules of §39.45(a);
> `SP` = single point (an energy evaluation at a fixed geometry, no optimisation);
> `T31-se` = a single-ended transition-state attempt on the 31-atom Li(EC)₃ system;
> `stage 0` = the unbiased comparator run that precedes the metadynamics (MTD) pilot, §39.42(d);
> `first-passage time` = the trajectory time at which a target reaction first occurs;
> `competing risk` = a different event that removes the possibility of the one being timed.

### (a) 🔴 THE SCAN BUDGET — the cap belongs to the ENGINE, not to the scan. Two caps, not one.

**The blocking question, answered first, then justified**: the reverse scan required by G-SCAN-1 is
**GFN2-only and never touches the DFT budget.** `TOTAL_POINTS_MAX = 20` stays exactly as it is.

```
CONSTANT                    VALUE   APPLIES TO                          WHY THIS NUMBER
COARSE_STEPS_REGISTERED       12    both engines, per direction         §39.42(b), unchanged
REFINE_STEPS_MAX               8    both engines, triggered only        §39.42(b), unchanged
TOTAL_POINTS_MAX              20    🔴 DFT ONLY, ONE DIRECTION          cost control. UNCHANGED.
SCAN_POINTS_GFN2_MAX  🆕     512    GFN2, ALL directions and both       not a cost control at all
                                    dimensions, summed per reaction     — see below
SCAN_STEPS_MIN                 8    both                                a scan with <8 points
                                                                        cannot place a maximum away
                                                                        from its own endpoints
```
**Why one cap cannot serve both, in one line of arithmetic**: a DFT scan point costs **4.5 / 14 / 34
core-h** (engineer7 §R39.18); a GFN2 scan point costs **~0.001–0.006 core-h** (§R39.20's corrected
rates). **Three orders of magnitude.** A cap of 20 is a real cost control on one engine and, on the
other, forbids doubling something that costs 0.05 core-h to double. 🔒 **A constant whose reason is
"cost" must live at the same level as the cost, and here the cost is a property of the engine.**

**And 20 is already impossible for the work we have actually done**: §39.43's 2-D grids were
**104 points**, and the R-C fine refine was 41. A single cap of 20 would refuse the very run that
found the hysteresis it exists to guard against.

```
🔒 WHY THE REVERSE SCAN IS GFN2-ONLY, AND IT IS NOT A BUDGET DODGE:
   the gate's PURPOSE is to decide whether to fund the DFT attempt. The plan of record generates
   the TS guess at GFN2 ⟹ the bidirectional check runs where the guess is made, which is where it
   is free. By the time a DFT scan runs at all it is a C-12 FALLBACK, and the gate has ALREADY
   returned a verdict for that reaction.
   ⟹ HYSTERESIS IS A PROPERTY OF RELAXED SCANNING AND OF THE REACTION'S DIMENSIONALITY, NOT OF THE
     ENGINE. A DFT relaxed scan has the same pathology; what it does NOT have is a different
     ANSWER about how many coordinates the reaction needs.
   ⟹ RULE: the DFT fallback scan INHERITS the GFN2 gate verdict and runs ONE direction. If GFN2
     returned "2-D needed", the DFT fallback is 2-D or it is refused — it is never run 1-D anyway.
🟢 ⟹ NO REPRICE FOR engineer7: the DFT scan row is unchanged at 54 / 224 / 680 core-h. The
   doubling lands entirely on the engine where it is invisible.
🔴 ONE THING THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated so it is not assumed away: if a reaction ever reaches a
   DFT scan WITHOUT a GFN2 path (no cheap surface available for its elements — the ADR-014
   transferability case), the gate has no verdict to inherit and the DFT scan is UNGATED. That
   case does not exist in B0-F and it will exist eventually. When it does, the choice is 2× the
   DFT scan or an ungated guess, and it should be taken deliberately then, not defaulted now.
```

### (b) 🔴 STAGE 0 — I am refusing BOTH 50 ps and 500 ps. The same money buys a better experiment as MORE SEEDS.

engineer7's repricing makes 3 seeds × 500 ps cost about what 3 × 50 ps was quoted at, and the lead
asked me to pick the length. **The chemistry says the axis is wrong.**

```
🔴 REASON 1 — COMPETING RISKS, not censoring. At 1500 K the ring opens in <1 ps. Everything after
   that is a DECOMPOSING system. T3 (C2H4 elimination) and T4 (CO release) need the ring-opened
   intermediate TO STILL EXIST. If the precursor is destroyed at t = 30 ps, the trajectory after
   30 ps contributes NOTHING to T3/T4's first-passage time — it is not censored, the event has
   been made impossible. ⟹ EXTRA LENGTH PAST THE PRECURSOR'S LIFETIME BUYS ZERO INFORMATION ABOUT
   THE TARGETS, while extra seeds buy a fresh precursor every time.
🔴 REASON 2 — THE READ-OUT IS A DISTRIBUTION AND 3 SAMPLES CANNOT ESTIMATE ONE. §39.44(a) made
   stage 0's output a per-target first-passage time. n = 3 gives essentially no distribution at
   ANY length. This is §39.39(c)-2's argument (a rate needs a denominator) applied to my own
   instrument, which is where I should have applied it first.
🟢 REASON 3 — free by-product: ADR-051's D1 (seed-split capture-recapture) needs INDEPENDENT SEEDS
   BY DESIGN. 12 seeds is a usable D1 sample; 3 is not.
```
```
🔒 RULING — STAGE 0 = 12 SEEDS × 100 ps, unbiased NVT at the ladder's top rung.
   1,200 ps total vs 3 × 500 = 1,500 ps ⟹ slightly CHEAPER than engineer7's option.
   100 ps = 100× T1's measured first-passage time (<1 ps) [MEASURED, §39.42(d)].
   wall: 100 ps at 21 atoms, 1 thread ≈ 0.54 h **[MEASURED, DEV BOX; on KNL = 0.54 × κ_xtb
   (2.4–12) = 1.3–6.5 h/seed]** [basis: 39.0 s for 2 ps, §39.44(c)]. 🔴 The bracket is in the cell
   because a dev-box wall travelling without one is exactly how the 0.247 anchor escaped
   (engineer7 §R39.23, correcting my own citation). Conclusion unchanged: nowhere near
   `max_wall_h` 48, and 12 seeds pack trivially.
🟢 AND A FREE STAGED READ-OUT: report recall and first-passage at 25 / 50 / 100 ps checkpoints.
   The trajectory is dumped anyway. If recall saturates by 50 ps, that is a MEASUREMENT that the
   window was sufficient — which is the thing engineer7's length worry wanted and neither 50 nor
   500 ps could have supplied from a single window.
🔴 REQUIRED ALONGSIDE, or the first-passage times are uninterpretable: for every target, record
   whether its PRECURSOR was still intact at the end of the run. An unfound target with a destroyed
   precursor is a COMPETING-RISK outcome, NOT a censored one, and the two must never share a bucket.
🟢 ADDENDUM (engineer7 §R39.22, accepted): stage 0 must emit BOTH `work_core_h` (Σ threads × wall)
   and `charged_core_h` (total_cores × wall) ⟹ it measures the packing efficiency η by construction,
   at zero marginal cost, alongside κ_xtb and the on-KNL size exponent. 🔴 AND THE 12-SEED DESIGN
   MEASURES η BETTER THAN THE 3-SEED ONE, for the same reason it measures first passage better:
   η from 3 tasks has no denominator worth the name. The same argument, on a third quantity.
🔴 CORES MUST BE DECLARED, NOT INHERITED — this is now a SUBMITTABILITY constraint, not hygiene:
   engineer7 measures the MTD pilot's guard ceiling at 36,864 core-h on a whole node (REFUSED
   against the 21,000 guard) versus 2,304 with cores declared = 4. **A 16× ceiling swing on
   identical work, decided by one field.** Stage 0's seeds are therefore submitted as independent
   small tasks with cores declared (1-4 each), P3's `xargs -P NP` pattern — never as one node-wide
   job. 🟢 Twelve short tasks also carry a far smaller ceiling footprint than one long one.
```
⚠ **Honest limit**: 12 × 100 ps still cannot distinguish "T3 is 200× slower than T1" from "T3 is
impossible under competing risks". **Nothing we can afford can.** What the design buys is that the
distinction is *visible in the data* rather than absorbed into a boolean.

### (c) engineer7 §R39.21 — the n = 3 limit ACCEPTED, the SP ladder ACCEPTED with one condition he could not add

**The hard limit stands and his restatement is stronger than mine.** T31-se's ceiling is 24,576
core-h against a 21,000 guard ⟹ **the package is refused at submit.** ⟹ **Δ_shell(n) has exactly ONE
DFT step, for the lifetime of this project, by any design.** 🔒 And therefore: *per-reaction
production-size barriers are not expensive, they are impossible.* The matched-pair design is not the
cheaper option — **it is the only option that submits.** My §39.43(e) said "the only affordable
design"; the correct word is *submittable*, and the difference matters because a budget can be
raised and a guard, by §R24.1, cannot.

🔴 **And it kills my own extrapolation as a validatable claim**: §39.45(b)'s "Δ_shell converges by
n ≈ 4–5" can never be checked at DFT. It is a **GFN2-only observation** and must always be reported
as one. I registered it labelled as an extrapolation; it is now known to be a *permanently*
unvalidatable one, which is a stronger warning and belongs with the number.

**The SP ladder: accepted.** A DFT single-point ladder along the gate-passed GFN2 path, calibrated at
n = 1 and n = 2 where we are buying full attempts anyway, is the standard hierarchical design and the
overlap is free. His two conditions (same level and route flags; every rung's path must have passed
the §39.45 reverse gate) are correct and I add nothing to them.

```
🔴 THE CONDITION HE COULD NOT ADD, because it is about what the calibration MEANS:
   the n = 1/2 calibration measures the SP-vs-full-attempt bias AT n = 1 AND 2. Using it at n = 3
   and 4 assumes that bias is INDEPENDENT OF n — which is the SAME TRANSFERABILITY ASSUMPTION
   Δ_shell itself is under scrutiny for. ⟹ THE CALIBRATION IS ITSELF EXTRAPOLATED.
   🔒 This does not sink the design. It means the ladder converts ONE unquantified extrapolation
   (GFN2 → DFT at every n) into a SMALLER, NAMED one (an SP bias measured at two points and
   assumed flat), which is real progress and must be reported as what it is rather than as a
   calibrated number. **You cannot escape the extrapolation here; you can only make it explicit,
   smaller, and labelled.**
🟢 FREE TEST OF THAT VERY ASSUMPTION, and it costs nothing extra: the bias is measured at TWO
   points, so its n-DEPENDENCE has one degree of freedom. If bias(n=1) and bias(n=2) differ by more
   than their own noise, the flat-bias assumption is already refuted at the only two places we can
   look, and the ladder's n = 3/4 rungs must be reported with that spread rather than as points.
🔴 AND THE NOISE TERM — engineer7 (§R39.23) correctly observed the test cannot fire without one,
   and offered ~25 core-h to buy it by running the ladder on BOTH of the gate's two paths.
   **I accept the instrument and REJECT THAT SAMPLE, at the same price.**
   THE FLAW: the §39.45 reverse gate SELECTS FOR PATH AGREEMENT — a reaction only reaches the
   ladder BECAUSE its forward and reverse paths matched. ⟹ the forward/reverse spread is
   CONDITIONED ON BEING SMALL, and using it as noise systematically UNDER-estimates it.
   ⚠ DIRECTION: an under-estimated noise term makes flat-bias look REFUTED too easily ⟹ the
     n = 3/4 rungs get reported with a spread instead of as points ⟹ MORE uncertainty reported.
     That is the safe direction, but it must be a stated property and not a lucky accident.
   🟢 THE BETTER SAMPLE, AT THE SAME COST: use paths from INDEPENDENT KICK SEEDS — which §39.42(a)
     already requires (>= 3 seeds) and which are already generated. Independent seeds are NOT
     conditioned on agreeing with each other, so they sample the real question: "which path does
     GFN2 hand us?" The DFT single points are the cost and their number is unchanged ⟹ same ~25
     core-h, an unconditioned sample instead of a conditioned one.
   🔴 WHAT IT STILL IS NOT (engineer7's own caveat, endorsed): a PATH-SELECTION spread, not a total
     uncertainty. It does not cover basis, functional, or the GFN2 geometry's own error.
```

**The three-tier deliverable: accepted, and it is the right shape.** DFT-resolved over 2 rungs,
SP-resolved over 4 (calibrated at 2), GFN2-shaped beyond — three provenance labels, one number.
🔴 His warning is the load-bearing part and I endorse it in my own words: **reporting one spread with
one label would hide exactly the tier boundary the user's decision turns on.**

### (d) 🔒 A standing heuristic, because engineer7 counted it and he is right

Four times in this exchange the cheapest available item was the one that could kill the expensive
one: §39.40(d)'s free GFN2 pre-check (7 core-h, could have killed the MTD arm), stage 0 (~10–60,
can retire the pilot), the reverse-scan gate (~0.05, gates ~6,400), and P-D (~0, can invalidate
Δ_shell entirely). **That is not a coincidence, it is the shape of a correctly ordered plan.**
```
🔒 HEURISTIC, proposed for an ADR: BEFORE FUNDING AN EXPENSIVE ITEM, ASK WHETHER A CHEAPER ITEM
   COULD MAKE IT UNNECESSARY — AND IF SO, RUN THAT FIRST, EVEN IF IT DELAYS THE EXPENSIVE ONE.
   The test is not "is the cheap item informative" but "can the cheap item CHANGE THE DECISION".
   ⚠ The failure mode of this heuristic, named so it does not become an excuse: an endless chain
   of cheap probes that never funds anything. The guard against it is that each cheap item must
   have a PRE-REGISTERED read-out that releases or kills the expensive one — which every one of
   the four above has.
🔴 AND engineer7 (§R39.23) MEASURED THE REAL FAILURE MODE, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE I NAMED. The cheap
   probes total 140–290 core-h against the 3,514 they gate — 4–8 %, a healthy ratio. **The risk is
   LATENCY**: four cluster-side probes serialised at ~3.5 days per round trip is TWO WEEKS against
   a 21.5-week cap whose every open condition is wall-clock.
   🟢 FREE GUARD, ADOPTED: BUNDLE cluster-side cheap probes into ONE submission. And the specific
     consequence he draws is right — P-U2' at 0.7 core-h should run UNCONDITIONALLY, because the
     round trip saved by not deferring it exceeds its entire cost. My conditional ordering was
     correct when P-U2' cost 9 core-h and is wrong at 0.7.
   🔴 ONE CONDITION ON RELAXING IT, because this project has a history: **a measured ν is NOT
     evidence for funding the pilot.** Running it early creates exactly the sunk-cost sentence
     ("we already have ν, so..."). ⟹ pre-registered: only stage 0's read-out releases or kills the
     pilot; P-U2''s output is an INPUT to a pilot that stage 0 has already released, and it enters
     no funding argument.
   🔒 And his closing point is the one that makes the heuristic affordable at all: the dev-box
     sorting rule (§39.43(a)) is what turns most of these probes from a round trip into an
     afternoon. Without it, four cheap probes WOULD have been two weeks.
```
