> Answers engineer7 §R39.24's blocking question and ratifies his two open design points.
> Artefact: `data/gfn2_pes_precheck_20260820/18_gate_verdicts/`. **GFN2, dev box, 0 cluster core-h.**
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `G-SCAN-2` = the structural half of the discontinuity gate,
> §39.45(a); `rung` = one coordination number `n` of the single-point (SP) ladder;
> `soft coordinate` = one whose displacement costs energy below the scan's own resolution.

### (a) He asked whether I had verdicts for n = 1 and n = 3. I did not, so I ran them.

```
                    d(Li-O2) at the SAME constrained d(O2-C3) = 1.40 A       forward   reverse
                    forward reactant   reverse endpoint   Δd      ΔE_endpoint   max       max
n=1  R-A (11 at)         2.490              2.138       -0.352     +0.000     +0.486    +0.473
n=2  R-C (21 at)         2.73               2.13        -0.60      +0.482     +0.856    +0.320
n=3  Li(EC)3 (31 at)     2.575              1.997       -0.579     +0.448     +1.255    +0.438
                                                          [MEASURED, GFN2, dev box, 2026-08-20]
```

### (b) 🔴 MY OWN G-SCAN-2 IS WRONG, and n = 1 is the counter-example. Correcting it here.

§39.45(a) made the primary test **structural identity** — *"the reverse scan must terminate at the
certified reactant"* — and I chose it precisely because it needs **no threshold**. **n = 1 shows it
produces a false positive.** The reverse endpoint sits 0.35 Å away in `d(Li–O2)` and **0.000 eV**
away in energy, and the two directions' barriers agree to **0.013 eV**. Nothing is wrong with that
path; `d(Li–O2)` at n = 1 is simply a **soft coordinate** — §39.43(a)'s R-A grid measured it
directly, with rows from 1.95 to 3.40 Å spanning 0.06 eV.

🔒 **A structural test cannot distinguish a soft-mode displacement from a reaction-relevant one, and
that distinction is the entire content of the gate.** My no-threshold property was bought by
measuring the wrong thing.

```
🔴🔴 **THIS (v2) IS ALSO SUPERSEDED — BY §39.50(a). The self-referential tolerance is UNDEFINED at
   n = 1 (the refine pass is triggered and R-A's grid is clean) and, worse, is ANTI-CORRELATED with
   the pathology: refining a hysteretic path does not converge it (measured 1.4× under a 5× refine).
   v3 takes an explicit declared constant: 0.05 eV on both comparisons, intra-GFN2. Text kept:**
🟢 G-SCAN-2, CORRECTED — and it keeps the no-imported-constant property by making the tolerance
   SELF-REFERENTIAL, which is ADR-015 §1's principle rather than a borrowed number:
   FIRE unless BOTH hold —
     (i)  the reverse scan's endpoint ENERGY matches the certified reactant's within the SCAN'S OWN
          RESOLUTION (measured from the refine pass: how much the profile moves when the grid is
          halved — §39.42(b) already generates it), AND
     (ii) the two directions' BARRIERS agree within that same resolution.
   ⟹ structural identity is NEITHER NECESSARY NOR SUFFICIENT and is demoted to a REPORTED
     COVARIATE (still emitted — d(Li-O_break) is §39.42(a)'s required field and stays).
🟢 CHECK AGAINST ALL THREE MEASURED CASES — it separates them cleanly:
   n=1  ΔE_endpoint 0.000, Δbarrier 0.013  ⟹ PASS   (structural test would have blocked it)
   n=2  ΔE_endpoint 0.482, Δbarrier 0.536  ⟹ FIRE
   n=3  ΔE_endpoint 0.448, Δbarrier 0.817  ⟹ FIRE
🔴 AND THE FALSE-POSITIVE DIRECTION MATTERS: my version would have blocked a GOOD path, i.e. refused
   to fund a legitimate attempt and looked like a pipeline failure — the exact error I said a
   funding gate must not make when I argued it had to be SPECIFIC rather than sensitive
   (§39.45(a)). I wrote the requirement and then failed it in the same section.
```

### (c) 🔴 A second finding: HYSTERESIS GROWS WITH n, and it validates the matched-method rule again

```
1-D forward max   vs   2-D MEP max        hysteresis
n=1   0.486             0.489              -0.003   (none — one ligand, Li has nowhere to go)
n=2   0.955             0.855              +0.100
n=3   1.255             1.045              +0.210
```
⟹ **the 1-D scan's inflation more than doubles from n = 2 to n = 3**, consistent with the mechanism:
more ligands ⟹ Li's rearrangement is a larger, more discrete event ⟹ a sequential 1-D scan carries
the wrong basin further before it releases.
🟢 **§39.45(b)'s Δ_shell table used 2-D values at every rung, so it is unaffected** — matched method
protected the number for the second time. 🔴 Had I used 1-D values the ladder would have read
Δ_shell(2→3) = 0.300 instead of 0.190, i.e. **58 % high, in the direction that exaggerates the shell
effect.**

**⟹ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LADDER, and it is not a blocker**: at n ≥ 2 the 1-D paths FIRE, so the SP
ladder consumes the **2-D** paths — which exist for n = 2 and n = 3 (`12_scan2d/`, `16_ec3/`). n = 1
may use its 1-D path (it passes). **n = 4, if funded, needs a 2-D scan first** — free, dev box, and
it is now a precondition rather than an option.

### (d) engineer7's two design points — RATIFIED, both toward buying more

**1. The within-n spread goes at EVERY rung, not only at the calibration rungs (+65–210 core-h).**
```
REASON, and it is the same defect one level down: path-selection spread is a property of the SYSTEM,
and the system gets ROUGHER with n — measured, not assumed: at 21 atoms 1 of 6 kick seeds landed
0.686 eV high (§39.42(a)), and hysteresis doubled from n=2 to n=3 (c). Importing the spread from
n = 1,2 is ANOTHER flat-in-n assumption, which is exactly the defect I flagged in the calibration.
🔒 THE PRINCIPLE: BUY WHAT CAN BE MEASURED; ASSUME ONLY WHAT CANNOT. The calibration at n = 3/4 is
   impossible (a full attempt is unsubmittable, §39.47(c)) — the SPREAD is not. Assuming a
   measurable quantity, next to one we are forced to assume, is a choice with no excuse.
```
**2. Not 5 points, not a full profile — 7, with a triggered extension to ≤ 9.**
```
WHY 5 IS NOT ENOUGH: it evaluates DFT at the GFN2 MAXIMUM. 🔴 The DFT maximum along a GFN2 path need
  not sit at the GFN2 maximum, and sampling a maximum on a coarse grid UNDER-estimates it — measured
  in this project at 0.10 eV (§39.43's 0.05 A vs 0.01 A grids). A barrier biased LOW is a rate
  biased HIGH: §0-h's optimistic direction, the one we have never self-corrected from.
WHY A FULL PROFILE IS MORE THAN NEEDED: the profile's shape is what the free GFN2 scan is for.
🟢 SPEC: both endpoints + a bracket of FIVE consecutive path points centred on the GFN2 maximum = 7.
  If the DFT maximum lands at a bracket EDGE, extend by 2 (≤ 9). Same coarse+triggered-refine
  pattern as §39.42(b), so it is one rule reused rather than a new one.
🟢 AND IT MAKES THE LADDER SELF-CHECKING, which 5 points cannot: comparing WHERE the DFT maximum
  sits against where the GFN2 maximum sits MEASURES how well a GFN2 path serves as a DFT path —
  the ladder's own foundational assumption, tested by the ladder, for free.
```

### (e) His four preconditions, and the claim discipline

Preconditions 1–4 accepted **as funding conditions**, which is the right place for them: 1 and 2 are
my own rules, and a rule in a paragraph is a rule that gets skipped — §39.32's `nosymm` and
§39.41(b)'s grid seam are both instances of exactly that. On **precondition 2 he was right to ask**:
I had verdicts for n = 2 only, and (a) is the answer — obtained for ~0 in the time it took to reply.

**Claim discipline on return — accepted verbatim and it is stricter than my three-tier version:**
```
"DFT-resolved over ONE rung · SP-resolved over four, CALIBRATED AT ONE · GFN2-shaped beyond"
🔴 ONE calibration point measures an OFFSET. It cannot measure whether the offset is CONSTANT IN n,
   and constancy in n is the ladder's whole claim. It becomes my two-rung version only after
   T21-se runs in wave 1 — and NOT BEFORE, whatever the rungs look like when they land.
```
🔒 **And his flag on his own weakest number is the right disclosure**: no standalone SP has ever been
measured on this project, so the per-SP cost is a derived stack. ⟹ **the first rung to return is
this project's first SP measurement, and every later rung is re-derived from it, not from the
stack.** That is the same rule as "measure κ per run, never store a correction factor" (§39.29(f)).

## 39.49 🟢 coder11's SP-LADDER QUESTION — ANSWERED WITH A MEASUREMENT, and the wave-1 collision is premature (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `SP ladder` = the DFT single-point ladder of §39.47(c);
> `rung` = one coordination number `n`; `kick seed` = one random out-of-plane perturbation of a
> starting geometry (§39.32(e)); `path-selection noise` = how much the SP barrier moves when GFN2
> hands us a different path; `hysteresis` = how much a relaxed scan's profile depends on the
> DIRECTION it is run. Artefact: `data/gfn2_pes_precheck_20260820/19_seed_n1/`.

### (a) 🔴 coder11's option (c) is a category error — and it is MY sentence that invited it

coder11 leaned toward *"11 atoms needs no noise term, because §39.45(b) measured no hysteresis
there."* **That conflates two different quantities, and the conflation is my fault for putting them
in adjacent sections:**
```
HYSTERESIS            forward vs reverse of THE SAME scan.  Path DIRECTION dependence.
PATH-SELECTION NOISE  different STARTING BASINS (different kick seeds) -> different paths.
⟹ zero hysteresis does NOT imply zero seed-to-seed spread. They are different measurements and
  neither licenses the other. At n = 1 both happen to be ~0 — but that is TWO measurements, not
  one inference, and the second one did not exist until I ran it below.
```

### (b) 🟢 So I measured it. **RULING: option (a) — the ≥3-seed rule extends to EVERY rung that feeds the ladder.**

Six kick seeds on the shipped 11-atom reactant, GFN2 `--opt tight`:
```
all 6 seeds -> ONE basin, spread 0.0005 eV      (21-atom comparison: 0.686 eV, 1 seed of 6)
⚠ and d(Li-O2) ranges 2.275 - 2.610 A across them at ZERO energy cost — §39.48(b)'s soft-coordinate
  finding reproduced independently, from the other direction.        [MEASURED, GFN2, dev box]
```
```
🔒 WHY (a) AND NOT (b) OR (c):
  · the noise term must be measured WHERE THE CALIBRATION LIVES. n = 1 is a calibration rung.
    Importing its noise from n = 2 (option b) is the same flat-in-n import I have now refused
    twice — in the calibration itself (§39.47(c)) and in the per-rung spread (§39.48(d)).
  · option (c) rests on the category error in (a).
  · it costs SECONDS at GFN2, and it turns "n = 1 needs no noise term" from an assumption into a
    NUMBER (0.0005 eV, below any resolution the ladder can use). 🟢 THE IMPLEMENTATION IS THE SAME
    EITHER WAY; what changes is whether the zero is measured or asserted.
⟹ SPEC FOR coder11: >= 3 kick seeds for EVERY rung that feeds the SP ladder (n = 1, 2, 3, 4),
  floor test per §39.32(e)-2, lowest taken forward, SPREAD AND BASIN COUNT REPORTED PER RUNG.
  The second ladder path is the second DISTINCT basin if one exists; if all seeds land in one
  basin (as at n = 1), the reported path-selection noise is "below resolution" WITH THE NUMBER
  ATTACHED, and the ladder's second path at that rung buys nothing and is not run.
  🟢 That last clause is what stops (a) from costing anything where it is not needed.
```
**And his second question — yes: G-SCAN runs PER PATH, once per kick-seed path that feeds a rung.**
The gate is a statement about *that path*, not about the reaction, so a per-reaction verdict would
certify a path nobody used.

### (c) 🔴 AN OPERATIONAL FINDING FROM THE RUN ITSELF, and it is the same selection effect one level down

One of the six seeds terminated with `[ERROR] Program stopped due to fatal error` under six-way
concurrency and produced **no output file**; re-run alone it converged normally.
```
🔴 A PIPELINE THAT GLOBS THE SURVIVING `xtbopt.xyz` FILES WOULD HAVE COMPUTED THE SPREAD OVER
   SURVIVORS AND REPORTED "6 seeds" or, worse, "5 seeds" with no note. That is a SELECTION EFFECT —
   the same defect as computing a rate over the runs that finished (§39.34) and as the gate
   selecting for path agreement (§39.47(c)).
⟹ REQUIRED: a failed seed is COUNTED AND REPORTED, never dropped. `n_seeds_attempted` and
  `n_seeds_converged` as TWO fields. If they differ, the spread is over survivors and must say so.
⚠ I do not know whether the failure was a concurrency race or a bad draw — n = 1, not diagnosed,
  and I am not asserting a cause. What is certain is that it was SILENT at the file level.
```

### (d) engineer7's wave-1 collision — **the decision is premature and an already-scheduled experiment makes it**

```
MTD pilot @ C = 3,000 + THREE production-class attempts = 24,747 ceiling > 21,000 guard  ⟹ REFUSED
MTD pilot + TWO attempts = 17,834                                                        ⟹ fits
```
🟢 **But stage 0 runs in THIS round and wave 1 is the NEXT one, and stage 0's read-out is what
releases or kills the pilot (§39.42(d), §39.47(d)).** ⟹ by the time wave 1 is composed we already
know whether the pilot exists. **The collision only materialises in the branch where stage 0
releases the pilot, and deciding it now would be deciding a branch we are paid to observe.**

🔒 **And a pre-registered answer FOR that branch, so this is a deferral with a trigger and not
indecision:** if stage 0 releases the pilot, **take wave 1 at THREE attempts and defer the pilot.**
```
REASON — it is the futility rule's operating characteristic, which is mine:
  0 of 3 leaves a 95 % upper bound on p of 0.632   (engineer7 §R39.15 §6)
  0 of 2 leaves                                0.776   [computed here: 1 - 0.05^(1/2)]
⟹ at n = 2 the wave-1 futility rule is very nearly BLIND — it would fail to detect anything short
  of total collapse, and §39.43(d) already pre-registered that it is a CATASTROPHE DETECTOR rather
  than an estimator. Dropping to 2 attempts takes the one property it still has.
⟹ the pilot has no deadline; the wave's operating characteristics are already marginal. Spend the
  scarce guard headroom on the item whose statistics degrade, not on the item that can wait.
```

## 39.50 🔴 coder11 FOUND TWO MORE DEFECTS IN G-SCAN-2 — the tolerance and the Hamiltonian. THIRD iteration, and this time I take the constant (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `G-SCAN-2` = the primary test of the discontinuity gate;
> `refine pass` = the triggered second scan at finer spacing (§39.42(b)); `Hamiltonian` = the
> energy model (GFN2-xTB vs the DFT level) — energies from two different ones are not comparable;
> `certified reactant` = an endpoint that passed C-8 (converged, `n_imag == 0`, at the TS search's
> DFT level). Both defects were found by coder11 reading the spec before implementing it.

### (a) 🔴 DEFECT 1 — the tolerance is undefined exactly where the gate was falsified, AND my proposed tolerance is inflated by the pathology it detects

coder11 is right twice over. §39.48(b) set the tolerance to *"the scan's own resolution, measured
from the refine pass"* — and §39.42(b) makes the refine pass **triggered**, with **R-A's clean grid
as the named example of when it does not fire.** ⟹ at n = 1 there is no refine pass, no halved grid,
no resolution, and **no tolerance — for the very case that falsified the previous version.**

**And his option (b) — always refine — fails for a reason he could not have known, which is in my
own §39.41(b):**
```
ON A HYSTERETIC PATH, REFINING DOES NOT CONVERGE THE PROFILE. Measured: refining R-C's grid 5x
(0.05 -> 0.01 A) shrank the jump by only 1.4x. ⟹ "how much the profile moves when the grid halves"
is LARGE precisely on the paths the gate must fire on.
🔴 ⟹ a tolerance defined that way GROWS WITH THE PATHOLOGY IT IS MEANT TO DETECT. It is not merely
   unavailable at n = 1; it is ANTI-CORRELATED with the thing being tested. Option (b) is worse
   than option (a), and both are worse than the answer below.
```
**⟹ THIRD ITERATION, and I stop trying to avoid the constant.**
```
🔒 I have now tried twice to buy a no-threshold property and failed twice:
   attempt 1  structural identity   — measured the WRONG QUANTITY (soft coordinate, §39.48(b))
   attempt 2  scan resolution       — ANTI-CORRELATED with the pathology (above)
   ⟹ the honest move is to take an EXPLICIT, DERIVED, DOCUMENTED constant rather than a proxy
     that looks constant-free. A hidden constant inside a proxy is worse than a stated one.

🟢 G-SCAN-2, THIRD AND FINAL FORM — the tolerance is DECISION RELEVANCE, not numerical resolution:
   FIRE unless BOTH
     (i)  |E(reverse endpoint) - E(forward first frame)|   < 0.05 eV
     (ii) |barrier_forward - barrier_reverse|              < 0.05 eV
   🔴 **CLAUSE (ii) DISAMBIGUATED 2026-08-20 (coder11) — BOTH BARRIERS ARE MEASURED FROM THE
     REACTANT END: the FORWARD profile's FIRST frame and the REVERSE profile's LAST frame.**
     My prose said only "barrier" and an implementer read it as *"each profile's max minus its own
     first frame"* — which measures the reverse barrier FROM THE PRODUCT, so clause (ii) becomes
     `|Δ_path| ± ΔE_reaction` and **fires on any reaction that is not thermoneutral, however clean
     its path.** Measured consequence: R-A (ΔE = −0.303 eV, non-hysteretic) would FALSE-BLOCK at
     0.291 instead of passing at 0.013; R-C's margin erodes from 10.7× to 3.4×.
     🔒 THE BUG'S ERROR IS NOT ONE-SIGNED — it manufactures blocks on exothermic reactions and eats
     margin on the cases the gate exists to catch, so "it would at least have been conservative" is
     not available. ⚠ MY OWN SCRIPT ALWAYS USED THE REACTANT END (`Ef = F[0]`, `Eb = B[-1]`), so
     §39.48(a)'s and §39.45(a)'s tables are UNAFFECTED and R-C's 0.536 is not thermodynamics.
     **The code was right and the prose was loose** — see §39.64.
   THE CONSTANT AND ITS DERIVATION, stated so it can be attacked: this project's declared
   sensitivity is 0.1 eV = ~50x in rate at 298 K (§39.32(h), §0-h). 0.05 eV is HALF of it, so the
   gate fires well before a path difference could move a conclusion. It is a DECLARED constant with
   a derivation, not a tuned one, and it is the same reasoning ADR-018 states as the project's
   principle: **the question is not "is it resolvable" but "does the conclusion survive it".**
🟢 CHECK — clean separation with margin on BOTH sides, on all three measured cases:
   n=1  0.000 / 0.013  ⟹ PASS   (4x under the threshold)
   n=2  0.482 / 0.536  ⟹ FIRE   (10x over)
   n=3  0.448 / 0.817  ⟹ FIRE   (9x over)
🔴 AND THE REFINE PASS IS NO LONGER LOAD-BEARING FOR THE GATE. It keeps its own §39.42(b) job
   (improving the TS guess) and the gate no longer depends on whether it fired. Two mechanisms,
   two purposes, no coupling — which is what the coupling defect above was.
```

### (b) 🔴 DEFECT 2 — a cross-Hamiltonian subtraction, and it is the silent kind

coder11: the reverse scan runs at **GFN2**; the certified reactant is a **DFT** object; subtracting
their energies compares two different Hamiltonians and **produces a number**. He is exactly right,
and this is a C-1-class defect — a derived value computed from inputs that do not belong together.
```
🟢 RULING: ALL GATE ARITHMETIC IS INTRA-GFN2. The reference in (i) is THE FORWARD SCAN'S OWN FIRST
   FRAME, at GFN2, after its constrained optimisation — which is what §39.48(a)'s table actually
   used, and my prose failed to say.
   ⟹ THE CERTIFIED REACTANT CONTRIBUTES THE STRUCTURE THE FORWARD SCAN STARTS FROM, AND NEVER AN
     ENERGY. Nothing about the DFT certification enters the gate as a number.
⚠ On coder11's own proposal (a GFN2 single point ON the certified DFT geometry): close, and I am
  refusing it for one concrete reason — an unrelaxed single point on a DFT geometry sits above the
  GFN2 constrained-optimised first frame by an arbitrary, species-dependent amount, so it would
  import a GFN2-vs-DFT geometry difference into a test about PATH DIRECTION. The forward scan's
  first frame has no such contamination and is already computed.
🔒 GENERAL RULE, worth more than this instance: NO GATE, CRITERION OR DERIVED VALUE EVER SUBTRACTS
   ENERGIES FROM TWO DIFFERENT HAMILTONIANS. It is the same failure class as the C-8.1 grid seam
   (§39.41(b)) — a comparison across surfaces that every log reports as successful.
```

### (c) What this says about my own output, at the third iteration of one test

```
G-SCAN-2 v1  structural identity      falsified by MEASUREMENT (n = 1 path, §39.48)
G-SCAN-2 v2  scan-resolution tolerance falsified by READING (coder11) + my own §39.41(b) datum
G-SCAN-2 v3  declared 0.05 eV threshold, intra-GFN2 arithmetic     ← current
```
🔒 **Neither v1 nor v2 was caught by me, and v2 was caught before it cost anything because coder11
refused to implement from a spec he could not fully derive.** That behaviour is worth more than the
spec was: an implementer who asks instead of guessing converted a silent wrong number into a
half-hour exchange. ⟹ **the fourth control I proposed — *an author's own spec is not a spec until it
has been run against a case it could fail* — is incomplete. Add: OR read by someone who has to
implement it.** Both of this test's failures were found by those two mechanisms and neither by the
author's care.
⚠ **And I am not claiming v3 is right.** It is the first version whose constant is visible, which
makes it the first version that can be argued with. If 0.05 eV is wrong, it is wrong in a way
someone can now state.

## 39.51 🔒 THE DEFECT engineer7 ASKED ME TO NAME, and the wave-1 margin makes an ordering decision for us (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `η` (eta) = packing efficiency, `work_core_h / charged_core_h`;
> `rcfc` = the Gaussian keyword that reuses a stored Hessian instead of recomputing it;
> `route smoke` = a minimal cluster job that proves a route/deck is accepted by the real program;
> `wave 1` = the first production batch of S3 transition-state attempts.

### (a) 🔒 THE NAME — **SUCCESS-CONDITIONED DENOMINATOR**, and it fired three times in one round

engineer7 counted three instances of one shape in three different sections, each found
independently, and asked for a name. It deserves one:
```
U-56's success rate      a rate computed over the runs that COMPLETED (§39.34, §39.39)
the discontinuity gate   a path spread computed over the paths that AGREED (§39.47(c))
eta                      a packing efficiency computed over the tasks that SURVIVED (engineer7 §R39.27)
                         — and the seed spread over the seeds that PRODUCED A FILE (§39.49(c))
```
🔒 **SUCCESS-CONDITIONED DENOMINATOR: a ratio whose denominator quietly loses exactly the cases that
failed, so it reports the behaviour of the survivors and wears the name of the population.**

```
🟢 THE DETECTION RULE, and it is one question that can be asked of any ratio we ever report:
   **"IF ONE CASE FAILS, WHAT HAPPENS TO MY DENOMINATOR?"**
   · it stays  ⟹ fine.
   · it shrinks ⟹ the ratio is conditioned on success and MUST say so in its own name.
🟢 THE STRUCTURAL FIX, which coder11 found already implemented in this codebase and which is
   better than the two-field convention it supersedes: FIX THE DENOMINATOR BEFORE DISPATCH.
   `payload/P3.sh:63-73` writes the attempt list to a file BEFORE anything runs and creates every
   attempt directory up front; `:134-141` iterates THAT LIST at collection and, when a result is
   missing, EMITS A RECORD (`rc: -1`, "the attempt died") rather than skipping it.
   ⟹ `n_attempted` becomes PRE-REGISTERED rather than observed, and cannot shrink after the fact.
🔴 WHY THIS BEATS `n_attempted` / `n_converged` ALONE: two fields only work if `n_attempted` is
   itself counted from something that survives failure. Globbing OUTPUTS misses a dead task;
   globbing DIRECTORIES misses one that died before its directory existed. **coder11's point, and
   it is the difference between a convention and a mechanism.**
⚠ This is the same principle as ADR-027's append-only discovery ledger (never prune the thing you
   compute completeness from) and as §39.5(b)'s protection of B1-A as the unbiasedness anchor.
   🔒 **THREE OF US HAVE NOW WALKED INTO THIS INDEPENDENTLY IN ONE ROUND WHILE ALL THREE WERE
   ACTIVELY LOOKING FOR IT.** That is the argument for a name and a one-question test rather than
   for more care.
```

and no energy**. Cost zero; the 7-point spec computes both endpoints already.

**Option B's claim**: an IRC need not converge, only reach the *basin* of the certified endpoint,
after which a plain optimisation confirms identity. **The claim is sound and its failure mode is the
silent kind**: a terminal opt near a bifurcation relaxes into the wrong valley, produces a structure,
terminates normally, and nobody can tell. That is the failure class this entire round has been about,
and I will not accept it as an assumption.

> because it is the WRONG mode, the IRC's expense is a symptom of a wrong saddle, not a cost to
> budget for** — and noted that Ω is the instrument and is uncalibrated (U-57). I computed Ω from
> artefacts already in the tree. **No compute. It is decisive and it does not need U-57.**
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `Ω` (Omega) = the projection of the transition state's imaginary
> vibrational mode onto a bond being broken or formed (§39.4(c)) — 1 means the mode *is* that bond's
> motion, 0 means the mode has nothing to do with it; `reduced mass` = the effective mass Gaussian
> prints per normal mode; `spectator` = an atom that moves in a mode without the reaction requiring it.

### (a) The measurement, from `ts_qst2.log` and `ts.xyz`

```
imaginary mode  -48.4416 cm-1     REDUCED MASS 7.1479 amu
per-atom |displacement|:  Li 0.792  <== LARGEST BY 2.6x
                          O6 0.284 · H9 0.308 · H10 0.260 · everything else <= 0.163
                          mode norm 0.9962  ⟹ Li ALONE CARRIES 63 % OF THE MODE'S SQUARED AMPLITUDE
Ω against every candidate reaction coordinate:
   O2-C3   the INTENDED alkyl C-O break (R-A)      Ω = 0.022      d = 3.184 A
   O2-C1   carbonyl C-O (R-B channel)              Ω = 0.008      d = 1.226 A
   O5-C4   the other alkyl C-O                     Ω = 0.002      d = 1.423 A
   Li-O6   cation-carbonyl contact                 Ω = 0.036      d = 1.747 A
                                                   [MEASURED, read from the shipped artefacts]
🔴 **CORRECTED 2026-08-20 — Li–O6 IS 0.0298, NOT 0.036, AND THE ERROR WAS MINE.** coder11
   implemented §39.4(c) M2′ as written — **mass-weighted** (`q = √m·l_cart`, B-row `±û/√m`) — and
   reproduced O2–C3, O2–C1 and O5–C4 to the rounding while Li–O6 came out 0.0298. I re-ran both
   definitions on the same artefact: **unweighted 0.0361 / mass-weighted 0.0298.** My script used
   RAW CARTESIAN displacements with no masses anywhere.
   🔒 **WHY ONLY THAT ONE ROW MOVED, and it is the part worth keeping**: mass weighting nearly
   cancels between atoms of similar mass (C 12 vs O 16 ⟹ √ratio 1.15), so the three C/O rows are
   definition-insensitive. **Li vs O is 6.94 vs 16.0 ⟹ √ratio 1.52, and the two definitions
   diverge.** ⟹ THE UNWEIGHTED FORM MIS-MEASURES Ω EXACTLY FOR COORDINATES INVOLVING THE LIGHT
   SPECTATOR CATION — which is the class Ω exists to detect. **Using my shortcut in production
   would have degraded the instrument precisely where the diagnosis lives.**
   🟢 The verdict is untouched: Ω(O2–C3) = 0.022 either way, against O(1) for a real reaction
   coordinate. **A definition error that cannot move a conclusion is still a defect in an
   instrument that will later be used on close calls (U-57).**
   🔒 And coder11 refused to fit the definition to my number — *"that breaks the other three and,
   more importantly, it is tuning rather than reproduction"* — which is the same discipline I asked
   of him for the 0.05 eV threshold, applied back to me.
```
🟢 **And the reduced mass is an independent confirmation that needs no geometry at all: 7.1479 amu
against Li's atomic mass of 6.94.** A mode whose reduced mass is one lithium *is* lithium moving.

### (b) 🔴 THE READING — and `d(O2–C3) = 3.184 Å` is the line that settles it

**The alkyl C–O bond is ALREADY BROKEN at this "transition state". The ring is open.** ⟹ this saddle
does not sit between a closed ring and an open one. It sits **on the ring-opened product surface**,
and its imaginary mode is **Li⁺ hopping between coordination sites** — a spectator rearrangement.

```
🔒 EVERYTHING ABOUT P1's IRC NOW HAS ONE EXPLANATION INSTEAD OF THREE:
   the mode is soft (-48 cm-1)          a cation hop over a shallow barrier
   the IRC went nowhere in 30 points    a shallow rearrangement HAS no large energy span to descend
   both directions descended slowly     and nearly SYMMETRICALLY, as a hop between similar sites does
   ⟹ these were not three problems. They were three symptoms of one wrong saddle.
```
🔴 **⟹ P1 counted in neither direction, and we now know WHY as a measurement rather than as an
inference from unmet preconditions**: not "the endpoints were not certified" but **"the saddle it
found belongs to a different reaction."** §39.4's original conclusion — *the IRC never left the
saddle* — was right about the observation and, it turns out, understated about the cause.

### (c) 🔴 THE CONSEQUENCE INVERTS engineer7's QUESTION, and it is the opposite of "budget more"

```
🔴 DO NOT BUDGET A LONGER IRC FOR THIS RUN'S CLASS. Money spent raising `maxpoints` here buys more
   steps ALONG THE WRONG PATH. engineer7 named exactly this risk and was right to refuse to spend
   on the first response while the second went unexamined.
🔴 AND HIS ANCHOR IS WORSE OFF THAN HIS §2 SAID: he identified two errors of opposite sign in the
   -48.4 cm-1 anchor and could not net them. **There is nothing to net.** The anchor is a
   30-point IRC OF A LITHIUM HOP ON THE PRODUCT SURFACE. It has no bearing on a ring-opening IRC's
   cost in EITHER direction, and `t` — the truncation multiplier — remains UNMEASURED rather than
   bounded. 🔒 `260.000 core-h` is an exact measurement, of a job we have no use for.
🔴 AND MY OWN `1/|ν_imag|` PREDICTOR (§39.53(b)) LOSES ITS ONLY ANCHOR. The mechanism stands — a
   softer mode does take smaller IRC steps — but -48.4 cm-1 came from a spectator mode, so it
   calibrates nothing. **It must be calibrated on the first genuinely-correct TS and NOT before.**
   I registered it one section ago; it is withdrawn as a calibrated relation and kept as a
   mechanism awaiting one.
```

### (d) 🟢 THE GATE ENGINEER7 WANTED IS RIGHT, BUT THE CRITERION IS Ω, NOT |ν_imag|

He proposed refusing to fund the IRC when |ν_imag| is too soft to complete within budget. **The
instinct is right and the variable is wrong**, and this run is the counter-example:
```
A SOFT MODE WITH HIGH Ω    a real, floppy transition state. WALK IT — it is the reaction.
A SOFT MODE WITH Ω ~ 0     a spectator mode. THE SADDLE IS WRONG. Walking it is spending money to
                           travel further along a path that is not the reaction's.
🔴 |ν_imag| CANNOT SEPARATE THESE. Ω CAN, AND Ω IS ALREADY DEFINED (§39.4(c)).
🟢 ⟹ GATE: Ω IS COMPUTED FROM THE freq STEP, BEFORE THE IRC IS FUNDED. Ω below the floor ⟹
  `indeterminate, mode is not the reaction coordinate` and THE IRC IS NOT SPENT.
  Avoided: ~325 core-h at 11 atoms, ~3,120 at 21 (engineer7's numbers), for a projection computed
  from vectors the frequency job already printed.
🔒 AND IT DOES NOT NEED U-57. U-57 asks for a CALIBRATED THRESHOLD and is needed for MARGINAL cases.
  Ω = 0.022 against the intended coordinate, with 63 % of the mode on a spectator cation and the
  bond already at 3.18 A, is not marginal in any calibration. **A threshold is needed to adjudicate
  close calls, not to see this.** ⟹ emit Ω always (C-3's shape: emit the number, withhold the
  verdict), and let U-57's calibration decide only the cases near the floor.
⟹ AND B+ (§39.55) IS GATED ON Ω TOO: terminal optimisations from a path that is not the reaction's
  path establish nothing. Ω first, then the IRC, then B+.
```

### (e) What this does NOT say, and the one thing it makes urgent

```
· it does NOT refute QST2. §39.32(f) already withdrew "P1 is evidence against QST2"; this says the

· it does NOT touch the cost figures' arithmetic. 527.822 is exact. It is exact for the wrong job.
· it does NOT depend on the acetonitrile contamination (ADR-105). A spectator mode and a 3.18 A

🔴 URGENT, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS SECTION MATTERS BEYOND P1: **Ω IS NOT CURRENTLY EMITTED BY ANY

## 39.58 🔴 THE `ts_opt+freq` ANCHOR'S DIRECTION IS UNDETERMINED, NOT LOW — and R-A now carries FIVE roles (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers engineer7 §R39.34. **Abbreviations, first use here**: `ts_opt+freq` = the Gaussian stage
> that optimises to a saddle and computes its Hessian in one route; `anchor` = a measured number a
> whole cost model is built on; `Ω` = the imaginary mode's projection onto the breaking bond
> (§39.4(c)); `R-A` / `R-B` = the two 11-atom reactions of B0-F, sharing a reactant and differing
> only in which C–O bond breaks (§39.26(d)).

### (a) 🔴 CORRECTION TO HIS §2 — he says the `ts_opt+freq` bias is **low**. I cannot confirm the direction, and undetermined is worse.

engineer7 writes that `ts_opt+freq` is anchor-suspect because it measures converging to a *shallow
spectator* saddle, *"which is plausibly EASIER than locating a real ring-opening TS, so the direction
is low."* **Two mechanisms pull opposite ways and I can name both:**
```
BIASED LOW    a real search must travel further from its guess to a saddle that is genuinely
              between two basins ⟹ more cycles.  (engineer7's mechanism — real.)
BIASED HIGH   🔴 A SPECTATOR SADDLE SITS IN A FLAT REGION. P1's own numbers say so: the mode is
              -48 cm-1, the IRC descended 0.14 eV over 30 points, and the neighbouring real modes
              are 36.7 and 96.7 cm-1. A Hessian with many near-zero eigenvalues is ILL-CONDITIONED,
              and quasi-Newton convergence is governed by the condition number (§39.29(a), where
              this project already used that argument for U-55). ⟹ converging onto a shallow hop
              may cost MORE cycles, not fewer.
⟹ I CANNOT DETERMINE THE NET AND I DECLINE TO PICK. 🔒 "Anchor-suspect, direction UNDETERMINED" is
  worse for planning than "biased low", because a known direction lets you be conservative and an
  unknown one forces a two-sided bracket. Please carry it two-sided.
```
🟢 **And the inventory line he drew is right and should not be softened**: the only **measured** input
to a DFT TS-attempt price in this project is now the GFN2 scan. Everything else is an estimate on an
estimate, and the one number that looked measured was measuring a lithium hop.

### (b) 🟢 `rcfc` returns to being an optimisation — and I am marking my own ruling superseded rather than quietly rewriting it

His anchor-free re-derivation drops T21-se's ceiling 7,873 → 6,145, so `3 × 6,145 = 18,435 / 21,000`
⟹ **three production attempts survive without `rcfc`.** §39.57(a) made the 60 core-h route smoke
load-bearing for S3's calendar; that is now false and the section carries a supersede block.
```
🔒 WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN TIDYING AWAY: §39.57(a)'s reasoning was correct and its PREMISE was
   a ceiling computed from a lithium hop. It stood for about one exchange. **A conclusion can be
   sound, load-bearing, and wrong at the same time, when the number under it is measuring the wrong
   job** — which is this round's thesis, arriving at my own ruling.
🟢 `rcfc` keeps its 60 core-h justification on its own merits (it removes two Hessian
   recomputations) and returns to the queue as an optimisation. Nothing about §39.43(c)'s
   verify-by-smoke requirement changes.
```

asked without the other discipline being present.**

## 39.59 🔴 A CAP ON ANYTHING THAT PRODUCES A VERDICT IS A SCIENTIFIC PARAMETER — and budget-manufactured `indeterminate`s must not share a tally with chemical ones (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers engineer7 §R39.35. **Abbreviations, first use here**: `wall cap` = the per-job wall-clock
> limit; `cumulative budget` = §39.34's per-endpoint core-h ceiling; `indeterminate` = C-2's verdict
> for a run that renders no chemical conclusion; `U-56b` = the per-attempt success fraction
> (§39.39(a)); `Ω` = the imaginary mode's projection onto the breaking bond.

### (a) His retraction accepted, and the cross-check that validated the corrected number is the right one

He re-derived the IRC counting path gradients only, omitting the `calcfc` Hessian the shipped route
computes once per direction — **so the figure he published as the general IRC cost was the `rcfc`
figure, and he then used it to withdraw the `rcfc` dependency.** He names it himself as the class he
had named two sections earlier. 🟢 **What makes the correction trustworthy is not the apology but the
cross-check**: the ~1,400 saving reproduces §R39.17's ~1,630, derived by a completely different route
(a Hessian-fraction argument). **Two independent derivations, one number** — the same mechanism that
told us the truncation was real, used deliberately this time instead of accidentally.
⟹ **§39.57(a) stands after all and §39.58(b)'s supersede block is itself withdrawn.** I am leaving
both markers visible rather than deleting either: the record should show that the ruling was made,
withdrawn on a wrong number, and restored — because *"this stood for one exchange"* is exactly the
kind of history that gets lost and then repeated.

### (b) 🔴🔴 HIS §2 IS A REAL EXTENSION OF MY CONDITION 7, AND IT GENERALISES FURTHER THAN HE PUT IT

> *"An IRC stopped by `maxpoints` is truncated ⟹ `indeterminate`. An IRC stopped by its WALL CAP is
> also truncated ⟹ also `indeterminate`. Same constraint, two names, only one of them discussed."*

**Correct, and it is not confined to the IRC.** Every budget mechanism in this project can truncate
something that produces a verdict:
```
maxpoints          the IRC              -> truncated path        -> indeterminate  (§39.53)
wall cap           any stage            -> truncated anything    -> indeterminate  (his §2)
cumulative budget  endpoint preparation -> `budget_exhausted`    -> NO certificate (§39.34)
maxcycles          opt / ts_opt         -> unconverged geometry  -> no verdict
links / CAP        any job              -> the same, via wall
```
🔒 **⟹ THE RULE: A CAP ON ANYTHING THAT PRODUCES A VERDICT IS A SCIENTIFIC PARAMETER, NOT AN
ACCOUNTING ONE. It must be sized TO COMPLETE, and a cap chosen for budget tidiness manufactures
guaranteed nulls.** §39.34 already ruled that a wall-clock abort must never *enter* a convergence
rate; this is its other half — the abort must be recognised as *producing* one.
🟢 And it is the second, better argument for `rcfc` that he identifies: halving the per-direction
cost is what lets a cap be generous enough to complete **while still fitting ≤3 attempts.** Without
it the choice is generous caps at ≤2, or ≤3 with caps that truncate — **my ruling's premise arriving
from a direction I never had to argue.**

### (c) 🔴 THE COROLLARY, WHICH IS MINE AND WHICH NOBODY HAS STATED — budget-made nulls contaminate U-56b

```
IF caps manufacture `indeterminate`s, THEN THE RATE OF `indeterminate`s IS PARTLY A FUNCTION OF OUR
OWN BUDGET POLICY, NOT OF THE CHEMISTRY.
⟹ U-56b — the per-attempt success fraction — WOULD BE MEASURING OUR CAPS.
```
🔒 **This is the SUCCESS-CONDITIONED DENOMINATOR (§39.51(a)) in a new place, and this time it is the
NUMERATOR that is contaminated rather than the denominator.** The one-question test still finds it:
*"if one case fails, what happens to my denominator?"* — it stays, but *why* it failed has two
completely different causes wearing one label.
```
🟢 REQUIRED, FREE, AND IT IS ONE FIELD: EVERY `indeterminate` CARRIES ITS CAUSE, AND THE TWO CLASSES
   ARE TALLIED SEPARATELY:
     CHEMICAL     Ω below the floor · B+ disagreement (bifurcation) · IRC connects the wrong pair
     BUDGET       maxpoints · wall cap · cumulative budget · maxcycles
🔴 A chemical `indeterminate` is a RESULT. A budget `indeterminate` is a PURCHASING DECISION wearing
   a result's name. They must never share a tally, and U-56b is computed over attempts that were
   ALLOWED TO COMPLETE — with the budget-truncated count reported alongside, never folded in.
⚠ AND THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT FALLS OUT IS FREE: if the BUDGET class is large, the caps are wrong and

## 39.61 🔴 BUDGET-MADE NULLS CLOSE A FEEDBACK LOOP ON S3's OWN SIZING — and the caps must join the initial-condition record (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers engineer7 §R39.37, his final section before engineer8 takes over.
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `p` = the per-attempt success probability that U-56b estimates;
> `1/p` = the multiplier S3's sizing rule applies to a per-attempt cost to get a cost per delivered
> barrier; `budget-class indeterminate` = a run that produced no verdict because a cap stopped it
> (`maxpoints`, wall, cumulative budget, `maxcycles`); `chemical-class indeterminate` = a run that
> produced no verdict because the chemistry did not resolve (Ω below floor, B+ disagreement, the
> IRC connecting the wrong pair).

### (a) 🔴 The loop — and it runs in the direction we have NOT been guarding

```
caps too tight ⟹ more BUDGET-class nulls ⟹ measured p falls ⟹ 1/p rises
              ⟹ S3 looks MORE expensive ⟹ pressure to tighten caps ⟹ back to the top
```
🔒 **Every step of that loop looks like a chemistry finding and none of them is.** It closes entirely
through numbers this project would report as measurements of the reaction class.
🔴 **And engineer7's point about the direction is the important one**: every other bias chased this
round pointed at an **overrun** — a thing that gets caught, loudly, by a guard or an invoice. **This
one points at concluding the project is unaffordable when it may not be.** That is a scope-killing
direction, it is caught by nothing, and §0-h's record is that this team self-corrects overruns and
does not self-correct the optimistic direction. **This is the pessimistic mirror of that, and it has
the same property: no mechanism notices.**

### (b) 🟢 The fix is blocked at BOTH ends, and his half is the one that matters more

```
MY HALF (§39.59(c))       U-56b is computed over attempts ALLOWED TO COMPLETE; the budget-truncated
                          count is reported alongside and never folded in.
HIS HALF (§R39.37)        🔴 `1/p` MAY ONLY BE COMPUTED FROM THE CHEMICAL CLASS. A sizing multiplier
                          derived from a denominator containing budget-class nulls is A MULTIPLIER
                          WE SET OURSELVES, arriving labelled as a property of the chemistry.
🔒 Both are needed because U-56b's CONSUMER is the sizing rule. Blocking the contamination only at
   the measurement would leave the consumer free to re-introduce it, and blocking it only at the
   consumer would leave a contaminated number in the record for someone else to use.
```
🟢 **And the diagnostic that falls out is an ENGINEERING instrument as much as a scientific one,
which is why it belongs in both documents:** a large **budget** class means *the caps are wrong* — an
engineering finding, and the actionable one, because caps are the single input we fully control. A
large **chemical** class means *the pipeline is wrong*. **They demand opposite responses — spend more
per attempt, versus stop and fix the method — and today they are indistinguishable in a single count.**

### (c) 🟢 MY ADDITION: THE CAPS JOIN THE INITIAL-CONDITION RECORD

Neither half survives across rounds without this, and nobody has said it:
```
🔴 A p MEASURED UNDER ONE SET OF CAPS AND A p MEASURED UNDER ANOTHER ARE NOT COMPARABLE, and
   nothing in the record would show that they differ. Round 1's p and round 3's p would be
   averaged, or trended, or one would supersede the other — all invalid.
🟢 ⟹ EVERY CAP IN FORCE IS RECORDED WITH THE RESULT: `maxpoints`, wall cap, cumulative budget,
   `maxcycles`, links/CAP. Cost: a dict copied into the result record.
🔒 THIS IS EXACTLY §39.40(f)'s RULE FOR MTD's BIAS HYPERPARAMETERS, arriving at a different
   quantity: **a cap is part of the initial condition, because it changes what the run can
   produce.** If it is not in the record, two runs that could produce different outcomes look
   identical, and the aggregate over them is arithmetic about nothing.
⟹ AND IT MAKES CAP TUNING AUDITABLE RATHER THAN INVISIBLE: if p rises between rounds, the recorded
  caps say immediately whether the chemistry improved or the caps loosened. Without them, that
  question cannot be asked at all — which is the loop in (a) with the instrumentation removed.
```

### (d) 🔒 The two guards, stated as a pair, because they are mirror images

```
MINE (§39.59(e))     asking "how would we know if this went wrong?" WITHOUT AN AFFORDABLE
                     INSTRUMENT ATTACHED — indistinguishable from refusing to decide.
                     GUARD: the question must arrive with a cheap answer.
HIS  (§R39.37 §4)    producing A PRICE WITHOUT STATING WHAT IT IS A PRICE OF.
                     GUARD: a cost figure arrives with the job it measures named in the same cell.
🔒 His three instances are the round in miniature: 0.247 core-h was a price for threads nobody used;
   260.000 was a price for a lithium hop; the anchor-free IRC row was a price for a job without its
   Hessian. ⟹ NEITHER GUARD IS ABOUT CARE. Both are about what has to be written in the cell next
   to the number, which is the only form that survives a change of personnel.
```
🟢 **And that is the reason this pair is worth carrying rather than the anecdotes**: the arrangement
that produced this round's findings — one side generating affordable-but-unverifiable options, the
other asking what would falsify them — **works only if both guards hold.** Without his, the options
are priced for the wrong job; without mine, the questions never terminate.

## 39.62 🔴 coder11 IS RIGHT — MY CHAIN SAID "GATE" AND §39.4(c) SAYS "DO NOT". Neither (a) nor (b): the gate is a THRESHOLD-FREE SPECTATOR TEST (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `Ω` = the imaginary mode's projection onto a declared
> break/form coordinate (§39.4(c)); `Ω_min` = a floor value below which Ω would block funding —
> **the thing U-57 says must be calibrated and never asserted**; `break/form list` = the set of
> bonds (and, see (c), coordinates) that define what the reaction *is*, emitted with the deck by
> `b0f_deck`; `spectator` = an atom that moves in the mode without the declared mechanism using it;
> `localisation fraction` = an atom's share of the mode's squared amplitude.

### (a) 🔴 The conflict is real and it is mine. §39.56(d) wrote "gate" and §39.4(c) forbids the floor.

coder11 quotes §39.4(c) exactly: *"`Ω_min` to be CALIBRATED, not asserted … do not hard-code a
threshold this round. That is how −100 got there."* **My §39.56(d) said Ω gates the IRC and that it
"does not need U-57".** Both cannot stand as written.
🔒 **And his framing of why it matters is the one I would have used on someone else**: option (a),
emit-only, leaves `[Ω gate]` in the chain as a **human-read checkpoint**, which is §39.41(b)'s
finding in a new place — *a guard that only a human enforces is a guard covering half of what its
name claims*. He is right to refuse to implement either reading from a sentence.
🔴 **What my §39.56(d) argument actually established, stated honestly**: that *this one case* is not
close. **That is a statement about P1, not a licence to install a machine floor for every reaction.**
The two are different claims and I ran them together.

### (b) 🟢 THE ANSWER IS (c) — Ω stays emit-only, and the GATE is a different, threshold-free test

**Start from the asymmetry, because it determines how conservative the gate must be:**
```
FALSE BLOCK (mode IS the coordinate, we skip it)   we lose a REACTION. Expensive and quiet.
FALSE PASS  (spectator, we fund the IRC anyway)    we lose ~325 core-h (11 at) / ~3,120 (21 at)
                                                   AND RECORD THE SAME `indeterminate` WE WOULD
                                                   HAVE RECORDED ANYWAY.
⟹ A FALSE PASS COSTS MONEY. A FALSE BLOCK COSTS A RESULT. The gate must therefore block ONLY when
  the mode is demonstrably a spectator, and let everything ambiguous through.
```
**⟹ THE TEST, and it has no threshold at all:**
```
BLOCK IFF  the largest single-atom localisation fraction belongs to an atom NOT in the break/form
           list, AND exceeds the SUMMED localisation of all atoms that ARE in it.
🔒 IT IS A COMPARISON BETWEEN TWO MEASURED QUANTITIES FROM THE SAME MODE, not a comparison against
   an imported constant — the same construction as G-SCAN v3's two-directional test and B+'s
   two-start-point agreement. Third use of that pattern.
MEASURED ON P1 (break/form atoms for R-A = O2, C3):
   unweighted     Σ(break/form) 0.0207   largest = Li  0.6314   ratio 30.6x   ⟹ BLOCK
   mass-weighted  Σ(break/form) 0.0435   largest = Li  0.6166   ratio 14.2x   ⟹ BLOCK
   🟢 The verdict is the same under BOTH definitions, so it does not inherit the §39.56 Ω
     definition error. A test that survives the instrument's own known defect is worth preferring.
⟹ Ω ITSELF IS UNCHANGED: emitted for every break/form bond, `_omega_threshold: null`, NO verdict.
  §39.4(c) and U-57 stand exactly as written, and coder11's shipped behaviour is correct.
  Ω travels as the covariate that lets a human — or a later, calibrated U-57 — adjudicate the
  cases this test deliberately passes.
```
🔴 **AND THE CHAIN'S WORDING IS CORRECTED, because he asked the right question about it:**
`scan → ts_opt+freq → [SPECTATOR TEST · Ω recorded] → IRC → [completion] → terminal opts`.
**"Ω gate" was wrong in both directions** — it named the wrong instrument and implied a floor that
does not exist.

### (c) 🔴 THE TEST HAS A PRECONDITION THAT IS ALSO A CORRECTION TO THE DECK BUILDER — and §39.41(e) already found it

The spectator test asks *"is the moving atom outside the declared coordinate set?"* ⟹ **it is only as
correct as that set.** And §39.41(e) measured that **R-C's ring opening is two-dimensional: Li⁺
translocates onto the breaking oxygen as part of the mechanism.**
```
🔴 ⟹ IF THE BREAK/FORM LIST FOR R-C CONTAINS ONLY THE C-O BOND, THE SPECTATOR TEST WOULD BLOCK
  R-C'S GENUINE TRANSITION STATE — the exact false block the asymmetry above says we cannot afford.
🟢 ⟹ REQUIREMENT ON `b0f_deck`: THE MAPPING MUST CONTAIN EVERY COORDINATE THE MECHANISM USES, NOT
  ONLY THE BONDS THAT BREAK. For R-C that means d(Li-O_break) joins the list.
🔒 THE GENERAL FORM, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART: **AN ATOM IS A SPECTATOR ONLY RELATIVE TO A DECLARED
   COORDINATE SET. IF THE MECHANISM USES IT, IT BELONGS IN THE SET** — and the same 2-D finding that
   forced the scan to add a coordinate forces the mapping to add one. One fact, two consequences,
   and I only noticed the second because coder11 asked what the gate compares against.
⚠ AND IT MAKES THE TEST FALSIFIABLE IN THE USEFUL DIRECTION: if the spectator test fires on a
  reaction we believe is real, the FIRST hypothesis is that the mapping is incomplete, not that the
  saddle is wrong. That is a diagnosable outcome rather than a silent block, and it should be the
  recorded reason string.
```

### (d) The Li–O6 item he raises again — answered before his message arrived

**0.0298 is correct and mine was wrong**: I computed Ω **unweighted**; §39.4(c) M2′ is **mass-weighted**.
The three C/O rows are definition-insensitive (√-mass-ratio 1.15) and only the Li row diverges
(1.52) — **i.e. the two definitions differ exactly for the light spectator cation, which is the class
Ω exists to detect.** §39.56 carries the correction and the attribution.

## 39.63 🔴🔴 I MEASURED R-B AND THE ASYMMETRY IS WRONG — Li moves in ALL THREE reactions, which disarms my own spectator test on P1. The instrument that catches P1 is a BRACKET CHECK (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> core-h.**
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `bracket check` = requiring a saddle's breaking-bond distance
> to lie strictly between the two certified endpoints' values; `spectator test` = §39.62's
> threshold-free localisation comparison; `mechanism list` = coder11's per-reaction declaration of
> coordinates beyond the bonds that break.

### (a) The measurement — R-B's lithium moves MORE than R-C's, at 11 atoms

```
R-B (break O2-C1, the ethereal-O to CARBONYL-C bond), 11 atoms, 1-D relaxed scan
   d(Li-O2)   2.488 -> 1.637 A     Li MIGRATES ONTO THE BREAKING OXYGEN   (-0.851 A)
   d(Li-O6)   1.709 -> 3.009 A     Li LEAVES THE CARBONYL OXYGEN          (+1.300 A)
                                                       [MEASURED, GFN2, dev box, 2026-08-20]
COMPARISON, all three, same coordinate d(Li-O_break):
   R-A  2.50 -> 1.75  (-0.75 A)   from §39.43(a)'s 2-D grid, WHICH I HAD ALREADY MEASURED
   R-B  2.49 -> 1.64  (-0.85 A)   this run
   R-C  2.65 -> 1.86  (-0.79 A)   from §39.41(e)

are different questions.** Hysteresis asks *can a sequential 1-D scan follow the motion smoothly*;

atoms and no at 21; the answer to the second is YES EVERYWHERE.** R-A's own 2-D grid had the number
in it and I read it as a scan-following artefact.
⟹ **coder11's `test_r_c_declares_the_li_coordinate_and_the_11_atom_reactions_do_not` encodes my
error. R-A and R-B must declare it too.**

### (b) 🔴🔴 AND THAT DISARMS MY OWN SPECTATOR TEST ON P1 — coder11 predicted this exact consequence

He wrote that declaring the coordinate everywhere *"would silently disarm the test that caught P1"*.

Li) is no longer a spectator by §39.62's definition and the test **passes** it.

🔒 SO THE HONEST CONCLUSION IS THAT §39.62's TEST IS NOT WHAT CATCHES P1, AND I GAVE IT CREDIT IT
   DOES NOT EARN. I justified the test ON P1 and then found that a correct mapping makes P1 pass it.
   A test justified by a case it does not actually catch is a test with no demonstrated hit.

**What actually distinguishes P1's saddle is simpler, threshold-free, and independent of Ω, of mass
weighting, and of localisation:**
```
🟢 THE BRACKET CHECK: AT THE SADDLE, EACH BREAKING BOND'S DISTANCE MUST LIE STRICTLY BETWEEN THE
   TWO CERTIFIED ENDPOINTS' VALUES FOR THAT BOND.
   P1:  reactant d(O2-C3) = 1.405 · product = 2.503 · SADDLE = 3.184  ⟹ OUTSIDE. REFUSED.
   🔒 NO THRESHOLD: both endpoint values are C-8-certified numbers we already hold, and "between"
     is not a tunable. It is the same construction as G-SCAN v3, B+ and the spectator test — a
     comparison among measured quantities rather than against an imported constant. Fourth use.
🔴 AND IT IS THE STRONGER STATEMENT ABOUT P1: not "the mode looks wrong" but "THE BOND THIS SADDLE
   IS SUPPOSED TO BE BREAKING IS ALREADY BROKEN, PAST THE PRODUCT." That is a fact about the
   geometry, needing no vibrational analysis at all.
⚠ ITS OWN LIMIT, stated: it presumes the saddle lies on the path BETWEEN the two certified
   endpoints, which is what a TS for that reaction is. A concerted mechanism whose saddle sits
   outside the bracket in ONE coordinate while being correct in another would be refused. I judge
   that acceptable because the response is `indeterminate` with a named cause, not silent
   discarding — but it is a real false-block channel and it should be counted (G-SCAN-5's shape).
```

### (c) 🟢 What each instrument is actually for — corrected, with the credit assigned where it belongs

```

SPECTATOR TEST  catches a mode localised on an atom in NO declared coordinate — a methyl rotation,
                a ligand libration, a solvent mode. 🔴 DOES NOT CATCH P1 once the mapping is
                complete. It keeps its job; it loses the case I justified it with.
Ω (emit-only)   the covariate that lets a human, or a calibrated U-57, adjudicate what both pass.
⟹ RUN THE BRACKET CHECK FIRST: it is cheaper (distances, no normal modes) and it is the one with a
  demonstrated hit.
```

> energy difference between reactant and product, which has nothing to do with path dependence;

                     forward's first frame = the REACTANT · reverse's first frame = the PRODUCT

   It fires on any reaction that is not thermoneutral, however clean its path.

times the threshold) **and eats margin on R-C**, the case the gate exists to catch (10.7× → 3.4×).
⟹ *"it would at least have been conservative"* is not available as a consolation, which is the
thing worth knowing about it.

### (b) 🟢 His correction is right, and — answering the question he could not check — MY TABLES ALREADY USED IT

He asked whether §39.45(a)'s R-C row (*"reverse max +0.320 eV, from its OWN endpoint"*) used the
definition he now believes is wrong, because if so R-C's 0.536 would be partly thermodynamics.
**It did not.** My script used `Ef = F[0]` (forward's first frame) and `Eb = B[-1]` (reverse's **last**
frame), and both reverse scans were run large-d → small-d, so `B[-1]` **is the reactant end.**
```

   n=1 / n=2 / n=3 separations are unaffected.
🔴 ⟹ THE DEFECT WAS ENTIRELY IN THE PROSE. The phrase "from its OWN endpoint" is ambiguous in
   exactly the way that matters, and I wrote it while the script beside me was doing the right
   thing. **§39.50's clause (ii) now names both references explicitly.**
```
🔒 **A sub-class worth naming, because it is different from the five other spec failures this round:
A SPEC DERIVED FROM A WORKING SCRIPT, WRITTEN LOOSELY. The code was correct; the sentence describing
it was not; and nothing catches that except someone implementing from the sentence alone.** ⟹ when a
spec is written from a script that already works, **the script is the authority and the prose must be
checked against it** — the reverse of the usual direction, and the reason coder11's *"I do not want
to re-derive your table from a guess"* was the right instinct: the table was fine, the sentence was
not, and only re-deriving would have shown which.

  FROM THE REACTANT END — the forward profile's FIRST frame and the reverse profile's LAST frame.
🟢 CONSISTENCY CHECK THAT FALLS OUT FREE, and it is worth asserting in code: clause (i) already

## 39.65 🔴 THE BRACKET CHECK COVERS ONE ARM OF THREE — a one-sided bracket covers all three today, and R-A calibrates the rest (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers coder11's open question. **Abbreviations, first use here**: `bracket check` = §39.63(b)'s
> requirement that a saddle's breaking-bond distance lie strictly between the two certified
> endpoints' values; `certified` = passed C-8 (converged, `n_imag == 0`, at the transition-state
> search's level); `one-sided bracket` = the same test applied against only the endpoint we hold.

### (a) 🔴 His finding is the important part and it is a guard-scope defect, not a gap in coverage

> *"The gate with the demonstrated hit does not cover two of the three arms, and the arm it does
> cover (R-A) is the one least likely to need it."*

**Correct, and it is §39.41(b)'s class again**: a guard that is present, correct and reached, while
covering a third of what its name implies. R-B and R-C are single-ended **by design** — R-B because
*"its product is a chemical claim the run exists to test"* (§39.39(d)) — so neither has a certified
product to bracket against, and that is not an oversight to fix but a property to work around.
🟢 **His refusal to turn it into a block was right** (a false block costs a reaction, §39.62(b)) and
so was **counting the non-applicable cases**: *a gate that is never applicable must not read as a
gate that never fires.* That distinction is the same one §39.51(a) names for denominators.

### (b) 🔴 CORRECTION FIRST — his "weakness is in the safe direction" is UNVERIFIED, and it may be backwards

He proposes bracketing R-B/R-C against the GFN2 forward scan's product-side endpoint, *"weaker, but
its weakness is in the safe direction (a looser bracket refuses less)."*
```
🔴 A GFN2 BRACKET IS NOT NECESSARILY LOOSER. If GFN2's product-side distance comes out SHORTER than
   the DFT one, the bracket is TIGHTER and the check FALSE-BLOCKS — the failure his own reasoning
   forbids. The direction of the GFN2-vs-DFT offset for a dissociating, Li-coordinated O···C
   distance is UNMEASURED, and I will not assume its sign any more than I would assume a cost bias's.
```

### (c) 🟢 THE ANSWER — three parts, and the first covers all three arms today with certified numbers only

```
1  ONE-SIDED BRACKET, NOW, ALL THREE ARMS, THRESHOLD-FREE:
   🟢 THE REACTANT IS CERTIFIED FOR EVERY ARM. ⟹ refuse if the saddle's breaking-bond distance is
     SHORTER THAN THE CERTIFIED REACTANT'S — a "transition state" with the bond MORE FORMED than
     the reactant is not on a bond-breaking path at all.
   Uses only certified numbers, no threshold, no GFN2, and it applies where the two-sided version
   cannot. ⚠ IT DOES NOT CATCH P1 — P1 failed on the PRODUCT side — so it does not inherit the
   demonstrated hit and must not be described as if it did.
2  TWO-SIDED BRACKET, NOW, R-A ONLY: unchanged, both endpoints certified, catches P1.
3  🟢 PRODUCT-SIDE BRACKET FOR R-B / R-C — DEFERRED TO A CALIBRATION THAT LANDS IN THIS SAME ROUND.
   R-A is the one arm holding BOTH a C-8-certified product distance AND a GFN2 product-side
   distance from its own forward scan. ⟹ THEIR DIFFERENCE MEASURES THE GFN2-vs-DFT OFFSET FOR
   EXACTLY THIS COORDINATE, on exactly this chemistry, for free.
   ⟹ once measured, R-B/R-C bracket against their GFN2 product-side end WIDENED BY THAT OFFSET,
     which makes "looser" a MEASURED property instead of an assumed one.
   🔒 FOURTH USE OF HIERARCHICAL-WITH-OVERLAP: buy the expensive version where it is affordable,
     run the cheap one on the same case, let the overlap calibrate. SP ladder · B+ · `maxpoints` ·
     this.
⟹ UNTIL (3) LANDS, coder11's `applicable: false` WITH ITS REASON AND ITS COUNT IS THE CORRECT
  BEHAVIOUR FOR THE PRODUCT SIDE. It should now read `awaiting_calibration` rather than a bare
  non-applicability, because the two say different things to whoever reads the reply.
```
⚠ **And the honest limit of (3):** a bracket built from a GFN2 endpoint is only as good as the GFN2
product being the same species as the DFT product. For R-B that is exactly what is in question — its
product is the claim under test — so **if R-B's GFN2 scan lands on a different channel than its IRC
does, the bracket is bracketing the wrong reaction and will say nothing useful.** ⟹ (3) applies to
R-C confidently and to R-B only if its GFN2 and IRC products agree, **which is itself a read-out
worth having** and costs nothing beyond a graph comparison we already run.

### (d) 🟢 His reach-test finding is a sixth instance, and it is the most literal one yet

> *"The reach test had stopped seeing part of the payload — its heredoc pattern matched only
> `<<'PY'`, and a shell script cannot nest two heredocs sharing a delimiter, so every renamed block
> I added was invisible to it."*

🔒 **A guard that is correct, tested, and quietly covering less than its name claims** — §0-o.4's rule
2 (existence · correctness · REACH · satisfiability) failing on **reach**, with the reach test itself
being the thing that lost reach. **Fixed at the root rather than by renaming the blocks back**, which
is the right choice: the alternative would have made the guard green by changing the code it was
supposed to be watching.

## 39.66 🔴🔴 TAKE THE DIRECTION-AWARE VERSION — it catches P1 on ALL THREE ARMS with certified numbers only, and the direction is DERIVED, not declared (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Answers coder11's contract question. He asked whether the one-sided bracket should stay

> the certified reactant; `forming coordinate` = one whose distance SHORTENS along the reaction;
> `mechanism coordinate` = §39.63's declared non-bond coordinate, here `d(Li–O_break)`.

### (a) 🔴 The measurement that decides it — P1 violates the LITHIUM coordinate harder than the breaking bond

```
coordinate               reactant   product   P1 SADDLE   inside [reactant, product]?
O2-C3   (breaks)           1.405     2.503      3.184      NO — 0.681 A past the product
Li-O2   (forms)            2.489     1.803      3.980      NO — 1.491 A past the REACTANT
Li-O6   (breaks, weakly)   1.709     1.795      1.747      yes
                                                    [MEASURED, from the shipped P1 TS geometry]
```
🔴🔴 **P1's lithium is FURTHER from the breaking oxygen at the saddle than at EITHER endpoint — by
1.49 Å, more than twice the break coordinate's violation.** And the one-sided form of that test needs
**only the certified reactant**: *for a forming coordinate, the saddle must not be LONGER than the
reactant.* 3.980 > 2.489 ⟹ **REFUSED.**

```
🟢 ⟹ THE DIRECTION-AWARE ONE-SIDED CHECK CATCHES P1 ON ALL THREE ARMS, TODAY, WITH CERTIFIED
   NUMBERS ONLY — no certified product, no GFN2 bracket, no calibration (3).
   It closes coder11's coverage gap NOW instead of after the R-A calibration lands.
🔒 AND IT IS A THIRD INDEPENDENT ROUTE TO THE SAME VERDICT ON P1: the mode character (§39.56), the
   break-coordinate bracket (§39.63), and now the mechanism-coordinate bracket. Three instruments,
   three different quantities, one conclusion — which is the mechanism this round has repeatedly
   found is what tells you a finding is real rather than merely possible.
```

### (b) 🟢 DO NOT ADD A DIRECTION FIELD — derive it. A declared direction can be mis-declared; a measured one cannot.

coder11 correctly refused to add a direction field on his own. **He should not add one at all:**
```
BREAK / FORM BONDS   direction is ALREADY CARRIED — §39.26(d)'s lists are literally labelled BREAK
                     and FORM. Nothing to add.
MECHANISM COORDS     🟢 DERIVE THE DIRECTION FROM THE GFN2 FORWARD SCAN, which runs anyway: does the
                     distance increase or decrease along the path? Measured, self-referential, and
                     IMPOSSIBLE TO MIS-DECLARE — the failure mode a config field would introduce.
                     R-A -0.75 · R-B -0.85 · R-C -0.79 A ⟹ all three FORMING, all three monotonic
                     along their scans (checked: 2.50→2.20→1.95→1.85→1.75, 2.75→...→1.80,
                     2.49→1.88→1.76→...→1.64).
🟢 FREE CROSS-CHECK where both endpoints are certified (R-A): the DERIVED direction must agree with
   the sign of (product - reactant). Disagreement means the scan and the endpoints describe
   different reactions, which is worth knowing on its own.
🔴 HONEST EDGE CASE, and it must be handled rather than assumed away: A NON-MONOTONIC COORDINATE
   HAS NO WELL-DEFINED DIRECTION. Then the one-sided check is `applicable: false, non_monotonic`
   and is COUNTED — coder11's own pattern. All three arms are monotonic today; that is a
   measurement, not a guarantee for future reactions.
⚠ Deriving direction at GFN2 and applying the test to a DFT saddle is cross-engine, but it transfers
  a SIGN rather than a magnitude, which is the robust part. Stated, not hidden.
```

### (c) 🟢 So the contract widens — and coder11's guard against widening it becomes the guard that permits it

His `test_the_contract_is_BREAKING_bonds_and_orientation_therefore_matters` pinned exactly the right
hazard: **feeding a forming coordinate into a breaking-bond test refuses by construction.** The fix
is not to keep the input narrow — it is to make the test know which kind it has.
```
CONTRACT, FINAL:  one_sided(coordinate, direction):
   direction == BREAK  ⟹ refuse if saddle < reactant   (bond more formed than the reactant)
   direction == FORM   ⟹ refuse if saddle > reactant   (partners further apart than the reactant)
   direction == NONE   ⟹ applicable: false, non_monotonic, counted
INPUT WIDENS to break + form + mechanism coordinates, WITH their derived directions.
🔒 His test does not get deleted — it gets INVERTED: feeding a forming coordinate with a BREAK
   direction must still refuse, and the same coordinate with its CORRECT direction must not. That
   keeps the hazard pinned while permitting the widening, and it is a better test than either
   version alone.
```

### (d) Answers to his two calibration questions, made explicit rather than inferred

```
1  WHICH DISTANCE the R-A offset is measured on: 🔴 BOTH — the break coordinate AND the Li
   mechanism coordinate, separately. They are different bond types (a covalent C-O and an ionic
   Li-O contact) and there is no reason a GFN2-vs-DFT offset measured on one transfers to the
   other. One offset per coordinate KIND, never pooled — §39.51(a)'s prohibition in a new place.
2  DOES R-B GET THE CALIBRATION: 🔴 ONLY IF ITS GFN2 AND IRC PRODUCTS AGREE BY MOLECULAR GRAPH, and
   that is a RECORDED PRECONDITION, not an inference. He is right to want it explicit: R-B's
   product is the claim under test (§39.39(d)), so a GFN2 bracket built on a GFN2 product that
   turns out to be a different channel would be bracketing the wrong reaction. If they disagree,
   R-B keeps `awaiting_calibration` indefinitely and that is the correct outcome, not a failure.
```
🔒 **And his closing observation is the one I would carry forward**: *the heredoc fix was invisible
from inside the guard — every renamed block was silently outside its own regex, and nothing about the
test's output suggested it was seeing less than before.* **A guard that loses reach reports exactly
what it reported before.** That is why reach has to be measured by construction (AST calls, emitted
counts, `applicable: false` tallies) and can never be inferred from a green result.

## 39.67 🔒 CORROBORATING A READING IS NOT CORROBORATING AN ARTEFACT — and the P1 geometry has only the first (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Recorded because it arose in messages, has a pending consumer in this round, and is the kind of
> distinction that is obvious once stated and invisible until then.
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `artefact` = a primary output of a real calculation, here P1's
> `ts_qst2.log` and `ts.xyz`; `reading` = a value extracted from an artefact by a parser; `derived
> record` = a document that repeats a value taken from elsewhere.

### (a) Three levels of support, and only the weakest two exist for `d(O2–C3) = 3.184 Å`

```
LEVEL 1  A DERIVED RECORD.  ADR-112 carries the number, and it carries it BECAUSE §39.56 measured
         it. 🔴 NOT A SECOND SOURCE. Two documents agreeing because one copied the other is ONE
         SOURCE WITH TWO NAMES — and if the measurement were wrong, both would be wrong identically
         while the agreement read as confirmation.
LEVEL 2  AN INDEPENDENT READING.  🟢 EXISTS: coder11's `bracket_check` test RE-DERIVES 3.184 A from
         the TS log's own geometry rather than hard-coding it. A second implementation, reading the
         same primary artefact, agreeing. This is real support and it is what should be cited.
LEVEL 3  AN INDEPENDENT ARTEFACT.  🔴 DOES NOT EXIST. Both parsers read THE SAME G16 RUN. Nothing we
         hold can corroborate the artefact itself, only our reading of it.
```
🔒 **The distinction is not pedantry: level 2 protects against a parsing error and level 3 protects
against the run being pathological.** They fail differently, and this round has already been bitten
by the second kind — `0.247 core-h` was read correctly from a real log and was still a measurement of
the wrong thing.

### (b) 🟢 What would supply level 3, and it is already funded

**R-A's attempt in this round**: a different reaction, a different run, producing a saddle whose
geometry either brackets correctly or does not.
```
brackets correctly  ⟹ P1's 3.184 A was an ISOLATED PATHOLOGY of an uncertified-endpoint QST2 run,
                      not something the pipeline produces. The bracket check keeps its demonstrated
                      hit and gains a demonstrated PASS, which it currently lacks entirely.
does NOT bracket    ⟹ 🔴 the pipeline produces wrong-side saddles even from certified endpoints,
                      which is a far larger finding than P1 and would put C-8 itself in question.
🔒 EITHER OUTCOME IS INFORMATIVE, WHICH IS THE PROPERTY WORTH PRE-REGISTERING. The bracket check
   today has one demonstrated FIRING and zero demonstrated PASSES — a gate that has only ever
   fired is not yet distinguishable from a gate that always fires (§39.45(a)'s G-SCAN-5 rule,
   applied to a different gate).
```
⚠ **And the honest limit on level 3 even then**: one passing reaction does not establish that the
pipeline never produces wrong-side saddles. It establishes that it does not always do so, which is
the weaker and still-necessary claim. **n = 1 is not a rate** — the same arithmetic as §39.39(c)-2,
arriving at a third quantity.

### (c) 🔒 The general rule, stated so it can be applied without this example

> **When a number appears in two places, establish WHICH LEVEL the agreement is at before citing it
> as support. A derived record agreeing with its own source is not evidence. An independent reading
> is evidence about the parser. Only an independent artefact is evidence about the world.**

⚠ **The trap is that all three look identical in a citation.** *"Confirmed against ADR-112"*,
*"confirmed by coder11's test"* and *"confirmed by a second run"* are the same sentence shape
carrying three different strengths — which is why the level, and not merely the source, belongs in
the citation.

## 39.68 🔴 THE SCAN'S STARTING PROTOCOL — ruled, and my own §39.48(a) numbers were right for a reason I never checked (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> coder11 found that the gate's verdict depends on a starting protocol nobody had ruled, stopped
> three guesses in, and asked. **He is right that it was unruled, and right that his earlier clean
> PASS rested on a hand-picked range.**
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `frame 0` = the first point of a relaxed scan, after its own
> constrained optimisation; `settled` = frame 0's constrained optimisation has converged, so the
> energy measured there is the reactant's and not a snapshot of an unfinished relaxation;
> `d_break` = the distance of the bond the reaction breaks.

### (a) 🔴 FIRST — MY OWN NUMBERS. They stand, and I did not check why at the time.

His diagnosis applies to my run as much as his, so I checked it before ruling:
```
02_scan_ra — the run that produced §39.48(a)'s R-A row
  input structure (free opt of the shipped guess, the PLANAR TRAP)   -20.919671 Eh
  scan FRAME 0                                                       -20.936321 Eh  (-0.453 eV)
  free relax OF frame 0                                              -20.936331 Eh  (-0.0003 eV)
  profile from frame 0:  +0.000  +0.020  +0.086  +0.191   — RISES MONOTONICALLY
⟹ frame 0's constrained optimisation ABSORBED the entire 0.453 eV relaxation and settled to within
  0.0003 eV of a free relaxation. My numbers are sound.
🔒 AND I NEVER CHECKED THAT. It held because the first constrained optimisation happened to converge,
  which is exactly the property coder11 has now shown is NOT automatic. **My §39.48(a) row was right
  for a reason I did not verify — the same luck as his hand-picked range, one layer down.**
```

### (b) 🔴 The mechanism, and why "just relax first" is not available

A relaxed scan's frame 0 is *supposed* to be the reactant relaxed subject to `d = d_start`. If the
input is already that, the constrained optimisation is a no-op. If it is not — a DFT geometry
evaluated on the GFN2 surface, or a trapped structure — **the constrained optimisation must do the
relaxing, and whether it finishes is a fact about the optimiser, not an assumption.** When it does
not finish, the relaxation leaks into frames 1–2 and **corrupts both clauses at once**, because
§39.64 references both to the reactant end. coder11 measured the consequence: **forward barrier 0.019
eV instead of 0.471.**
```
🔴 AND A FREE PRE-RELAXATION IS NOT THE FIX — HE MEASURED THAT TOO: a free GFN2 `--opt` of the
   reduced radical LEAVES THE RING-CLOSED BASIN, so the scan then starts from an already-opened
   structure. Same class as §39.42(a)'s kicked seeds and ADR-067's n_imag = 5: **an idealised guess
   relaxed without a leash goes somewhere else.**
⚠ AND IT IS NOT CONFINED TO GUESS GEOMETRIES. In production the reactant is DFT-optimised, which is
  not a GFN2 minimum either — so the same lag appears, smaller, ON THE FRAME EVERYTHING IS MEASURED
  FROM. His point, and it is the one that makes this a protocol question rather than a fixture bug.
```

### (c) 🟢 THE RULING — three answers, in the form he asked for

```
1  STARTING GEOMETRY: the C-8-CERTIFIED (DFT) REACTANT, then a **CONSTRAINED** GFN2 relaxation
   holding `d_break` at the certified value. 🔴 NEVER A FREE ONE — the constraint is what preserves
   the basin, and "free relaxation leaves the basin" is measured, not feared.
2  RANGE: **already ruled in §39.42(b) and his implementation differs from it in two ways.**
   §39.42(b): "+1.2 A from the CERTIFIED ENDPOINT's own d, not from an assumed value. Emit the
   start." ⟹ (i) 11 x 0.10 = +1.1 A should be +1.2 A; (ii) 🔴 the anchor is the **PRE-RELAXED**
   d, not the raw certified d, because after (1) those differ and the scan must start where the
   structure actually is. **The range was ruled; the anchor was not, and that is my omission.**
3  🟢 YES — FRAME 0 GETS ITS OWN CRITERION, AND ITS FAILURE IS `indeterminate`, NEVER `FIRE`:
     (i)  frame 0's constrained optimisation must report CONVERGED (xtb says so; do not infer it)
     (ii) the profile must NOT DESCEND from frame 0 to frame 1 — a scan climbing toward a barrier
          that starts by falling is measuring an unfinished relaxation, not chemistry.
   Neither is a tuned constant: (i) is the program's own verdict and (ii) is a sign comparison.
🔴🔴 THE `indeterminate` CLAUSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. An unsettled frame 0 produces a FALSE
   FIRE — his measurements show exactly that (dBarrier 0.4530 from a corrupt reference against
   0.0216 from a good one). **A gate that blocks because its own reference was unfinished is
   reporting on itself, and it must say so rather than blaming the reaction.**
   ⟹ cause class BUDGET/PROTOCOL, not CHEMICAL (§39.59(c)): it is a fact about our procedure.
```

### (d) On his third measurement — 73 eV is not a chemistry result, and it should not eliminate a protocol

His constrained pre-relaxation attempt returned `dE 73 eV (reverse degenerate)`. 🔴 **73 eV is not a
number the potential energy surface can produce for this system; it is a broken run or a broken
parse.** ⟹ **it must be diagnosed, not used as evidence against option (1)** — which is otherwise
the option this ruling selects. If the constrained protocol genuinely cannot produce a reverse
profile, that changes the answer, but *"one run returned an absurd number"* does not establish it.
🔒 Same discipline as §0-g's rule that this project has now applied six times: **before attributing a
computational failure to the chemistry, check the input.**

### (e) What he did right, recorded because it is the reason this cost nothing

```
· he STOPPED at the point where the next step would have been a guess, three guesses in, and said so
· he shipped the protocol with NO INVENTED PRE-RELAXATION — the only variant adding no unratified
  step of his own — with `_protocol_status` stating outright that the verdict is not a chemical
  result until ruled
· he WITHDREW his own earlier clean-PASS report on noticing its range was hand-picked
🔒 The gate blocking R-A's arm today is a FALSE BLOCK if my n=1 PASS is the true answer — and he
   took that cost deliberately rather than shipping a verdict he could not derive. That is the
   asymmetry of §39.62(b) applied by the implementer, against his own previous result.
```
