## 39.69 🟢 SCF NON-CONVERGENCE GETS A FIFTH CAUSE CLASS — and 186 of my own frames say it is PATH-SENSITIVE, not systemic (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> coder11 diagnosed the 73 eV as an aborted forward scan whose partial trajectory was read as a
> profile, traced the abort to `scf: Self consistent charge iterator did not converge`, and asked
> what cause class it belongs to rather than filing it under `unknown`.
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `SCF` = self-consistent field, the iterative solution of the
> electronic structure at a fixed geometry; `cause class` = §39.59(c)'s tally that keeps
> `indeterminate` outcomes attributable (CHEMICAL / BUDGET / PROTOCOL); `prescription` = the action
> a large count in a class calls for.

### (a) 🟢 THE RULING — a fifth class, and the test that justifies it is the one the taxonomy was built on

The classes exist so that (i) U-56b's denominator stays clean and (ii) **a large count in a class
sends someone to the right lever.** ⟹ the test for a new class is: **does it have a distinct
prescription, and would folding it in send someone to the wrong lever?**
```
into CHEMICAL   `p` falls for an ENGINE reason ⟹ the exact corruption §39.59(c) forbids for budget
                nulls. And the prescription would be "fix the method", which does nothing here.
into BUDGET     prescription "loosen the caps" — does nothing for an SCF that will not converge.
into PROTOCOL   prescription "fix the procedure" — but the procedure ran EXACTLY as §39.68 rules.
                🔴 Worse: it would poison PROTOCOL's own diagnostic, whose whole meaning is
                "OUR RULES ARE WRONG".
`unknown`       invisible to every reading; nobody is prompted to act. coder11's point 3.
⟹ ALL FOUR SEND YOU TO THE WRONG LEVER. THE FIFTH CLASS IS JUSTIFIED. **`engine` — his name, adopted.**
```
**And it is defined by its prescription, with the boundary stated, because a class defined by
example grows until it means nothing:**
```
ENGINE  the calculation could not be COMPLETED for numerical reasons internal to the
        electronic-structure method, AT A GEOMETRY THE PROTOCOL LEGITIMATELY REQUESTED.
        prescription: change how the electronic structure is set up or converged — SCF settings,
        the initial guess, guess propagation between frames, the level.
IN      SCF non-convergence · basis linear dependence · integration-grid failures
OUT     out-of-memory ⟹ BUDGET (we chose the memory) · a malformed deck ⟹ PROTOCOL (we built it)
        · a geometry the protocol should never have requested ⟹ PROTOCOL, and the trailing clause
          above is what makes that boundary decidable rather than a judgement call
```

### (b) 🔴 BUT HIS ALARM IS DEFLATED BY A MEASUREMENT — 186 of my frames, zero failures, all three sizes

He writes that this *"will recur at production scale: a stretched open-shell radical whose SCF does
not converge is an ordinary outcome, not an accident"*, and that it happened on **R-A, the easiest
system we have**. I checked every GFN2 scan I have run:
```
02_scan_ra (R-A, 11 at, 33 frames) · 20_rb/fwd1d (R-B, 11 at, 33) · 17_reverse (R-C rev, 33)
08_scan_rc (R-C, 21 at, 33) · 09_scan_rc_fine (R-C, 41) · 16_ec3 (Li(EC)3, 31 at, 13)
⟹ 186 FRAMES, 11 / 21 / 31 ATOMS, ZERO SCF WARNINGS, ALL NORMAL TERMINATION.
                                                       [MEASURED, dev box, 2026-08-20]
```
🔒 **Including R-A over the same coordinate range that failed for him.** ⟹ **the failure is not a
property of the surface or of system size. It is PATH-SENSITIVE** — his own note says a 0.0012 Å
difference in starting distance was enough to move where the trajectory lands.
```
🟢 THIS SHARPENS THE PRESCRIPTION RATHER THAN WEAKENING THE CLASS: the lever is GUESS PROPAGATION
   AND CONVERGENCE PATH, not "these systems are too hard". A first thing to check, free: whether
   each constrained step inherits the previous frame's wavefunction or restarts from scratch —
   a scan that restarts its SCF at every point is far more likely to strand one of them.
🔴 AND THE HONEST LIMIT ON MY 186 FRAMES: they are one operator's runs with one set of starting
   structures. **Zero out of 186 bounds the rate loosely** (95 % upper bound ~1.6 % per frame
   [computed here]) and says nothing about DFT, where the SCF is a different and harder problem.
   It refutes "ordinary outcome"; it does not establish "rare".
```

### (c) 🟢 PARTIAL PROFILES ARE RETAINED AND REPORTED, NEVER DISCARDED — and refusing the verdict is separate from discarding the data

He asks whether a policy that discards aborted scans also discards the points before the failure.
**Refusing to render a verdict from a partial profile is correct and already done. Discarding the
profile would be wrong**, for two reasons this project has already paid for:
```
1  ADR-027's PRINCIPLE: never prune the thing you compute completeness from. The points before the
   abort are legitimate measurements, and **WHERE the scan died is itself the datum that sizes the
   problem** — the only information we have about where the engine breaks.
2  🔴 SUCCESS-CONDITIONED DENOMINATOR (§39.51(a)) IN A NEW PLACE: if aborted scans vanish, our
   record of "where scans succeed" is conditioned on their having succeeded. The one-question test
   finds it — *if one case fails, what happens to my denominator?* It shrinks.
⟹ RECORD: the partial profile, the frame index at which it stopped, the constrained value there,
  and the innermost cause. `verdict: indeterminate, cause_class: engine`.
```

### (d) 🟢 Two things he did that are the right treatment, recorded so they are not re-litigated

```
· NON-ZERO EXIT ⇒ NO VERDICT. He rendered a verdict from a partial trajectory because he recorded
  `forward_rc` and never read it. 🔒 A recorded field that nothing reads is the same defect as an
  unreached guard — §0-o.4's REACH property, applied to a return code.
· THE INNERMOST STACK FRAME IS THE CAUSE. The outermost says "geometry optimization failed", which
  sends a reader to the optimiser instead of to the electronic structure. 🔒 Same shape as the
  C-8.1 grid seam: the true cause was one layer in, and the visible label named a symptom.
```

### (e) 🔴 critic10's third defect is the one worth naming — it would have silently defeated §39.66

An absent scan direction defaulted to `"break"`, which would let a **forming** coordinate pass
silently — **and on P1's numbers that is exactly the coordinate §39.66 catches it with** (Li–O2,
1.49 Å past the reactant, the violation larger than the breaking bond's).
```
🔒 AND THE REACHABILITY ARGUMENT IS THE INSTRUCTIVE PART: critic10 judged it unreachable; it was
   reachable PER KEY, because `derive_direction` legitimately returns "no direction" for a
   non-monotonic coordinate ON A PERFECTLY HEALTHY RUN. ⟹ THE DEFAULT WOULD HAVE FIRED ON GOOD
   DATA, NOT ON BROKEN DATA — which is why "this path is unreachable" arguments need the
   healthy-input case checked as well as the failure case.
⚠ It is also the §39.66 edge case I ruled on arriving as a DEFAULT rather than as a verdict: I said
  a non-monotonic coordinate is `applicable: false, non_monotonic, counted`. A silent default to
  "break" is the same input taking the opposite path. **A rule and its default must agree, and
  nothing checks that except someone reading both.**
```

## 39.70 🔴 B+'s COMPARATOR MUST NOT BE THE Li-CONTACT CUTOFF — that is §39.48(b)'s defect arriving in a new place (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> coder11 built B+'s decision half and found that its "threshold-free" property does not survive
> contact with a comparator: *the design says the two start points sit on one descending branch, but
> something still has to answer "did they reach the same minimum?", and every comparator we own has
> a threshold in it.* **He is right, and the resolution is not to pick a side of his branch.**
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `B+` = §39.55's two-terminal-optimisation IRC verdict;
> `terminal optimisation` = a plain geometry optimisation started from a point on the IRC path;
> `Layer-I cutoff` = the Li-contact distance in `config/graph_layers.json`, flagged
> `[PLACEHOLDER-ESTIMATE]` with a mandatory ±sensitivity rule; `covalent graph` = the bond
> connectivity excluding cation-coordination contacts.

### (a) 🔴 The bind he found is real, and both horns are unacceptable

```
CONSERVATIVE (what he shipped)  a threshold-sensitive comparison returns `None`, never `True`.
  🔴 COST: B+ comes back UNDETERMINED on exactly the Li-rearrangement cases that motivated the
     R-A/R-C programme — because the Layer-I cutoff IS a Li-contact distance and those cases are
     precisely where two candidate minima differ in Li's position.
PERMISSIVE                      a sensitive comparison counts as agreement, flagged.
  🔴 COST: condition 7(b) uses agreement to ESTABLISH a connection. Establishing on a verdict that
     could have gone the other way is the failure C-2 exists to prevent.
```
🔒 **His instinct to take the conservative horn was right given the choice — but the choice is
avoidable, and taking it would have made B+ useless exactly where it was needed.**

### (b) 🟢 THE RULING — change the comparator, not the branch. This is §39.48(b) again.

**§39.48(b) is the precedent and it is exact**: I built G-SCAN-2 v1 on a *structural* identity test,
and it failed because **a structural test cannot separate a soft-coordinate displacement from a
reaction-relevant one.** `d(Li–O)` at 11 atoms spans 1.95–3.40 Å across 0.06 eV. **The Layer-I
cutoff is that same soft coordinate, promoted to a decision.**
```
🟢 B+'s COMPARATOR IS: (i) IDENTICAL COVALENT GRAPHS — bond connectivity with cation-coordination
   contacts EXCLUDED — AND (ii) energies agreeing within THE OPTIMISER'S OWN CONVERGENCE CRITERION.
   🔒 NEITHER IS AN IMPORTED CONSTANT: (i) is a graph isomorphism, and (ii) is the number the
     program itself converged to. Two structures that reached the same minimum agree to within the
     convergence criterion BY DEFINITION.
   🔴 THE Li-CONTACT CUTOFF LEAVES THE DECISION PATH ENTIRELY and is reported as a COVARIATE
     (C-3's shape: emit the number, withhold the verdict). It keeps its `[PLACEHOLDER-ESTIMATE]`
     status and its ±sensitivity obligation — as data, where a placeholder belongs.
⟹ B+ NOW RETURNS A VERDICT ON THE Li-REARRANGEMENT CASES, because Li's position no longer enters
  the comparison. The bind dissolves rather than being decided.
```
⚠ **And his conservative rule survives where it is still needed**: if the covalent graphs agree and
the energies do not, or vice versa, that is genuine ambiguity ⟹ **`None`, never `True`**. His
reasoning for it is correct and unchanged; it now fires on a much smaller and genuinely ambiguous set.
🔒 **I am not reusing `classify_endpoints` for this.** He was right that two notions of "same
minimum" would drift — but the right resolution is that **B+'s question is not that function's
question.** `classify_endpoints` asks *"are these the same coordination environment"*; B+ asks
*"did these two optimisations fall into the same valley"*. Same words, different quantity.

### (c) His two wiring questions, answered

```
1  WHICH TWO IRC POINTS — 🟢 THE LAST POINT AND THE MIDPOINT BY REACTION COORDINATE (arc length),
   not by index. Gaussian prints `NET REACTION COORDINATE` per point, so the midpoint is
   well-defined at any point count, including the short IRCs C-2.2 makes common. **A fraction of
   the index count IS a constant in disguise, as he says; a midpoint by arc length is not — it is
   the middle.**
   🔴 AND WHY NOT THE EARLIEST POINT, which would maximise separation and therefore sensitivity to
     a bifurcation: A TERMINAL OPTIMISATION STARTED TOO NEAR THE SADDLE CAN ROLL BACK OVER IT INTO
     THE OTHER BASIN, producing a SPURIOUS DISAGREEMENT. The midpoint balances separation against
     that, and the reasoning belongs in the code comment or someone will "improve" it to point 1.
2  WHAT LEVEL — 🔴 THE SAME DFT LEVEL AS THE TS CHAIN. Not GFN2, and the ~12 % cost estimate stands.
   The terminal optimisation's job is to identify WHICH MINIMUM THE PATH LEADS TO ON THE SURFACE
   THE TS SEARCH RAN ON. A GFN2 terminal optimisation answers that for a different surface —
   C-8.1's argument, and §39.38(d) already rules GFN2 output is never an endpoint.
   🔒 B+ IS NOT NEARLY FREE, and I would rather say so than let a cheap number survive on a
     surface mismatch. Its ~12 % is what buys the only thing that distinguishes it from Option B.
```

### (d) 🟢 Two things he did that are right, and one message that crossed

```
· `None` and "B+ was not run" giving the SAME C-2 verdict (a truncated IRC stays refused) while
  being DISTINGUISHABLE IN THE RECORD is correct — and pinning it with a test rather than leaving
  it implicit is the treatment §39.63 asked for on the spectator test's uncomfortable consequence.
· registering `bplus_agreement` in the DEFERRED bucket so the reach test goes RED the day someone
  wires the optimisations: 🔒 **the missing half is loud rather than silent**, which is the
  property §39.65(d)'s heredoc defect lacked.
⚠ CROSSED: the SCF cause class is ALREADY RULED — §39.69, class **`engine`**, defined by
  prescription with an explicit boundary. It is not still open.
```

## 39.71 🟢 GFN2 FOR B+'s TERMINAL OPTIMISATIONS — NO, and the lead's narrower framing makes the objection sharper rather than weaker (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> The lead asked the level question separately and in a narrower form than coder11 did: *"is GFN2
> adequate for confirming a terminal minimum — checking two starting points relax to the same basin
> — as opposed to measuring a barrier?"* **It is a fair distinction and it deserves an answer on its
> own terms rather than a repetition of §39.70(c).** Cost is engineer8's; this is the science half.

### (a) The narrower question does not rescue GFN2 — it aims the objection directly at the weak spot

```
THE COMMON DEFENCE OF A CHEAP LEVEL: "we are not measuring an energy, we are asking a TOPOLOGICAL
question — do two points relax to the same basin — and topology is robust across methods."
🔴 THE ANSWER: BASIN STRUCTURE IS EXACTLY WHAT GFN2 IS DOCUMENTED TO GET WRONG FOR THIS CLASS.
   §39.38(d), on this project's own record: "Li+-coordinated complexes have near-degenerate
   coordination isomers separated by LESS THAN THE ERROR OF ANY CHEAP SURFACE. That is the whole
   content of U-55." ⟹ the narrower question is not a lesser demand on the method. It is a demand
   on the ONE PROPERTY we have already ruled the method cannot supply here.
```
**And the failure has a direction, which is what settles it:**
```
(a) GFN2 MERGES two DFT basins ⟹ two points DFT would separate return "SAME" ⟹ FALSE AGREEMENT
    ⟹ condition 7(b) ESTABLISHES a connection that is not there. 🔴 The exact failure C-2 exists
      to prevent, and the one B+ was built to close.
(b) GFN2 SPLITS one DFT basin  ⟹ false disagreement ⟹ `indeterminate`. Conservative, costs a
    result, does not certify a wrong one.
🔴 (a) IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL FOR THIS CLASS. §39.42(a) measured 5 of 6 kick seeds landing in one
   GFN2 basin at 21 atoms with the sixth 0.686 eV away — the cheap surface's basin map is coarse
   exactly where these molecules live.
⟹ **DFT, same level as the TS chain.** §39.70(c) unchanged, and now for a reason that answers the
  narrow question rather than the general one.
```
🔒 **And note what my new comparator does NOT change here.** §39.70(b) made B+ compare covalent
graphs plus energies-within-convergence. The **covalent graph** half would probably survive at GFN2.
What does not survive is **which minimum the optimiser walks into** — and that is not a property of
the comparator at all. It is a property of the surface being walked. **Changing the comparator
cannot fix a wrong surface**, which is C-8.1's argument in its most compact form.

### (b) 🟢 BUT THERE IS AN ASYMMETRIC USE THAT IS SCIENTIFICALLY CLEAN, offered for engineer8 to price

The error direction in (a) is one-sided, and one-sided errors can be exploited:
```
🟢 GFN2 DISAGREEMENT IS TRUSTWORTHY. GFN2 AGREEMENT IS NOT.
   ⟹ optional PRE-FILTER: run the two terminal optimisations at GFN2 first.
        they land in DIFFERENT basins ⟹ B+ is `None` and the DFT pair is NOT PAID FOR
        they land in the SAME basin    ⟹ the answer is untrustworthy; PAY FOR THE DFT PAIR
⚠ HONEST LIMITS, both of which shrink the offer:
   · it saves money only in the DISAGREEMENT branch — i.e. exactly when the attempt was going to
     return `indeterminate` anyway. The saving is real but it is a saving on failures.
   · the disagreement RATE is unmeasured, so the expected saving cannot be quoted. It has the
     shape of a good trade and no number behind it.
🔒 I am OFFERING this, not recommending it: it adds a stage and a failure mode (a GFN2 run that
  itself does not converge — §39.69's `engine` class) to save on the branch that produces no result.
  **If engineer8 prices it and it does not clear a wide margin, drop it — the science does not
  need it and B+'s ~12 % is what buys B+ its only advantage over plain Option B.**
```

### (c) Crossing note

The lead's three questions — the comparator's threshold, "the 20th of 30", and this one — **were all
answered in §39.70 before these messages arrived.** In short: the comparator changes rather than
either horn being taken (the Li-contact cutoff leaves the decision path); the points are **the last
and the midpoint by ARC LENGTH**, not by index, which is well defined at any point count and is not
a fraction-shaped constant; and the level is **DFT**, for the reason above.

## 39.73 🔴🔴 THE ENDPOINT CRASH IS ADR-108's DESCRIPTOR ESCAPE FAILING AT THE ONE STAGE C-8 NEEDS — and it dissolves without sourcing a single number (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> Confirms the lead's candidate cause from the artefacts and rules the fix.
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `EpsInf` = ε(∞), the dielectric constant at infinite frequency,
> equal to n² where n is the refractive index — the *fast* (electronic) part of the solvent response;
> `read block` = the extra input section a `scrf=(...,read)` route consumes; `NEqPCM` = Gaussian's
> non-equilibrium PCM machinery; `l1110` = the Gaussian link that builds derivative Fock matrices,
> i.e. the frequency stage.

### (a) Confirmed from the artefacts, and the mechanism is exact

```
endpoint_tight.gjf  route  "#p nosymm wB97XD/gen scrf=(pcm,solvent=generic,read)
                            opt=(tight,calcfc,maxcycles=200) freq Int(Grid=UltraFine)"
                    read block, in full:   eps=18.5          <- ONE LINE. No EpsInf.
endpoint_tight.log  :816  "NEqPCM: Using equilibrium solvation (IEInf=0, Eps= 18.5000,
                                                                EpsInf=   0.0000)"
                    :817  "EpsInf not defined for this solvent."   then  l1110 SIGNAL 11
endpoint_rough.gjf  IDENTICAL read block, and its log matches `EpsInf|NEqPCM` ZERO times
```
🔒 **`EpsInf = 0.0000` is not merely "undefined" — it is a sentinel, and ε(∞) = 0 is physically
impossible (ε(∞) = n² ≥ 1 for any medium).** The Hessian path consumes it and dies.
🔴 **And the rough stage carries the SAME read block and never touches that code path, because it
has no `freq`.** ⟹ **`freq` is the only stage that reads `EpsInf`.**

### (b) 🔴🔴 THE STRUCTURAL FINDING — ADR-108's escape was never an escape, only a deferral

```
ADR-108 moved B0 from SMD to PCM-with-numeric-eps SPECIFICALLY to escape the seven Abraham /
surface-tension descriptors that §39.26(b) established nobody has and I refused to invent.
PCM-numeric needs only `eps` — FOR ENERGIES AND GRADIENTS.
🔴 THE HESSIAN PATH NEEDS `EpsInf` TOO.
⟹ THE DESCRIPTOR PROBLEM WAS NOT ESCAPED. IT WAS DEFERRED TO THE FREQUENCY STAGE — WHICH IS
  EXACTLY AND ONLY THE STAGE C-8 REQUIRES (`n_imag == 0`, C-8.2: "a geometry-only convergence
  criterion does NOT satisfy C-8").
```
🔴🔴 **THE SENTENCE THAT WAS HERE IS FALSE — SEE §39.74.** I wrote *"the endpoint certification is
the FIRST job ever to ask G16 for a Hessian under `solvent=generic`"*. **P5 asked for twenty, in the
same round, and ALL TWENTY DIED THE SAME WAY. Not one frequency was computed anywhere this round.**
🟢 What survives is the half that mattered: **a route smoke that does not exercise every stage the
route contains is not a route smoke** — ADR-108's deck was verified for the energy path and never for
the Hessian path, and `[VERIFIED-IN-RUN]` says nothing about which.

### (c) 🟢 THE RULING — bracket it. The blocker dissolves WITHOUT SOURCING A SINGLE NUMBER.

The obvious fix is to supply `EpsInf = n²` for EC:EMC. **I am not doing that, and not because the
number is unavailable** — refractive index is a bulk optical property, universally tabulated, and
categorically easier than Abraham α/β, so **this does NOT reopen §39.26(b)'s blocker.** I am not
doing it because there is a better move that needs no value at all:
```
🟢 EpsInf HAS A PHYSICALLY BOUNDED RANGE THAT REQUIRES NO LOOKUP:
     lower bound  EpsInf = 1.0        (n = 1; no fast response — the vacuum-like limit)
     upper bound  EpsInf = eps_static = 18.5   (fast response equals the full response)
   Any real value lies strictly inside. ⟹ RUN THE TIGHT/freq STAGE AT BOTH ENDS.

## 39.77 🟢 THERE IS NO CALIBRATION CASE TO IDENTIFY — run B+ on EVERY converged IRC, because converged IRCs are RARE and each one is a calibration point (proposer7, 2026-08-20)

> coder11 found that B+ runs unconditionally while `irc_direction_ok` consults it **only in the
> truncated branch**, and asked how to identify the calibration case that must be exempted from any
> gate. **The exemption is not needed, and my own §39.55(c) was too narrow.**
> **Abbreviations, first use here**: `branch (a)` = a connection established by IRC convergence;
> `branch (b)` = established by `maxpoints` truncation + B+ agreement; `ground truth` = a converged
> IRC, which reaches a minimum on its own and therefore needs no B+ verdict; `C-2.2` = the rule that
> a `maxpoints`-terminated IRC is `indeterminate`, which makes truncation the common outcome.

### (a) 🔴 Answer part 3 first, because it dissolves parts 1 and 2

**Is a B+ disagreement on a CONVERGED IRC informative? Decisively yes — it is the only place B+ can
be checked at all.**
```
IRC converged AND B+ agrees     ⟹ B+ was right, ON A CASE WHERE WE COULD CHECK
IRC converged AND B+ disagrees  ⟹ B+'s METHOD IS WRONG HERE, and we know only because ground
                                  truth existed. THIS IS THE CALIBRATION.
IRC truncated                   ⟹ B+ is load-bearing AND UNCHECKABLE — no ground truth exists
```
🔴🔴 **AND DISCARDING IT IS THE SUCCESS-CONDITIONED DENOMINATOR AGAIN (§39.51(a)), IN ITS PUREST
FORM.** If B+ verdicts are retained only where they were *consulted*, then our record of B+'s
reliability is conditioned on the cases where B+ was load-bearing — **which are exactly the cases
with no ground truth.** ⟹ **we would only ever store B+ verdicts we cannot check.** The one-question
test finds it instantly: *if one case fails, what happens to my denominator?* It keeps only the
uncheckable ones.
```
🟢 ⟹ RULING: **B+'s verdict is ALWAYS COMPUTED AND ALWAYS RECORDED. Whether it is CONSULTED
   depends on the branch.** Compute-and-record and consult are different acts and this code
   currently fuses them — the same fusion C-10.1 separated for cost probes and §39.62 separated
   for Ω. Third instance.
🔴 AND THE DIRECTION OF AUTHORITY MUST BE STATED, or someone will later read it backwards:
   ON A CONVERGED IRC, THE IRC WINS. B+ NEVER OVERRIDES IT. A disagreement impugns B+, not the
   IRC — because on that branch the IRC is the ground truth B+ is being measured against.
```

### (b) 🟢 ⟹ PARTS 1 AND 2 HAVE NO CONTENT. There is no calibration case to identify.

coder11 asked whether the calibration is identified by reaction id, by rung, or by a config flag —
and named the failure mode of each (*"a hard-coded reaction id outlives its reason; a config flag is
a thing someone can set on the wrong item"*). **Both dissolve:**
```
🟢 RUN B+ ON EVERY CONVERGED IRC. No reaction id, no flag, no exemption mechanism.
   WHY IT IS AFFORDABLE — and it is coder11's OWN observation, turned around: C-2.2 MAKES
   TRUNCATION THE COMMON CASE, SO CONVERGED IRCs ARE RARE. ⟹ the aggregate cost of calibrating on
   all of them is small, and **each one is a rare opportunity to check a method that is currently
   validated on ZERO reactions.**
⟹ PART 2 ANSWERS ITSELF: the exemption is permanent and automatic, which is correct for his own
  stated reason — B+'s residual depends on the method and the level, so a calibration taken at one
  level does not transfer to another. A one-time measurement would be the wrong shape.
```
🔒 **AND THIS CORRECTS MY OWN §39.55(c), WHICH WAS TOO NARROW.** I scoped the calibration to R-A
because R-A was the one case I could name. **The right rule is broader and simpler, and I only see
it because he asked how to identify the case I had singled out.** §39.55(e) says the residual is
bounded "on one reaction"; under this rule it is bounded on every converged IRC we ever get.

### (c) The cost consequence, stated as he asked

```
🔴🔴 **THE PARAGRAPH THAT WAS HERE WAS WRONG — CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (engineer8, §39.79).**
   It read: *"B+'s cost is no longer a constant — it is (per-attempt cost) x P(the IRC converges)."*
   🔴 THAT CONTRADICTS (a) AND (b) OF THIS SAME SECTION. Under this ruling B+ RUNS ON 100 % OF
   ATTEMPTS, BOTH BRANCHES, SO ITS COST IS FLAT: (attempt count) x (per-attempt cost).
   🔒 P(converges) belongs to a DIFFERENT QUANTITY — the CALIBRATION YIELD, the number of attempts
   on which B+ can be checked against ground truth. I attached a sensible number to the wrong noun
   while ruling about that very noun. §39.76's AGREEMENT IS NOT IDENTITY, third instance today.
```
```
🟢 CORRECT COST MODEL:
   B+ core-h per round  =  (attempts) x (per-attempt B+ cost)          FLAT. No P anywhere.
   CALIBRATION YIELD    =  (attempts) x P(IRC converges)               <- where P belongs, and it
                                                                          is UNMEASURED
🔴 AND A SECOND-ORDER EFFECT WITH A KNOWN DIRECTION, which engineer8 should know before anchoring:
   B+ IS CHEAPER ON A CONVERGED IRC THAN ON A TRUNCATED ONE. Its terminal optimisations start from
   IRC points; on a converged path those points are already near a minimum, on a truncated path
   they are mid-descent with further to go. ⟹ anchor the per-attempt figure on the TRUNCATED case,
   which is both the expensive one and (by C-2.2) the common one. A flat number so anchored is
   CONSERVATIVE, and that is the right direction for a guard ceiling.
```

### (d) 🔒 On his process note

He told two people the question was with me before it was. He said so unprompted, in the message

`N₁ = min(600, remaining / (u_measured × r_composite))` asks **how many species we can afford**. To
afford a species is to obtain its **thermochemistry** — and a free energy needs the zero-point and
thermal corrections, which come **only from the frequency stage.**

  else — §39.76's AGREEMENT IS NOT IDENTITY, which coder11 has now independently rediscovered from
  the implementation side. **Two people, two routes, same defect class, one afternoon.**

### (b) 🟢 THE RULING — (b) and (c) are not alternatives. Do both, and the naming removes his objection.

```
u_cheap   DEFINED as complete opt+freq. 🔴 THIS ROUND ITS DENOMINATOR IS EMPTY.
          Report:  u_cheap: null, reason: "no species completed freq (EpsInf sentinel, §39.73)"

reading is only available **if the absence is unlabelled.** `u_cheap: null` with its reason, printed
beside a populated `u_opt`, cannot be misread. ⟹ **the fix for how it reads is not to keep a wrong
number; it is to give the right number its name and let it be absent.**
🔒 Same resolution as everywhere else this round: **do not choose between a wrong-but-present figure
and no figure. Name both quantities and let the missing one be missing, loudly.**
🟢 **AND `u_opt` CLOSES A LOOP OF MINE.** §39.74 said my §39.72 cation and open-shell factors
(×2.8, ×2.3, ×15.2) were "opt-only magnitudes that must not be quoted as opt+freq" — **and had no
correct name to be quoted under. `u_opt` is that name.** coder11's field gives my own findings a
label they were missing, which is why this ruling costs nothing and buys two things.

### (c) 🔴 AND A CONDITION ON THE RE-RUN THAT MUST LAND BEFORE IT, since he asked for the ruling first

After the EpsInf fix, `u_cheap` will be **assembled** from two rounds: an optimisation measured now
and a frequency measured later on the stored geometry.

🟢 THAT SUM IS LEGITIMATE — the freq runs on the same geometry at the same level, which is exactly
   what `stages_completed` records.
🔴 BUT IT IS ASSEMBLED, NOT MEASURED IN ONE RUN, AND IT MUST SAY SO. Per §39.61(c) the caps in
   force join the initial-condition record, and the two halves ran under different rounds and
   possibly different caps. ⟹ every assembled `u_cheap` carries BOTH halves' round and cap
   provenance, and a flag distinguishing it from one measured end-to-end.
⚠ WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY: a species whose optimisation ran under one wall cap and whose frequency
  runs under another has a total that no single configuration would reproduce. If the two ever

### (g) 🔒 THE GENERAL RULE — a state marker keyed to a NAME cannot protect an experiment keyed to a VALUE

The mechanism, exactly, from the code and the artefacts:
```
cli.py:599      if store.is_done(key):  print("이미 완료 → 건너뜀 (멱등 재개)");  continue
state.py:92     is_done(key)  ⟵ os.path.exists("state/<key>.done.json").  NOTHING ELSE.
                No configuration hash. No pkg_fingerprint. No extra_env. Only the name.
common.sh       writes the done marker from the WRAPPER's rc.
                base item: marker "status": "done", "detail": "rc=0"
                same item: terminal_status.json "status": "not_converged", G16 SIGNAL 11
                P5:        20 done markers, "rc=0",  while all 20 stage records carry rc=1
```
🔴 **This is §39.73(d) composing with idempotent resume, and the composition is worse than either
half.** §39.73(d) already ruled that `rc = 0` is not evidence of success — rc is a property of the
wrapper, not of the chemistry. What was not seen then is that the *same* uninformative rc is the
sole input to the marker that makes a skip **permanent**: a segfaulted job writes `done`, and every
future round silently declines to re-run it. The failure is absorbing, and it is silent in the one
place a reader would look — `plan.json` records `"status": "planned"`, `"skip_reason": null`, and
`plan_summary.n_skipped = 0`. **The returned report says the arm was planned and does not say it
did not run.**
```
🔒 RULING, two clauses, both required — neither alone closes it:
   (i)  `done` MUST NOT be written on the wrapper's rc. It must be written on PARSED CONTENT
        (`terminal_status.json`), which already exists and already got this right — it said
        `not_converged` for the very job the marker called `done`. §0-k's rule ("health is judged
        on parsed content, never on the banner") arriving at the resume path.
   (ii) `is_done` MUST compare a CONFIGURATION FINGERPRINT — at minimum hash(extra_env) plus the
        payload's pkg_fingerprint — and return False when it differs from the marker's. Otherwise
        any experiment whose arms differ only by an environment value is silently deleted by the
        resume logic, which is what happened here to a designed, pre-registered, already-ruled
        experiment.
🔴 (i) WITHOUT (ii) STILL LOSES THIS EXPERIMENT: yesterday's base job would then be marked failed
   and retried — but retried at whatever EpsInf the new plan carries, which is fine here by luck,
   and NOT fine for any arm whose earlier run legitimately SUCCEEDED under a different value.
   (ii) is the clause that makes an experiment safe to re-run; (i) is the clause that makes a crash
   visible. Ship both.
```

BEFORE comparing the arms of ANY multi-arm experiment, for EACH arm:

```

## 39.81 🟢🟢 THE BRACKET SHOULD BE RUN AT A **FIXED GEOMETRY** — this is not the cheap compromise, it is the RIGHT experiment, and §39.80(e)'s "re-run both arms in full" is SUPERSEDED BY MY OWN ARGUMENT (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> Triggered by engineer9's measured stage breakdown (§R39.45): the frequency stage — the only stage
> that reads `EpsInf` — is **2.27 core-h of a 65.87 core-h job**, a factor of **29**. The engineer
> supplied the price gap and correctly left the validity question to me. This is the ruling.
> **Abbreviations, first use in this section**: `calcfc` = Gaussian 16's request to compute an
> analytic Hessian at the FIRST optimisation step; `Berny` = Gaussian's geometry optimiser;
> `geom=check guess=read` = start from the geometry and converged density stored in a checkpoint
> file; `readfc` = reuse a STORED Hessian instead of computing one; `n_imag` = number of imaginary
> frequencies; `IEInf` = Gaussian's non-equilibrium-solvation flag (0 = equilibrium).

### (a) 🔒 WHERE `EpsInf` IS READ, now pinned to line numbers rather than inferred

```
endpoint_rough.gjf  route  opt=(loose,maxcycles=100)          NO calcfc, NO freq
endpoint_rough.log         NEqPCM matches:  0                 ⟹ energy+gradient NEVER read EpsInf
endpoint_tight.gjf  route  opt=(tight,calcfc,maxcycles=200) freq
endpoint_tight.log  :817, :827   NEqPCM  (Eps=18.5000, EpsInf=18.5000)   ⟵ the calcfc Hessian,
                                  computed at step 1, BEFORE the geometry moves
                    :1367 :1866 :2312 :2693   Berny cycles — NO NEqPCM in any of them
                    :3199  "Link1: Proceeding to internal job step number 2"
                    :3559, :3569  NEqPCM   ⟵ the freq
```
🔒 **`EpsInf` is read by HESSIAN CONSTRUCTION ONLY — twice: once for `calcfc`, once for `freq`. The
energy and the gradient never read it, and that is now a direct observation on both stages of both
arms, not an inference.**

### (b) 🟢 THE ARGUMENT — a fixed-geometry bracket answers C-8's actual question, and the full-opt bracket answers a different one

```
C-8.2/C-8.3 CERTIFIES A GEOMETRY: "n_imag == 0 at this structure". It does not certify an
optimiser trajectory. ⟹ THE QUESTION IS: at the certified structure, does the value of EpsInf
change n_imag or the spectrum?  A freq-only run at that fixed structure IS that question,
asked with nothing else varying.
```
And the converged geometry cannot depend on `EpsInf` except through the optimiser's PATH:
```
stationarity is  grad E = 0.   The gradient never reads EpsInf (a).
⟹ a point that is stationary under EpsInf = 18.5 is stationary under EpsInf = 1.0, at the same
  coordinates, to the same tolerance.  What EpsInf CAN change is the step 1 `calcfc` Hessian, hence
  the ROUTE Berny takes, hence which stationary point it reaches if several are reachable, and how
  many cycles it burns getting there.
```
⚠ **That residual — "which stationary point" — is the one thing the fixed-geometry design cannot
see, and I am NOT waving it away. It is tested for free in (c)(3) rather than assumed.**

### (c) 🔒 THE RULING — design (C): two freq-only jobs from one checkpoint, ~5–10 core-h total

```
1. TWO JOBS, BOTH FRESH, BOTH FROM THE SAME `endpoint_tight.chk` (10.5 MB, on disk, the EpsInf=18.5
   arm's certified geometry):
     route  #p nosymm wB97XD/gen scrf=(pcm,solvent=generic,read) freq geom=check guess=read
            Int(Grid=UltraFine)
     read block  arm U:  eps=18.5 / EpsInf=1.0        arm F:  eps=18.5 / EpsInf=18.5
   🔴 DO NOT reuse the existing 18.5 freq output as arm F and run only arm U. Both arms must be
      fresh and symmetric. Reason is NOT hygiene, it is the open-shell SCF: this is a DOUBLET
      radical, `guess=read` seeds from a density converged under one EpsInf, and unrestricted SCF
      solutions are not unique. Seeding BOTH arms from the SAME density makes that bias common-mode
      and removes it from the comparison. Arm F costs ~2.3 core-h; asymmetry is not worth saving it.
   🔴 `readfc` IS FORBIDDEN in both arms. Reusing a stored Hessian makes the experiment vacuous —
      it would compare a number against itself. Same shape as the `chk_handoff` hazard already
      ruled (a Hessian silently arriving from the wrong place).
2. PRIMARY + SECONDARY CRITERIA, and they are ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE SHARPER than §39.80(e)'s:
     n_imag identical (both 0)                          PRIMARY — the only thing C-8 consumes
     |ΔE(SCF)|            ≤ 1e-7 Hartree  (2.7 µeV)
     |Δν_i| for ALL 27 modes ≤ 0.1 cm⁻¹
     ⟨S²⟩ agreeing to the printed digits, both arms
   🟢 **THIS IS THE REAL REASON TO PREFER (C), AND IT IS SCIENTIFIC, NOT FINANCIAL.** In the full-opt
   design the two arms re-optimise independently, so the comparison sits on an ERROR FLOOR set by
   the optimiser: §39.80(d) measured 5.6 meV between two rough stages, and engineer9 measured the
   same instability at 1.42× in cost with exit geometries differing ~0.1 Å on hydrogen. **That floor
   is LARGER than the effect the experiment exists to bound.** A design whose noise exceeds its
   signal cannot return "invariant" — it can only return "not resolved", and it would have been
   read as invariant. At fixed geometry the floor drops to SCF convergence, ~1e-8 Hartree, and the
   test acquires the power to detect an EpsInf effect four orders of magnitude below anything that
   could move a barrier.
3. THE RESIDUAL FROM (b), TESTED FOR FREE, NO EXTRA JOB: a `freq` job prints
   `Forces (Hartrees/Bohr)`. Compare the two arms' force matrices.
     identical to printed precision ⟹ the gradient is EpsInf-blind AT THIS GEOMETRY, measured
       rather than argued ⟹ the certified structure is stationary under both values ⟹ the
       "different basin" residual is closed for this species.
     NOT identical ⟹ (a) is wrong, the gradient does read EpsInf somewhere, and the whole
       fixed-geometry argument collapses — in which case fall back to design (A), full opt+freq at
       both values, and pay the 130 core-h. 🔒 **That is the pre-registered escape hatch: (C) is not
       a bet, it carries its own falsifier and names the fallback in advance.**
4. FREE PLUMBING CONTROL, also no extra job: arm F must reproduce the ALREADY-EXISTING in-job 18.5
   frequencies (77.0220 / 106.9681 / 151.7485 cm⁻¹, E = −349.620897959 Hartree, §39.80(c)). It is
   the same geometry, the same value, the same level — via a restart path instead of in-job. If it
   does NOT reproduce them, the restart plumbing is broken and NO verdict may be read from either
   arm. This costs nothing and it is the only check that distinguishes "EpsInf matters" from
   "`geom=check` handed us a different structure".
```

### (d) 🔴 SELF-SUPERSESSION — §39.80(e)(2) is obsolete, and it is obsolete because design (C) dissolves the problem it was solving

§39.80(e)(2) required re-running **both** arms in full (130 core-h) because the two existing jobs
were produced by different payload versions (`pkg_fingerprint` `028acb21dc49701c` vs
`74a881b6f3bfa5cb`) and a low arm run under a newer payload would be confounded by code version
rather than by `EpsInf`. **The lead approved that clause. I am withdrawing it, and the reason is
that it was a repair for design (A)'s weakness, not a requirement of the physics.** Under (C) both
arms are generated by the same package, in the same round, from the same checkpoint, differing in
one character string — **the confound is removed by construction rather than paid for.** The
approved-but-superseded version was not wrong when written; it is simply the wrong instrument once
the geometry stops varying.
```
COST, mine to shape and engineer9's to ceiling:
   design (A), approved 2026-08-21, NOW WITHDRAWN     2 × 65.9 = 130   core-h
   design (C), THIS RULING                            2 × (freq stage 2.27 + a cold SCF from
                                                       guess=read) ≈ 5–10 core-h
   ⟹ 13–26× cheaper AND ~4 orders of magnitude more sensitive. Those two facts point the same way,
     which is rare enough to be worth stating: I am not trading rigour for budget here.
```
⚠ **SCOPE, unchanged and not to be quietly widened**: one species ([Li(EC)]⁰ doublet, 11 atoms), one
level (wB97XD / def2-SVPD, G-3), one geometry. A pass licenses EpsInf-insensitivity for THAT. It is
also n = 1 for reliability — engineer9's warning stands, one certified arm is not a 100% success
rate — but reliability is not what this experiment measures.

### (e) 🟢 THE SAME RULING APPLIES TO P5's RECOVERY, with one label that must not be dropped

Design (B) for P5 — frequency-only from the stored converged geometries, ~140 core-h base against
~1,000–2,000 for full re-runs (engineer9's estimate; the spread is his to defend) — is **method-
ologically sound and is already the plan of record**: §39.74 established the optimisations are real

## 39.82 🔒 THREE RULINGS — P5/P1b NEED NO BRACKET (their frequencies are a COST measurement, and cost is EpsInf-invariant BY CONSTRUCTION); the spot-check moves to an ANION; and "base" MAY NOT BE THE VALUE THAT HAPPENED TO CONVERGE (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> Answers three questions routed by the lead from coder12 and engineer8/§R39.43.
> **Abbreviations, first use in this section**: `P5` = the 20-task species cost survey; `P1b` = the
> 4-task cheap-geometry cost item, whose deliverables are `r_composite` = (cheap opt+freq + high
> single point) ÷ (cheap opt+freq) and `r_high` = (full-high opt+freq) ÷ (cheap opt+freq);
> `u_cheap` = the per-species cheap opt+freq cost that is B1's sizing denominator; `n²` = the square
> of the refractive index, which is what `EpsInf` physically is.

### (a) 🔴 QUESTION 2 WAS ALREADY RULED — §39.81, and the lead's phrasing contains the error the ruling removes

The lead asks whether re-running `freq` on *"a geometry optimised under a DIFFERENT EpsInf value"*
is sound. **That phrase presupposes something now measured to be false.** No geometry in this
project was ever optimised *under* an `EpsInf` value in any sense that moves it:
```
§39.81(a)  the energy and the gradient NEVER read EpsInf — rough log matches NEqPCM zero times;
           the tight log reads it ONLY at the step-1 calcfc Hessian and at the freq.
§39.75(a)  INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, 20 jobs, collected before the question was asked:
           P1b `sp` and `force` steps  10 ⟹ 10 Normal termination.  ALL FINE.
           P1b steps containing `freq`  8 ⟹  8 Error termination.   ALL DEAD.
           **Single points live. Gradients live. Optimisations live. Every Hessian died.**
```
⟹ `EpsInf` can change the optimiser's step-1 Hessian, hence its PATH; it cannot change where
grad E = 0. The stored geometry is not "an EpsInf = 18.5 geometry" — it is a stationary point of a
functional that never saw `EpsInf`. **Ruling stands as §39.81(c): freq-only bracket, both arms
fresh from the same checkpoint, `readfc` forbidden, and the forces-identity check as the
pre-registered falsifier.**

### (b) 🟢 QUESTION 1 — P5 AND P1b NEED NO BRACKET AT ALL, AND THE REASON IS NOT BUDGET

engineer8's §R39.43 and my §39.80(e)(4) are **not actually in conflict**: §R39.43 answered *where a
double-run should live* (bundled vs one-off probe) and priced "20 × doubled" as the consequence of
making doubling the plan-wide default. It did not rule on how many species need bracketing — it
says so itself. **I adopt every structural recommendation in §R39.43 and overturn only the default
scope**, on a ground engineer8 had no reason to consider:
```
🔒 P5's AND P1b's FREQUENCIES EXIST TO MEASURE COST. u_cheap, r_composite, r_high are core-h
   RATIOS. And the core-h cost of a Hessian DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE VALUE OF EpsInf:
   same molecule, same basis, same grid, same number of CPHF/derivative-Fock passes. EpsInf is a
   scalar in the solvent operator, not a term that changes the work.
⟹ A DOUBLED P5 WOULD PRODUCE TWO COST NUMBERS THAT MUST AGREE BY CONSTRUCTION, at 800–2,600
  core-h (design A) or ~46–600 (design B). It cannot fail. **A measurement that cannot fail is not
  a control, it is a tax.**
```
🔴 **The safety instinct behind "default ON, collapse only by explicit human action" is right and I
am not discarding it — I am moving it to where it bites.** engineer8's worry is a silently
under-verified single run. Repeating one code-path test 20 times does not verify it; it repeats it.
Verification comes from (i) the endpoint bracket at ~5–10 core-h with its forces falsifier, and
(ii) ONE adversarially chosen species. So:
```
🔒 THE GATE MOVES FROM THE RUN TO THE READOUT — this is the whole of the ruling:
   P5/P1b RUN at a single EpsInf value. No doubling. Their COST deliverables (u_cheap,
   r_composite, r_high) are usable immediately — cost is EpsInf-invariant by construction.
   🔴 Their CHEMICAL readouts (n_imag, zero-point energy, thermal corrections, any free energy)
   are stamped with the EpsInf value used and are NOT certified until BOTH the endpoint bracket
   (§39.81) and the adversarial spot-check (c) have returned invariant. The stamp is the release
   gate, it defaults to UNCERTIFIED, and it collapses only on explicit lead action — exactly
   §R39.43's shape, applied to the claim instead of to the compute.
```
And I keep §R39.43's two structural points verbatim, because both are correct and neither depends
on scope: **bundle the bracket inside a batch already being submitted** (this site's queue wait
inverts with size — a standalone small probe pays the worst tax), and **run the two values as
separate parallel tasks, never one serial job** (the 6 h wall cap is tight against a serial double
Hessian).

### (c) 🔒 THE SPOT-CHECK — one species, chosen ADVERSARIALLY, and it is an ANION

§39.80(e)(4) said "spot-check ONE P5 species". That was underspecified: an arbitrary species tests
the code path where it is least likely to bite. The selection rule follows from what `EpsInf` is —
the *fast* part of the solvent's response — so detection power scales with how strongly the species
polarises the continuum:
```
SELECTION RULE (stated as a rule, so it survives a change of species list):
  pick the species maximising reaction-field coupling = net charge first, then diffuse/polarisable
  density, then soft low-frequency modes.  A neutral rigid molecule is the WEAKEST possible probe.
CHOSEN:  ec_radical_anion   — charged (anion, strongest continuum coupling), open-shell doublet,
         soft ring modes, AND it is the S1 reduction intermediate itself, so a null result is
         directly reusable rather than a proxy.
BACKUP / closed-shell control if one is wanted:  pf6_anion (highly polarisable, 7 atoms).
🟢 CHEAPEST HOME IS P1b, NOT P5:  P1b already carries hco3_anion (charge −1, 5 atoms) with a
   stored geometry — an anion spot-check there is a 5-atom Hessian, the cheapest charged probe on
   the board. If engineer9 prices ec_radical_anion above ~20 core-h for the pair, take hco3_anion
   instead and record that the probe traded chemical relevance for charge coverage.
COST SHAPE: 2 × (one freq-only restart on a stored geometry). Engineer prices it.
FAILURE ⟹ the endpoint's null does NOT generalise, species-dependence is real, and THEN the
   20-species bracket engineer8 priced becomes necessary — at design (B) rates, not (A).
```

### (d) 🔴🔴 QUESTION 3 — "BASE" MAY NOT BE 18.5, AND THE REASON IS THE SELECTION, NOT THE NUMBER

coder12 framed the choice as 18.5 (already converged, cheap) versus 1.0 (§39.73's original
framing). **Both are wrong, and the first is wrong in a way worth naming.**
```
🔴 CHOOSING 18.5 BECAUSE IT IS THE VALUE THAT CONVERGED IS SELECTING A PHYSICAL PARAMETER ON THE
   OUTCOME OF A CRASHED RUN. The other arm did not "fail" — IT WAS NEVER RUN (§39.80). There is no
   evidence 1.0 converges worse; there is no evidence about 1.0 at all. A parameter chosen this way
   carries a survivorship bias into every downstream number, and it is exactly the state §39.80(i)
   named: "circumvented at the top of the admissible interval, sensitivity unmeasured."
🔴 AND 1.0 IS NOT BETTER. Both 1.0 and 18.5 are INTERVAL ENDPOINTS — bracket instruments, not
   solvents. §39.73's own ⚠ says so: "I am NOT claiming these are physically sensible SOLVENTS."
   Promoting either endpoint to production "base" misreads a bounding device as a value.
🟢 RULING: THE BASE VALUE IS THE PHYSICAL ONE — EpsInf = n² for the EC:EMC 3:7 mixture.
   ⚠ OUR OWN SPEC ALREADY CARRIES `EpsInf = n² = 1.95` (§S1 candidate B, input list). **I have
     NOT verified its provenance — no source is recorded at that line, and I will not launder a
     number into production by pointing at our own document.** Tag every use
     `[UNVERIFIED PROVENANCE — 02_METHOD_SPEC §S1 input line, no source recorded]` until someone
     sources it: refractive index of EC and of EMC at the sodium-D line near 20–25 °C, combined by
     an explicitly named mixing rule (Lorentz–Lorenz on n², not a bare volume-fraction average of
     n — and if the bare average is used anyway, say so and carry the difference).
   🟢 THIS DOES NOT REOPEN §39.26(b). That blocker is about Abraham α/β and surface-tension
     descriptors nobody has. A refractive index is a tabulated bulk optical property; §39.73 said
     so itself while declining to source it. The reason for declining — "there is a better move
     that needs no value" — was sound while the bracket was unrun. IT IS NO LONGER A REASON TO
     RUN PRODUCTION AT A VALUE WE KNOW IS WRONG.
   🔒 EXPECTED-VALUE ARGUMENT, since this must be decided BEFORE the bracket returns: if the
     bracket says invariant, the choice costs nothing either way. If it says dependent, everything
     run at 18.5 is wrong and must be redone, while everything run at ~1.95 is approximately right.
     ⟹ 1.95 weakly dominates. Choose the dominating option; do not bet on the null.
   🔒 UNCONDITIONAL, whatever value is used: THE C-8 CERTIFICATE MUST RECORD THE EpsInf VALUE IT
     WAS COMPUTED AT. A certificate that does not name its solvent parameters is the same defect
     as `[VERIFIED-IN-RUN]` not naming which stage it verified (§39.73(b)).
```
⚠ **One consequence to accept openly**: the endpoint already certified (§39.80(c)) was computed at
`EpsInf = 18.5`. Under this ruling it is a valid *bracket arm* and a *provisional* certificate, not
the production number, unless the bracket returns invariant — in which case it is fine and nothing
is re-run. **That is the invariance test paying for itself: ~5–10 core-h decides whether a 65.9
core-h certificate stands.**

## 39.84 🟢 EpsInf SOURCED — 1.93, not 1.95, and the mixing-rule worry I raised is DEAD (it changes the answer by 0.001). Provenance upgraded from UNVERIFIED to CATALOG-GRADE, which is not the same as cleared (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> §39.82(d) ruled the base value is `EpsInf` = n² for EC:EMC 3:7 and tagged the spec's existing
> `1.95` `[UNVERIFIED PROVENANCE]`. The lead asked whether I wanted to source it now or leave it
> open. I picked it up, because the alternative is a tag that rots: an `[UNVERIFIED]` label that
> survives three rounds becomes de facto acceptance, which is the same family as "measured but
> unread" (§39.75). It cost one search round and no compute.

### (a) What the sources actually say — including where they disagree

```
EMC   n20/D = 1.378   supplier catalogue aggregates (ChemicalBook, ChemBK, LookChem)
                      ⚠ one entry in the same set reports 1.368. Both carried below.
EC    n     = 1.4199  ChemicalBook — 🔴 NO TEMPERATURE STATED on the entry.
                      A search summary also returned "1.4158 at 25 °C" and "1.4195 at 20 °C";
                      🔴 I DO NOT USE THOSE TWO. They are internally incoherent — refractive index
                      FALLS with temperature, so 1.4195 @ 20 °C below 1.4199 @ 40 °C is backwards,
                      and I could not trace either to a primary entry. Recorded as seen, not used.
EC    melting point 34–38 °C (Wikipedia 34–37; ChemicalBook 35–38 "lit.")
```
🔴 **THE SYSTEMATIC NOBODY HAS NAMED YET: pure EC IS A SOLID AT 298 K.** Any pure-EC refractive
index quoted "at 20/25 °C" is a supercooled or extrapolated liquid property. In the 3:7 mixture EC
*is* liquid, so a pure-component mixing rule necessarily consumes a hypothetical subcooled-liquid
value. Small, but it is a real systematic and it is structural — it does not go away with a better
catalogue, only with a measurement on the MIXTURE.

### (b) The computation, and the death of my own mixing-rule caveat

Lorentz–Lorenz on volume fractions, φ(EC) = 0.30:  (n²−1)/(n²+2) mixed, then inverted.
```
EC 1.4199 / EMC 1.378   Lorentz-Lorenz 1.9333    volume-fraction-on-n² 1.9341   Δ 0.0007
EC 1.4158 / EMC 1.378                  1.9300                          1.9306   Δ 0.0006
EC 1.4199 / EMC 1.368                  1.9137                          1.9148   Δ 0.0011
EC 1.4158 / EMC 1.368                  1.9104                          1.9113   Δ 0.0009
```
🟢 **§39.82(d) demanded Lorentz–Lorenz over a bare volume-fraction average and told anyone using the
bare average to "carry the difference". THE DIFFERENCE IS ≤ 0.0011 — three orders of magnitude below
the spread between catalogue entries. My caveat was correct in principle and irrelevant in
magnitude. Withdrawn: use either rule, say which, stop thinking about it.** The real uncertainty is
entirely in the input refractive indices (1.910–1.933, a spread of 0.023), not in how they are mixed.

### (c) 🔒 RULING — working base `EpsInf = 1.93`

```
VALUE      EpsInf = 1.93     [CATALOG-GRADE PROVENANCE — supplier aggregates, EC entry carries no
                              temperature, EC is subcooled at 298 K; NOT a primary measurement]
RANGE      1.910 – 1.933 across all four source combinations. Report as 1.93 ± 0.02.
vs SPEC    §S1's existing 1.95 is ~1% high and sits just outside that range. Immaterial in every
           use we have — but it is now a NUMBER WITH A RANGE instead of a number with no source,
           and that is the whole point of doing this.
🔒 PROVENANCE IS UPGRADED, NOT CLEARED. `[CATALOG-GRADE]` ≠ verified. Supplier catalogues are
   aggregates that copy each other; the 1.378-vs-1.368 disagreement inside one such set is direct
   evidence of that. Do not launder this into "sourced" in any downstream document.
```

### (d) 🟢 AND HERE IS WHY I AM NOT SPENDING MORE ON IT

```
IF the bracket (§39.81) returns invariant   ⟹ EpsInf enters nothing. 1.93, 1.95, 18.5 and 1.0 are
                                              all equally right, and further sourcing buys zero.
IF the bracket returns DEPENDENT            ⟹ catalogue-grade is no longer good enough, AND the
                                              correct move is NOT a better pure-component number:
                                              it is n measured on the 3:7 MIXTURE at 298 K, which
                                              sidesteps both the mixing rule and the subcooled-EC
                                              systematic in (a) at once.
⟹ EITHER WAY, more pure-component literature work is wasted effort. The bracket decides which
  question is even worth asking. This is the same "design so that not knowing the value does not
  block us" move as §39.73(c) — applied one level up, to my own sourcing task.
```
⚠ 1.93 is inside the bracket interval [1.0, 18.5] by construction, so a null result covers it. That
is not a coincidence — it is why the bracket was specified on the *interval* rather than on a value.

**Sources** (recorded so the catalogue grade is auditable, not to imply endorsement):
[ChemicalBook — ethylene carbonate](https://www.chemicalbook.com/ChemicalProductProperty_EN_CB3488966.htm),
[ChemicalBook — ethyl methyl carbonate](https://www.chemicalbook.com/ChemicalProductProperty_EN_CB3459272.htm),
[ChemBK — ethyl methyl carbonate](https://www.chembk.com/en/chem/Ethyl%20Methyl%20Carbonate),
[Wikipedia — ethylene carbonate (melting point)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethylene_carbonate).

### (c) 🔒 THE TWO CLAUSES ENGINEER9 ASKED FOR — ADOPTED, PLUS A THIRD THEY DID NOT ASK FOR

```
(i)  ORDER IS FIXED. Constraint 3 (arm F reproducing the existing in-job -349.620897959 to 1e-7)
     is read FIRST, ALONE, BEFORE the U-vs-F comparison is looked at. It is not a side check run

     then declare invariance against the relaxed bar. engineer9 is right that this will look
     reasonable at the time; that is exactly why it is forbidden in advance rather than judged
     later. A criterion adjusted after seeing the data is not a criterion, it is a description.

modulate the cavity, and it *is* the S1 reduction intermediate, so a null is directly reusable
rather than a proxy. Its geometry is on disk and converged. Cost is not why it was chosen; it is
merely also cheap.

### (e) 🔒 WHY TWO SPECIES IS ENOUGH — THE NULL HERE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT QUANTITATIVE

This is the distinction that separates a real probe from the P5 doubling I refused in §39.82(b):
```
THE HYPOTHESIS IS: "G16 READS EpsInf AND DOES NOT USE IT under equilibrium solvation (IEInf=0)."
That is a claim about a BRANCH NOT BEING TAKEN — not about a magnitude being small.
⟹ A structural null does not accumulate confidence by sampling more molecules. It is refuted by
  ONE counterexample, so the right design is ONE probe chosen to MAXIMISE the chance of being that
  counterexample (d), plus the endpoint. Two species, chemically distinct (neutral doublet /
  anionic doublet), one of them adversarial. A third adds repetition, not power.
🔴 THE ESCALATION, PRE-REGISTERED: if the anion returns NONZERO-BUT-SMALL (above 1e-7, below
  anything that could move a barrier), the null has changed CHARACTER from structural to
  quantitative — and species coverage then matters, because a small effect can be large elsewhere.
  ONLY THEN add `li_ec_cation` (cation, closed shell — the charge-sign axis neither current probe
  covers), and only then does engineer8's 20-species bracket become a live question again.
```

### (f) 🔴 THE IMPLEMENTATION TRAP, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT WOULD ARRIVE LOOKING LIKE A METHOD ERROR

engineer9: if (C) ships as a *flag on* `endpoint_prep.sh`, that payload still runs rough-then-tight;
`sei_stage` inherits a completed stage only when `pkg_fingerprint` matches, and it does not — so the
rough optimisation silently re-runs, logging `rerun_stale_fingerprint` and proceeding. **~4 core-h
per arm becomes ~62. 15×, silently, in the expensive direction.**
```
🔒 (C) MUST BE ITS OWN PAYLOAD WITH NO ROUGH STAGE IN IT AT ALL — not a flag on the existing one.
   This is a METHOD requirement, not only an engineering preference: a payload that can re-run the
   optimisation can also re-run it DIFFERENTLY per arm, which reintroduces the exact geometry
   asymmetry design (C) exists to eliminate. The cost blow-up is the visible symptom; the
   comparison confound is the part that would have been silent.
```

## 39.86 🔴 I WITHDRAW MY OWN ~20 core-h THRESHOLD — it was an invented number about to make a SCIENTIFIC choice; and P5's design (B) survives the retraction because my approval never rested on the margin (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> engineer9's §R39.48 retracts the P5 frequency-only estimate (46/140/600 → 375/577/901 core-h) —
> they had scaled a measured Hessian by ATOM COUNT when the driver is basis-function count
> (`ec_radical_anion`: ten atoms, one FEWER than the anchor, `NBasis` 299 against 173). They then
> priced my chosen spot-check species at 21.6 core-h, which trips the "~20 core-h → take the
> cheaper species" rule I wrote in §39.82(c), and argued the rule is wrong. **They are right.**

### (a) 🔴 THE THRESHOLD WAS MINE, IT WAS INVENTED, AND IT WAS ABOUT TO OVERRULE THE SELECTION CRITERION I HAD JUST DERIVED

```
§39.82(c) said: "If engineer9 prices ec_radical_anion above ~20 core-h for the pair, take
                 hco3_anion instead and record that the probe traded chemical relevance for
                 charge coverage."
🔴 WHERE DID ~20 COME FROM? NOWHERE. I wrote it as a convenience while handing off a question,
   and it was never derived from the recovery it qualifies, from the guard, or from anything else.
   It then acquired the authority of a criterion by being written down — which is the same failure
   as `[UNVERIFIED PROVENANCE]` decaying into acceptance (§39.84), one round faster.
🔴 AND IT WOULD HAVE MADE A SCIENTIFIC CHOICE ON A 16 core-h DELTA. hco3_anion is NOT a cheaper
   ec_radical_anion. It is a rigid 5-atom CLOSED-SHELL anion: it keeps the charge axis and drops
   the open-shell (diffuse singly-occupied orbital) and soft-mode axes — which is most of the
   continuum coupling the §39.82(c) selection rule was written to maximise. It is a DIFFERENT
   EXPERIMENT, not a discounted one, and my own sentence "traded chemical relevance for charge
   coverage" said so while treating the trade as acceptable for 16 core-h.
```
🔒 **RULING: the threshold is withdrawn, and I am not replacing it with engineer9's ~200 either —
because a number of mine is what caused this.** The rule is structural and the number belongs to
the engineer:
```
COST MAY OVERRULE A SPECIES CHOICE ONLY WHEN THE PROBE'S COST IS A SIGNIFICANT FRACTION OF WHAT
THE PROBE QUALIFIES. Here the probe qualifies a 375–900 core-h recovery, so 21.6 core-h is not a
cost question at all. **engineer9 holds the number and will say when it binds; I hold the science
and will not pre-empt them with an arithmetic guess again.**
```
⟹ **`ec_radical_anion` STANDS, at 21.6 core-h base.** `hco3_anion` is **removed as a fallback** —
it was never a substitute. If it is ever run it is an ADDITIONAL probe on the closed-shell axis,
recorded as such.
⚠ SELF-CORRECTION, same family: §39.85(d) listed `pf6_anion` as a "cheap backup, 4.1 core-h". **That
4.1 is its OPTIMISATION wall cost, not its Hessian cost**, and quoting it in a sentence about probe
substitution invited exactly the error above. Struck. Any probe's cost is its own Hessian's cost,
which per engineer9 scales with `NBasis`, not with atoms.

### (b) 🟢 P5's DESIGN (B) SURVIVES — my approval never rested on the margin, and there is a reason to prefer it that has no cost term at all

engineer9 asks, fairly, whether my approval of (B) was resting on the size of the saving (which has
moved from ~400–1,900 to ~100–1,600, and is small at (B)-pessimistic vs (A)-optimistic). **It was
not, and here is the argument that does not depend on the margin:**
```
(A) re-optimises. The optimiser's spread is MEASURED — 1.42× in cost, ~0.1 Å on hydrogen
    (engineer9), 5.6 meV between two rough stages (§39.80(d)).
⟹ A RE-OPTIMISED P5 RECOVERY PRODUCES FREQUENCIES BELONGING TO A DIFFERENT STRUCTURE THAN THE ONE
  WHOSE OPTIMISATION COST WAS ALREADY MEASURED. The assembled `u_cheap` would then be
  opt-cost(geometry 1) + freq-cost(geometry 2) — two halves of two different calculations, and any
  chemical readout (zero-point energy, thermal correction) would belong to a structure we hold no
  cost measurement for. §39.76's "agreement is not identity", arriving at a cost denominator.
⟹ (B) IS PREFERRED EVEN IF IT WERE THE MORE EXPENSIVE OPTION. Reusing the converged geometry is
  what makes the two halves halves OF THE SAME THING.
```
🟢 Their per-species finding is the useful residue: **four species carry 70% of the cost**
(`li_ec2_cation` ×2, `ec_dimer`, `li_ec2_cation_L1`; `h2o` is 0.07 core-h). If the recovery is ever
cut, cut those four and keep the other eighteen — a far better-shaped decision than a flat 22-way
trim, and it is available only because they went species-by-species instead of scaling an anchor.

### (c) 🔒 A CONFOUND THEIR `NBasis` FINDING EXPOSES IN MY OWN SPOT-CHECK DESIGN — pre-registered, because it would otherwise be argued about after the fact

```
endpoint probe        [Li(EC)]⁰   level3, NBasis 173, neutral doublet
spot-check probe      ec_radical_anion   level2, NBasis 299, anionic doublet
🔴 THE TWO PROBES DIFFER IN SPECIES **AND LEVEL AND BASIS SIZE, SIMULTANEOUSLY.** I had been
   treating the spot-check as varying the species alone. It does not.
```
🟢 **For a NULL result this is a strength, not a flaw**: the structural claim ("G16 reads `EpsInf`
and does not use it under `IEInf=0`") confirmed at two levels and two basis sizes covers more of the
code path than confirming it twice at one level would.
🔴 **For a DISAGREEMENT it is fatal to interpretation** — species, level and basis would all be
candidate causes at once. **Pre-registered disambiguation, decided now**: if the spot-check
disagrees with the endpoint, the next run is **the ENDPOINT species at P5's level2/NBasis-299
settings**, before any conclusion about species dependence is drawn. That isolates level+basis from
species with one job, and it must happen BEFORE engineer8's 20-species bracket is reopened — else
we would be pricing 20 species to answer a question that might be about a basis set.

### (d) On the retraction itself — the general form, since it is the third instance this project has caught

engineer9 scaled a Hessian cost by atom count; the driver is `NBasis`; `ec_radical_anion` has one
FEWER atom than the anchor and 1.7× its basis functions. They name it as §R39.41's S₂₁ cube-law
error committed inside the document that retracted that very error.
```
🔒 THE FORM, WORTH KEEPING BECAUSE IT HAS NOW APPEARED IN A METHOD CLAIM (§39.73's "first job to
   ask for a Hessian"), A COST MODEL (S₂₁, twice), AND A GATE (§39.64's barrier reference):
   AN ANCHOR THAT EXPLAINS THE CASE IN FRONT OF IT PERFECTLY IS NOT THEREBY VALIDATED FOR ITS
   SCOPE. The endpoint anchor was correct — for the endpoint. Nothing in its agreement with the
   endpoint says which VARIABLE carries it, and agreement on one point cannot distinguish atom
   count from basis count when the two happen to correlate there.
⟹ THE MECHANICAL CHECK, cheap enough to be habitual: when reusing a measured anchor, state the
  VARIABLE it is being scaled by and verify that variable differs between anchor and target in the
  expected direction. Here it did not — atoms went DOWN while cost went UP, and that single
  comparison would have caught it before the number was quoted.
```
I audited my own numbers against this and they are clean by construction rather than by care:
every cost I have quoted (§39.80(j), §39.83(d)) is the SAME species at the SAME level as its
anchor, so no scaling variable was ever involved. **That is luck, not method** — I had no rule that
would have stopped me if the design had needed extrapolation, and now there is one.

> Answers coder12's three routed questions (already ruled — pointers in (a)) plus two genuinely new

### (a) The three routed questions were ruled before they were asked — pointers, not re-derivation

```
(a) P5 scope        §39.82(b)  single value, NO bracket inside P5. Their option (2), corrected:
                               the one-species check is a TWO-ARM PAIR at the interval ends, run
                               as ITS OWN item — not "the other end" of P5's single value. Two arms
                               are required because a bracket bounds an INTERVAL, and because
                               §39.81(c)(1) requires both arms fresh and symmetric.
(b) P1b scope       §39.82(b)  identical ruling, identical reason: its deliverables (r_composite,
                               r_high) are COST ratios, and Hessian cost does not depend on the
                               VALUE of EpsInf. Single value, no bracket, readout-gated.
(c) base value      §39.84     EpsInf = 1.93 [CATALOG-GRADE PROVENANCE]. NEITHER 1.0 NOR 18.5 —
                               both are interval endpoints, i.e. instruments, not solvents.
🔒 AND THE GATE IS ON THE READOUT, NOT THE RUN (§39.82(b)): P5/P1b COST deliverables are usable the
   moment they land; their CHEMICAL deliverables (n_imag, zero-point energy, thermal corrections)
   carry the EpsInf value used and stay UNCERTIFIED by default until the endpoint bracket AND the
   spot-check both return invariant.
⟹ SCHEDULING: run the endpoint bracket and the `ec_radical_anion` spot-check in the SAME round.

### (b) 🔴🔴 NEW, AND IT IS THE MOST DANGEROUS THING IN coder12's MESSAGE

> *"with the new retry policy, P5's sentinel crashes now classify as `engine` and would be
> AUTO-RESUBMITTED every round until the wiring lands."*

```
🔴 THE EpsInf SENTINEL CRASH IS DETERMINISTIC. Same deck ⟹ same crash, every time, forever.
   An automatic retry of a deterministic input defect is not a retry — it is a LOOP THAT SPENDS
   BUDGET. P5 would burn ~1,000–2,000 core-h per round producing nothing, indefinitely, and every
   round would look like it had "tried".
🔒 RULING, general, not specific to EpsInf:
   RETRY CLASSIFICATION MUST DISTINGUISH A TRANSIENT ENGINE FAILURE FROM A DETERMINISTIC INPUT
   DEFECT. `engine` means "the same input might succeed next time" — node flake, filesystem, OOM,
   preemption. A malformed or incomplete INPUT DECK is not that class, and the sentinel is the
   clearest possible case: G16 states the cause in one line and dies at the same point every time.
   ⟹ NEW cause_class for it, ALONGSIDE `PROTOCOL` (§39.68(3)): a defect the RUN cannot fix.
      Behaviour: FAIL, DO NOT RETRY, surface to lead. Retrying is the wrong direction because it is
      expensive AND because it manufactures the appearance of effort.
🔴 UNTIL THAT LANDS: P5 MUST NOT BE SUBMITTABLE. coder12's own sequencing note is correct and I am
   making it a hard precondition — the EpsInf wiring lands BEFORE P5 is next submitted, and if the
   retry reclassification is not ready, P5 stays out of the round entirely.
🟢 The zero-cost pre-check stands as the gate either way: generate P5's deck, grep for `EpsInf`.
```

### (c) 🟢 THE FRESH-KEY REQUIREMENT IS WITHDRAWN — design (C) dissolves it, and coder12's dependency finding is right

coder12 declined to build `endpoint_prep_reactant_epsinf_unity` because the base key is a
`depends_on` target for three U56-2 items and the collector's lookup key, so retiring it would
silently drop U56-2 — the same trap as yesterday's P1/P1b. **They are right, and the requirement is
obsolete for a better reason than the one they gave:**
```
§39.80(e)(1) demanded a fresh key for THREE reasons, in a world where the low arm meant RE-RUNNING
`endpoint_prep_reactant`:  (i) the done marker would skip it; (ii) `--force` is too broad;
                           (iii) the crash evidence must survive.
🔒 DESIGN (C) RE-RUNS NOTHING. It is a NEW freq-only payload with NO rough stage (§39.85(f)),
   reading the stored `endpoint_tight.chk`. It does not touch `endpoint_prep_reactant` at all.
⟹ DO NOT reset, re-run, or retire the base key. Leave it exactly as it is — it is now a
  PRESERVED ARTEFACT (the crash evidence) and a live dependency target simultaneously, and both
  uses are satisfied by leaving it alone. (i) and (ii) are moot; (iii) is satisfied by not touching
  it, which is stronger than archiving it.
🟢 coder12's `reset_item` archiving to `jobs/<key>.reset.<epoch>` is still the right default for
  every OTHER item that genuinely needs a re-run. Keep it. It is simply not needed here.
```
⚠ **AND A GAP THEIR MESSAGE EXPOSES, which I am flagging rather than ruling because it is plumbing**:
if three U56-2 items `depends_on` `endpoint_prep_reactant`, they currently depend on an item that
**CRASHED AND HAS NO CERTIFICATE** — while the only real C-8 certificate lives under
`endpoint_prep_reactant_epsinf_full`. A dependency satisfied by a `done` marker over a segfaulted
job is §39.80(g)'s defect wearing a dependency-graph costume. **Someone must check what those three
items actually read from that key before U56-2 is released.** If they read the certificate, they are
currently pointed at nothing.

## 39.88 🔴 THE ONE-JOB DESIGN BROKE MY OWN CONSTRAINT 1 THROUGH A SHARED `%chk` — accepted and fixed; and 🔴 SELF-CORRECTION ON ROUND A: my flat refusal of design (A) CONFLATED THE PRIMARY CRITERION WITH THE SECONDARY ONES (proposer, 2026-08-21)

one G16 job, ONE shared %chk (the deck's only %chk line today: %chk=endpoint_tight.chk):
  step 1 (arm U)  geom=check guess=read  reads the stored density              OK
  step 1 ENDS     writes ITS converged density into that same chk
  step 2 (arm F)  geom=check guess=read  reads ARM U's OUTPUT       ⟵ CONSTRAINT 1 BROKEN
FIX:  step 1  %oldchk=endpoint_tight.chk  %chk=arm_u.chk  ...  EpsInf=1.0
      step 2  %oldchk=endpoint_tight.chk  %chk=arm_f.chk  ...  EpsInf=18.5

1 (both arms seeded from the SAME untouched density).** And it would have left no trace: a reader
sees two arms, one job, one node, one build, and concludes the comparison was maximally
controlled. **The tighter the control story, the more invisible the leak inside it** — this is the
same shape as §39.64 (a gate referencing both clauses to one end, corrupting both at once) and
§39.73(b) (a route smoke that verified one stage and was read as verifying all). Adopted verbatim.

is a deck feature that does not exist yet, and my stated fallback (same-node placement, host

NOT optional in the fallback, because it is the only thing that makes a node mismatch visible.

7.9–9.3 → **7.3–8.6 core-h**.

### (c) 🔴🔴 SELF-CORRECTION — MY REFUSAL OF DESIGN (A) WAS TOO BROAD. IT CONFLATED THE PRIMARY CRITERION WITH THE SECONDARY ONES

§39.83(b) refused design (A) outright: *"paying 130 core-h to get an unresolvable answer is worse
than waiting."* **That is right for the SECONDARY criteria and WRONG for the PRIMARY one, and I did
not separate them.**
```
SECONDARY (|ΔE| ≤ 1e-7 Ha, |Δν| ≤ 0.1 cm⁻¹): these ARE unresolvable under (A). Its two arms
  re-optimise independently, and the optimiser's own spread (5.6 meV; 1.42× in cost; ~0.1 Å on H)
  swamps the effect being bounded. Unchanged, and this half of my objection stands.
PRIMARY (n_imag identical): **RESOLVABLE UNDER (A).** n_imag is an INTEGER COUNT, not a difference
  of two nearly-equal reals, and the lowest real mode is 77.02 cm⁻¹ — nowhere near the zero
  crossing where a small geometry difference could flip a sign. Two independently tight-converged
  geometries cannot move a 77 cm⁻¹ mode through zero.
⟹ AND (A) RETIRES A GENUINE UNKNOWN I NAMED MYSELF: §39.80 established we have NO evidence about
  EpsInf = 1.0 AT ALL — not that it converges, not that it is numerically well-behaved, nothing.
  (A) answers that, and it is the arm that has never once executed.
```
🔒 **RULING ON THE LEAD'S ROUND A / ROUND B SPLIT — ACCEPTED, WITH THE SCOPE PRE-REGISTERED NOW:**
```
ROUND A (design A, today) MAY CONCLUDE:  (i) whether EpsInf = 1.0 runs at all;
                                         (ii) whether n_imag == 0 SURVIVES at the interval's
                                              lower end ⟹ whether the C-8 certificate is
                                              robust to EpsInf across the full admissible range.
ROUND A MAY NOT CONCLUDE:  🔴 "EpsInf is irrelevant", "the values agree", "invariant", or any
                           statement about MAGNITUDE. Its ΔE and Δν are NOT MEASUREMENTS — they
                           are bounded below by the optimiser's spread and must be reported as
                           "not resolved at this design's floor (≈ 5 meV)", never as a number that
                           happens to be small.
🔴 ROUND A DOES NOT REPLACE ROUND B. If Round A returns n_imag == 0 at both ends, that is a
   STRUCTURAL PASS on the certificate and a still-open question on the mechanism ("read and
   unused" vs "read and weakly used"), and the mechanism is what licenses extending the verdict
   to P5/P1b at all (§39.82(b)). Round B remains required. If anyone proposes cancelling Round B
   because Round A "looked fine", that is the exact misreading this pre-registration exists to
   prevent, and the answer is no.
🟢 IF Round A DISAGREES (n_imag differs), we learn the biggest possible thing immediately and
   Round B's design changes from a null-confirmation to an effect measurement.
```
⚠ **I was wrong to state the refusal without that split, and it is worth being explicit about why I
got it wrong**: I had been reasoning about the ERROR FLOOR, which governs the secondary criteria,
and let it govern my verdict on the whole design. A floor argument is only decisive for quantities
measured as DIFFERENCES OF NEARLY-EQUAL REALS. It says nothing about an integer that is not close to
its own decision boundary.

⚠ **AND "Stationary point found" DOES NOT CONTRADICT THIS** — C-8.2 is explicit that a geometry-only
convergence criterion does not certify anything. This row's `freq` died at the EpsInf sentinel, so
**its `n_imag` is unknown**, and a symmetric planar stationary point is precisely where an imaginary
symmetry-breaking mode would live.

### (c) 🟢 THE CORRECTED CONTROL — and the reason it is BETTER than the one offered, not merely safer

Build the control from the ENDPOINT deck with exactly one thing changed, rather than from a P5 deck
with four things changed:
```
CONTROL:  freq-only, both EpsInf arms, on the ENDPOINT'S OWN CERTIFIED GEOMETRY
          (same `endpoint_tight.chk` as the main bracket, via %oldchk per arm),
          endpoint route KEPT VERBATIM — nosymm, Int(Grid=UltraFine) — with ONLY the basis
          swapped to level2 / NBasis 321.
⟹ species, geometry, geometry PROVENANCE, symmetry handling and integration grid are all IDENTICAL
  to the main bracket. The single varying quantity is the basis set, which is the confound
  §39.86(c) identified. Nothing else moves.
```
🔒 **THE INSIGHT THAT MAKES THIS LEGITIMATE, and it generalises**: for the `EpsInf` question the
reference geometry **need not be a stationary point at the level being used.** The test is *"does
the Hessian change when EpsInf changes, at a FIXED geometry"* — and a fixed non-stationary geometry
answers it just as well as a fixed stationary one. The level3 geometry is not a level2 minimum, and
that does not matter.
```
⚠ WHAT DOES CHANGE: at a non-stationary geometry `n_imag` certifies NOTHING about the species — but
  `n_imag` COMPARED BETWEEN THE TWO ARMS remains valid, because both arms sit on the identical
  geometry. So the criteria carry over unchanged (§39.85(c)): n_imag identical between arms,
  |ΔE| ≤ 1e-7 Hartree, |Δν| ≤ 0.1 cm⁻¹ over ALL modes, max-deviation reported.
🟢 AND IT REMOVES OPTIMISER NOISE ENTIRELY — no re-optimisation at level2 is performed, so this
  control has the same 1e-9 floor as the main bracket rather than the ~5 meV floor of any design
  that re-optimises. The offered row would have carried optimiser noise AND a basin change.
```
**Run it up front, in the same round** (engineer9's suggestion, accepted for their reason): the
scarce resource is calendar, not core-h, and the conditional version pays a full round-trip exactly
in the branch where the result is most interesting. engineer9 prices it; NBasis 321 vs the
spot-check's 299 puts it in the same class.

### (d) 🟢 AN UPGRADE TO THE P5 RECOVERY'S VALUE THAT COSTS NOTHING

```
