of them may be symmetry-trapped planar stationary points — the P5 decks cannot break a symmetric
seed, and at least one demonstrably did not.
⟹ 🟢 **THE FREQUENCY RECOVERY IS THE ONLY INSTRUMENT THAT CAN DETECT THIS**, because the diagnostic
  IS `n_imag`, and it is already being computed for cost reasons. The recovery was justified as a
  cost measurement; it is simultaneously a C-9 audit of every P5 geometry, at zero marginal cost.
🔴 AND THE CONVERSE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS TODAY: **P5's converged geometries MUST NOT be
  reused as chemical structures by anything downstream until that audit exists.** §39.82(b)'s
  readout gate already blocks P5's chemical READOUTS; this extends it to the GEOMETRIES themselves,
  which the gate as written did not cover. A geometry is a chemical claim.
⚠ SEPARATELY, for whoever fixes the decks: adding `nosymm` (and `Int(Grid=UltraFine)`, for
  low-frequency modes) to P5 is a DECK CHANGE THAT INVALIDATES THE EXISTING GEOMETRIES for

## 39.90 🟢 THE USER'S DIAGNOSIS IS RIGHT AND THE LOG PROVES IT HARDER THAN EXPECTED — `Generic` supplies A ROW OF ZEROS, not just a missing EpsInf. But the remedy should be NARROWER than the one proposed, and the reason is counterintuitive (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> The user proposes `scrf=(pcm,solvent=acetone,read)` with `eps=18.5` overriding acetone's own
> permittivity, so that G16 has a real built-in `EpsInf` to fall back on. Three questions routed:
> does it work, is acetone defensible, is it clean. **Answers: yes / yes-but-unnecessary / no —
> and the investigation their question forced produced the most reassuring result of the day.**

### (a) 🟢 THE MECHANISM IS DOCUMENTED, AND OUR OWN LOG CONFIRMS THE DIAGNOSIS

Gaussian's SCRF documentation: *"Unspecified parameters default to the values for the solvent
specified with the Solvent option (or to water if this option is omitted)."*
⚠ A secondary source states the opposite — that unspecified parameters default to **water** — so
documentation alone does not settle it. **Our own log does, and it settles more than was asked:**
```
endpoint_tight.log (the CONVERGED 18.5 arm), PCM block, verbatim:
  Solvent              : Generic,
                         Eps                           =  18.500000
                         Eps(infinity)                 =  18.500000
                         RSolv                         =   0.000000 Ang.
                         Molar volume                  =   0.000000 cm**3/mol
                         Thermal expansion coefficient =   0.000000 K**-1
                         Numeral density               =   0.000000 Ang**-3
                         Hydrogen bond acidity         =   0.000000
                         Hydrogen bond basicity        =   0.000000
```
🔒 **`Generic` DOES NOT FALL BACK TO WATER. IT IS A ROW OF ZEROS.** The user's causal claim is
correct and now has direct evidence: `EpsInf = 0` was never a special sentinel — **it is one member
of a whole row of zeros, and it crashed only because the Hessian path is the one code path that
consumes its member of that row.** Every other zero is consumed by nothing, silently.

### (b) 🟢🟢 THE REASSURING PART — I CHECKED WHETHER THOSE OTHER ZEROS ARE USED, AND THEY ARE NOT

This is the question the user's suggestion exposed and nobody had asked: **a crash is the LUCKY
case. `RSolv = 0` and `Numeral density = 0` do not crash — they would corrupt silently.**
```
cavity actually used   "Scaled VdW (van der Waals Surface) (Alpha=1.100)", GePol, UFF radii
                       ⟹ a scaled-VdW surface does NOT consume RSolv (that is a solvent-excluded /
                         solvent-accessible surface parameter). RSolv = 0 is INERT here.
non-electrostatic terms  grep -ci "cavitation" = 0. No G(cav)/G(disp)/G(rep) anywhere.
                       (the only "dispersion" in the log is R6Disp — Grimme-D2, the wB97XD
                        SOLUTE functional's own term, intramolecular, nothing to do with PCM)
                       ⟹ molar volume, numeral density, thermal expansion, HB acidity/basicity are
                         consumed by NOTHING in this setup. All INERT.
```
🟢 **⟹ NO B0 ENERGY COMPUTED UNDER `solvent=generic` HAS BEEN SILENTLY CORRUPTED BY THE ZEROS.**
That is stated as a measurement on the log, not as reassurance. It is the single most useful thing
the user's question produced, and it was invisible until someone asked why `Generic` was special.

### (c) 🔴 THEREFORE THE REMEDY SHOULD BE NARROWER THAN PROPOSED — and the argument closes both ways

```
🔒 THE DILEMMA, AND EITHER HORN FAVOURS BEING EXPLICIT:
   IF the other solvent parameters do NOT enter the calculation (shown in (b): they do not),
      then naming acetone buys NOTHING EXCEPT AN IMPLICIT EpsInf — i.e. it converts an auditable
      number into a hidden consequence of a solvent name.
   IF they DID enter, then naming acetone would have SILENTLY CHANGED THE SOLVENT MODEL — importing
      acetone's RSolv, density and Abraham descriptors into a calculation whose parameters are
      currently known, zero, and provably unused.
   ⟹ Moving from "known zeros, verified inert" to "acetone's values, used or not, unexamined" is a
     change in the direction of LESS control, not more.
```
**RECOMMENDED, and it is the same one-line change the user asked for, just a different line:**
```
KEEP  scrf=(pcm,solvent=generic,read)
READ  eps=18.5
      EpsInf=1.93          ← §39.84's sourced value, [CATALOG-GRADE PROVENANCE]
```
Certainty: **this is already proven to work** — the converged arm ran exactly this deck shape with
`EpsInf=18.5`. Nothing needs testing to adopt it. The acetone route would need a test to adopt.
⚠ **AND ACETONE IS A DEFENSIBLE CHOICE IF WE EVER GO THAT WAY** — dipolar aprotic, carbonyl-bearing,
ε ≈ 20.7 against our 18.5. Its inherited `EpsInf` would be n² ≈ 1.85 (n_D ≈ 1.359), which is ~4%
BELOW §39.84's sourced 1.93 ± 0.02 and outside that range, though far inside the bracket [1.0, 18.5].
So the objection to acetone is **not that its number is bad — it is that the number would be
unstated.** Overriding `eps` while inheriting the rest also creates a formally inconsistent solvent
("acetone with the wrong permittivity"), which is harmless *precisely because* (b) shows the rest is
inert — the same fact that makes naming it pointless.

### (d) 🔒 WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT RESOLVE — the framing must not collapse two questions into one

```
🟢 RESOLVED (and already was): THE CRASH. Supplying EpsInf explicitly fixes it, proven by a
   converged run. The user's route would also fix it. Neither is "cheaper" than the other — both
   are one line.
🔴 NOT RESOLVED BY EITHER: WHETHER THE VALUE MATTERS. That is the bracket's question, and no deck
   change answers it. **If anything the acetone route makes the bracket MORE necessary**, because
   it introduces a value nobody chose deliberately and nobody would later be able to defend.
   ⟹ The bracket is NOT superseded. At 7.3–8.6 core-h it is the cheapest item on the board, and
     if it returns invariant, every choice discussed here — 1.93, acetone's 1.85, even 18.5 —
     becomes retrospectively irrelevant, which is the outcome that would let us stop spending
     attention on this permanently.
```
🟢 **A FREE EMPIRICAL TEST, since G16 answers this itself in one line**: any deck using a named
solvent prints `NEqPCM: ... Eps= …, EpsInf= …` and the `Solvent :` parameter block. **Run the
existing H2 smoke molecule with `scrf=(pcm,solvent=acetone,read)`, `eps=18.5`, and `freq`, and read
those two lines.** Seconds of compute, and it converts the documentation conflict in (a) into a
measurement. **Worth doing regardless of which remedy is adopted** — it is the only way to know what
`Generic` versus a named solvent actually supplies on THIS G16 build, and the whole EpsInf episode
began with a deck verifier that checked `eps` and never checked what else the block contained.

### (b) 🔒 THE PROVISIONAL CERTIFICATE — the wording is fine; THE SHAPE IS THE HAZARD

coder12 asks whether `certificate_status: "provisional_bracket_arm (EpsInf=18.5; stands only if the
§39.73 bracket returns invariant, otherwise redo at the physical value 1.93)"` is strong enough, or
should be `UNCERTIFIED` per §39.82's default.

🔴 NEITHER — the question is aimed at the string, and the string is not the risk.
   "UNCERTIFIED" is TOO STRONG and destroys information: this IS a real C-8 computation —
   converged, real Hessian, n_imag == 0, clean <S²>. What is provisional is the VALUE it was
   computed at, not the quality of the computation.
🔴 THE ACTUAL HAZARD: a provisional certificate is TRUTHY. Any downstream `if cert: use it` treats
   it as a pass, and no wording inside the string prevents that. **That is §39.80(g) again — a
   marker whose truthiness outruns its meaning** (a `done` marker over a segfault), one document
   over.

   A consumer that does not know about provisionality must FAIL CLOSED — i.e. find no certificate —
   rather than find one and read its adjective.
```
And make the clearing condition structured rather than prose, because §39.88(c) created **two**
clearing levels and a single sentence cannot express them:
```
eps_inf                 18.5
eps_inf_provenance      "bracket arm, interval UPPER bound — NOT the physical value.
                         Physical base is 1.93 [CATALOG-GRADE PROVENANCE, §39.84]."
clears_structural       "Round A: n_imag == 0 at EpsInf = 1.0 AND the §39.70 covalent-graph check

clears_mechanism        "Round B (design C): invariant ⟹ licenses extending the EpsInf verdict to

usable_for              ["cost"]
not_usable_for          ["any chemical claim, until clears_structural is satisfied"]
```
⚠ **The two levels are not interchangeable and the difference is the whole point**: a structural
pass says THIS certificate survives the interval; only the mechanism pass licenses extending the
verdict to anything else. Anyone who reads a structural pass as permission to unstamp P5's readouts
has made exactly the §39.88(c) misreading the pre-registration exists to block.

- §39.92(d) verify a QUALIFICATION against the artefact, not only a disqualification.

- The readout gate (§39.82(b)) on P5/P1b CHEMICAL deliverables — now gated on the production
  solvent rather than on a bracket verdict.
🔒 These were discovered during the EpsInf investigation but none of them is ABOUT EpsInf. A
  cancelled experiment must not take its by-products with it.
```

## 39.94 🔒 AN H2 NULL IS SUFFICIENT FOR THE QUESTION IT CAN ANSWER AND NOT FOR THE ONE ENGINEER9 ASKED — and the certificate does not transfer for a reason that has NOTHING to do with EpsInf (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> engineer9 (§R39.55) asks whether an H2 `freq` comparison — (a) `generic` + `EpsInf=18.5` versus
> (b) `acetone` — can settle whether this project's only C-8 certificate transfers to the new
> production solvent, for ~0.1 core-h instead of ~66. They correctly flag that the answer is mine
> and invoke my own §39.85(e) structural-null argument. **The argument does not extend, and I have
> to split their question into three before it can be answered honestly.**
> ⚠ **NONE OF WHAT FOLLOWS REOPENS THE CANCELLED EpsInf QUESTION.** The conclusion is reached
> without it, which is the point.

### (a) 🔴 WHY H2 IS THE WRONG MOLECULE FOR THE CLAIM THEY WANT — my own selection rule says so

```
§39.82(c) SELECTION RULE: detection power scales with reaction-field coupling — net charge first,
then diffuse/polarisable density, then soft low-frequency modes. **"A NEUTRAL RIGID MOLECULE IS THE
WEAKEST POSSIBLE PROBE."**
H2 is a neutral, nonpolar, closed-shell DIATOMIC with ONE mode and a negligible reaction field.
It is not merely a weak probe — it is the minimum-coupling molecule available.
⟹ A NULL ON H2 IS CONSISTENT WITH BOTH "the value is never read" AND "the value is read, but the
  solute barely polarises the continuum so the effect is below the printed digits." Those are the
  two hypotheses the test exists to separate, and H2 cannot separate them.
🔴 §39.85(e) said: a structural null is refuted by ONE counterexample, so choose the probe most
  likely to BE that counterexample. **H2 is the least likely molecule on the board to be it.**
  Invoking that argument for H2 inverts it.
```

### (b) 🟢 BUT THE SMOKE DECK ANSWERS A DIFFERENT AND MORE IMPORTANT QUESTION, AND FOR THAT H2 IS FULLY ADEQUATE

The decisive readout of that job is **not the frequencies at all**:
```
DOES THE SWITCH ACTIVATE A CODE PATH OR CHANGE THE CAVITY MODEL?
   read from the acetone log:  the `Solvent :` parameter block (what acetone populates)
                               `Atomic radii :`   and  `Cavity type :`   lines
                               grep -ci cavitation ; presence of G(cav)/G(disp)/G(rep)
                               the `NEqPCM:` line (what EpsInf is actually used)
🔒 THESE ARE MOLECULE-INDEPENDENT FACTS. A term is either computed or it is not, and G16 PRINTS the
   terms it computes. H2 is a perfectly good witness for "which code paths ran" — that claim does
   not scale with reaction-field coupling, because it is not about magnitude at all.
🟢 engineer9's own pre-registration is exactly right and I adopt it as the criterion: if
   `Atomic radii` or `Cavity type` differ between the two decks, the cavity changed and every cost
   anchor needs re-measuring. If they match and no new terms appear, the switch is inert on the
   code-path question — permanently, for all molecules.
```
**⟹ RUN IT. ~0.2 core-h, both decks, one job. It is the highest information-per-core-h item on the
board and it is the first `freq`-containing route smoke this package has ever had (§39.73(b)).**

### (c) 🔒 AND THE CERTIFICATE QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED — WITHOUT EpsInf, WHICH IS WHY THE CANCELLATION DOES NOT REOPEN

engineer9 framed it as a dichotomy: *EpsInf unused ⟹ the certificate transfers; used ⟹ re-certify.*
**The dichotomy is incomplete, and its missing branch decides the case:**
```
🔴 GOING FROM `generic` TO `acetone` DOES NOT ONLY CHANGE EpsInf. It replaces an ALL-ZERO parameter
   row with acetone's populated one — RSolv, molar volume, numeral density, thermal expansion,
   hydrogen-bond acidity and basicity, ALL of them, at once.
   §39.90(b) showed those are inert — but MEASURED ON THE ZEROS, under `generic`. engineer9 is
   right that inertness does not transfer BY ARGUMENT to a populated row.
⟹ EVEN A DEFINITIVE "EpsInf IS NEVER READ" WOULD NOT ESTABLISH TRANSFER, because EpsInf is not the
  only thing that changed.
🔒 THE CERTIFICATE DOES NOT TRANSFER, AND THE REASON IS ORDINARY HYGIENE RATHER THAN ANY OPEN
   PHYSICS: **a certificate is a certificate OF A MODEL. The production model changed. A C-8
   certificate computed under a solvent model we have abandoned is not a certificate of what we
   now compute** — that is true for any solvent change, in any project, independent of EpsInf.
⟹ RE-CERTIFY THE ENDPOINT UNDER ACETONE. ~66 core-h, one arm, engineer9's measured endpoint cost.
  It is the C-8 gate input for everything downstream, so schedule it EARLY. This is not the
  cancelled experiment in disguise and it does not measure EpsInf sensitivity — it produces one
  certificate under the settings production actually uses.
⚠ IF (b) RETURNS FULLY INERT the re-certification is *likely* to reproduce the existing numbers.
  That is a prediction, not a substitute: predicting a certificate is not holding one.
```

### (d) The three questions, separated once so they stop being conflated

```
Q1 does the switch activate code paths / change the cavity?   H2 smoke ANSWERS IT.        ~0.2 core-h
Q2 does EpsInf's VALUE move a Hessian on a coupled solute?    CANCELLED by user ruling.   not asked
Q3 does the existing C-8 certificate transfer?                NO — by (c), model changed. ~66 core-h
🔒 Q3 was never downstream of Q2. Treating it as though it were is what made a 0.1 core-h test look
   like it could replace a 66 core-h certificate.
```

## 39.95 🟢 A FREQUENCY-ONLY RE-CERTIFICATION **DOES** SATISFY C-8 — because the freq job PRINTS ITS OWN FORCES, so it verifies stationarity on the new surface rather than assuming it. The job decides its own branch (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> engineer9 (§R39.56) shows the acetone re-certification is a 4–5 vs 42–66 core-h branch and asks
> me to rule whether the cheap side satisfies C-8. **It does — conditionally, self-verifyingly, and
> the condition is free.** And the branch does not need the smoke to decide it.

### (a) What C-8 actually requires, and what a freq-only job can and cannot show

```
A MINIMUM ON A SURFACE REQUIRES TWO THINGS:
   (i)  the gradient vanishes there        ← what an OPTIMISATION establishes
   (ii) every Hessian eigenvalue is positive (n_imag == 0)   ← what a FREQ establishes
C-8.2's own wording — "a geometry-only convergence criterion does NOT satisfy C-8" — is the
complaint that (i) alone was being accepted. **The mirror complaint is equally true and nobody has
stated it: (ii) ALONE DOES NOT SATISFY C-8 EITHER.** A geometry that is not stationary on the
surface in use can carry n_imag == 0 and be certifying nothing.
🔴 A freq-only run on a geometry converged under `generic`, executed under `acetone`, supplies (ii)
   on the new surface and inherits (i) FROM A DIFFERENT SURFACE. That inheritance is the whole
   question, and it is exactly the assumption that must not be made by argument.
```

### (b) 🟢 THE RESOLUTION — the job already contains the missing half, printed

```
🔒 A GAUSSIAN `freq` JOB PRINTS `Forces (Hartrees/Bohr)`. So condition (i) is MEASURED in the same
   output that supplies condition (ii), at zero extra cost. Same move as design (C)'s forces check,
   surviving the cancellation because it was never about EpsInf.
RULING — a freq-only re-certification satisfies C-8 iff ALL THREE hold, read from the ONE job:
   1. n_imag == 0
   2. max force  ≤ the convergence threshold of the optimisation level being claimed
   3. RMS force  ≤ the same
   ⟹ then the stored geometry IS a converged minimum on the production surface, certified by the
     two conditions C-8 requires, both measured on that surface, neither inherited.
   Fail 2 or 3 ⟹ the surface moved enough to matter; the certificate is NOT granted and the full
     rough+tight re-run is required (~42–66 core-h).
⚠ THE THRESHOLDS MUST BE READ FROM G16's OWN CONVERGENCE TABLE IN THE ORIGINAL OPTIMISATION LOG,
  not quoted from memory or from a manual — the stored logs contain the table, and the threshold
  must be the one the optimiser actually applied. And it must MATCH THE CLAIM: the endpoint was
  `opt=(tight)`, so tight thresholds; **P5's rows were plain `opt`, so DEFAULT thresholds — applying
  tight criteria to a default-converged geometry would fail every row for a reason that is not
  about acetone at all.**
```
🔒 **⟹ THE BRANCH IS SELF-DECIDING AND DOES NOT WAIT ON THE SMOKE.** Run the freq-only
re-certification (~4–5 core-h); its own forces say which branch we were in. This is better than
deciding from the smoke's PCM-block diff, because **the PCM block is a PROXY** — it could match
while numerics still shift the geometry, or differ in a way that never moves it. **Measure the
thing you care about (is this geometry stationary on the surface we now use), not the thing that
correlates with it.** The smoke remains worth running for the code-path and cost-anchor questions,
which the forces cannot answer.

### (c) 🟢 AND THE SAME PRINTED FORCES RESCUE THE C-9 AUDIT — per row, not globally

engineer9 is right that if the surface moved, off-stationary geometries produce imaginary modes for
the wrong reason and `n_imag` cannot separate the causes. **But that is not an all-or-nothing fate
for the audit:**
```
FOR EACH of the 17 P5 rows, read that row's OWN printed forces in its OWN recovery job:
   forces within the DEFAULT opt thresholds ⟹ the geometry is stationary on the acetone surface
       ⟹ an imaginary mode means genuine symmetry trapping. AUDIT VALID FOR THIS ROW.
   forces outside ⟹ AUDIT INDETERMINATE FOR THIS ROW (recorded as such, never as a pass and never
       as a failure). The COST measurement for that row is unaffected — a Hessian at a fixed
       geometry is exactly what a cost measurement needs, stationary or not.
🔒 ⟹ the C-9 audit survives PER ROW, conditioned on that row's own measurement, at zero marginal
   cost. Not "survives either way" and not "dies if the surface moved" — a per-row validity flag,
   which is the honest shape and the only one that lets a mixed outcome be reported.
```
🟢 engineer9's scoping correction accepted and it matters for how the switch is judged: only
`endpoint_prep_reactant` is re-certification caused BY the switch. `endpoint_prep_product` and
`endpoint_prep_rc_reactant` were never certified under any solvent — that is pre-existing work and
must not be charged to the acetone decision.

### (d) On pre-registered predictions with named falsifiers

engineer9 flags that their own §R39.55 prediction (cavity from UFF radii ⟹ cost is
solvent-label-independent) is reasoning from a log rather than a measurement of the acetone path,
and has written it as a prediction with a falsifier (`Atomic radii` or `Cavity type` differing)
rather than as a conclusion.
```
🔒 That is the correct handling, and it is worth stating as a standing rule because this project
   has repeatedly been bitten by its absence: A MECHANISM THAT EXPLAINS A MEASUREMENT IS A
   HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE NEXT MEASUREMENT, NOT A RESULT ABOUT IT. §39.73(b) (a mechanism that
   explained the endpoint crash and was wrong about its scope) and §39.86(d) (an anchor that
   explained the endpoint cost and was wrong about its variable) are the same failure twice.
   The fix both times was a named falsifier attached BEFORE the next measurement.
```

## 39.96 🟢 A WARM-STARTED TIGHT OPTIMISATION IS A COMPLETE C-8 CERTIFICATE — and the COLD start is the option with a documented failure mode, not the safe one (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> engineer9 (§R39.57) withdraws the freq-only re-certification and proposes instead a full
> `opt=(tight,calcfc) freq` **on the acetone surface, warm-started from the certified geometry via
> `geom=check`** — ~8 core-h base against ~42–66 cold. They ask whether that is a complete C-8
> certificate, and offer to withdraw it too if a certificate must re-derive the PATH.

### (a) 🟢 RULING: YES, AND THE PATH QUESTION HAS A SHORT ANSWER

```
C-8 IS A PROPERTY OF THE ENDPOINT, NOT OF THE TRAJECTORY THAT REACHED IT.
   gradient converged by the optimiser's own criteria ON THE ACETONE SURFACE   ✅ warm start does this
   n_imag == 0 from a real Hessian ON THE ACETONE SURFACE                      ✅ warm start does this
   deck_verification naming the production solvent                             ✅
⟹ THE STARTING GEOMETRY IS AN INPUT GUESS, AND A GUESS IS NOT PART OF WHAT A CERTIFICATE
  CERTIFIES. The original certification began from a packaged idealised guess and nobody claims
  that guess was certified.
🔒 AND A CERTIFICATE THAT REQUIRED ITS PATH TO BE RE-DERIVED WOULD BE UNCHECKABLE — no two
   optimiser runs take the same path on this machine, which is MEASURED, not asserted: the same
   molecule at the same level cost 40.57 vs 57.99 core-h across two builds (1.43×), with exit
   geometries differing ~0.1 Å on hydrogen. A criterion no two valid runs could both satisfy is
   not a criterion.
```
This is exactly the distinction that killed the freq-only version and spares this one: **freq-only
never re-derived the geometry on the production surface at all; the warm start re-derives it and
merely starts nearby.**

### (b) 🔴 THE STRONGER POINT — COLD START IS NOT THE CONSERVATIVE CHOICE HERE

```
§39.89, TODAY: P5's `li_ec_radical_s0_L2` was COLD-STARTED from a packaged idealised seed —
planar heavy atoms, Li collinear above the carbonyl O — and converged to exactly that symmetry:
Li–O=C 180.00°, heavy atoms coplanar to 0.0000 Å, sitting on its own pre-registered falsifier.
🔒 ⟹ A COLD START FROM A PACKAGED GUESS IS THE DOCUMENTED FAILURE MODE (C-9 / ADR-066), demonstrated
   in this project TODAY, on THIS SPECIES at a different level. Re-certifying the endpoint by
   cold start would re-expose it to that hazard for no benefit.
🟢 THE WARM START PRESERVES BASIN IDENTITY, WHICH IS THE PROPERTY THE DOWNSTREAM CHAIN ACTUALLY
   NEEDS: U56-2 consumes this certificate as the REACTANT endpoint of a specific reaction. We need
   the same chemical species on the new surface — not an independent search that might return a
   different minimum and silently change what the reaction is.
⟹ THE WARM START IS THE SCIENTIFICALLY PREFERRED ROUTE. Its being 5–8× cheaper is a coincidence,
  and it should be chosen on the basin argument even if it were the more expensive one.
```

### (c) 🔒 TWO CONDITIONS, BOTH FREE, BOTH RECORDED ON PASS AS WELL AS FAIL

```
1. BASIN CHECK. Run the §39.70 covalent-graph comparison between the new converged geometry and
   the stored one. Identical graph ⟹ same species, certificate granted. DIFFERENT ⟹ the acetone
   surface moved the structure to another species, the certificate is REFUSED, and that fact is
   itself a major finding about the switch — it must be surfaced, not retried.
   🟢 Recorded when it PASSES too (engineer9's rule): a control leaving no trace on success is one
      nobody can later confirm was run.
2. CONVERGENCE BY THE OPTIMISER'S OWN CRITERIA on the acetone surface, read from G16's own
   convergence table in the new log.
   ⚠ **CONVERGING IN ONE STEP IS A VALID OUTCOME, NOT A DEFECT.** If the optimiser reports
     convergence immediately, that means the stored geometry WAS already stationary on the acetone
     surface — which is precisely the freq-only claim, now MEASURED BY THE OPTIMISER instead of
     assumed. The difference between the rejected design and this one was never the number of
     steps taken; it was whether anything checked.
```
🟢 And the smoke (§39.94(b)) now only chooses which PRICE is paid (~8 warm vs ~42–66 cold), not
whether the certificate is valid. **The warm start is self-verifying**: if the surface moved
materially, the optimiser takes more steps and costs more, or the basin check fails and says so.
⚠ Unchanged and worth repeating because it is the whole reason this item exists: **predicting a
certificate is not holding one.** A fully inert smoke does not substitute for the re-certification.

### (d) On engineer9 withdrawing the H2 argument

They note the inversion was theirs — invoking §39.85(e)'s "choose the probe most likely to BE the
counterexample" to justify the minimum-coupling molecule on the board.
```
🔒 WORTH KEEPING AS A PATTERN RATHER THAN AN INCIDENT: A RULE CITED BY NAME IS NOT A RULE APPLIED.
   §39.85(e) was quoted accurately and used to license its own opposite, because the quoted phrase
   ("one probe is enough") is the CONCLUSION of the rule, while the part that does the work is the
   SELECTION CRITERION that decides WHICH probe. A rule compressed to its conclusion inverts easily.
   ⟹ when citing a prior ruling to license a choice, cite the criterion, not the verdict.
```

## 39.97 🔴 MY C-8 FORCE CRITERION COMPARED TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES — engineer9 caught it in the log before it cost anything. Corrected to a like-for-like gradient comparison, and the warm start is KEPT as the escalation rung rather than withdrawn (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> §39.95(b) ruled that a freq-only re-certification satisfies C-8 if `n_imag == 0` and the job's
> printed forces meet "the convergence threshold of the optimisation level being claimed".
> engineer9 (§R39.58) checked that against the real log. **The mechanism was right and the
> criterion was wrong, in the expensive direction.**

### (a) 🔴 THE DEFECT — G16 prints forces in two places and they are not the same quantity

```
endpoint_tight.log, freq step (after Link1 step 2):
  :4258  Cartesian Forces:  Max  0.000032681   RMS  0.000016752      ← raw gradient
  convergence table:        Max  0.000000  Threshold 0.000015  YES   ← optimiser's INTERNAL /
                            RMS  0.000000  Threshold 0.000010  YES     redundant coordinates,
                                                                       translations + rotations
                                                                       + redundancies projected out
🔴 MY RULE READ THE FIRST AGAINST THE SECOND'S THRESHOLD: 3.27e-5 vs 1.5e-5 ⟹ REFUSE — on the very
   geometry G16 itself certified as tight-converged, by 2.2× on max and 1.7× on RMS.
   ⟹ EVERY warm re-certification false-refused into the ~42–66 core-h cold path. ~58 core-h per
     certificate, **and the refusal would have been read as a real finding about acetone.**
```
⚠ **Why the two differ, and it matters for reading a FAILURE later**: the Cartesian residual
contains components the optimiser projects out — translations, rotations, and redundant
combinations. Under PCM a discretised cavity does not preserve exact rotational invariance, so part
of that 3.27e-5 is **cavity-tessellation noise, not chemistry.** That is precisely why a
like-for-like comparison is required, and it also means a FAILED comparison says *"something about
the solvent model changed at this geometry"* — which may be the cavity rather than the surface.

### (b) 🟢 THE CORRECTED CRITERION — same quantity, same geometry, measured floor

engineer9's replacement, adopted:
```
🔒 The re-certification freq job's `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS` must reproduce the ORIGINAL
   optimisation's FINAL `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS` — never a convergence-table threshold.
   measured floor, from data already on disk:
     final opt cycle (:2688)   Max 0.000032685  RMS 0.000016753
     freq step      (:4258)    Max 0.000032681  RMS 0.000016752
     agreement 4e-9 absolute / 1.2e-4 relative  ⟹ CALIBRATED, not asserted
```
🟢 **And their inference is valid — I am ruling it sufficient, with its premise stated rather than
left implicit**: the convergence VERDICT is a deterministic function of the gradient, so if
∇E(acetone) = ∇E(generic) at that geometry, the point satisfies on acetone exactly the criterion it
was certified against on generic. With `n_imag == 0` measured on acetone, both C-8 conditions hold
on the production surface — **one measured directly, the other by demonstrated gradient invariance
rather than by assumption.** That is the inheritance §39.95(a) demanded be measured, now measured.
```
⚠ PREMISE MADE EXPLICIT, so nobody later demands more than the point can give: this covers the
  FORCE criteria only. The DISPLACEMENT criteria in G16's table are properties of the optimiser's
  LAST STEP, not of the point — a freq-only job takes no step, so they are not merely unavailable,
  they are IRRELEVANT to stationarity. A certificate must not be blocked for lacking them.
```

### (c) 🔴 BUT THE WARM START IS **NOT** WITHDRAWN — it is the escalation rung, and removing it leaves a cliff

engineer9 withdraws §R39.57's warm start as "unnecessary". **Half accepted**: it is unnecessary as
the DEFAULT. It is necessary as the FALLBACK, because their withdrawal leaves ~4–5 core-h jumping
straight to ~42–66 with nothing in between.
```
🔒 THREE RUNGS, STOP AT THE FIRST THAT HOLDS:
 1. freq-only, self-verifying                    ~4–5 core-h
    forces reproduce the original to the measured floor ⟹ CERTIFICATE GRANTED.
 2. forces do NOT reproduce ⟹ do NOT refuse and do NOT jump to cold.
    ⟹ WARM-STARTED opt=(tight,calcfc) freq (§39.96)          ~8 core-h
    The gradient field moved at that geometry; a warm start RE-DERIVES the minimum on the acetone
    surface and settles whether the move mattered. It is the correct instrument precisely when
    rung 1 is inconclusive — and §39.96's basin check comes with it.
 3. basin check FAILS at rung 2 (covalent graph changed) ⟹ the acetone surface has moved the
    structure to another species. Certificate REFUSED, surfaced as a finding, cold path considered
    only after someone has looked at what changed.                      ~42–66 core-h
⚠ I DO NOT SET A NUMERIC BAND for "reproduce". The measured floor is 4e-9; anything at that scale
  is agreement. I refuse to invent a middle threshold — that is exactly the invented-number failure
  of §39.86(a), and rung 2 exists so that the ambiguous case is RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT rather than
  adjudicated by a constant I made up.
```

### (d) 🟢 THE P5 THRESHOLD HAZARD IS REMOVED BY THE SAME FIX, AND THE NUMBERS CONFIRM IT WAS REAL

```
endpoint, opt=(tight)      Max Force threshold 0.000015
P5 rows, plain opt         Max Force threshold 0.000450        30× looser
P5 ec_radical_anion_s0 converged:  Max Force 0.000195 — PASSES default, FAILS tight by 13×
⟹ my §39.95 warning was right that a mismatched threshold would fail every P5 row — and the
  CORRECTED criterion removes the hazard at its root: a per-row same-quantity comparison never
  touches a threshold, so it cannot mismatch one. The per-row C-9 validity flag stands unchanged,
  at one grep per row.
```

### (e) The rule this instance belongs to, pointed at me this time

```
§39.95(d): "a mechanism that explains a measurement is a hypothesis about the NEXT measurement."
My forces-are-printed mechanism was correct. The CRITERION I built on it named a quantity I had
never opened a log to identify — and the two quantities differ by 2.2× at the same geometry.
🔒 ⟹ THE GENERALISATION: A MECHANISM BEING TRUE DOES NOT MAKE A CRITERION BUILT ON IT WELL-FORMED.
   The mechanism licenses that the data EXISTS; only reading the file identifies WHICH datum it is.
   It cost one grep to settle and would have cost ~58 core-h per certificate to discover.
```

generally**: neutral EC and methoxy radical differ by 0.006 eV between seeds — the trap does not
bite where the symmetric structure is genuinely (near-)correct. A test that convicted everything
would be worthless; this one convicts two rows and clears two.
⚠ **THIS IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND §39.72's SEED SPREAD.** proposer7 measured that within-species seed
spread exceeded every ratio we planned around and could not say why. For at least these two rows the
why is now named: **seed 0 is symmetry-trapped and seed 1 is not.** That is not variance — it is one
seed being wrong.

### (c) 🔴 WHAT THIS COSTS US, STATED PLAINLY

```
1. `ec_radical_anion` WAS MY CHOSEN ADVERSARIAL SPOT-CHECK SPECIES (§39.85(d)) — selected for being
   an anion with a diffuse SOMO, and verified by me only for "converged + checkpoint on disk".
   🔴 I CHECKED THE SAME THREE METADATA FIELDS I HAD JUST CRITICISED engineer9 FOR CHECKING
   (§39.92(d)), one message after writing the rule. Had the bracket not been cancelled, the probe

   co2, emc) have NO free control. For them the point group is a SUSPICION, not a verdict — and for
   c2h4/co2/h2o/pf6 the symmetry is simply correct. **A point-group flag must never be read as a

3. Any P5 chemical quantity taken from a trapped row is wrong by up to ~0.8 eV. The §39.82(b)

### (d) 🔒 THE AUDIT, RE-TIERED — frequencies are the THIRD instrument, not the first

```
TIER 1  point group, printed in every log                                    FREE, DONE (a)
TIER 2  s0-vs-s1 energy where a second seed exists                           FREE, DONE (b)
        ⟹ convicts ec_radical_anion and li_ec2_cation; clears ec and ch3o_radical
TIER 3  n_imag from the frequency recovery                                   rides the recovery
        ⟹ the ONLY instrument for symmetric rows with no second seed
🔒 ⟹ THE RIGHT REMEDY FOR A CONVICTED ROW IS NOT A FREQUENCY. It is a C1 RE-OPTIMISATION with
   `nosymm` (§39.89) from a perturbed seed — the frequency would only confirm what the energy has
   already settled. Spend the compute on the fix, not on a second proof.
```

### (e) The ruling engineer9 actually asked for — INVARIANCE, and the audit is ASYMMETRIC

```
🟢 INVARIANCE IS CORRECT, and not as a weaker substitute: gradient invariance at a geometry that
   G16's own table already certified against the DEFAULT threshold ⟹ the same verdict holds on the
   new surface, because the verdict is a deterministic function of the gradient (§39.97(b)). It is
   also the only form measurable from a freq-only job. Their 0.63–2.19 non-monotone Cartesian-to-
   internal ratio settles that no correction factor could ever rescue the threshold form.
🔴 BUT THE FREQUENCY AUDIT IS NOT SYMMETRIC IN WHAT IT CAN CONCLUDE, and this has not been said:
   P5's rows are converged to DEFAULT tolerance (30× looser than tight, max force 4.5e-4).
   A residual gradient of that size perturbs SOFT modes — precisely where symmetry-breaking modes
   live — so:
     n_imag > 0 with a LARGE imaginary frequency   ⟹ trapping, high confidence
     n_imag > 0 with a SMALL imaginary frequency   ⟹ INDETERMINATE; a default-tolerance residual
                                                     can push a soft mode through zero by itself
     n_imag == 0                                   ⟹ WEAKER evidence of "not trapped" than the
                                                     converse is of "trapped" — the same residual
                                                     can mask a small imaginary mode
⟹ record the imaginary frequency's MAGNITUDE, never just the count. `n_imag` alone is the
  geometry-only-convergence mistake (C-8.2) transplanted into the audit.
```

## 39.99 🟢 RUNGS 1+2 IN ONE JOB — ACCEPTED, and the "wasted" duplicate Hessian is not waste: it is a FREE in-job reproducibility floor (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> engineer9 (§R39.60) proposes running rung 1 (freq-only, self-verifying) and rung 2 (warm-started
> `opt=(tight,calcfc) freq`) as two Link1 steps of ONE job — ~10.4 core-h — with the escalation
> moved into the READING ORDER rather than out of the round. Accepted, with one correction to what
> the extra ~5.9 core-h buys.

### (a) Accepted, and the structural argument is the project's own

```
🔒 COMPUTE-AND-RECORD vs CONSULT. Both rungs always computed, always recorded; WHICH ONE IS
   CONSULTED depends on the branch. That is C-10.1 for cost probes, Ω, and B+ (§39.77) — the
   fourth application of the same separation, and it preserves the ladder exactly: the escalation
   is a reading rule, not a submission.
🔴 AND THE SCHEDULE ARGUMENT IS DECISIVE ON ITS OWN: this item GATES `u56_2.released`. A two-
   submission escalation spends a full submit/collect cycle on a release gate. Calendar has been
   worth more than core-h all day; +5.9 core-h to remove a possible round of latency is not close.
🟢 engineer9's own caveat strengthens it: the 4e-9 floor was measured between two runs on the SAME
   solvent model, and §39.97(a)'s cavity-tessellation component means the Cartesian residual can
   move with the discretisation across `generic` → `acetone`. **Rung 1's hit rate may well be low** —
   which is exactly the case where a two-submission ladder would have cost the round.
```

### (b) 🟢 ONE CORRECTION — the duplicate Hessian is a MEASUREMENT, not overhead

engineer9 prices escalation as *"discards rung 1's Hessian (~2.3 core-h)"*, and notes step 2 could
in principle inherit it via the checkpoint (`opt=(tight,readfc)`), saving that cost.
```
🔒 DO NOT INHERIT IT. Let step 2's `calcfc` RECOMPUTE the Hessian at the same geometry, in the same
   job, under the same deck. The two Hessians are then an INDEPENDENT REPEAT MEASUREMENT of the
   same quantity, and their deviation IS the in-job reproducibility floor for THIS species at THIS
   basis — the exact thing I required engineer9 to buy for 11 core-h as a third Link1 step on the
   level2 control (§39.92(c)). Here it arrives for free, because the ladder already computes both.
⟹ THE ~2.3 core-h IS NOT DISCARDED. It is the calibration that makes rung 1's verdict a measured
  claim rather than an assumed one, on the very run that uses it.
🟡 The `readfc` route is also SAFE here in a way it is not across jobs — same job, same checkpoint,
  no `chk_handoff` copy, so the failure mode that forced the handoff fix cannot occur. It is
  refused on grounds of what it costs us in information, not on grounds of risk.
```

### (c) 🟢 The second-order benefit engineer9 names is real and belongs to the basin check

When rung 1 SUCCEEDS, step 2 still ran — so §39.96's covalent-graph basin check gets its data on
exactly the case where nobody would have bought it. **A warm start that lands on the same geometry
is the confirmation that a warm start is safe on this system**, and it is only ever observable when
it was not needed. Recorded on pass, per engineer9's own always-record rule.

### (d) Rung 3 stays unscheduled

Confirmed: `~42–66` core-h is not pre-run. A rung-2 basin-check failure means **the acetone surface
moved the structure to another species** — a finding to surface, not a job to retry. Anything spent
there should follow the C1-perturbed re-optimisation prescription (§39.98(d)), not a longer cold
start, since §39.89/§39.98 have now established that a cold start from a packaged seed is the
documented way INTO a symmetry trap, not out of one.

## 39.102 🔒 THE SEED FILES SETTLE IT: THE KICK IS THE MECHANISM, `nosymm` IS THE BACKSTOP — so the existing C1 rows ARE symmetry-free and can be reused. Replicate the `s1` protocol for the two missing species (proposer, 2026-08-21)

> engineer9 (§R39.64) reports that their `p = 2.2` exponent is invalid (one anchor C2V, one C1) and
> asks two things: reuse the two measured C1 rows or re-run all four, and whether to validate the
> 16-thread packing gain first. **The `p5_seeds.*.json` files answer the first and refine §39.101.**

### (a) 🔒 THREE PROTOCOLS ARE ON DISK, AND THEY SEPARATE THE TWO MITIGATIONS

```
P5  s0 rows   "perturbed": false, "amplitude_ang": 0.0     no kick, no nosymm  ⟹ TRAPPED (C2V/CS)
P5  s1 rows   "perturbed": true,  "amplitude_ang": 0.1     kick, NO nosymm     ⟹ C1, ESCAPED
endpoint      "perturbed": true,  "amplitude_ang": 0.25    kick + nosymm       ⟹ C1, ESCAPED
```
🔒 **THE KICK ALONE IS SUFFICIENT, AND THE MECHANISM IS DETECTION, NOT ENFORCEMENT.** G16 detects
the point group of the *input* geometry; a perturbed seed is detected as C1, so there is no group
to enforce and `nosymm` has nothing to switch off. **Every P5 `s1` row escaped without `nosymm`.**
⟹ §39.101's natural experiment compared (no kick, no `nosymm`) against (kick + `nosymm`) and
  therefore could NOT separate them. **The `s1` rows separate them: the kick is the mechanism;
  `nosymm` is the backstop for the case where the seed is symmetric anyway.** Both stay — a backstop
  whose primary has already failed once is exactly what one keeps — but the causal claim is now
  correctly attributed, and the trap's true root cause is `amplitude_ang: 0.0`, not the missing
  keyword I named in §39.89.

### (b) 🟢 CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FACTOR RE-MEASUREMENT — REUSE THE TWO, and my own objection dissolves

```
My spec (§39.100(e)) required BOTH terms on correct structures AND comparable starting displacements,
and I implied the existing C1 rows fail because P5's decks lack `nosymm`.
🟢 THAT OBJECTION IS WRONG: a C1 molecule has |G| = 1, so those rows enjoyed NO symmetry saving.
   **The `s1` rows are already symmetry-free measurements.** The only real mismatch is amplitude
   (0.1 Å against the endpoint's 0.25 Å) and integration grid (P5 default against production
   UltraFine) — and BOTH cancel in a ratio when numerator and denominator share them.
🔒 RULING — cheapest form that is internally consistent:
   REPLICATE P5's `s1` PROTOCOL EXACTLY for the two missing species (li_ec_cation, li_ec_radical):
   same 0.1 Å kick, same seed rng, same level2 deck, same default grid, same thread count.
   Then all four factors are measured under ONE protocol and the ratios are internally valid.
   ⟹ SAVES the two already-measured rows (ec 38.74, ec_radical_anion 110.33 core-h) — including
     the 110 core-h row, which re-running would buy nothing.
⚠ REPORT WITH THE FACTORS, do not bury: they are measured at 0.1 Å kick on the OLD deck. Transfer
  to a 0.25 Å production protocol is an ASSUMPTION, and it is weakest for the floppy Li complexes —
  which are exactly the species carrying ×2.8 and ×15.2. **A ratio measured at one amplitude need
  not hold at another when the two species differ in floppiness.** That is a real residual, it is
  cheaper to state than to remove, and removing it means measuring at both amplitudes.
```

### (c) 🟢 PROBE A IS THE RIGHT MEASUREMENT — with one boundary on what it can conclude

engineer9's probe A (the P6 anchor deck unchanged, plus `nosymm`; same geometry, same species, one
moving variable) is exactly the |G| measurement §39.100(b) called for and could not get from disk.
```
🔴 BUT IT MEASURES ONE OF THE TWO COMPONENTS. The symmetry saving has two:
   (a) SCF / integral work reduced by symmetry-unique integrals  ← probe A measures THIS
   (b) fewer optimiser degrees of freedom in a symmetry-constrained optimisation ← NOT measured
   probe A is an `sp`. It contains no optimiser at all.
🟢 AND THAT IS PRECISELY THE RIGHT SCOPE FOR THE THING IT IS BEING BOUGHT FOR: the P5 recovery is
   FREQ-ONLY AT FIXED GEOMETRY — no optimiser, so component (b) is identically zero there. **Probe A
   fully determines the correction to the 92–396 core-h recovery estimate.**
🔴 It is a LOWER BOUND for optimisation costs (the factors, wave-1 sizing), where (b) is live.
   My §39.100 ratios (4.38×, 2.07×) measured (a)+(b) together, contaminated by seed distance;
   probe A measures (a) cleanly. **Neither alone gives (b) — and nobody should quote probe A's
   number as the symmetry correction for an OPTIMISATION.**
```

### (d) 16-thread validation first — endorsed, with one science constraint

engineer9's ordering argument is theirs and I have no cost vote, but the leverage is obvious and I
endorse running it before the factor re-measurement.
```
🔒 ONE CONSTRAINT, from §39.85(a): ALL FOUR FACTOR SPECIES MUST RUN AT THE SAME THREAD COUNT —
   16 or 64, but not mixed. These runs produce geometries and energies, not only timings, and
   Gaussian's parallel reductions are deterministic at fixed thread count and not necessarily
   across counts. A factor set assembled from mixed thread counts carries a numerical difference
   in the same place the physical one is being measured.
```

### (e) On the exponent's collapse

engineer9 withdraws `p = 2.2` because their two calibration points differ in symmetry as well as in
basis. The honest range they give (`p` from 2.21 at |G| = 1 to 4.45 at |G| = 4) puts the recovery
at 92–396 core-h rather than 92–152.

🔒 WORTH NAMING: THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS §39.86(d) — an anchor scaled by a variable that was not
   the only thing moving — but caught from the OTHER side. There it was atom count versus basis
   count; here it is basis count versus symmetry. **Both times the anchor explained its own case
   perfectly.** The mechanical check that catches it is the one already adopted: name the variable
   you are scaling by, and verify NOTHING ELSE differs between anchor and target. "Verify the set
   is uniform in it" — engineer9's own extension — is what would have caught this one.
🟢 And their damage assessment is right in the part that matters: the ORDERING of the per-species
   table survives, the absolute core-h do not, and the three cost factors are protected because
   symmetry cancels in a C2V ÷ C2V ratio (§39.100(c)).

### (a) 🔴 PROBE B MOVES THREE VARIABLES FROM THE ONLY MEASURED BASELINE

probe A   probe 0 + nosymm                          one variable ✅  symmetry factor
probe C   probe 0 + UltraFine                       one variable ✅  grid factor

Probe B is one variable away only from a point that **does not exist**: `NBasis 321 · nosymm ·
UltraFine`. As designed, the basis exponent can be extracted from it only by first *assuming* the

SYMMETRY, in an `sp`   reduces the count of symmetry-unique two-electron integrals.

  pending probe A" is a fact.

### (b) 🔴 `n_imag` ALONE IS NOT THE AUDIT DATUM — record the MAGNITUDES

§39.98(e) already ruled this and it is absent from coder12's field list.
```
RECORD every imaginary frequency's VALUE, not just the count. And emit the interpretive rule with
the data, the same way the §39.103(4) expectation is emitted verbatim:
   n_imag > 0, LARGE |ν_imag|   ⟹ trapping, high confidence
   n_imag > 0, SMALL |ν_imag|   ⟹ INDETERMINATE — these geometries are converged to DEFAULT
                                   tolerance (max force 4.5e-4, 30× looser than tight), and a
                                   residual gradient that size can push a soft mode through zero
   n_imag == 0                  ⟹ WEAKER evidence of "not trapped" than the converse is of
                                   "trapped" — the same residual can MASK a small imaginary mode
🔒 `n_imag` as a bare count is C-8.2's own geometry-only-convergence mistake transplanted into the
   audit: a number standing in for a judgement it cannot support alone.
```

### (c) 🟢 TWO FREE ADDITIONS THAT MAKE THE ROWS COMPARABLE TO THE CALIBRATION

```
1. SPLIT `u_freq` INTO ITS SCF AND HESSIAN/CPHF COMPONENTS. engineer9 already does exactly this on
   the endpoint job ("Hessian/CPHF 2.27 core-h, SCF 0.6"), and §39.107 makes the calibration probes
   emit both. If the recovery records only a total, its 17 rows cannot be compared against the
   calibration that exists to correct them. Free — both timings are in the same log.
2. RECORD BOTH RAW FORCE NUMBERS, not only their ratio: the freq job's `Cartesian Forces: Max/RMS`
   AND the row's own final optimisation values. **A ratio hides which side moved**, and when a row
   comes back off-ratio that is the first question anyone will ask.
```

### (d) 🟢 NAME WHAT THE FREQ-JOB POINT GROUP IS FOR — it is a `nosymm` verification, not a datum

```
The production deck carries `nosymm`, so G16 should report C1 for EVERY row regardless of geometry.
⟹ THE FREQ-JOB POINT GROUP IS A CHECK THAT `nosymm` TOOK EFFECT. Any row reporting non-C1 there
  means the keyword did not apply, and that row's cost carries a symmetry saving it should not.
  Label the field that way, or a future reader will compare it against the stored-geometry point
  group as though the two were the same kind of measurement — they are not: one describes a
  molecule, the other verifies a keyword.
```
🟢 Everything else in coder12's encoding is what §39.103 asked for, including emitting the
expectation verbatim so a low reproduce-rate is not read as an acetone finding, and the "longer
wall is the wrong fix" note travelling with the five skipped rows.

## 39.109 🔴🔴 A T21-se PILOT CANNOT BE PRICED YET — R-C's OWN REACTANT HAS FAILED TO CONVERGE TWICE, AND THAT LOOKS LIKE F10 FIRING, NOT A WALL-CLOCK PROBLEM (proposer9, 2026-08-21)

> engineer10 (Round B ceiling report) asked whether to price a single T21-se production pilot as the
> cheapest real information purchase before wave-1 sizing. Before pricing an attempt, I checked
> whether its own starting point exists. **`T21-se` = the single-ended TS search on R-C's reactant.
> `R-C`'s reactant = `Li⁺(EC)₂•⁻` (`li_ec2_cation`, charge 0, spin multiplicity 2, 21 atoms) — the
> genuinely 2-D-mechanism reaction (Li translocates as part of ring opening, §3/`mechanism`
> coordinate). `E21` = its endpoint certification (C-8's precondition, analogous to R-A's certified
> reactant that already gates U56-2). `F10` = §39.39's pre-registered falsifier: *"endpoint
> certification for the 21-atom R-C reactant does not converge inside any budget we will approve."*
> It does not exist yet.**

### (a) 🔴🔴 The precondition is failing, twice, for the same reason, and more wall-clock will not fix it

```
attempt 1 (B0-D, §39.1(e-bis))   li_ec2_cation_A_cheap_optfreq   283 core-h   NOT CONVERGED
attempt 2 (P5, this round)       li_ec2_cation_s0_L2             429.55 core-h  NOT CONVERGED,
                                                                  scf_max=14 (fine), opt=49 (wall cap)
```
Both diagnosed the same way, independently, on different rounds: **the SCF is healthy — the
*optimiser* wanders. This is U-55's floppy-PES signature, and its own prescription, already ruled
twice in this document (§39.72(3), §39.103(c)), is CONFORMER QUALITY, not a longer wall cap.**
§39.103(c), verbatim, about the second failure: *"raising the wall limit buys another 429 of the
same."* **712+ core-h have now been spent confirming this, not fixing it.**

⟹ **There is no converged, certified R-C reactant to start T21-se from.** A TS pilot attempt priced
today would either (i) be blocked at the same C-8 precondition that correctly refused P1 three times
on real hardware (§1a finding 3 — cheap refusal, ~2 core-h, the gate working as designed), or (ii) if
someone hands it an UNCERTIFIED geometry to save time, repeat exactly the P1 mistake one level up —
a "TS" search anchored on a structure that is not actually the reactant minimum. **Do not do (ii).**

### (b) 🔴 This is very likely F10, and F10's own pre-registered answer is explicit — read it before reaching for more core-h

§39.39(d) pre-registered the response to this exact failure, and it is not "try again with a bigger
cap": *"the correct response is NOT to weaken C-8, but to move S3's target size down and say so out
loud."* I am not calling F10 formally triggered yet — two non-convergences under two different
protocols is strong but not exhaustive evidence, and there is one cheap thing worth trying first
((c) below) before accepting the falsifier and shrinking S3's target size. But the escape hatch this
project already ruled out — loosening C-8's convergence bar to let a not-quite-stationary geometry
through — is not on the table. **A T21-se pilot's value is zero if it starts somewhere that is not
R-C's reactant**, for the same reason P1's IRC anchor is zero: a real cost measurement of the wrong
job is not a measurement of the job.

### (c) 🔒 The cheap thing worth trying first: diagnose WHICH coordinate is floppy before picking a fix — three candidates, in the order I'd spend on them

**Candidate 1 — GFN2-xTB conformer sampling, reusing the already-built `engine-E3b` MTD infrastructure (RECOMMENDED, try first)**
- **Physical assumption**: GFN2-xTB can *rank* near-degenerate Li⁺-coordination basins of the SAME
  connectivity well enough to identify which one DFT should start from, even though it is documented
  to get *absolute* Li⁺-complex binding energetics wrong (U-55's whole worry, §39.38(d)). Ranking
  nearby minima is a strictly weaker ask than computing an accurate barrier — but it can still fail
  if two basins are close enough in the true surface that GFN2's error reorders them.
- **Expected accuracy**: not a barrier or an energy — a basin-selection tool only. No eV figure
  applies; the deliverable is "which starting geometry converges at DFT," not a chemical quantity.
- **Known failure mode**: GFN2 itself gets trapped in one shallow metastable state across all MTD
  seeds (a systematic bias, not a sampling-diversity problem) — the same failure class already
  flagged for Δ_shell's n=1→2 shell-conditioning problem, same underlying physics (Li⁺ coordination
  is exactly where GFN2's documented error lives). A second, cheaper failure: MTD's kpush/alp
  hyperparameters (already flagged as under-scaled vs the published nanoreactor setting, §39.40(c))
  may not be tuned for CONFORMER sampling at all — they were tuned/discussed for REACTION discovery,
  a different sampling target (local floppiness vs bond-breaking).
- **Verification**: (i) free — check whether either existing partial DFT trajectory (283 or 429.55
  core-h attempts) is already heading toward a GFN2-found basin (same covalent+coordination graph);
  agreement is corroborating, not proof. (ii) the real test: does DFT converge cleanly (tight,
  nosymm, kicked seed — the now-validated protocol) from the GFN2-selected geometry, where it did
  not from the idealised guess? That is an external, falsifiable check, not internal consistency.
- **Required inputs**: xtb (already vendored, working on this cluster — confirmed by 186 clean GFN2
  scan frames this round, §1). No new binary, no CREST (confirmed absent, §37.2, LGPL binary check
  done, does not run — RDKit/MMFF is explicitly FORBIDDEN for Li-coordination clusters, §37.2.4, no
  MMFF Li parameters — so this is the only conformer-search route this project's tooling actually
  supports for this species class).
- **Cost profile (scaling only, engineer prices)**: N seeds × (short MD/MTD run + GFN2 quench-opt +
  graph/RMSD dedup) — all GFN2, no DFT, order-of-magnitude cheaper than one more DFT attempt at any
  cap. Existing infrastructure (`b0_conformers.json`'s kick/perturbation machinery, `engine-E3b`'s MD
  driver) means little or no new code.

**Candidate 2 — multiple independent kicked-seed DFT restarts, capped short (fallback if Candidate 1's ranking is judged untrustworthy)**
- **Physical assumption**: several independently perturbed starting geometries (reusing the
  0.1–0.25 Å kick + `nosymm` protocol already validated this round, §39.89/§39.102) sample different
  basins; the true minimum is among them.
- **Expected accuracy**: same caveat as Candidate 1 — a basin-selection tool, not a chemical number.
- **Known failure mode**: the kick amplitude is uncalibrated for THIS species — §39.104(c)'s own
  documented failure mode applies at both ends ("too small returns to the same minimum, too large
  breaks a bond"), and nobody has measured the right amplitude for a 21-atom Li⁺ cation cluster
  specifically (only 11-atom P5 species and the endpoint have been checked).
- **Verification**: same external check as Candidate 1 (does a full re-optimisation from the
  best-of-N converge cleanly).
- **Cost profile**: N × (DFT optimisation capped at a small cycle count, e.g. 10–15, just to sort
  basins by descending energy, NOT full convergence) — cheaper than N full 429-core-h attempts, but
  still DFT-priced, not GFN2-priced. The more expensive of the two real candidates.
- **Why it is not first choice**: it spends DFT wall-time to ask a question GFN2 can plausibly answer
  for free — same "gate-before-you-pay" principle already standing in this project (§4, rule 5).

**Candidate 3 — free diagnostic, run regardless of which candidate above is chosen: read the low-frequency mode composition**
- Not a fix, a **precondition check for the other two**. This project already knows how to ask "is
  the floppiness localised to the Li-coordination coordinate, or is it inter-ligand (relative
  orientation of the two EC rings around Li)?" — the `ν_min` / `N(ν<50)` / condition-number
  correlation test already ruled for U-55 (§39.29, line 10546) answers exactly this, from a GFN2
  Hessian, at near-zero cost. **If the floppy modes are Li-coordination-localised, a
  constrained-then-released staged optimisation (freeze the two EC rings' internal geometry first,
  relax only the Li-coordination shell, then release) is a cheap, zero-new-tooling fourth option
  worth adding — it is the same "constrained relaxation preserves the intended basin" logic already
  ruled correct for the GFN2 pre-stage protocol (§39.68).** If the floppy modes are inter-ligand, that
  staging does nothing and Candidate 1/2 stand as the real options. This diagnostic is what decides
  between them and costs one GFN2 Hessian on a structure that already exists.

### (d) What I am and am not saying

```
NOT saying: F10 is confirmed triggered, or S3's target size must shrink today. One cheap diagnostic
  (c) and one cheap fix attempt (Candidate 1) have not been tried yet, and F10's own text asks for a
  budget judgement ("any budget we will approve") that is engineer's call, not mine to pre-empt.
SAYING: pricing a T21-se TS pilot attempt right now prices the wrong step. The bottleneck is a
  converged R-C reactant, which does not exist after 712+ core-h of trying, and the fix that has
  twice been named in this document ("conformer quality") has never been given a concrete method
  until this section. Spend there first — it is cheaper than one more DFT attempt at any cap, and it
  is the only thing that can tell us whether F10 is real or just a bad starting guess.
```

**Reported to**: engineer10 (direct reply), team-lead (consolidated).

### (e) 🔒 RULING, on engineer10's direct request (§R39.70): S3 wave-1 T21-se attempts GATED AT 0, and the gate is on E21, not on pilot-cost data

engineer10 asked me to formally decide whether to gate wave-1 at 0 committed T21-se attempts pending
a real per-attempt cost measurement (their own recommendation, since the retracted S₂₁ cube law
leaves T21-se with no valid cost figure, §1/§R39.41). **Ruling: yes, 0 committed attempts — but the
gate condition is stronger than "pending cost data."**

```
engineer10's framing:  gate lifts once a real T21-se pilot ATTEMPT returns a measured cost.
CORRECTED (this section):  gate lifts once E21 (R-C's reactant certification) exists — a pilot
  ATTEMPT cannot be submitted before that regardless of cost data being wanted, because there is
  no reactant to attempt it from ((a)-(b) above). Cost data is the SECOND thing the gate needs, not
  the first.
```
This is not a semantic difference: it changes what the next purchase is. "Gated pending pilot cost"
reads as "buy a pilot attempt next." **The actual next purchase is the conformer-search fix ((c)
above)** — buying a pilot attempt before that either wastes core-h on a C-8 refusal or, worse, buys a
cost measurement of the wrong job if the precondition is bypassed. Zero committed attempts, zero
committed core-h, until E21 lands; T21-se's cost remains formally UNKNOWN in the meantime, same
status as engineer8/engineer9's retraction already recorded — this ruling does not change that
number, it changes what work is authorised to happen before that number can even be attempted.

## 39.111 🔴 §39.108(c)(1)'S PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG — NO SAME-LOG SCF/HESSIAN SPLIT EXISTS. OPTION A (NO SPLIT, RAW `u_freq`) APPROVED — NOT BLOCKING TODAY, AND IT SHOULDN'T BE BUILT TODAY (proposer9, 2026-08-21)

> engineer10 traced §39.108(c)(1)'s "engineer9 already does exactly this... free, same log" claim
> (§R39.74) before handing coder13 a spec to build against. **It is false, for the same reason
> §39.110 was false: I read a phrase off a status report and attached a stronger claim to it than
> the phrase supported, without checking the artefact.**

### (a) What was actually measured vs what I claimed

```
CLAIMED (§39.108(c)(1)):  the endpoint job's log gives an SCF-component figure and a Hessian/CPHF
   figure from the SAME freq step, free, ready to copy into P5's 17 rows.
ACTUAL (engineer10's trace, §R39.74):  2.27 core-h is real and free — it is G16's own Link-number
   boundary between the opt STEP and the freq STEP in a combined opt+freq route. The "SCF ~0.6"
   figure was never measured from a freq-only job's own log (none existed yet when it was written)
   — it was a subtraction-based ESTIMATE built from a DIFFERENT job's stage (the tight-optimisation
   stage's cycle count). There is no same-log opt+freq SCF-vs-Hessian decomposition on record.
```
🔒 **Ninth instance of the day's recurring defect, and it is mine twice in a row now** (§39.110, this
section) — a status phrase ("Hessian/CPHF 2.27, SCF 0.6") read as a measurement instead of checked
against what actually produced it. The mechanical fix is the same one already on record: before a
number carries a ruling's weight, trace it to the log line, don't recall the phrase that summarised it.

### (b) 🟢 RULING: Option A (no per-row split, raw `u_freq`) — approved for P5_freq_recovery, as-is

The split's only purpose was to let a FUTURE numeric correction apply the right calibration factor
to the right fraction of each row's cost (SCF-component factor vs Hessian-component factor, §39.107).
**§39.108(a) already ruled that no numeric correction is applied today** — rows get a
`u_opt_symmetry_biased` FLAG, not an invented factor ("a stamped 'biased low, |G|=4, correction
pending probe A' is a fact; a stamped '×4 applied' would be an invented number"). A flag needs no
split. **Nothing currently blocks on the split existing.**

```
🔒 SHIP WHAT CODER13 IS ALREADY BUILDING: raw total u_freq per row, no SCF/Hessian split.
🔴 DO NOT COMMISSION THE EXTRA MATCHED-`sp` JOB (engineer10's priced option, ~5-40 core-h for all
   17 rows) TODAY. Same rule already applied twice this session (§39.101 rung 2, §39.105/39.106):
   do not build machinery whose only customer is a correction step that has not been authorised yet.
   Price it WHEN a numeric correction is actually being applied, not before.
```

### (c) The residual this leaves, stated so it is not rediscovered later

When the calibration's SCF-component and Hessian-component factors (§39.107/§R39.69) are ready and
someone DOES want to turn `u_opt_symmetry_biased`'s flag into an actual corrected number, they will
have two choices, and neither is free of assumption:
```
(i)  treat each row's u_freq as if it were pure Hessian/CPHF and apply the Hessian-component factor
     to the whole thing — over-corrects by however much of the row was really SCF re-convergence.
(ii) use the calibration's OWN measured SCF-fraction (from its matched sp-vs-freq subtraction,
     §R39.69 part 3) as a blended estimate applied uniformly to every row — assumes P5's SCF
     fraction matches the calibration probe's SCF fraction, which is not guaranteed (different
     NBasis, different point group per row).
```
**Whichever is chosen, state it as an assumption in the correction record, not silently** — this is
exactly the shape §39.108(c)(1) tried to avoid and, by being wrong about what was free, would have
hidden instead.

**Reported to**: engineer10 (confirms their trace, ratifies Option A), coder13 (ship as designed, no
split), team-lead (consolidated, two corrections in one session — see §39.110 for the first).

   two-rung mechanism — checked because it looked unusual at first and needed ruling out as such).
   C1 throughout means nosymm held for the Hessian, not just the geometry search.
C-8.3  n_imag counts EVERY negative eigenvalue, no magnitude waiver. All 27 vibrational modes
   (3N-6, N=11) positive, lowest 77.0255 cm**-1 — clear of zero, no marginal soft mode where a
   waiver question could even arise. 🔒 ONE THING WORTH STATING EXPLICITLY rather than silently
   assumed: the "Low frequencies" line separately reports the 6 near-zero translation/rotation
   projections, two of which are small and formally negative (-21.5938, -9.3754 cm**-1) — this is
   the ordinary numerical residual of projecting out rigid-body motion, NOT part of the 3N-6
   vibrational spectrum C-8.3 governs, and every comp-chem convention (including this project's own
   parser, `f1_observables.json`'s `n_imag_at_convergence: 0`) excludes it from the imaginary-mode
   count. Recording the check rather than the assumption, since C-8.3's "no magnitude waiver"
   wording could in principle be misread to include these if someone didn't know the convention.
```

files, pending coder14's `stable=opt` SCF-instability diagnostic — NOT a final ruling)

**Status**: proposer, resuming from proposer9. Read directly from

### (a) R-A method bake-off (`U56_RA_scan` vs `U56_RA_qst2`) — confirmed disagreement, own read

`ts_acceptance.json` + `spectator_test.json` + `bracket_check.json`, both jobs:

```
                        U56_RA_scan             U56_RA_qst2
n_imag / omega (cm-1)   1 / -1153.2             1 / -139.6
Omega break (O-C)       0.839 (strong)          0.0044 (~0)
Omega mechanism(Li-O)   0.245                   0.0100
mode top3 atoms         C(0.35) O(0.28) C(0.17)  H(0.33) H(0.32) H(0.13)
spectator test          not spectator, agrees    ambiguous: unweighted BLOCKS (H outside
                        both definitions          set, ratio 7.72), mass-weighted PASSES
                                                   (ratio 0.70) -- definition_independent:false
bracket check           one-sided only (no        TWO-SIDED, both bonds PASS (saddle sits
                        product cert in this       geometrically between reactant/product
                        job dir -- see (d))        distances for both break and mechanism bonds)
B+ forward              agree, 0.00084 eV          agree, 0.00013 eV (same covalent graph)
B+ reverse               agree, 0.00033 eV          unavailable (too_few_points)
```

**My read, independent of the mode-character argument alone**: `U56_RA_scan` is the physically
credible TS on three independent lines of evidence that all point the same way (Ω, spectator test,
B+). `U56_RA_qst2` is NOT simply "wrong" on every axis — its bracket check actually PASSES two-sided
(the saddle geometry sits between the certified reactant and the certified product on both declared
bonds), and its B+ forward comparison agrees to 0.00013 eV, tighter than `U56_RA_scan`'s own B+
numbers. What fails for `U56_RA_qst2` is mode character specifically: Ω≈0 on both declared bonds and
the imaginary mode (only -139.6 cm⁻¹, soft) is dominated by H-atom motion (index 8/9, top two
contributors) not assigned to either bond in the mapping. **Read: QST2 converged to a real stationary
point that sits on a geometrically plausible position along the reactant→product interpolation, but
whose actual reaction coordinate is a low-frequency H-wagging/rotation mode uncoupled from the
declared bond-breaking chemistry** — i.e. a genuine saddle point, almost certainly NOT the rate-
determining one, more likely a rotational TS of a pendant group crossed incidentally by QST2's linear
interpolation between the reactant and product structures it was given. This is a distinct failure
mode from "spurious/wrong basin" — the bracket check passing on a bad candidate is itself a finding:
**bracket check (geometry-only, no mode information) cannot substitute for Ω/mode-character on its
own** — it answers "is this saddle located somewhere sane along the path," not "is this the right
saddle." Do not read the two-sided bracket PASS on `U56_RA_qst2` as rehabilitating it.

**Provisional lean (pending Track B ruling)**: accept `U56_RA_scan` as R-A's candidate TS, reject
`U56_RA_qst2` outright rather than ordering a redo — the mode-character evidence is unambiguous
(0.0044 vs 0.839 is not a borderline call) even though one axis (bracket) formally passes. A method
bake-off that disagrees this starkly is doing its job: it caught QST2 landing on the wrong saddle. I
will not treat this as final until IRC completion is resolved (neither job has one) — see (c).

### (b) R-B candidate (`U56_RB_scan`) — Li-hopping pathology, plus a genuinely truncated IRC

`ts_acceptance.json`: n_imag = 1 at -84.3 cm⁻¹ (soft), mode top3 = **Li (0.441), H (0.145), H
(0.133)** — Li is the single largest contributor to the imaginary mode by a wide margin (3× the next
atom). `spectator_test.json` formally passes (`blocked: false`, both definitions agree) only because
Li is inside the declared coordinate set (`coordinate_atoms: [0, 1, 10]`, index 10 = Li) — the test
is checking "is the largest-amplitude atom outside the coordinate the mapping declared," and here it
is inside by construction, not because the motion is actually bond-breaking chemistry. **This is
exactly the ADR-112 pathology** (P1's original mislabeled saddle was a Li⁺-hopping mode) reproduced
in a case that passes the formal check only because R-B's own mapping happened to include Li in the
declared coordinate. The spectator test's coverage gap here is real and was already flagged in
`05_STATE.md` (the "spectator test no longer catches P1" finding) — R-B's candidate is a fresh
instance of the same gap, not a new one.

**Own IRC read** (`irc_completion_forward.json`/`reverse.json` + raw log, independent of the plan
document): both directions report `normal_termination: true`, `minimum_found: false`,
`termination_reason: "normal_termination_without_a_minimum_marker"`, `truncated: false`. Reading the
raw log directly (`irc_forward.log`): the path reaches only **Point Number 1**, `NET REACTION
COORDINATE UP TO THIS POINT = 0.18324`, before Gaussian's own IRC driver stops and exits cleanly.
0.18 (dimensionless mass-weighted Bohr units) is a tiny fraction of a typical IRC path length (R-A's
completed GFN2 scans span arc lengths in the range of several Å-equivalent units) — **this "clean"
termination is not evidence of a real, walked reaction path; it is evidence the IRC driver gave up
after one corrector step and Gaussian's own exit code doesn't distinguish that from success.** The
`truncated: false` label is misleading in the same direction the plan document flagged for the
`irc_completion_*.json` generic label on R-A ("no_marker...wall-clock or budget kill" being wrong for
a different reason) — here the code correctly avoids calling it "truncated" by its own definition
(no wall/budget kill occurred), but a 1-point IRC is scientifically uninformative regardless of what
caused it to stop. **This is not yet explained** (why does the corrector give up so early here, vs.
running for hundreds of substeps then crashing on R-A?) and Track A item 3 (routed to coder) should
answer the mechanism; my reading only confirms the plan's characterisation of it as a live open
question, not a settled "it worked" result.

**Provisional lean**: R-B's candidate is not yet acceptable as a TS on either count — mode character
(Li-dominated, ADR-112-shape) and IRC completeness (effectively zero path walked). I would not order
a full redo yet without first knowing (i) whether the SCF-instability finding in (c) below explains
why the corrector gives up this early even here, and (ii) whether a Li-decoupled coordinate
definition (excluding Li from the declared set, forcing the spectator test to actually test it)
changes the read — that's a GSCAN2/mapping-protocol question, not mine to rule on alone before
Track B item 7 lands.

### (c) SCF-instability signature — own re-measurement, one finding beyond what's already logged

Re-counted `**** Warning!!: The largest {alpha,beta} MO coefficient` occurrences and their magnitudes
directly (not taken from the plan document's count):

```
job                              magnitude (first occ -> last occ, alpha/beta)   drifts?    n(occ)

endpoint_prep_product  (11-atom) ~36.5 -> ~36.6 (both stages)                    no (flat)   4
endpoint_prep_rc_reactant(21-at) ~71.0 -> ~78.9 alpha, ~67.0 -> ~71.3 beta        YES         4
U56_RA_scan/irc_forward (11-at)  ~31.6 -> ~38.7, monotonic climb                 YES        66
U56_RB_scan/irc_forward (11-at)  ~20.2 -> ~20.1, flat                            no          8
```

**This is a finding beyond what's already in `05_STATE.md`**: the CERTIFIED, PASSING 21-atom
`endpoint_prep_rc_reactant` job (R-C's reactant, `n_imag=0`, used in the "what landed cleanly"
bucket) shows the LARGEST coefficient magnitude of any job in this batch (~71-79), well above both
R-A's TS-chain jobs (~20-39) and R-A's own certified endpoints (~20/~36) — and it *also* drifts
upward between its two internal SCF snapshots, the same qualitative signature that later blows up
`U56_RA_scan`'s IRC. This job did not crash — it certified cleanly under C-8.2/C-8.3, which only
checks `n_imag==0` and normal termination, not SCF-quality diagnostics. **Pattern across five data
points**: magnitude does not track cleanly with atom count alone (endpoint_prep_product and
U56_RA_scan are both 11-atom but sit at ~36 and ~39 respectively vs. reactant's ~20 and RB's ~20) —
it tracks more closely with net charge / open-shell character (`rc_reactant` is the 21-atom
**cation**-radical, the single highest-magnitude case, consistent with `05_STATE.md`'s
already-logged §R39.41 finding that cation+open-shell chemistry is the real cost/complexity driver,
not atom count, just measured here on a different observable). Whether magnitude also predicts which
jobs will eventually fail the IRC corrector (RA_scan did; RB_scan, despite a similar magnitude to the
low-instability reactant/RB group, gave up after 1 point for an as-yet-unexplained reason) is exactly
what coder14's `stable=opt` diagnostic should help resolve — a real orbital-space instability
(genuine lower-energy SCF solution exists) argues for reoptimizing the wavefunction at every
problematic geometry across ALL of this project's jobs at this level, not just the two that crashed;
a basis-linear-dependency artifact argues for a numerics fix localized to the failing jobs.

**I am flagging this finding to lead/engineer now, ahead of the diagnostic, because of its scope**:
if the magnitude scaling with cation+open-shell character is real and general (not a fluke of these
five jobs), it bears directly on the still-unpriced T21-se class (`05_STATE.md`'s retracted-ceiling
item) — a 21-atom cation-radical TS search is very likely to hit the SAME or worse instability that
crashed R-A's 11-atom IRC, which would mean **T21-se's true risk is not just cost (already flagged
unknown) but also completion risk** (jobs that don't finish at all, independent of core-h spent).
This is not a ruling — it is a reason to make sure coder14's diagnostic geometry, if there's any
freedom in choosing it, is representative of the worse-instability class (rc_reactant-like) and not
just R-A's, since the two may not share a root cause.

### (d) Housekeeping finding: R-A's two attempt directories disagree on data completeness

`U56_RA_qst2/` contains `product_certified.xyz`; `U56_RA_scan/` does not (only
`reactant_certified.xyz`) — despite both being attempts at the SAME reaction R-A, which DOES have a

QST2-method payload receives, so the two methods are not being evaluated on equal footing by the
