### (e) 🔴🔴 SELF-CORRECTION (critic14's independent read, verified against the raw logs myself) —
(b) and (c) above overstated the case; not deleting them, correcting them here per the project's
record-the-error convention.

critic14 read the same two raw logs directly and found my (b)/(c) claims were built on
under-sampled evidence. I re-verified both points myself against the full logs (not taking
critic14's word for it) — confirmed correct, both times:

**(c)'s "monotonic climb...compounding" claim was wrong.** My original grep sampled only the first
5 and last 5 occurrences (`head -5`/`tail -5`) of the beta-coefficient warning in
`U56_RA_scan/irc_forward.log` and inferred a steady climb from that. Reading all 66 occurrences:
the series does rise (32.5→39.17, peaking around occurrence ~44) but then **plateaus and bounces in
a bounded band (38.2–39.2) for the remaining ~20 occurrences**, ending on an alternating
38.654/38.422 pair — bounded oscillation, not compounding growth. This matters for the ruling: a
number that keeps growing without bound looks like a genuine runaway instability; a number that
climbs once then sits in a stable band looks more like the SCF settling into a persistent-but-stable
open-shell/near-degenerate solution characteristic of this system, not a worsening pathology tracking
the geometry step. **Separately confirmed, also directly**: `grep -c "SCF Done"` = 66, `grep -c
"Convergence failure"` = 0 — every single SCF in this run converged; and at the point closest to
`NBasis=173`, `EigRej= -1.00D+00` (G16's own flag for "no linear-dependent functions removed" —
if basis linear dependency were being triggered and handled, this would be a small positive number of
rejected functions, not -1). **Both planks of my (c) discussion — "the coefficient keeps growing"
and "possibly a linear-dependency artifact in the large diffuse basis" — are weaker than I stated.**
Reading the actual death point in the log myself (tail of `irc_forward.log`): the terminal messages
are `Angle between gradients (degrees)= 55.7131`, `Maximum DWI gradient std dev = 0.362012992`,
`Delta-x Convergence NOT Met`, `Maximum number of corrector steps exceded` — all Bulirsch-Stoer
corrector-integration diagnostics, at a point where `Cartesian Forces: Max 0.004792 RMS 0.001534`
Ha/Bohr are already small (a flat region of the surface). **Nothing in the death-point text names an
electronic-structure failure.** This is a real, sharper alternative hypothesis to the one I helped
carry forward from the plan document: the IRC integrator's own tolerance is failing in a flat valley
near the path's end, independent of (possibly coincident with, but not shown to be caused by) the MO
coefficient warning — which is also present, at comparable or higher magnitude, in jobs that did NOT
fail (endpoint_prep_product ~34-36, U56_RB_scan ~20, endpoint_prep_rc_reactant ~71-79, all clean).
**On the data as it stands, "large MO coefficient" cannot be the sole explanation for which jobs die
and which don't — it's present in every job examined, at both higher and lower magnitude than the
failing case, with no fail among the higher-magnitude cases.** This narrows what I'm asking
coder14's `stable=opt` diagnostic to settle, and critic14's suggested cheaper/faster alternative
(restart from `irc_forward.chk` with `IRC(Recorrect=Never)` or a tighter/looser step size, to
isolate whether the integrator tolerance alone explains the failure) is a fair, likely cheaper
parallel test — I'd want engineer's cost read on both, but scientifically neither should be skipped:
`stable=opt` answers whether the wavefunction itself is unstable (a real chemistry question
regardless of whether it explains THIS crash); the recorrect/step-size restart answers whether the
crash is purely numerical. **Falsifiability, since critic14 asked directly**: `stable=opt` at the
flagged geometry finding an internal instability (a lower-energy solution upon following the
instability direction) would support treating this as real open-shell/near-degeneracy physics needing
systematic reoptimization; finding NO instability (the SCF is a genuine local minimum in orbital
space) would falsify "unstable wavefunction" as the explanation and point entirely to the integrator/
numerics, consistent with what the raw log's own failure text already suggests.

**(b)'s R-B "1-point, uninformative IRC" claim was incomplete, not wrong about the number of points
but wrong about what happened at that point.** I grepped `"Point Number"` and `"Normal termination"`
and missed the line that actually explains the stop. Re-checked myself, both directions:
`irc_forward.log:2703` and `irc_reverse.log:2611` both read **`PES minimum detected on this side of
the pathway.`**, immediately followed by `Reaction path calculation complete.` — this is Gaussian's
own IRC algorithm concluding it has already reached a minimum, one point (NET REACTION COORDINATE
0.18324 forward / 0.22291 reverse) after leaving the saddle in each direction. **This is a completed,
successful IRC by Gaussian's own criterion, not a truncation** — my earlier "genuinely tiny number of
points, uninformative" framing undersold it: the path is short because the barrier is narrow along
the mass-weighted reaction coordinate, which is itself a real (if unusual) result, not a failure to
finish. `05_STATE.md`'s/coder11's parser apparently doesn't match this exact G16 output string
(`minimum_found: false` in the JSON despite the log saying exactly that) — a parser bug, not a
science problem, and not mine to fix (routed to coder14 per critic14). **This changes my R-B
provisional lean, partially**: the IRC-completeness objection I raised in (b) is retracted — the
path is short but real, not truncated. The mode-character objection (Li dominates the imaginary mode
at 44%, ADR-112-shape) is UNCHANGED and still stands on its own — a narrow, low, Li-migration-coupled
barrier is consistent with either (i) a genuine very-low-barrier ion-hopping elementary step (real
chemistry SEI kMC would want to know about) or (ii) the same spectator-test coverage gap already on
record projectwide. Distinguishing (i) from (ic) needs the same GSCAN2/mapping-protocol question
already deferred to Track B item 7 — I am not resolving it here, only correcting what the IRC data
actually shows.

**Acknowledging the pattern**: this is the second time this session an under-sampled grep (head/tail
instead of the full series, or missing a specific string) produced a wrong or incomplete read that a
second reader caught by going back to the same raw file. Recording it plainly rather than quietly
fixing the text, per the project's own repeated lesson about measured-but-unread signals.

`U56_RA_scan`'s reverse arm crashed after only 5 IRC points with its B+ mid/last start points close
together and close to the saddle. **I re-derived the actual arc-length numbers from the raw logs
myself** (not taken from critic14's characterisation) to make sure the ruling is grounded in the real
data, not a restatement:

```
                  points reached   arc length reached   B+ "mid" arc   B+ "last" arc   mid-last gap
RA_scan forward   21 (idx 0-20)    6.83                 3.42 (idx 10)  6.83 (idx 20)   3.41
RA_scan reverse   6  (idx 0-5)     1.71                 0.68 (idx 2)   1.71 (idx 5)    1.02
```

Forward's B+ pair is well separated from each other (3.41 arc units) and the last point is well past
the saddle (6.83 vs a total forward reach of 6.83 — it IS the endpoint, deep into the path). Reverse's
pair is close together (1.02 arc units) and neither point is far from the saddle at all — the entire
reverse "path" barely left the TS region before the corrector failed. **Both arms report B+
`agreement: true`**, but they are not equally trustworthy: forward's agreement is evidence of a real,
distant, independently-confirmed basin; reverse's agreement could just as easily mean both terminal
optimisations relaxed back toward the SAME nearby (possibly saddle-adjacent, possibly reactant-side)
structure without ever testing whether the reverse direction actually reaches a distinct product/
reactant basin — exactly the "false agreement via basin roll-back" failure mode §39.70(2) already
worried about for the single-earliest-point case, now shown to recur in a second, worse shape:
**not "the earliest point was chosen badly" but "there weren't enough distant points to choose from
in the first place."**

**Ruling**: narrowing branch (b) to `maxpoints_reached` only (lead's first option) does not fix
this — a `maxpoints_reached` truncation after only 2-3 points would have the identical problem, and
the failure mode is about geometry (how far the available points are from the saddle and from each
other), not about why the path stopped. **The gate belongs on the B+ start points themselves, not on
the truncation cause.** Add an explicit arc-length-separation precondition to branch (b), evaluated
before B+ is trusted as establishing a connection:
- `last`'s arc length must exceed a floor distance from the saddle (point 0) — not yet a tuned
  constant; I am NOT inventing a number here (same discipline as §39.71's tolerance, which was
  derived from measured brackets, not picked). What the two real cases above show: 6.83 arc units is
  clearly enough (forward, trusted); 1.71 is clearly not (reverse, a single path essentially still at
  the saddle) — the true cutoff is somewhere in between and needs more measured cases (a handful more
  truncated IRCs at varying lengths) before it can be pinned the way §39.71 pinned its energy
  tolerance against real brackets. Until then: **any arm reaching fewer than ~10 IRC points (a round
  number chosen only to flag review, explicitly NOT the ruled threshold) should get `agreement:
  low_confidence` rather than a bare `true`/`false`**, carrying both the raw agreement result and the
  arc length reached, so a human reads it rather than the gate silently trusting it.
- `mid`-to-`last` separation should also be checked directly (not just `last`'s absolute position) —
  a long path that still picked two close-together points (possible under a different midpoint
  definition) would have the same problem.
- This is a **conservative gate** (same direction as every other gate this project has chosen when in
  doubt): it downgrades some currently-`true` verdicts to `low_confidence`, it does not manufacture
  new `false` verdicts, and it does not touch `maxpoints_reached` cases whose last point is already
  far along (no regression for the well-behaved case).

**Consequence for R-A specifically**: `U56_RA_scan`'s FORWARD arm's B+ agreement stands as reported
(6.83 arc units, well past the danger zone) — this does not change my provisional lean on R-A in
§39.113(a). The REVERSE arm's B+ agreement should be read as `low_confidence` pending either (i) a
longer reverse IRC (once the crash-cause diagnostic below is resolved and a rerun is possible) or
(ii) a principled floor once more truncated-IRC arc-length data exists. Not itself disqualifying —
just not yet load-bearing evidence on its own.

### (2) Track A item 2's diagnostic: build BOTH `stable=opt` and critic14's integrator-only restart

Already stated my lean to lead/critic14; making it an explicit ruling here so coder14 has a concrete
green light rather than two open options. **Both tests answer different, non-substitutable
questions**, and both are cheap (single small jobs, no full IRC rerun):

- **`stable=opt` at TWO geometries, not one**: my own re-read of the full MO-coefficient series
  (§39.113(e)) shows the value rises through the early-to-mid path then plateaus for the back half —
  a single "point right before it starts climbing past ~35" (the original Track A item 2 wording) is
  no longer a well-defined single transition given the corrected shape. Recommend: (a) an early point
  where the coefficient first stabilises after its initial rise (~point 5, arc 1.7, coefficient ~32),
  and (b) the LAST point actually computed before the crash (point 20, arc 6.83, coefficient ~38.7,
  the corrector's own failure point). Running both for barely more cost than one tells whether any
  instability found is a persistent feature of the whole back-half plateau or specific to the terminal
  region where the integrator gives up — directly relevant to whether a fix means "reoptimize the
  wavefunction at every step" (broad, expensive) or "handle the terminal region specially" (narrow).
- **critic14's `IRC(Recorrect=Never)` or altered-StepSize restart from `irc_forward.chk`**: tests the
  competing, currently better-supported-by-the-raw-log hypothesis (integrator tolerance failing in a
  flat valley, not an electronic-structure problem) directly and cheaply, reusing the existing
  checkpoint rather than any new DFT work beyond the restart itself.
- **Do not treat either as a substitute for the other.** `stable=opt` finding no instability would
  falsify "unstable wavefunction" as an explanation (per the falsifiability statement in §39.113(e))
  but would NOT by itself confirm the integrator-tolerance hypothesis — that needs the restart to
  actually show the path can be walked further under different integration settings. Symmetrically, a
  successful restart would show the crash is avoidable numerically but would not by itself rule out a
  real (if not currently disqualifying) electronic-structure quirk worth knowing about for other jobs
  in this class (e.g. the higher-magnitude `rc_reactant` case in §39.113(c)).

Routing cost/scheduling of both to engineer; the scientific case for running both rather than
choosing is made above and does not change with price — if budget genuinely forces a choice, that's
engineer's/lead's call to make explicitly, not mine to pre-empt by silently dropping one.

### (3) 🔴 Two implementation corrections to (1), caught by critic14 reading the code, not just the ruling

**(a) The trap.** `guards.py:200` reads `bplus.get("agreement") is True`. As I originally wrote (1),
a natural (and wrong) implementation would keep `agreement: true` and add a sibling `confidence:
"low"` field — which guards would never read, so branch (b) would still fire off RA_scan's reverse
arm exactly as before. **Ruling, stated explicitly so this can't be implemented the harmless-looking
way**: in the low-confidence case, `agreement` itself MUST become something other than bare `True` —
either `None`/absent (matching the existing "an unrun comparison is not an agreement" convention
already used for `too_few_points`) or the gate must read the arc-length/separation fields directly
before trusting `agreement`, not after. Do not add a field nobody reads — same defect shape as the
`rcfc` `copied` flag, `cores_observed`, `forward_rc`/`reverse_rc`, all already found and fixed this
project by exactly this mistake once each.

**(b) The convention.** My arc-length table in (1) counted G16's own `Point Number` labels, which
INCLUDE the saddle as point 0 (RA_scan forward: points 0-20, 21 total; reverse: points 0-5, 6 total).
`parse_irc_path_frames` — the function that will actually feed whatever gate gets built — returns
frame counts that do NOT include the saddle (20 and 5 respectively, per critic14's read of the
parser). The two countings agree on which geometries exist, they disagree on the number attached to
them by one. **Whatever threshold eventually gets pinned (still not ruled — see (1), pending more
measured cases) must state which convention it's expressed in** — `parse_irc_path_frames`'s frame
count (saddle excluded), not raw `Point Number` (saddle included) — since that's the count the gate
will actually see. Recording this now so the eventual number isn't picked against one convention and
implemented against the other.

**Reported to**: team-lead, critic14 (confirms and adopts both corrections), coder14 (both are
build-time requirements on whatever implements (1), not optional).

geometry, because this one touches an ALREADY-ISSUED certificate, not an open TS search

critic14 independently re-derived (not took from me) the one number in §39.113(e) they hadn't measured

`Normal termination`, `n_imag=0`, C-8 certified. This is the single largest MO-coefficient magnitude
anywhere in the returned tree, roughly double `U56_RA_scan`'s failing plateau (38.4-38.7) — and it
belongs to a job that PASSED, not one that crashed.

**Why this is a different question from Track A item 2, not a bigger version of the same one**: item
2 asks "did an unstable wavefunction kill this IRC" — a question about a candidate TS still being
evaluated, no standing claim depends on the answer either way yet. This one asks **"does a Hessian
this project already certified and is treating as a satisfied precondition (`endpoint_prep_rc_reactant`
is R-C's reactant cert, feeding U56-2's still-to-come R-C wave) stand on a wavefunction C-8's own
checks (n_imag==0, normal termination) cannot see"** — Track B item 4 already asked, in general terms,
whether any certified result should be revisited; this is the concrete case that question was asking
about, now with a number in hand.

**Ruling**: add `endpoint_prep_rc_reactant`'s tight-stage geometry as a THIRD `stable=opt` target,
kept as a SEPARATE line item on engineer's pricing list, not folded into or substituted for the 11-atom
pair in §39.114(2) — three reasons, matching critic14's framing, verified against my own read of

1. **Different cost class, unpriced**: this is the 21-atom cation+open-shell unit engineer8 explicitly
   retracted any cube-law estimate for — nobody can honestly size a follow-up (e.g. a reoptimization,
   if instability is found) for this class yet, so it should not quietly ride along inside the 11-atom
   item's budget line.
2. **Different question, independently informative**: a `stable=opt` PASS or FAIL at 11 atoms tells us
   nothing about whether the 21-atom certificate is sound — the two must both be measured, neither
   substitutes.
3. **Different stakes**: the 11-atom case affects a candidate not yet accepted as anything; the 21-atom

   for this class of system — a scope question for C-8 itself, not just this one job — and should be
   escalated the moment it's known, not batched with routine Track B closure.

**Not yet ruling** whether the certificate should actually be revoked or how C-8 should change if
instability is confirmed — that depends on the result, same as the 11-atom question, and stays with

## §39.116 🟢 RULED — `U56_RB_scan`'s completed 1-point IRC is NOT `budget`, but it is also NOT
plain `CHEMICAL` — the "minimum" reached is structurally indistinguishable from the saddle itself

critic14 ran `guards.irc_direction_ok` against the real data (post their own `parse_irc_completion`
fix) and found `U56_RB_scan` forward tagged `budget` (triggered by `n_points=1 < IRC_MIN_POINTS=5`,
never consulting `minimum_found`), asked me to rule what the correct tag is since that's a C-2
question, not a plumbing one.

### (a) The `budget` tag is simply false — ruled without needing the deeper chemistry question

289 s of wall time was used; no per-attempt or per-job cap was anywhere near exhausted; the run
stopped because Gaussian's own IRC algorithm printed `PES minimum detected on this side of the
pathway.` and `Reaction path calculation complete.` — a self-declared, voluntary stop, not a
resource-exhaustion stop. `budget` asserts "the caps were too tight, spend more per attempt"; nothing
about that sentence is true here regardless of how the chemistry question below is eventually
answered. **This part of the ruling does not need to wait for anything**: `budget` is wrong on its
face and should never be applied when `minimum_found: true` and no wall/point cap was hit, independent
of which replacement tag is correct.

### (b) Before accepting critic14's tentative "`CHEMICAL`" default, checked the actual geometry myself

Read the `Input orientation` blocks at the saddle (point 0) and at the declared minimum (point 1),
both directions, directly from the raw logs — not inferred from the arc-length number alone.
**Forward, atoms 1(C)/2(O) — the declared BREAKING bond**: saddle distance 4.1330 Å, point-1 distance
4.1339 Å — a 0.0009 Å change. The other nine atoms move by comparably tiny amounts (coordinates agree
to 3-4 decimal places across every atom I checked). **This is not a structurally distinct minimum —
it is, to any chemically meaningful precision, the SAME geometry as the saddle.** Consistent with
this: `Cartesian Forces` are already tiny (Max 0.00011-0.00016, RMS 0.00004-0.00006 Ha/Bohr) at every
printed point in this log, including the very first — the whole region around this saddle is
extremely flat (consistent with the mode's own softness, -84.3 cm⁻¹), which is exactly the condition
under which a fixed gradient-norm "at a minimum" stopping criterion can fire almost immediately
without the path having gone anywhere. **Reading: this looks like an algorithmic artifact of applying
a fixed force-threshold minimum-detection test to an intrinsically very soft/flat coordinate, not
confirmation of a genuine, structurally distinct product or reactant basin one step from the TS.**

### (c) Ruling: neither `budget` nor plain `CHEMICAL` — a THIRD outcome, and a methods flag for future IRCs

`budget` is wrong (a); `CHEMICAL` (asserting the arm establishes a real, informative connection)
would overstate what (b) actually shows — the "minimum" is not distinguishably different from the
saddle, so this is not good evidence FOR a real narrow-barrier connection any more than it is evidence
against one. **This arm should be tagged as its own kind of indeterminate** (not `engine` either —
§39.69's definition is specifically about failure to complete at a legitimately requested geometry,
and this job completed without failing) — call it what it is: **the IRC's own stopping criterion
fired at a geometry statistically identical to its own starting point.** If the existing vocabulary
has no slot for "declared complete, but the completion criterion was met trivially," that is itself
a gap worth naming rather than forcing this into `CHEMICAL` or `UNKNOWN` by default — routing the
exact tag name to coder14/lead since it's a classification-scheme question, but the SUBSTANCE is
ruled: **do not count this arm as C-2 "connection established" evidence, and do not count it as a
budget failure either.**

**Consequence for the `1/p` CHEMICAL denominator** (critic14's original concern): this arm should be
excluded from BOTH the `budget` numerator/denominator (a) AND from being counted as a positive
`CHEMICAL` connection (b) until further work resolves what it actually shows — counting it either way
would bias the statistic in a direction nobody has justified yet.

**Consequence for Track B item 6 (still held)**: this sharpens rather than resolves the R-B candidate
question. The mode-character objection (Li 44%, §39.113(b)) stands independently. This finding adds a
second, independent problem: the IRC "confirming" a connection next to that mode does not actually
show a distinct basin was reached. Two separate reasons to distrust this candidate now, not one —
still not finalizing the verdict per lead's hold, but the lean is unchanged (not yet acceptable) and
now has a second independent leg.

**Methods flag, separate from the R-B verdict**: if G16's default IRC minimum-detection criterion can
fire this early on a soft-mode system, other soft/floppy Li-coordinate TS attempts in this project
(R-B is not likely to be the only Li-migration-coupled saddle in the network) may be at risk of the
same false-early-stop. Worth asking whether a tighter/non-default stopping criterion for the IRC's own
minimum test is needed for this system class — a candidate addition to the GSCAN2/IRC protocol
questions already open under Track B item 7, not something I'm ruling on unilaterally here.

**Reported to**: team-lead, critic14 (structural check goes beyond what you asked, but changes the
answer — not a plain `CHEMICAL` default), coder14 (tag name TBD, but `budget` must go and `CHEMICAL`
should not simply replace it).

### (d) Addendum — critic14's independent, rotation-invariant re-derivation; precision correction; tag adopted

critic14 re-checked (b) with a stronger method than mine (centroid-removed RMSD + the full
rotation-invariant pairwise-distance set, computed within the same log so no frame-origin mismatch is
possible) and confirms the conclusion: forward translation-removed RMSD 0.0112 Å, reverse 0.0163 Å;
max pairwise-distance change 0.0203 Å (forward), 0.0228 Å (reverse) — chemically negligible either
way. **Correcting my own imprecise phrasing**: I wrote "every other atom moves by amounts comparable
to" the 0.0009 Å break-bond change — the actual largest pairwise-distance change is 0.0203 Å, about
20× that. Still negligible, conclusion unchanged, but the number in (b) was loose and the real one
belongs on record. critic14 also flagged a real trap for whoever checks this next: comparing `ts.xyz`
(the payload's own extracted structure) against the IRC log's `Input orientation` gives a spurious
0.71 Å "displacement" that is pure coordinate-origin translation, not motion — only same-frame or
rotation-invariant comparisons are valid here, worth stating plainly since it would be an easy trap
to fall into from the file names alone.

**Tag ruling: adopt `protocol`, not a new class.** critic14's match to §39.68(3)'s existing definition
("this run says something about our procedure rather than the chemistry or our caps," prescription
"fix the procedure and re-run") is exact, and the precedent shape (the unconverged-frame-0 case) is
the same failure ONE STAGE LATER in the pipeline. Ruled: `U56_RB_scan` forward gets `cause_class:
protocol`, excluded from both `CHEMICAL` and `BUDGET` denominators as already ruled in (c). Rejected
`unknown` for the reason critic14 gave: it would file a systematic, fixable defect (the IRC's own
stopping criterion needs review for soft-mode systems, per (c)'s methods flag) alongside genuinely
unmeasured cases, losing the prescription. Implementation note (relayed by critic14, confirmed
correct): `_class_from_tags` must stop appending `budget` when `minimum_found` is true BEFORE
`protocol` is added, or the combination reads as `mixed` instead of `protocol` — a sequencing
requirement, not an optional detail.

## §39.117 🟢🟢 A THIRD, independent problem with `U56_RB_scan`'s candidate — the declared breaking
bond is already fully broken AT the saddle, an ADR-112-shaped overshoot on the side the bracket check
cannot see

critic14 read `bracket_check.json` (no new spend — already-returned data) and found a third
independent line of evidence against R-B's candidate, on top of the Li-dominated mode (§39.113(b))
and the non-distinct-minimum finding (§39.116). **Verified the numbers myself, matches exactly**:

```
break:O_ether-C_carbonyl   reactant 1.4317 A -> saddle 4.1348 A   (+2.703 A)   one_sided_ok: true
mechanism:Li-O_ether       reactant 3.1133 A -> saddle 1.7880 A   (-1.325 A)   one_sided_ok: true
product side: awaiting_calibration (no certified product exists for this arm, by design)
```

**Reading**: 4.13 Å is not a bond by any convention (a C-O single bond is ~1.4 Å; 4.13 Å is not even a
loose electrostatic contact at this level) — **the declared breaking bond is already fully severed at
the saddle itself, 2.7 Å past the reactant**, and Li has already substantially completed its migration
onto the newly-freed ether oxygen (1.79 Å, well inside typical Li-O contact range) at the SAME point.
A genuine transition state for this bond-breaking step should sit somewhere between "bond intact"
(reactant, 1.43 Å) and "bond broken" (product, presumably ~3+ Å based on R-A's analogous product
distance of 3.11 Å for its own O-C bond) — not past the fully-broken endpoint already. **This candidate
looks like it has walked well past the actual saddle region into product-like geometry before the
optimizer stopped**, consistent with (and possibly the same root cause as) the extremely soft,
Li-dominated imaginary mode already flagged: a shallow, nearly-barrierless region where the
optimization can overshoot considerably before the gradient becomes small enough to satisfy TS
convergence.

**Why the bracket check passed this**: confirmed from the file's own `reasons` field, which states its
own limit plainly — "does not catch a saddle that overshoots the product and must not be read as
though it did (§39.65)." The direction-aware one-sided check refuses a BREAK coordinate only when the
saddle is SHORTER than the reactant distance (undershoot); it structurally cannot see an OVERSHOOT past
where the product would be, because no certified product exists for this arm to bound against. **This
is the exact coverage gap §39.65/§39.66 predicted, now confirmed as a LIVE instance, not a
hypothetical** — worth noting the asymmetry with ADR-112 explicitly: P1 was convicted by an overshoot
on the FORM coordinate (the side a reactant-only bound CAN catch, per §39.66's derivation); R-B has the
overshoot on the BREAK side, which the same reactant-only architecture cannot catch by construction.
Same family of pathology, opposite side of the gate's blind spot.

**Consequence, not yet a final ruling (Track B item 6 still held)**: this is now the THIRD independent
reason to distrust `U56_RB_scan`'s candidate (mode character, non-distinct IRC minimum, and now a
break-bond overshoot past product-like geometry), each found by a different method (Ω/spectator test,
direct geometry re-derivation, bracket-check reading) and each sufficient on its own to raise serious
doubt. My provisional lean strengthens further toward rejection, still held for the formal ruling.

**Consequence for the deferred product-side calibration (05_STATE.md §1's part 3, previously
"an improvement, cuttable if the round is squeezed")**: this is no longer a hypothetical gap-closing
nice-to-have — it is the SPECIFIC missing check that would have caught this SPECIFIC candidate. I am
not overriding the cuttable/not-cuttable engineering call (that's engineer's/lead's to make against a
real cost figure), but the scientific case for prioritizing it just went from "closes a theoretical
gap" to "would have flagged a real candidate we are independently rejecting anyway by three other
routes" — worth weighing that against whatever it costs, explicitly, rather than defaulting to
"cuttable" on the strength of the old framing.

**Reported to**: team-lead (priority framing for the deferred calibration), critic14 (confirms the
finding, both numbers and the ADR-112-asymmetry framing).

## §39.118 🟢 RULED — Q1: the R-A wavefunction-instability hypothesis is FALSIFIED at both probed
geometries, with one honestly-stated residual gap (the crash geometry itself was never probed)

**Status**: proposer, successor to proposer10, ruling on the returned diagnostic batch (PBS 23731675,
`cpu_machine_pilot_results/u56_diagnostics_2026-08-21/`). Read every raw `.log`/`.gjf`/`manifest.json`
under stages 1-4 directly myself before ruling — none of the numbers below are inherited from a
report.

### The falsifiability test, applied literally

proposer10's own manifest (`1_point4_arc1.71/manifest.json`, identical text in stage 2's manifest)
states the criterion in advance: *"an internal instability (G16 reports the wavefunction unstable,
reoptimises to a LOWER energy) supports real open-shell/near-degeneracy physics... NO instability
(already a genuine local minimum in orbital space) FALSIFIES 'unstable wavefunction' as the
explanation and points to the IRC integrator/numerics instead."*

Both stages returned NO instability, unambiguously:

```
                        stage 1 (arc 1.71)          stage 2 (arc 6.83)
termination             Normal (30m49s CPU)          Normal (43m41s CPU)
stable=opt verdict      "wavefunction is stable       "wavefunction is stable
                        under the perturbations       under the perturbations
                        considered" / "already        considered" / "already
                        stable"                       stable"
lowest eigenvalue       +0.1419360                    +0.1842609
<S**2> (before/after    0.7549 / 0.7500               0.7546 / 0.7500
 annihilation)                                        (ideal doublet = 0.7500)
EigRej (linear-dep.     -1.00D+00 (none rejected)     -1.00D+00 (none rejected)
 functions removed)
SCF Done                after 17 cycles               after 15 cycles
```

Both eigenvalues are clearly positive (not a marginal ~0.001 call), spin contamination is negligible
at both points, and G16's own linear-dependence safeguard found nothing to reject at either geometry.
This meets the stated criterion at face value: the wavefunction is a genuine local minimum in orbital
space at both tested points. **On the criterion as written: FALSIFIED.**

### The loophole check — three specific ones, checked against the raw data, not asserted

**(i) Is arc 6.83 the crash geometry, or a step before it?** Re-derived from `irc_forward.log` myself
(not taken from any prior summary): the log shows `Point Number: 20 ... NET REACTION COORDINATE UP TO
THIS POINT = 6.83462`, immediately followed by `Point Number 21 in FORWARD path direction.` — the walk
toward point 21 is where the actual failure lives. That segment runs through **~20 repeated corrector
sub-iterations**, each ending `Delta-x Convergence NOT Met`, with `Angle between gradients` **rising
monotonically from 31.4° to 59.4°** over those iterations, before the run dies with `Maximum number of
corrector steps exceded`. **So: the probed geometry (arc 6.83, point 20) is the LAST fully-converged,
successfully-computed IRC point — the geometry the corrector was stepping FROM, not the geometry (or
family of divergent trial geometries) it failed to reach.** The actual failure point was never
converged to any single well-defined geometry — it exists only as a diverging sequence of rejected
corrector trials — and therefore cannot be probed with `stable=opt` at all without first inventing a
geometry nobody has independently justified. Probing arc 6.83 is the closest well-defined geometry
available, and it is load-bearing for one specific sub-question — "was the wavefunction already
unstable at the point immediately upstream of the failure, in a way that could destabilize the
corrector's local finite-difference gradients" — and the answer to that sub-question is no. It is
**not** load-bearing for the broader question "is there any geometry along the attempted-but-uncomputed
path to point 21 where the wavefunction is unstable" — that remains formally unprobed. I read this as a
weak residual gap, not a live alternative hypothesis: a 28° swing in gradient angle over ~20 sub-steps
that never converge is the textbook signature of a corrector failing to track a flat/curved valley
(exactly what the death-point text names — Bulirsch-Stoer corrector diagnostics, not an SCF error), not
of an electronic structure that was fine one step ago and catastrophically unstable one step later.
Flagging it explicitly rather than silently closing it.

**(ii) Internal vs. external instability.** The route ran default `Stable=Opt` on a doublet UKS
reference; the log shows `Doing stability rather than CIS` / `Stability analysis using <AA,BB:AA,BB>
singles matrix` — this is the standard **internal** UHF-type stability test (does a lower-energy
solution exist by rotating occupied↔virtual orbitals of the same spin, within the same real-orbital
space). It does **not** test external instabilities (UHF→GHF non-collinear spin mixing, real→complex).
This is exactly the test proposer10's own criterion calls for ("reoptimises to a LOWER energy... genuine
local minimum in orbital space") — external instabilities are a different, more exotic pathology that
was never the hypothesis on the table. Real gap, correctly scoped, does not weaken the falsification.

**(iii) `stable=opt` at a doublet — right matrix?** Yes: `<AA,BB:AA,BB>` is precisely the UHF-type
combination needed for an open-shell (multiplicity 2) reference; an RHF-type matrix would have been the
wrong tool. No gap here.

### Verdict

**FALSIFIED** for the two tested geometries, on the criterion as proposer10 stated it in advance. The
one honest residual gap (i) does not reopen the wavefunction hypothesis — it narrows what remains
unknown to a geometry that was never computed to convergence in the first place, and the death-point
diagnostics (escalating gradient-angle mismatch, Bulirsch-Stoer-specific error text) already pointed
away from an electronic-structure cause before this diagnostic ran. The integrator/numerics hypothesis
is now the only one with any positive support; see §39.121 (Q4) for why that is not yet "confirmed."

## §39.119 🟢 RULED — Q2: large MO coefficients are the expected signature of a diffuse basis
approaching (not crossing) linear dependence; benign for energies/gradients on the evidence measured
so far

### Physical reading

All three probed geometries — the two 11-atom RA_scan IRC points and the 21-atom rc_reactant tight
geometry (before its SCF was interrupted, see §39.120) — show **`EigRej = -1.00D+00`**, G16's own flag
that zero AO basis functions were removed at its numerical linear-dependence threshold (1.00D-06). At
the same time, `EigKep` (the smallest eigenvalue of the AO overlap matrix actually kept) **shrinks with
system size**: ~4.2-4.5×10⁻⁵ at 173 basis functions (11 atoms) vs. **1.06×10⁻⁵** at 334 basis functions
(21 atoms, the certified rc_reactant geometry — the highest-magnitude MO-coefficient case in the whole
returned tree). This is a consistent, coherent picture, not two disconnected facts: `def2-SVPD` is a
triply-augmented diffuse basis; as more diffuse-shell-bearing atoms (O lone pairs, Li's diffuse p
shells) sit near each other at typical bonding/coordination distances, the AO overlap matrix
accumulates more near-redundant combinations (smaller minimum eigenvalues), without yet crossing the
threshold that would force G16 to discard functions. **A large "largest MO coefficient" warning is
exactly the numerical symptom of this**: when two AOs are nearly linearly dependent, representing a
smooth physical density in that subspace requires large, nearly-cancelling coefficients on the two
near-redundant functions — a basis-representation artifact of how the density is expressed, not a
statement about the electronic structure itself.

**Why I read it as benign here, not just plausible in general** — three independent pieces of evidence,
all measured, none asserted:
1. `EigRej=-1` at every geometry checked (11-atom ×2, 21-atom ×1) — G16's own safeguard was never
   triggered.
2. `stable=opt` found no internal instability at either 11-atom point carrying this signature (§39.118)
   — large coefficients did not correlate with an unstable wavefunction at the two points tested.
3. Spin contamination stays at the ideal doublet value (`<S**2>` 0.7546-0.7549 vs. 0.7500 ideal) at
   both 11-atom points — no sign of a genuine near-degeneracy/spin-symmetry-breaking pathology, which
   is the other thing a large coefficient could in principle indicate.

`critic14`'s prior finding (already on record, §39.113(e)/`05_STATE.md`) that this magnitude does not
discriminate pass from fail — present in the certified `endpoint_prep_product`, present at the highest
magnitude in the certified `rc_reactant`, present at low magnitude in `RB_scan` which terminates fine —
is fully consistent with this reading: a basis-conditioning artifact correlating loosely with
charge/open-shell character (§39.113(c)'s own observation) and diffuse-shell proximity, appearing in
passing and failing jobs alike, is exactly what a benign artifact should look like. A real
discriminating chemistry signal would be expected to track which jobs die, not appear uniformly.

### What would falsify this reading

1. `EigRej` crossing from `-1` to a positive rejected-function count at these or nearby geometries
   (redundancy actually triggering G16's safeguard rather than merely approaching it).
2. A `stable=opt` internal instability appearing at a large-coefficient geometry — would mean the large
   coefficients are compensating for/masking a real lower-energy solution, not just basis linear
   algebra. (Not yet observed at either 11-atom point tested; genuinely open at the 21-atom point, see
   §39.120.)
3. Guess-dependence: the SAME geometry converging to different SCF energies/densities from different
   initial guesses. Not tested by anything in this batch — flagging as the natural next falsification
   probe if this reading is ever doubted, not ordering it now (no evidence currently calls for it).
4. Energy/gradient discontinuities (kinks) along a scanned coordinate that track coefficient magnitude
   rather than nuclear geometry. Not independently re-derived by me here — I am relying on
   `05_STATE.md`/§39.113(e)'s prior finding (66/66 SCF cycles converged, zero convergence failures in
   the RA_scan IRC) rather than re-checking energy smoothness myself; flagging this as inherited, not
   freshly verified, per this project's own discipline about attributing claims correctly.

### Does this change C-8's certification criteria?

**Not on this evidence, not yet.** The reading is now well-supported for the 11-atom regime (both
tested points: EigRej=-1, no instability, ideal spin) and directionally supportive but **not proven**
for the 21-atom cation-radical regime specifically — that is exactly what stage 3 exists to close (its
partial SCF trace, discussed in §39.120, is reassuring but not a `stable=opt` verdict). C-8's criteria
(n_imag==0 + normal termination) stay as currently defined pending stage 3's actual result. If stage 3
returns unstable, this ruling and C-8's sufficiency both need revisiting together — see §39.120.

**Reported to**: team-lead, critic (independent re-verification of the EigRej/EigKep numbers requested
— I pulled them directly with `grep -n "EigRej\|NBasis"` against all three raw logs, but a second
reader should confirm before this is treated as settled).

## §39.120 🟢 RULED — Q3: stage 3 (`endpoint_prep_rc_reactant`'s 21-atom cation-radical) still MUST
RUN — it answers an independent, higher-stakes question that stages 1/2 cannot answer for it

### What actually happened to stage 3, read from the raw log myself

Stage 3 was **not** a computational failure of any kind — it was killed by the shared job's walltime
(`7244s` elapsed against a `7200s`/2h limit) while its SCF was progressing completely normally. The
tail of `stability_probe.log` shows Cycle 7 converging cleanly (`DIIS: error= 1.19D-04`, `Delta-E=
-0.000167553296`, monotonically decreasing) and Cycle 8 beginning (`E= ...-691.712078713649`) when the
job was cut off. `EigRej=-1.00D+00` was already recorded (printed early, at basis-diagonalization time,
before the SCF loop) — consistent with §39.119's reading holding at this geometry too, as far as it
goes. **This is a pure scheduling failure**: the ad-hoc `submit_diagnostics.pbs` ran all four stages
sequentially inside one 2h walltime slot; stages 1+2 alone consumed ~74.5 minutes (30m49s + 43m41s CPU
on 1 core, this route being essentially serial), leaving only ~45 minutes for a 21-atom job whose own
per-stage timing (`03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md` §R39.78) already showed comparable single-point costs run
1.5-2.8 core-h — i.e., the remaining budget was never going to be enough, and this was foreseeable from
the pricing already on record before the job was submitted this way.

### Does stages 1/2's stable result transfer to the 21-atom case? No — three real differences, not one

1. **Different molecule.** `rc_reactant` is R-C's 21-atom cation-radical reactant, not an R-A 11-atom
   TS-chain geometry — different bonding pattern, different charge state entirely (cation-radical vs.
   the neutral-radical-derived doublet probed in stages 1/2).
2. **2× the coefficient magnitude, in a regime that does not scale with atom count.** §39.113(c)'s own
   measurement: `rc_reactant` sits at ~71-79, roughly double RA_scan's failing plateau (~38-39), despite
   RA_scan being an 11-atom system and `rc_reactant` a 21-atom one — magnitude tracks
   charge/open-shell character more than size (already established, not re-derived here). This means
   the 21-atom case is not a scaled-up version of what stages 1/2 tested; it sits in a genuinely more
   extreme regime on the one axis this whole diagnostic is about.
3. **Different stakes** (already ruled in §39.115, restated because it is the reason stage 3 cannot be
   skipped): this is an ALREADY-CERTIFIED result (C-8 passed: n_imag=0, normal termination) being relied
   upon as R-C's satisfied precondition for the whole future R-C wave, not an open TS candidate nobody
   has committed to yet.

The partial SCF trace obtained before the kill (clean, converging, EigRej=-1) is **reassuring but not
a substitute for the actual test**: it only confirms the ground-state SCF converges cleanly — which was
already implicitly known, since the original `endpoint_prep_rc_reactant` job completed its own
opt/freq/certification under exactly this SCF. It does **not** test whether an internal, lower-energy
solution exists (the `stable=opt` question), which is the one thing stage 3 was built to answer and the
one thing nothing else in the returned tree answers.

### Decision-relevance framing (per the user's explicit ask)

- **If stage 3 returns UNSTABLE**: this would be the first positive instability finding anywhere in
  this diagnostic batch, at the single highest-magnitude case in the project, on a job C-8 has already
  certified and that R-C's wave is already treating as a satisfied precondition. This directly reopens
  whether C-8's criteria (n_imag==0 + normal termination only, no SCF-quality check) are sufficient for
  cation+open-shell chemistry as a **class** — not just this one job — with knock-on consequences for
  (a) whether `rc_reactant`'s certificate itself should be revoked or requires reoptimization at a
  lower-energy solution, (b) T21-se's already-flagged completion risk (§39.113(c): if this scales, a
  21-atom cation-radical TS search is likely to hit the same or worse instability), and (c) whether
  other already-certified endpoints in this project's cation/open-shell class need re-examination.
- **If stage 3 returns STABLE**: closes the loophole §39.115 raised cleanly for this one job, extends
  §39.119's benign-diffuse-basis reading to its most extreme measured case, and removes the single
  strongest reason to distrust any C-8 certificate in this batch. It does **not** prove the reading
  generalizes beyond n=1 data point at 21 atoms — a single stable result at the highest-magnitude case
  is strong but not exhaustive evidence.

**Verdict: MUST RUN.** Resubmit as its own job with a walltime sized to the actual cost estimate already
on record (§R39.78: 3-30 core-h at 1 core, i.e. 3-30h wall at 1 core; engineer's own suggestion to run
at 4-8 cores to bring worst-case wall under ~8h is sound and I have no scientific objection to it). Do
not re-bundle with any other stage in one shared walltime slot — that is what caused this round's
failure and is entirely avoidable.

**Reported to**: team-lead (resubmission priority — this is the escalation-priority item from §39.115,
now doubly justified since it's also the only remaining unanswered half of Q1/Q2), engineer (re-pricing
not needed, §R39.78's estimate stands; only the scheduling/bundling needs to change).

## §39.121 🟢 RULED — Q4: stage 4 (`irc=(restart,recorrect=never)`) is now the single load-bearing
test for the surviving hypothesis, and priority went UP, not down

### Why "surviving by elimination" is not "confirmed" — restating §39.114(2)'s own prior ruling, now
applicable

§39.114(2) already stated this in advance, before any diagnostic data existed: *"`stable=opt` finding no
instability would falsify 'unstable wavefunction' as an explanation... but would NOT by itself confirm
the integrator-tolerance hypothesis — that needs the restart to actually show the path can be walked
further under different integration settings."* §39.118 (Q1) has now delivered exactly that half: no
instability at either tested geometry. The integrator/numerics hypothesis is the only one left with any
positive support (the death-point text itself — Bulirsch-Stoer corrector diagnostics, escalating
gradient-angle mismatch — always pointed this way, per critic14's original re-read in §39.113(e)), but
it has never been **positively tested**, only left standing after its competitor was ruled out. Stage 4
is the one test in this batch that would actually demonstrate it, not just fail to rule it out.

### Stage 4's actual status: never started, not degraded, not partially informative

Confirmed directly: `4_irc_recorrect_restart/` contains only the pre-staged checkpoint
(`irc_forward_recorrect_probe.chk`, a copy of the original `irc_forward.chk`, same timestamp as the
manifest) and the `.gjf`/`manifest.json` — no `.log` file exists, and the job's own stderr
(`sei_u56_diagnostics.e23731675`) shows the batch never reached the `=== 4_irc_recorrect_restart ===`
echo line before being killed. This is a pure scheduling gap, identical in kind to stage 3's (§39.120)
— not a result of any kind, not even a partial one.

### What a success vs. a repeat-crash would each mean

- **Success** (the restart walks past point 20/arc 6.83 and reaches new points, up to ~10 more per
  `maxpoints=30` minus ~20 already stored): direct, positive evidence the crash was a Bulirsch-Stoer
  corrector-tolerance failure in a flat valley, not a chemistry problem. R-A's forward IRC becomes
  extensible/completable with a numerics fix; the wavefunction question is closed for R-A's IRC crash
  specifically (Q1 already closed it for the two tested geometries; a successful restart would close it
  for the mechanism of the crash itself, which is the piece Q1 alone cannot reach per the residual gap
  in §39.118(i)).
- **Repeat-crash under `recorrect=never` specifically**: this would be genuinely uncomfortable, and
  worth stating plainly rather than softening. It does **not** resurrect the wavefunction hypothesis —
  that stays falsified at the two geometries actually tested — but it would mean neither leading
  hypothesis explains the crash cleanly as tested so far. Three live possibilities would remain, none
  yet distinguished: (a) the true problem sits at the specific unprobed geometry §39.118(i) flagged
  (never characterized, since the corrector never converged to it); (b) an integrator problem NOT fixed
  by `recorrect=never` specifically — needing a different `StepSize` instead, per §39.114(2)'s original
  menu of untried options; (c) something not yet hypothesized at all.

### Would a repeat-crash leave R-A's TS candidate worse off than today? Yes, specifically on one axis

It would **not** undo any of the independent evidence already accepted for `U56_RA_scan` (Ω=0.839,
spectator test passes, B+ forward agreement at arc 6.83, per §39.113(a) and now RULE NOW in §39.122) —
none of that depends on the IRC completing past point 20. But it would elevate "why does this IRC die"
from a side question, currently treated as an unexplained-but-probably-benign numerics quirk, to an
**unresolved anomaly sitting directly on top of this project's strongest TS candidate** with two
explanatory attempts both having failed. Concretely: nobody would yet have seen R-A's forward reaction
path walk cleanly to a genuine, independently confirmed product basin — the acceptance of
`U56_RA_scan` currently rests on B+ terminal optimizations from truncated-path points, which is exactly
the kind of evidence §39.114(1)'s arc-length-separation gate exists to be cautious about. This matters
directly for U-56a's closure question — see §39.123 (Q6).

### Verdict

**MUST RUN**, and now the **highest-priority remaining diagnostic** in this batch — no longer one of
two parallel, non-substitutable hypotheses (§39.114(2)'s original framing) but the last standing
positive-evidence candidate for explaining a crash that sits under the project's best TS attempt.
Resubmit as its own job, separately walltimed from stages 1-3 (same scheduling fix as §39.120), route
already built and `[NEEDS VERIFICATION]`-flagged for syntax only (no G16 available off-cluster to
smoke-test `irc=(restart,...)` + `geom=check guess=read` before now) — a malformed route fails at
near-zero cost, same as any other route-smoke rejection this project already treats as informative.

**Reported to**: team-lead (resubmission priority, now above stage 3 in urgency though both should run),
engineer (§R39.78's cost estimate for item 4 stands, ~1.92 core-h/point × up to 10 new points at most —
cheap either way).

## §39.123 🟢 RULED — Q6: stable-wavefunction result modestly STRENGTHENS R-A's candidate; U-56a's
closure does not depend on either stage 3 or stage 4

### Effect on R-A's candidate

**Strengthens, modestly, by removing one specific residual doubt — does not newly prove anything.**
The Ω/spectator/bracket/B+ evidence for `U56_RA_scan` (§39.113(a)) was already independent of the
SCF-instability question; today's result does not add new positive evidence on that axis. What it does
remove is a specific worry that could have undercut the forward arm's B+ evidence: B+'s "last" start
point (arc 6.83) is the same geometry probed in stage 2, and that geometry is now independently shown
to be a genuine local minimum in orbital space, not one sitting under an unresolved electronic-structure
flag. The B+ agreement measured there now rests on a geometry confirmed well-behaved, not merely
assumed so. This is real but narrow: it answers "was the reference geometry electronically sound," not
"does the reaction path actually connect to a genuine product basin past point 20" — that second
question is exactly what stage 4 (§39.121) would answer, and remains open.

### Does U-56a's closure require stage 3 and/or stage 4?

**No — U-56a is a binary feasibility gate keyed to R-A's endpoint certifications (ADR-109), and those
are already certified.** Per `05_STATE.md` §2: *"`endpoint_prep_product` (R-A product cert, 11-atom...)
GATE-CRITICAL — this is what actually closes U-56a."* That certification is independent of whether
`U56_RA_scan`'s TS candidate is ultimately accepted, and independent of whether its IRC crash is ever
explained — U-56a asks "is it feasible to start S3 production on this reaction class," not "has a
specific TS attempt succeeded." Neither stage 3 (a different reaction, R-C's reactant, feeding R-C's
wave, not R-A's) nor stage 4 (explains a crash mechanism, does not certify or decertify an endpoint)
touches U-56a's own gating input directly.

**One indirect, conditional risk worth naming plainly, not burying**: if stage 3 returns unstable
(§39.120), that would raise a live question about whether C-8's certification criteria are sufficient
for cation+open-shell chemistry as a class — and while R-A's own certified endpoints carry lower
MO-coefficient magnitude (~20/~36) than `rc_reactant`'s outlier (~71-79) and were not flagged as
escalation-priority in §39.115, a class-level finding about C-8's sufficiency would not stop cleanly at
R-C's boundary; it could in principle reopen whether R-A's own certificates should be re-examined too.
This is a second-order, conditional risk (contingent on stage 3's result, not yet realized) — **U-56a's
current closure is not conditioned on it today**, but the lead should track this dependency explicitly
rather than treat U-56a as permanently settled independent of what stage 3 finds.

**Reported to**: team-lead (U-56a status: closed on current evidence, one conditional risk flagged
explicitly for tracking, not for reopening now), critic (independent check on the "GATE-CRITICAL" quote
against `05_STATE.md` requested — I am relying on that document's own framing of what closes U-56a
rather than re-deriving ADR-109's scope myself from scratch).

🔴🔴 **SUPERSEDED, 2026-08-22, by ADR-116's same-day retraction (`05_STATE.md` §1e).** "Does U-56a's
closure require stage 3 and/or stage 4?" above is answered **wrong**: it treated endpoint certification

## §39.124 🟢 RULED — U-56a condition 7, reverse arm: re-derived cause of `low_confidence`, three
candidate protocols to lift it (one rejected), and a program-evaluable acceptance criterion (R-9)

**Status**: proposer12, fresh spawn, 2026-08-22. Everything below is re-derived directly from primary
sources (`irc_completion_reverse.json`, `irc_reverse.log`, `bplus_reverse.json`, the four B+
`.xyz`/`.log` files, `guards.py`) — not inherited from any summary, per the lead's explicit
instruction. Answers `05_STATE.md` §1e/§5 R-9: *"the reverse arm needs a longer or redone IRC to lift
`low_confidence`, unscheduled, unpriced."*

### (1) What actually causes `low_confidence` — re-derived, not inherited

**The arc-length table, read directly from `irc_reverse.log` (grep'd myself, not copied from
§39.114(1)):**

```
                  points reached   arc length reached   B+ "mid" arc   B+ "last" arc   mid-last gap
RA_scan reverse   6 (idx 0-5)      1.70584              0.68385 (idx 2) 1.70584 (idx 5) 1.02199
```

This reproduces §39.114(1)'s "~1.0 arc-length" figure to the fourth decimal (1.02199, not the
second-hand "~1.0") — confirmed independently, not restated. `bplus_reverse.json`: `agreement: true`,
`energy_delta_ev: 0.0001268`, well inside the 0.001 eV tolerance; both `bplus_reverse_mid.log` and
`bplus_reverse_last.log` show genuine `Optimization completed. Stationary point found.` under
`opt=(loose,maxcycles=100)` — this is a real, converged (at loose tolerance) agreement, not a stalled
job.

**Direct code trace (`guards.py:48-70,161-336`), confirming the mechanism, not just the symptom**:
`BPLUS_LOW_CONFIDENCE_MIN_POINTS = 10` (already ruled §39.114(1)(3), NOT a value I am re-deriving).
`parse_irc_path_frames` convention excludes the saddle point, giving `n = 5` for the reverse arm
(points 1-5; point 0 is the saddle). `5 < 10` → `bplus_low_confidence = True` →
`bplus_agreement_effective` is downgraded from the raw `True` to the string `"low_confidence"` — and
critically, this downgrade happens **before** the `elif completion.get("truncated") and
bplus_agreement_effective is True:` branch that would set `connection_established_via = "b: ..."`. So
`connection_established_via` is **never set** for the reverse arm today: not "set but low-confidence",
literally absent. I traced the forward arm the same way for contrast: `n = 20 ≥ 10`, no downgrade,
`connection_established_via = "b: maxpoints + B+ agreement"` **is** set. This is the direct, code-level
mechanism behind the state doc's prose, confirmed by reading the function, not assumed from its
comments.

**Three findings beyond what's already on record, all from primary sources I read myself:**

**(a) The reverse crash is a genuine engine crash, not a `maxpoints` stop — and it shares forward's
exact terminal signature.** `irc_completion_reverse.json`: `maxpoints_reached: false`,
`normal_termination: false` (an actual `Error termination via Lnk1e`, not G16 exiting cleanly at its
point cap — `irc_reverse.gjf` requested `maxpoints=30`, the run died at point 6, nowhere near it).
Grepping `Angle between gradients (degrees)` in both logs: **forward** climbs 31.4°→52.0° over its
first ~7 failed corrector sub-iterations, then **plateaus into an oscillating band, 55.1-59.4°**, for
its last ~12 sub-iterations before `Maximum number of corrector steps exceded`. **Reverse** jumps
straight to 48.9°/59.7° on its *very first* failed sub-iteration and immediately settles into an
oscillating band, **51.8-58.9°**, for all ~15 of its sub-iterations before the identical death message.
Both arms die in the same narrow band (~52-59°) via the same Bulirsch-Stoer corrector diagnostic — a
genuinely new observation (§39.113(e)'s own self-correction already found forward's MO-coefficient
series *plateaus rather than growing*; this shows the **gradient-angle** series does the same thing,
in both directions, previously undocumented). Reverse skips forward's initial escalation and starts
already inside the failure band — consistent with the reverse path being intrinsically closer to
whatever geometric feature triggers the limit cycle, but this is a hypothesis, not yet tested.

**(b) The current B+ comparator would likely have called this "agreement" almost regardless of how far
apart the two points were — because the near-reactant surface is measurably flat along the
comparison's own decisive coordinate.** I read the actual `.xyz` geometries (`reactant_certified.xyz`,
`bplus_reverse_mid.xyz`, `bplus_reverse_last.xyz`) and measured the declared breaking bond
(O(index 1)-C(index 2), the same pair `ts_acceptance.json`'s Ω calculation uses):

```
reactant_certified   O-C = 1.4143 Å
bplus_reverse_last   O-C = 1.4364 Å   (Δ from reactant = 0.022 Å)
bplus_reverse_mid    O-C = 1.6111 Å   (Δ from reactant = 0.197 Å)
TS (ts.xyz)          O-C = 1.7286 Å
```

`last` (arc 1.71, closest to the crash point) sits close to the certified reactant. `mid` (arc 0.68,
closer to the saddle) sits **0.17 Å further out** — nearly a fifth of the total break-bond range being
probed — yet the two optimizations agree to 0.000127 eV. Both converged genuinely (I read the `Item`
convergence tables directly, not just the `Optimization completed` line: max/RMS force both under
the loose thresholds at both points). This means the reactant-side PES is close to flat along this
coordinate at `opt=loose` tolerances over at least a 0.17 Å range — so an "agreement: true" verdict
here carries less discriminating power than the same verdict on forward, where mid/last differ by
0.40 Å (2.33 vs 2.73 Å) in unambiguously product-like territory. **This is not evidence the reverse
arm is wrong** — `last` matches the reactant to 0.022 Å, which is reassuring — but it is evidence that
`mid` may not have fully relaxed under loose convergence, and that the graph+energy-only comparator
cannot currently distinguish "both points really are in the same basin" from "the local surface is too
flat for this comparator to tell the difference within 0.17-0.2 Å of geometric spread." Neither
possibility is ruled out by anything on record.

**(c) A gap between the ruled spec and the shipped code, found by grepping, not by inference.**
§39.32(g) condition 7's own text (line 11522-11523 above) requires: *"in both branches the reverse
endpoint must match the certified reactant."* `grep -rn "certified_reactant\|reactant_certified" `
across `guards.py` and `collect.py` returns **nothing** — `bplus_agreement()` (guards.py:373-467)
compares `mid` against `last` to each other; it never reads `reactant_certified.xyz` at all. This is a
genuine implementation gap against the ruled spec, not a finding about the chemistry — but it matters
here specifically because of (b): applying the literal spec text to **both** B+ start points (not just
whichever one the code currently treats as "the" reverse endpoint) would today reject `mid` (0.197 Å
from the certified reactant) on a stricter reading than `low_confidence` alone, even though `last`
passes comfortably (0.022 Å). I am not resolving which reading is correct — that is a coder/critic
build question, flagged here because any protocol I recommend must not be certified as "fixed" while
this gap is silently unaddressed.

### (2) Candidate protocols

**Candidate A — mirror the already-decided stage-4 fix onto the reverse arm**: restart from
`irc_reverse.chk` (confirmed intact: 10,342,400 bytes, same size as `irc_forward.chk`, not corrupted)
with `irc=(restart,recorrect=never)`, exactly parallel to stage 4's forward recipe.
- **Assumption**: the reverse crash shares forward's failure mechanism. Directly supported by finding
  (a) above — same oscillating gradient-angle band, same corrector diagnostic, same error message.
- **Failure direction**: if stage 4 (forward) itself repeat-crashes under `recorrect=never`, candidate
  A is very likely to fail too — these are **not independent draws** on the integrator question (see
  part (4)). Also inherits stage 4's own risk (§1e's fourth correction): `irc=restart` may silently
  drop `recorrect=never` from the checkpoint; the same post-run grep for `Recorrection delta-x
  convergence threshold:` is mandatory here too.
- **Cost class**: cheapest of the three — reuses an existing, uncorrupted checkpoint, no new SCF/IRC
  integration before the restart point.

**Candidate B — redo the reverse IRC from the certified TS geometry with a genuinely different
corrector setting** (smaller `StepSize`, or the `EulerPC` algorithm instead of G16's default
Hessian-based predictor-corrector), motivated specifically by finding (a)'s **oscillating**, not
runaway, failure pattern — a limit cycle is the textbook signature of a predictor step too large for
the local curvature, a distinct mechanism from what `recorrect=never` addresses (corrector
re-linearization behavior, not step size).
- **Assumption**: shrinking the predictor step keeps the corrector inside its convergence radius
  through whatever feature produces the ~52-59° gradient mismatch.
- **Failure direction, load-bearing for part (3)**: a smaller step size can reach `n ≥ 10` frames
  while covering **less** absolute arc-length than today's crashed 5-frame, 1.71-arc path — satisfying
  a bare point-count criterion while gaining nothing on the actual concern (distance from the saddle).
  Any acceptance criterion for this candidate must check arc-length directly, not just frame count.
- **Cost class**: a full IRC redo from the TS, not a restart — more expensive than A, no existing
  checkpoint to build on.

**Candidate C — change which points B+ starts from, not the IRC itself. REJECTED as a standalone
fix, in two variants:**
- **(i) Re-pick `mid`/`last` from the SAME already-computed 6-point truncated path** (e.g., use point
  1 instead of point 2 as "mid" to maximize the nominal gap): rejected — this cannot manufacture
  arc-length coverage that does not exist. Every point in the set is still within the same 1.71-arc,
  near-saddle window; the underlying concern (has the reverse direction gone anywhere the saddle
  itself doesn't already answer for) is untouched. This is the kind of criterion-gaming the "would it
  look any different" self-test in part (3) exists to catch, applied here to a candidate protocol
  rather than to my own acceptance criterion.
- **(ii) Source a farther point from the existing GFN2 constrained scan** (`gscan_reverse/`, already
  computed, 12 points per direction over `d(O-C)` 1.41→2.61 Å, per `gscan_verdict.json`), re-optimized
  at the TS chain's DFT level as a third, more distant B+ point: rejected for a different reason —
  `gscan_verdict.json`'s own `_protocol_status_unused` field states the pre-relaxation/mapping
  protocol behind this scan is **NOT ratified** and produces wildly different barriers (0.0216 to
  ~15 eV) depending on unresolved choices, which is precisely Track B item 7, still open (§2 below).
  Using its geometries to fix U-56a's condition 7 would import one unresolved unknown into another,
  entangling two things the project has so far kept correctly separate. **Do not use G-SCAN-2
  geometries to source B+ points until item 7 is ruled.**

**Candidate D — zero new DFT, data-already-on-disk checks. Not a substitute for A or B; run
regardless of which (if either) is chosen, and regardless of engineer's cost ceiling:**
- Re-run the *existing* `bplus_reverse_mid.xyz`/`bplus_reverse_last.xyz` geometries at **tight**
  convergence (matching C-8's own certification criteria, not `opt=loose`) to determine whether
  finding (b)'s 0.17 Å gap is a genuine nearby feature or a loose-optimization artifact. Reuses
  existing starting geometries; no new IRC integration; single reoptimization jobs.
- Implement the missing reactant-match check named in finding (c): compare `bplus_reverse_mid.xyz`/
  `bplus_reverse_last.xyz` against `reactant_certified.xyz` (covalent graph + the declared break-bond
  distance), the literal text of condition 7. This is pure post-processing on files that already
  exist — effectively free, and should not wait on A/B's cost ceiling. Routed to coder as a build
  item, not gated on engineer.

### (3) Acceptance criterion — program-evaluable, and self-tested against "would it look different"

**Primary clause (already ruled, §39.114(1)(3) — I apply it, I do not re-derive it):**
```
n_frames_reverse_new (parse_irc_path_frames convention, saddle excluded) >= BPLUS_LOW_CONFIDENCE_MIN_POINTS (10)
AND bplus.agreement is True at that path's own mid/last pair
    (covalent_graphs_match == True AND energy_delta_ev <= BPLUS_ENERGY_TOLERANCE_EV (0.001 eV))
```
Satisfying this flips `guards.py`'s `bplus_agreement_effective` from `"low_confidence"` back to `True`
and sets `connection_established_via = "b: ..."` for the reverse arm, exactly mirroring what already
happened for forward.

**Additional clause, my own ruling, new — required specifically because of candidate B's failure
direction in (2):**
```
arc_length_reached_reverse_new >= 4.27
```
No principled floor exists yet for this constant — §39.114(1) explicitly declined to invent one
("somewhere between 1.71 and 6.83... needs more measured cases"), and I am not overriding that
discipline. 4.27 is the arithmetic midpoint of the one known-insufficient case (1.71) and the one
known-sufficient case (6.83, forward, same reaction) — **`[ESTIMATE]`, interim, same status as
`BPLUS_LOW_CONFIDENCE_MIN_POINTS` itself when it was first written**: a placeholder to flag review,
not a tuned number, and it should be superseded the moment more measured truncated-IRC cases exist to
pin it properly (the same event §39.114(1) already named as the prerequisite for a real threshold).
Its only job here is to stop a step-size change from satisfying the frame-count clause while covering
less real distance than today's failure.

**Self-test, applied to my own criterion, as instructed**: *if the reverse arm satisfied both clauses
above, but the two terminal optimizations had actually rolled back into the same near-saddle structure
rather than reaching a genuinely distinct basin, would this criterion look any different?* **Partially,
not fully.** Ten frames spanning ≥4.27 arc units is harder to fake by basin roll-back than five frames
spanning 1.71 — but it does not reach certainty: R-1/R-2 (already on record, `05_STATE.md` §5) name the
exact residual risk — B+ only catches a bifurcation *between* its two sampled points, never one past
the last sampled point, and this criterion does nothing to close that gap; it only brings the reverse
arm's residual risk down to **parity with forward's already-accepted level**, not to zero. State it
that way when this closes, not as "resolved." **Separately, this criterion does not by itself close
finding (c)'s gap** (no `reactant_certified.xyz` comparison exists in code) or finding (b)'s flatness
concern — Candidate D's checks should run and be read before the reverse arm is reported as full
confidence, even after the primary+additional clauses above are satisfied.

### (4) Interaction with the untested integrator hypothesis — flagged as instructed

Finding (a) is the load-bearing point here: forward and reverse do not just share a diagnosis by
label ("integrator/numerics"), they share the **same measured failure signature** (an oscillating
gradient-angle band in the Bulirsch-Stoer corrector, same terminal error). This means candidate A
(mirroring stage 4 onto reverse) and stage 4 itself are **not independent tests** of the integrator
hypothesis, even though ADR-117 correctly keeps them as separate PBS jobs for **wall-budget isolation**
(one overrunning must not starve the other — a resource-isolation ruling, unaffected by anything
here). They are, however, strongly correlated draws on the *same* underlying question in
**inference space**.

**Sequencing ruling**: run stage 4 (forward, already staged and decided) first; read its result before
committing core-h to any reverse-arm restart.
- **If stage 4 succeeds** (forward walks past point 20 under `recorrect=never`): candidate A on
  reverse has a high prior of also succeeding — try it before candidate B.
- **If stage 4 repeat-crashes**: candidate A on reverse is unlikely to succeed for the same reason —
  go directly to candidate B (a genuinely different fix: `StepSize`, not `recorrect`) rather than
  re-running A on reverse "to see," which would spend core-h repeating a fix already shown not to work
  on the same mechanism in the same molecule.

This is the same "measured but not read" defect class already logged 7+ times this project
(`05_STATE.md` §4's standing engineering rules), applied prospectively here rather than caught after
the fact: stage 4's result is genuine Bayesian evidence about candidate A's prospects, and treating the
two as scientifically unrelated just because they are administratively separate jobs would waste a
round trip.

### Secondary — Track B item 7 (G-SCAN-2 pre-relaxation protocol): naming what would resolve it

**Not attempting to resolve it** (ADR-116: "not resolvable on present data"). The specific measurement
that would resolve it: `gscan_verdict.json`'s own `_protocol_status_unused` field already shows the
G-SCAN-2 verdict is protocol-dependent to an extreme degree on the SAME reaction (R-A) — raw geometry
gives ΔE_barrier ≈ 0.0216 eV (matches the accepted n=1 value), a free pre-optimization gives ~15 eV
(the ring-closed basin is abandoned entirely), a constrained pre-optimization at the reactant's own
break-distance gives ~73 eV — three protocol choices, three results spanning four orders of magnitude,
with no external check to prefer one. What is missing is not another self-consistency run (frame0/
`fired` checks, already run under every variant above and passing or failing independent of which is
"correct") but an **external anchor**: a short, explicitly 2-D relaxed scan or constrained
optimization over **both** the C-O break coordinate **and** the Li-O(ether) distance simultaneously
for R-A, checked against the barrier height and geometry of the **already-accepted** `U56_RA_scan` TS
(Ω = 0.839, ω = -1153.2 cm⁻¹, independently verified, §39.113(a)/§39.122) — a fixed point the protocol
choice must reproduce, rather than being tuned to satisfy only its own internal consistency tests.
Whichever Li-coordinate treatment (frozen at reactant position / freely relaxed / intermediate
constraint) reproduces that already-known answer is the one the mapping protocol should declare. This
is a scheduling/pricing item for engineer, not a ruling — flagged here only so item 7 has a concrete,
boundable next step instead of sitting as an open-ended hold.

**Reported to**: team-lead (ruling above), engineer13 (candidate list + cost-relevant caveats, sent
directly per protocol before this write-up was complete), critic (the code-vs-spec gap in finding (c)
and the arc-length-floor `[ESTIMATE]` in (3) both need independent verification before either is
treated as settled).

### Addendum — Candidate A's `maxpoints` target, ruled after engineer13's pricing (§R39.81)

Priced against `03_COMPUTE_PLAN.md` §R39.81: all of A/B/D come in at 2-2.4% of the ~8,240 core-h
margin even combined at their most expensive plausible branch, and none is near ADR-114's 48h wall
cap. **Cost is confirmed non-binding for this decision** (engineer13's own conclusion, independently
reached). Engineer13 sized Candidate A's restart to `maxpoints=15` (9 new points beyond the 6 already
stored, targeting arc ≈5.1 / n≈14 frames — comfortably past the (3) floor of arc≥4.27/n≥10) and asked
whether that target is right or whether I want something else.

**Ruling: set `maxpoints=30`, matching the ORIGINAL reverse route's cap (`irc_reverse.gjf:4`), not
15.** Two reasons, both scientific, neither about cost:
1. **A genuine PES-minimum stop (branch (a), G16 declaring `PES minimum detected on this side` — the
   same self-declared stop `U56_RB_scan` produced, §39.116) is strictly stronger evidence than
   hitting my own interim arc/frame floor and falling back to branch (b) + B+.** My floor in (3)
   explicitly does not close the R-1/R-2 residual risk (a bifurcation past the last sampled point is
   invisible to B+, whatever the floor). A run that is allowed to keep going past the floor, if it is
   genuinely still descending, has a real chance at reaching a true minimum instead — categorically
   better evidence, and free to attempt since cost isn't limiting.
2. **The arc/point rate engineer13 independently re-derived (0.34117 reverse / 0.34173 forward,
   essentially identical) was measured under the ORIGINAL corrector settings, pre-crash — there is no
   guarantee `recorrect=never` preserves that rate.** A tight cap sized to just clear the floor at the
   OLD rate risks undershooting it if the new corrector behavior takes smaller steps, which would cost
   a full extra round trip (~3.5 calendar days per `RT-N`, per the glossary) to fix — a real cost,
   just not a core-h one, and the one cost axis engineer13's analysis didn't price. A generous cap
   avoids this without spending anything, since the run stops on its own (minimum found, or a repeat
   crash, whichever comes first) — `maxpoints=30` is a ceiling, not a target the run is forced to
   walk to.

No cost re-derivation needed from engineer13 for this change — worst case is 24 new points instead of
9, i.e. ≤~87 core-h stays the same order-of-magnitude ceiling I already gave them (their own quoted
worst case for `maxpoints=15` was 32.7 core-h for 9 points at 3.63 core-h/point; 24 points at the same
rate is ≤~87 core-h, already stated to engineer13 and confirmed by them as trivial against the
8,240 core-h margin). If the crash-mode rate turns out to differ materially once this actually runs,
that is new data, not a re-pricing of this ruling.

**Reported to**: engineer13 (this maxpoints ruling, direct reply), team-lead (folded into the same
thread).

**Ruling 1 — reactant-match tolerance, on the declared break bond, sourced two ways.**
```

```
Bracket: same-basin cases measured at 0.0002-0.0005 Å; the one different-basin case on record

better-grounded one; supersede if a third measured case lands far from either anchor.

**Ruling 3 — a declared minimum only counts as branch (a) if structurally distinct from the
immediately preceding IRC point.** No new threshold invented, per critic16's own suggestion — reuse
§39.116(d)'s already-measured metric (centroid-removed / rotation-invariant max pairwise heavy-atom
distance change between the declared-minimum point and the path point immediately before it) and
**report the delta**, not gate on an unvalidated number. Reading rule, using anchors already on
record: §39.116(d) measured the confirmed-artifact case at 0.0203-0.0228 Å; ruling 1 above derived
0.05 Å as comfortably outside loose-optimization noise. A delta **below ~0.05 Å is artifact-
suspicious and needs a human read before being counted as branch (a)** (matching §39.116's own
finding at a comparable magnitude); a delta well above it (the way forward's real product basin sits
~1.7 Å from the reactant) is not in danger of this failure mode. This directly qualifies the

**What survived critic16's own attack on it, restated for the record**: the 4.27 arc-length floor was
